segmentation.text: No motorcycle
or motor scooter
shall be ridden
upon any sidewalk
of the City

elements.justification: 'motorcycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground, excluding an electric bicycle, a tractor or a moped'), one atom, never replaced by ru.motorcycle.

No definition applies to 'motor scooter'. A seated motor-driven scooter is either a motor vehicle on not more than three wheels with a seat, already a member of the motorcycle aggregate of s1, or a small-engined scooter that DEF-NRS-484A-125 names as a 'motor-driven scooter', which the motorcycle definition excludes as a moped: ru.moped, 'a low-power two- or three-wheeler with a small engine or motor, as a jurisdiction classes it'. The standing electric scooter (ru.electric_scooter) is not a 'motor scooter' of this chapter: the code defines and regulates 'electric scooter' separately (DEF-LVMC-11-02-083, chapter 11.40).

'be ridden' is the machine in controlled motion: not drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation — complete cessation from movement', speed at or below a tolerance). A motorcycle at rest on a sidewalk is not ridden. Who rides is read through the machine's motion (observable_reading, agency).

'sidewalk' (DEF-NRS-484A-240: 'that portion of a highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a highway and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians') is st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; not a crosswalk, its exclusion. 'upon any' is the footprint overlapping it: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... sidewalk ...)').

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies within the territorial limits of the incorporated city whose ordinances the reading applies, as the map's reading classifies the area

LVMC_11_38_030.applicability: The subject is a motorcycle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle) or a moped (ru.moped) whose footprint overlaps a sidewalk (rel.occupies, st.sidewalk) at a place the reading declares within the city's limits (asm.within_city_limits), read at the judged observation.
LVMC_11_38_030.obligation: At every such observation the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance); moving while on the sidewalk is violated.

narrowings.why: 'be ridden' is read through the machine's controlled motion (not at rest); whether a person sits on it or pushes it is not told apart.

scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle (ru.motorcycle) moves at 3 m/s with its footprint on a st.sidewalk, at a place declared asm.within_city_limits true.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle stands at rest (kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance) on a sidewalk within the city.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle moves on the roadway and occupies no sidewalk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle is on a sidewalk within the city; the source does not observe kin.speed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A moped (ru.moped) moves at 2 m/s on a sidewalk within the city.

scenarios.name: branch_2

segmentation.text: Where sidewalks are provided
it shall be unlawful for any pedestrian
to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway

elements.justification: 'sidewalks' (DEF-NRS-484A-240: 'that portion of a highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a highway and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians') is st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; it is not read as a crosswalk, its exclusion. 'provided' is the sidewalk's presence on the map (an observable_reading of category status). The sidewalk is tied to the place of the duty by st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'): the sidewalk lies on the highway (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders') on which the roadway the pedestrian occupies lies. st.on_way is not read as nearness to a way, its exclusion: both regions are recorded as lying on that highway.

'any pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), one atom, never expanded; same atoms as 'Any pedestrian' (LVMC_11_30_060_B). 'it shall be unlawful for' states the prohibition the obligation span describes.

'upon ... roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is the footprint overlapping st.roadway ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; not the sidewalk, which is not read here): rel.occupies. 'adjacent' ties that roadway to the sidewalks of s1: the roadway lies on the same highway (st.on_way, st.highway). 'walk along' is moving (not drv.motion.complete_halt: the road user is not at rest) and not moving across the designated direction of the lane (st.lane) or roadway it occupies (not drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, 'Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r'): with the same tolerance that separates crossing from walking along in LVMC_11_30_050, motion within that angle of the direction of travel is along it. st.lane serves as a carrier of a direction only, never as a half of the roadway, its exclusion.

LVMC_11_30_090.applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps a roadway r (rel.occupies, st.roadway) that lies on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway) on which a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) also lies (st.on_way), read at the judged observation.
LVMC_11_30_090.obligation: At every such observation, for every roadway r the subject occupies that lies on a highway on which a sidewalk lies (re-bound with the whole selection), the subject does not walk along r: it is violated where the subject is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) and, for a lane or roadway carrier c of r that it occupies (st.lane on the same highway, or r itself), it is not moving across c (not drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos); at rest or moving across the roadway is compliant.

narrowings.why: A sidewalk is 'provided' where the map records one lying on the same highway as the roadway the pedestrian occupies (st.on_way); its presence is the evidence that it was provided. A sidewalk on either side of the highway counts.

'walk along' is read as moving faster than p.halt_speed_tolerance and not across the occupied carrier's designated direction by more than the angle p.crossing_motion_cos sets; 'walk' is read for every member of the pedestrian aggregate (a person in a wheelchair included) as its motion. 'adjacent' is read as lying on the same highway as a sidewalk (st.on_way); no relation atom states adjacency more narrowly.

The carriers of r (r itself, or an occupied st.lane on the same highway) are read existentially for compliance: moving across any one of them (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier) is crossing, not walking along; a moving pedestrian violates only where its motion is along every such carrier.

scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian (ru.pedestrian) walks at 1.4 m/s along a lane, velocity parallel to its st.lane_direction, footprint on the roadway; a st.sidewalk lies on the same st.highway (st.on_way).

scenarios.narrative: On the same roadway the pedestrian walks across the lane at right angles to its st.lane_direction (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier holds).

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks along the sidewalk and occupies no roadway.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within a business or residence district
emerging or entering an alley, driveway or building
shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to
driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway or driveway
yielding
the right-of-way
to any pedestrian
as may be necessary to avoid collision
and
upon entering the roadway
shall yield
the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on said roadway

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'The driver of' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency), which ru.aggregate's exclusion of 'who drives or controls a vehicle' requires.

st.driveway_or_alley_entrance 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway' and st.alley 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties': the subject emerges from or enters one where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies) as it reaches the sidewalk. A building's vehicle access is a driveway: DEF-NRS-484A-190 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel'. The exclusion 'which of them meets the highway there' does not matter: the words treat alley, driveway and building alike.

'stop', required here, is DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement' (DEF-NRS-484A-260 governs stopping 'when prohibited'), carried by drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'immediately prior to' places the halt outside the sidewalk s, its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of s, the ground distance st.region_geometry ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') that the e5 element claims.

st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (its exclusion 'a crosswalk' does not apply); the sidewalk area across a driveway or alley is the sidewalk region the source maps across the entrance. 'driving onto' is the observation at which rel.occupies(subject, s) rises; the distance of the body to s (st.region_geometry) places the halt the obligation searches for.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district or a residence district, as the map's reading classifies the area

LVMC_11_20_060_o1.applicability: asm.business_or_residence_district holds; the subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), begins at this observation to occupy a sidewalk region s (st.sidewalk; rel.occupies(subject, s) here and not at the previous observation) while it occupies a driveway-or-alley-entrance region or an alley region d (st.driveway_or_alley_entrance or st.alley).
LVMC_11_20_060_o1.obligation: Event: the entry onto s judged. Place: outside s (rel.occupies(subject, s) false) with the ground distance from the subject's body to s (st.region_geometry) at most p.stop_point_tolerance — the stop zone. Act: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) at an observation in the stop zone. Search: back from the observation before the entry through the unbroken run of observations at which the subject was in the stop zone (written as: (in the stop zone, or the entry observation itself) since (in the stop zone and halted)). The run ends at the last observation at which the subject was outside the zone upstream (farther than p.stop_point_tolerance from s and not on it) or on s (the previous entry onto s for the same s); nothing else ends it — not a change of carrier, a reverse within the zone, or speed noise. Met where a halt lies in the run; violated where the run ends at an observed observation outside the zone or on s with no halt; unknown where the run reaches the start of the recording without a halt, or where the speed, occupancy or distance is missing at an observation the verdict turns on. A halt before the previous entry onto s does not count for this entry.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'immediately prior' is read as a halt within p.stop_point_tolerance of the sidewalk, outside it, in the run of observations the subject spends in that zone before driving onto it

scenarios.narrative: District assumed; the subject leaves a driveway and rolls onto the sidewalk at walking pace without its speed ever falling to the halt tolerance in the stop zone, having approached from beyond the zone.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but the subject halts within p.stop_point_tolerance of the sidewalk edge before driving onto it.

scenarios.name: idle

or any driver of any vehicle
who approaches or comes in contact with
a person wholly or partially blind, carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person
with wisdom

and take such precautions before proceeding
as may be necessary to avoid an accident or injury to the person wholly or partially blind

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'). 'who is not wholly or partially blind' leaves out the pedestrians the law protects; blindness itself is no observable, and is read through the feature the same sentence names as its sign: the subject is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal ('pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'), which carries no exclusion of its own.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exclusions of devices moved by human power, electric bicycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices and electric scooters, which the reading classifies). 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is the role of who controls the vehicle, never membership: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Same atoms as 'The driver of a vehicle' (LVMC_11_20_060_o1).

'comes in contact with' is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', taken at the observation at which it begins; a near miss is not contact, its exclusion, and is read by 'approaches'. 'approaches' is the subject, while not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt), coming within a reach of the person: the centre-to-centre distance (rel.centre_distance, 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points') falls to p.blind_person_approach_reach. That atom is not read as a clearance between bodies or an order of arrival, its exclusions: only as how near the subject has come.

The person protected is identified by the features the words list: 'carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person' is ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, 'pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'. 'a person wholly or partially blind' with those features is the pedestrian the class describes: the ontology's class for exactly this description, whose contract states no exclusion. The person is another road user than the subject, quantified in the applicability.

'stop' is required here, so DEF-NRS-484A-255 applies by its own scope ('when required, means complete cessation from movement'; DEF-NRS-484A-260 is scoped to stopping 'when prohibited'). 'come to a full stop' is drv.motion.complete_halt, whose contract quotes that definition: 'The road user is at rest at the observation — complete cessation from movement'.

operationalizations.standard: immediately
operationalizations.convention: The stop is immediate when the subject is at rest within a window ahead of the approach or contact event no longer than a perception-reaction time plus the braking time from an urban approach speed (AASHTO stopping-sight-distance model).

residues.why: 'with wisdom' qualifies the person assisting, not the person protected; that the person assisted is wholly or partially blind and is being assisted is what identifies the protected person, and a helper's wisdom, a state of mind no trace shows, does not change that identification, so the duty owed to the person assisted is the same whether or not the helper's wisdom holds.

LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1.applicability: The subject is either a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) that is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, or a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) read through its controlled motion; and at the judged observation, for some other road user b of the scene (not the same as the subject) of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, an approach or contact event occurs: rel.contact between the subject and b holds here and did not at the previous observation, or rel.centre_distance between them is at most p.blind_person_approach_reach here and was not at the previous observation while the subject is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance).
LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1.obligation: At each observation at which such an event occurs, the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) at some observation of the window ahead of length p.immediate_stop_window, measured in time on the subject. No halt in that window is violated; a window that reaches past the end of the trace without a halt is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motor vehicle (ru.motor_vehicle) moving at 10 m/s comes within p.blind_person_approach_reach (rel.centre_distance) of a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal at the kerb and keeps moving: no observation of the window p.immediate_stop_window ahead has kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same vehicle decelerates and is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt) within p.immediate_stop_window after the centre distance first falls to the reach.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle drives past an ordinary pedestrian (ru.pedestrian, no cane, not led); no road user of class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal is in the scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal stands near the vehicle's path; rel.centre_distance is not observed and no contact occurs, so whether the vehicle approached is unknown; the vehicle does not halt.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject is itself a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal walking toward another such pedestrian.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian (ru.pedestrian, no cane) walking comes into rel.contact with a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal and keeps walking, never at rest within p.immediate_stop_window.

param_proposals.convention: the centre distance within which a moving road user has approached a pedestrian carrying a white cane or led by another person: the stopping distance from an urban approach speed of about 13 m/s with a 1 s perception-reaction time and a 4.5 m/s^2 deceleration

param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping-sight-distance model

segmentation.text: Whenever a
usable
path for bicycles, electric bicycles, or electric scooters has been provided
adjacent to a roadway
riders of bicycles, electric bicycles, and electric scooters
shall use such path and shall not use the roadway

elements.justification: 'path for bicycles, electric bicycles, or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them': the classes the path is for are those the kind is reserved for. 'has been provided' is its presence on the map (status). It lies on a highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway).

'adjacent to a roadway' ties the path to the roadway (DEF-NRS-484A-220, 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder'; st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') through the highway both lie on (st.on_way, st.highway); st.on_way is not read as nearness, its exclusion: both regions are recorded on that highway.

'bicycles' (DEF-NRS-484A-025, 'a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'electric bicycles' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-082) and 'electric scooters' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-083) are admitted aggregates, each claimed as one atom. 'riders' is read through the machine's controlled motion (agency).

'use such path' is the rider's footprint on the path singled out by s3 (rel.occupies, st.bicycle_lane_or_path); 'not use the roadway' is the rider not travelling along that roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway): while moving (not drv.motion.complete_halt) on the roadway and off the path, it moves across a lane (st.lane, as a carrier of a direction only, never a half of the roadway) or the roadway it occupies (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, 'Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r'), as it does when crossing to or from the path; travelling along the roadway instead of the path is what the words forbid.

operationalizations.standard: usable
operationalizations.convention: A bicycle path is usable where its width (st.lane_width) is at least the operating width of one rider, p.usable_path_width_min (AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities), and no device closes it: no dev.regulatory_sign of code closed_to_traffic or bicycles_prohibited and no dev.temporary_traffic_control governs it (dev.governs).

LVMC_11_40_120.applicability: The subject is a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter in controlled motion (not drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway or a bicycle lane or path that lies on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway) on which both a roadway and a usable bicycle lane or path p lie: p's width (st.lane_width) is at least p.usable_path_width_min and no dev.regulatory_sign of code closed_to_traffic or bicycles_prohibited and no dev.temporary_traffic_control governs p (dev.governs).
LVMC_11_40_120.obligation: At every such observation, re-binding h and p with the whole selection: where the subject occupies a roadway lying on h and occupies no such usable path p, it moves across a lane or the roadway it occupies (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.rider_crossing_motion_cos); travelling along the roadway (moving, not across) off the path is violated; on the path is compliant.

narrowings.why: 'has been provided' is read from the path's presence on the map.
'riders' is read through the machine's controlled motion.

'use the roadway' is read as travelling along it (moving, not across the occupied carrier's direction by more than p.rider_crossing_motion_cos allows); crossing the roadway to reach or leave the path is not a use of it. 'use such path' is judged where the rider would otherwise travel along the roadway: a rider elsewhere on the highway (a sidewalk) is not judged by this rule.
'usable' is read through the path's width and its closure by a device; an obstruction on the path (st.obstruction) is not read, no relation atom placing an object on a region.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter (ru.electric_scooter) rides at 5 m/s along a lane of the roadway, velocity parallel to its st.lane_direction; a st.bicycle_lane_or_path 3 m wide, governed by no closing device, lies on the same highway.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same rider travels on the bicycle path, its footprint inside it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides along the roadway of a highway on which no bicycle lane or path lies.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle moves on the roadway beside which a usable path lies; the source does not observe kin.velocity, so whether it travels along or across the roadway is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The only bicycle path on the highway is governed by a dev.temporary_traffic_control closing it; a bicycle rides along the roadway.

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in this Chapter:
No person shall stand or park a vehicle
in a roadway
other than parallel with the edge of the roadway headed in the direction of lawful traffic movement.

elements.justification: "Except as otherwise provided in this Chapter": no node of the corpus states such a provision; what the Chapter otherwise provides for the position of a standing vehicle shows on the road as posted angle parking: a dev.regulatory_sign with code angle_parking ("a point regulation by catalogue code ... angle_parking") governing (dev.governs "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies). The sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre.

"a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, one atom. "stand or park": "stand" (DEF-NRS-484A-250, "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers") and "park" (DEF-NRS-484A-155, "the standing of a vehicle ... otherwise than temporarily") both exclude a halt for a passenger or loading exchange; drv.motion.parked ("at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration ... A halt shorter than min_duration, which may be the temporary halt the definition leaves out, is not denoted") carries the halt with that exclusion read through its length (observable_reading purpose). "No person shall" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

"in a roadway" (DEF-NRS-484A-220, "that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder"): st.roadway "the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder" at its whole extent; rel.occupies anchors the subject on it. Not the sidewalk.

"parallel with the edge of the roadway headed in the direction of lawful traffic movement": the direction of lawful movement of traffic (the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, "vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel", whose lawful direction the carrier designates) is st.lane_direction "direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in" of the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies); the edge of the roadway runs along that direction, so a heading (kin.heading "direction the body points") aligned with it within a tolerance is both parallel with the edge and headed with traffic. The heading is not the direction of motion, and the ruling direction is the carrier's, not the vehicle's.

LVMC_11_52_040_A.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that stands or parks: drv_motion_parked(subject) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.standing_min_duration, and it occupies a region of kind st.roadway (rel.occupies). Exception: some dev.regulatory_sign with code angle_parking governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies.
LVMC_11_52_040_A.obligation: For every travel region l (kind st.travel_region, not an intersection) the subject occupies that carries a designated direction, the subject's heading is aligned with it: kin_heading(subject) dot st_lane_direction(l) is at least p.parked_heading_cos (both read normalised). Unknown where an occupied carrier's direction or the heading is unobserved.

narrowings.why: What the Chapter otherwise provides is read through a posted angle_parking sign governing the subject's travel region; a provision that shows in no posted feature is not read.

The definitions' exclusion of a halt for receiving or discharging passengers or for loading is read through the halt's length: a halt shorter than the standing duration is not standing; "No person shall" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

"parallel with the edge of the roadway" is read through the designated direction of the carrier the vehicle occupies, along which the edge runs, rather than through the edge's own outline; parallel within the heading tolerance.

scenarios.name: forbid

scenarios.name: idle

scenarios.name: branch_1

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in branch_1, but a dev.regulatory_sign with code angle_parking governs l.

segmentation.text: No person shall park
a vehicle
in an access aisle.

elements.justification: 'Park' applies DEF-NRS-484A-155: 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading of merchandise or passengers'. drv.motion.parked denotes 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, observed as a at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration'; 'A halt shorter than min_duration, which may be the temporary halt the definition leaves out, is not denoted', which carries the definition's exclusion of a temporary halt for loading. Same mapping as the index's 'It shall be unlawful for any person to park' (LVMC_11_40_170).

'vehicle' is admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. It is not a relational role (who drives) and no class atom replaces an admitted aggregate.

'Access aisle' applies DEF-LVMC-11-02-030: an area 'Adjacent to a parking space designated for the handicapped' and 'Marked by spaced, crosshatched or diagonal stripes'. st.parking_space is a 'marked bay for standing or parking; designation in {general, disabled, disabled_side_lift, access_aisle, municipal, charging}': the designation access_aisle is the marked aisle beside a disabled bay. 'in' places the vehicle there: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', anchors the vehicle to the aisle it is in, not to any aisle of the scene.

LVMC_11_52_136.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and its footprint overlaps a parking-space region whose designation is access_aisle (st.parking_space, rel.occupies) at the observation.
LVMC_11_52_136.obligation: The subject is not parked (drv.motion.parked with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.parking_min_duration) while its footprint overlaps that access-aisle region: for every parking-space region of designation access_aisle the subject occupies at the observation, the subject is not parked there.

narrowings.why: 'No person shall park' is read through the vehicle's own standing; whoever or whatever controls it, the duty binds the vehicle's conduct.

The definition's exclusion of a halt made 'temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading' is read through the halt's duration: a halt shorter than p.parking_min_duration is the temporary halt and is not parking; the loading purpose itself is not observed.

The defined area's design for 'unobstructed ingress, egress and access' and its adjacency to a disabled bay are read through the mapped marking: a parking-space region the source designates access_aisle is the access aisle.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car (vehicle aggregate) comes to rest with its footprint overlapping a st.parking_space of designation access_aisle beside a disabled bay and stays at rest there (kin.speed at or below the tolerance) for longer than p.parking_min_duration.

scenarios.name: idle

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car stands at rest next to an access-aisle region for longer than p.parking_min_duration; the source does not observe rel.occupies, so whether it is in the aisle is unknown.

segmentation.text: It shall be unlawful for any person driving or operating, propelling or causing to be propelled, any vehicle,
to fail to stop not less than fifty feet from the nearest side of
a school pedestrian lane
where any signal device, flagman or other person is stationed, giving warning that children are about to cross or are crossing the street;
and it is further declared unlawful to proceed
until such signal has stopped, raised, or been removed, or the flagman or person stationed at such pedestrian lane has given a signal to go, or has left the locality.

elements.justification: "any vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), one atom; the driving person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

"to proceed" refers to the stop the first clause requires, with its qualification kept: a halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, carrying DEF-NRS-484A-255 "complete cessation from movement", the definition whose scope is a stop "when required") made while the body distance to the crosswalk (st.region_geometry "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it") is not less than fifty feet, under the warning. The first clause's duty itself is node LVMC_11_46_030_o1; here the stop is the act this duty follows, carried in full, not the other rule's verdict.

Same words, same atoms as LVMC_11_46_030_o1: st.crosswalk "marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks" on the street (st.on_way to the st.highway the subject's travel region lies on), ahead of the subject along its travel region by prim.region_offset_along (positive, the side only).

Same words, same atoms as LVMC_11_46_030_o1: dev.crossing_warning_signal with active true, or dev.human_direction of any role with indication stop, governing (dev.governs "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

"unlawful to proceed": the vehicle stays at rest; drv.motion.complete_halt ("at rest at the observation ... speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance") failing is any movement after the stop. Not denoted by the concept: why it stays.

"until such signal has stopped, raised, or been removed": the same dev.crossing_warning_signal d no longer has its active attribute, or is no longer in the scene or no longer governs the subject's travel region (dev.governs). "or the flagman or person stationed at such pedestrian lane has given a signal to go": the same dev.human_direction d shows indication proceed ("indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}"). "or has left the locality": d is no longer in the scene or no longer governs the subject's travel region. "such" singles out the device that gave the warning the subject stopped for; each end condition reads that device.

LVMC_11_46_030_o2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). At the judged observation bind, as in LVMC_11_46_030_o1, a travel region g with rel.occupies(subject, g), a device d with dev.governs(d, g) giving warning (dev.crossing_warning_signal active, or dev.human_direction of any role with indication stop), a highway w with st.on_way(g, w), and the nearest crosswalk c on w ahead of the subject along g (prim.region_offset_along(subject, c, g) > 0). The subject stopped for that warning and the warning has lasted since: since(warning(d) and ahead(c), drv_motion_complete_halt(subject) and st_region_geometry_distance(subject, c) >= the literal fifty feet and warning(d) and ahead(c)), with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance. The duty ends ('until') at the first observation at which d gives no warning: the signal's active attribute is false or the signal is gone or no longer governs g ('stopped, raised, or been removed'); the person's indication is proceed ('a signal to go'), or the person is gone or no longer governs g ('has left the locality'); from then the since fails and the duty does not apply.
LVMC_11_46_030_o2.obligation: The subject does not proceed: drv_motion_complete_halt(subject) holds at the judged observation, with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance.

narrowings.why: "any person driving or operating, propelling or causing to be propelled" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
The school pedestrian lane is the crosswalk at which the warning of children crossing is given; the school designation is read through that warning.

"stationed" at the pedestrian lane is read as a warning device or person governing the subject's travel region, the lane being the nearest crosswalk ahead on the same way; "children are about to cross or are crossing" is read through the warning given.
"proceed" is read as any movement above the halt tolerance after the stop, forward or not.

segmentation.text: In no case shall any part of any vehicle
part of the load of such vehicle
or trailer
attached to such vehicle
project into the street more than fifteen feet measured on a line at right angles to the curb.

elements.justification: "any vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed whole and never expanded into classes. "any part of" the vehicle is any point of its body, whose size kin.extent carries ("the body's size along its axes about the reference point"), so the farthest point of the body is what the bound reads. "In no case" admits no exception.

"trailer" is the admitted aggregate DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer ("a vehicle, other than a commercial vehicle or recreational vehicle, that is without motor power, is designed and constructed to be drawn by a motor vehicle"), claimed whole: the trailer is judged as a road user of its own, its body read by the same bound.

"part of the load of such vehicle" is read through the outline the source reports for the vehicle's body, kin.extent ("the body's size along its axes about the reference point"): a load carried on the vehicle within that outline is judged with it; a load overhanging the reported outline is not seen, as the narrowing on span s5 discloses.

"project" states where a standing body stands out into the street, in a section of the chapter on stopping, standing and parking: it is read for a vehicle that stands in the street, drv.motion.parked ("Road user a is parked: \"the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not\", observed as a at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation"); the narrowing discloses the reading. "street" is DEF-NRS-484A-265 ("the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city", not an aggregate): st.highway ("the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders"); its "not a stand-in for: the roadway" clause is respected since the definition names the entire width; rel.occupies ("a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region") anchors the vehicle on its own street, as the mapping index reads "upon a street"; the city limits are the ordinance's own territorial scope. "more than fifteen feet" is the stated figure (literal): the body's projection, the ground distance from the curb to its outline (st.region_geometry, "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it") plus the body's own extent across the curb line (kin.extent, "a formula reads the full length, width and height"), is compared with it. "the curb" is st.road_edge ("curb or edge of the roadway") lying on the vehicle's street (st.on_way, "the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on"); the curb the vehicle stands at is the road edge of that street nearest its body (st.region_geometry ground distance). "on a line at right angles to the curb": the curb runs along the designated direction of the travel region the vehicle occupies (st.lane_direction, "direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in ... a roadway"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region), so the body's extent at right angles to the curb is its length (kin.extent) times the absolute cross product of its heading (kin.heading, read normalised) with that direction plus its width times their absolute dot product. The sign of the direction does not matter. st.lane_direction is not used as a manoeuvre or a path: only its line is read; the narrowing on this span discloses the reading.

residues.why: A trailer is itself "a vehicle" by its definition DEF-LVMC-11-02-170, so the duty binds its body through "any vehicle" whether or not it is attached; attachment adds no restriction.

LVMC_11_52_060.applicability: The subject, a vehicle or a trailer (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle or DEF-LVMC-11-02-170::trailer), is parked at the observation (drv.motion.parked(subject; speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration = p.parking_min_duration)) and its footprint overlaps a highway h (rel.occupies subject h, st.highway): it stands in a street.
LVMC_11_52_060.obligation: For every highway h the subject occupies (rel.occupies), every road edge c (st.road_edge) lying on h (st.on_way c h) whose ground distance from the subject's body (st_region_geometry_distance) is at most that of every other road edge lying on h (the curb the vehicle stands at), and every travel region r (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies): the ground distance from the subject's body to c, plus the subject's length (kin_extent length) times the absolute value of the cross product of its heading (kin_heading x, y) with r's designated direction (st_lane_direction x, y), plus its width (kin_extent width) times the absolute value of their dot product, is at most fifteen feet (literal 15 ft). Where r carries no direction, the heading or the geometry is unobserved, the sum is unknown.

narrowings.why: "project" is read for a vehicle that stands in the street, parked (at rest for p.parking_min_duration): a vehicle travelling or halted briefly in traffic is not judged, though the words name no state of motion; the section sits among the stopping, standing and parking rules and measures from the curb a vehicle stands at. A load is judged only within the body outline the source reports; a load overhanging that outline is not seen.

The curb's line is read as the designated direction of the travel region the vehicle occupies, and the curb as the road edge of its street nearest its body; the projection is the body-to-curb distance plus the body's extent across that line, which assumes the body lies on the street side of the curb.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car 1.8 m wide is parked for 10 minutes parallel to the curb, 0.3 m from it, heading along the roadway's direction: its body reaches about 2.1 m into the street.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car travels at 12 m/s along the far lane of the street, 8 m from the curb: it is not parked, so the rule does not apply.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A truck is parked at right angles to the curb, but the source maps regions without their outline (st.region_geometry absent): the distance from the body to the curb is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A detached trailer 8 m long is parked for 10 minutes at right angles to the curb, 0.1 m from it: as a vehicle in its own right its body reaches about 8.1 m into the street.

segmentation.text: Whenever any person is riding a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter upon a sidewalk
such person shall yield
the right-of-way
to any pedestrian
and shall give audible signal
before overtaking and passing
such pedestrian

elements.justification: As in LVMC_11_40_180_C_o1: the three admitted aggregates; 'riding' read through controlled motion (not drv.motion.complete_halt); st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', anchored by rel.occupies.

sig.horn: 'an ordinary horn ... sounding (audible)'; sig.siren: 'a siren, whistle or bell sounding (audible)' — a bicycle bell or a whistle is the latter, a horn the former; either sounding is an audible signal. Neither is read from a visible state ('no visible state stands in for it'); a source without audio declares them absent, and the rule is then unknown.

drv.interaction.overtake_pass: 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'. 'before' is read with the same relations the concept states: the pedestrian ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with headings aligned (rel.same_direction), during the run of observations that ends at the act's onset.
'such pedestrian' refers back to 'any pedestrian': the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot ...'), the road user b of the pass.

LVMC_11_40_180_C_o2.applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter. For a pedestrian p of the scene (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, not the subject), at the observation at which drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, p; p.overtake_window, p.overtake_same_direction_cos) holds (the pass is recognized), where at some observation while the pass was under way (from its onset to its recognition) the subject occupied an st.sidewalk region and was not at rest.
LVMC_11_40_180_C_o2.obligation: Act before an event (rule 4c). Event: the onset of the pass, the last observation of the window behind at which p was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction with p.overtake_same_direction_cos), read with atLast over p.overtake_window. Act: sig.horn or sig.siren sounding for the subject. Search: from the onset back through the run of observations at which p stays ahead of the subject; it ends at the observation at which that run began (p came to be ahead), which is the approach start, or at the recognition of a previous pass of p by the subject. A signal found in the search: compliant. The search reaching its start without a signal: violated. Where the run began before the recording, or the signal or the relations are unobserved at an observation the search crosses, without a signal found: unknown. A signal given while p is alongside or after it is behind does not discharge the duty.

narrowings.why: 'any person is riding' is read through the device's controlled motion.
An audible signal is read as a horn, bell or whistle sounding (sig.horn, sig.siren); a spoken warning has no atom, so a rider who warns only by voice is read as giving no signal.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on the sidewalk behind a pedestrian walking the same way, draws alongside and passes, and no horn, bell or whistle sounds while the pedestrian is ahead of it; the pedestrian came to be ahead within the recording.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same pass, with the bicycle's bell sounding while the pedestrian is still ahead of it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on the sidewalk behind a pedestrian at the same pace and never passes.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The same pass with no signal in the trace, from a source without audio that declares horn and bell absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter begins the pass on the roadway edge and moves onto the sidewalk while alongside the pedestrian, completing the pass there without any signal.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides on the sidewalk, leaves it for the roadway before drawing alongside, and passes a pedestrian on the sidewalk from the roadway without signal: it is on the sidewalk only before the act began.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the pedestrian already ahead of the bicycle on the sidewalk; the bicycle passes without a signal in the recording, and the search reaches the start of the recording without reaching the observation at which the pedestrian came to be ahead.
scenarios.boundary: the run of observations with the pedestrian ahead of the rider begins before the recording

segmentation.text: The City Traffic Engineer shall determine upon what streets angle parking shall be permitted,
and shall provide signage or other markings to indicate where such parking is permitted.
Where angle parking is permitted,
no person shall stand or park a vehicle unless the front of the vehicle is pointed toward the direction of lawful traffic movement.

elements.justification: The Traffic Engineer's determination of the streets where angle parking is permitted is a legal status no scene shows; the next words name its evidence, the signage or markings. It is read through them: a regulatory sign of code angle_parking (dev.regulatory_sign, "a point regulation by catalogue code ... angle_parking") governing (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") the travel region the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), or a marked parking bay (st.parking_space, "marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute") whose angle stands clear of zero. The sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre (its not-a-stand-in clause).

"signage" is the angle_parking regulatory sign (dev.regulatory_sign) governing (dev.governs) the travel region the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region); "other markings" is a marked bay (st.parking_space, "marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute") the vehicle occupies whose angle (st_parking_space_angle) stands clear of zero by more than the source's angle resolution. Their presence is the evidence of the permission they indicate.

"Where angle parking is permitted" is the place the signage or markings indicate: a travel region the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) that an angle_parking sign governs (dev.regulatory_sign, dev.governs), or that the vehicle occupies together with an angled marked bay (st.parking_space with its angle clear of zero). Presence of the feature, no size bound: the angle is read only against the source's resolution.

"no person shall stand or park a vehicle" has the same words and meaning as the mapping index's "No person shall stand or park a vehicle" (LVMC_11_52_040_A): drv.motion.parked ("Road user a is parked: \"the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not\"") with the standing duration as its window, covering standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250, "the halting of a vehicle ... otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers") and parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155); "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole. "No person" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion. "unless the front ...": same words as the mapping index's "headed in the direction of lawful traffic movement" (LVMC_11_52_040_A): "the front of the vehicle" points along kin.heading ("direction the body points"; not its velocity, so a standing vehicle has one); "the direction of lawful traffic movement" is the direction designated for traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, claimed whole as the word's admitted aggregate) on the travel region the vehicle occupies: st.lane_direction ("direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in"), read on that region (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). "pointed toward" is a positive dot product of the heading with that direction.

LVMC_11_52_070.applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region r (st.travel_region) where angle parking is permitted: a regulatory sign of code angle_parking (dev.regulatory_sign) governs r (dev.governs), or the subject also occupies a parking space (st.parking_space) whose angle (st_parking_space_angle), in absolute value, exceeds p.parking_space_angle_resolution.
LVMC_11_52_070.obligation: Where the subject is parked (drv.motion.parked(subject; speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration = p.standing_min_duration)), for every travel region r it occupies that is selected as in the applicability (governed by an angle_parking sign, or occupied together with an angled parking space), the dot product of the subject's heading (kin_heading) with r's designated direction (st_lane_direction) is positive: the front of the vehicle points toward the direction of lawful traffic movement. A subject that is not parked complies. Where r carries no direction or the heading is unobserved, the verdict is unknown.

narrowings.why: The Traffic Engineer's determination is a legal status read through the signage or markings that display it: a determination no sign or marking displays is not read.

The duty to provide signage or markings is the Engineer's and is not judged on a trace; the presence of the angle_parking sign or the angled marked bay is read as the indication of where angle parking is permitted.

"the direction of lawful traffic movement" is read as the designated direction of the travel region the vehicle occupies at the angle-parking place; a vehicle wholly inside a bay that overlaps no travel region is not judged.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car has backed into an angled bay (angle 45 degrees) on a street whose lane carries an angle_parking sign; its rear overlaps the lane and its heading is opposite the lane's direction; it stays at rest for 5 minutes.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car stands for 5 minutes in the same angled bay with its heading 45 degrees off the lane's direction, pointing forward with traffic: the dot product with the lane's direction is positive.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car is parked parallel to the curb on a street with no angle_parking sign and no angled bay: the rule does not apply.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car is parked in an angled bay at an angle_parking sign, but the source does not supply headings (kin.heading absent): where its front points is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car pulls into the angled bay heading against the lane's direction, halts 20 seconds to let a passenger out and leaves: it neither stands nor parks for the standing duration.

segmentation.text: The City Council may designate parking spaces upon City streets or in City parking facilities for the parking of City vehicles.
It is unlawful to park
a vehicle
other than a City vehicle
in any such space that has been duly posted or marked.

elements.justification: The designated space is the referent of 'such space' in s5. st.parking_space is a 'marked bay for standing or parking; ... designation in {general, disabled, disabled_side_lift, access_aisle, municipal, charging}': designation municipal is a bay reserved for the city's own vehicles, whether on a street or in a city parking facility (DEF-LVMC-11-02-050: a lot or garage 'which the City owns, operates or maintains'); the place of the bay restricts nothing beyond its municipal designation, which the Council makes only there.

'park' applies DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading'; drv.motion.parked denotes 'at rest at every observation of the window behind ... of length min_duration', a shorter halt 'is not denoted'. Same mapping as the index's 'It shall be unlawful for any person to park'.
'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

A City vehicle is one the incorporated city (DEF-NRS-484A-045) operates; ru.official_vehicle is 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment; kind in {..., municipal, ...}', and kind municipal is the city's own vehicle. 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' is respected: the exception reads the municipal kind, not the emergency class.

'such space' is the space s1 designates: a st.parking_space of designation municipal; 'duly posted or marked' is its posting or marking, whose presence on the road is the evidence of the designation. rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors the vehicle in that space, not any municipal space of the scene.

LVMC_11_52_340.applicability: The subject is a vehicle that is not a municipal official vehicle (ru.official_vehicle kind municipal does not hold), and its footprint overlaps a parking-space region of designation municipal (st.parking_space, rel.occupies) at the observation.
LVMC_11_52_340.obligation: For every parking-space region of designation municipal the subject occupies at the observation, the subject is not parked there (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.parking_min_duration).

narrowings.why: That the space was designated by the City Council and 'duly posted or marked' is read through the mapped municipal designation of the bay, the posting or marking on the road being the evidence of the designation.
The definition's temporary halt for loading or unloading is read through the halt's duration (min_duration p.parking_min_duration); the loading purpose is not observed.

A City vehicle is recognized by its municipal livery or equipment (ru.official_vehicle kind municipal); a city-owned vehicle without such livery, or a city emergency vehicle the source labels only by its emergency class, is read as not a City vehicle, so the duty is applied to it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A private passenger car (vehicle aggregate, not ru.official_vehicle municipal) comes to rest in a st.parking_space of designation municipal and stays at rest there for ten minutes.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A private passenger car halts for thirty seconds in a municipal parking space to let a passenger out and then drives off; it is never parked there.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A ru.official_vehicle of kind municipal stays at rest for an hour in a municipal parking space.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A private passenger car stands at rest for ten minutes beside a municipal parking space; the source does not observe rel.occupies, so whether it is in the space is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A private passenger car stays at rest for an hour in a parking space of designation general; it occupies no municipal space.

segmentation.text: The following regulations pertain to
the operation of vehicles within a roundabout
The operator of a vehicle
who intends to exit a roundabout
Shall use the right lane to turn right

elements.justification: "vehicles" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed as one atom. "within a roundabout": st.roundabout "a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches" carries DEF-LVMC-11-02-130 at its whole extent; rel.occupies "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region" anchors the subject to that roundabout. Same mapping as the index.

"a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; "The operator" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency). Same mapping as the index entry "The operator of a vehicle".

The intention to exit is read through the exit it leads to (observable_reading intention): the observation at which the subject's footprint (rel.occupies "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region") ceases to overlap the roundabout r (st.roundabout), the recognition of drv.motion.right_turn_through_region ("its exit from r").

"to turn right": drv.motion.right_turn_through_region ("a turn to the right through region r ... from minus u_turn_min exclusive to minus turn_min inclusive") with r the roundabout exited. "use the right lane": st.lane "a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles" with st.lane_adjacency "lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane": the right lane is the lane whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction; rel.occupies anchors the lanes the footprint overlaps. Lane membership is never read as an offset from the edge.

LVMC_11_43_010_C2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). Bind a region r of kind st.roundabout. At the judged observation the subject exits r having turned right through it: drv_motion_right_turn_through_region(subject, r) holds with step .param p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min. The intention to exit is read through this exit.
LVMC_11_43_010_C2.obligation: Re-bind the same roundabout: a region r of kind st.roundabout for which the concept holds for the subject at the judged observation. The subject used the right lane within r: at every observation from its entry into r (the latest observation at which rel.occupies(subject, r) rose) up to the judged observation, wherever rel.occupies(subject, r) holds, every region l of kind st.lane with rel.occupies(subject, l) has st_lane_adjacency_ordinal(l) = st_lane_adjacency_count(l), the rightmost lane of its direction. Written with since as for the left lane: since(phi, rises(occupies(subject, r)) and phi). Unknown where the entry lies before the recording or an occupied lane's ordinal or count is unobserved.

narrowings.why: "The operator" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle whoever or whatever controls it.
"who intends to exit a roundabout" is read through the exit itself: the duty is judged at the observation at which the vehicle leaves the roundabout, the recognition of the turn.

"use the right lane" is read as occupying, within the roundabout, no lane other than the rightmost lane of its carriageway (ordinal equal to the count of lanes in its direction) from the entry to the exit; a single-lane roundabout's only lane is the rightmost.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A two-lane roundabout r (st.roundabout) whose lanes carry st.lane_adjacency ordinals 1 (inner) and 2 (outer) with a count of two. The subject, a passenger car (ru.motor_vehicle), enters r heading east in the lane of ordinal 1 and leaves at the first exit heading south, its yaw rate observed at every scene integrating to a quarter turn to the right since the entry: the right turn through r is recognized and the subject occupied the lane of ordinal 1.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout and right turn, made in the lane of ordinal 2 throughout.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout; the subject enters heading east in the lane of ordinal 1 and leaves heading north, a quarter turn to the left since the entry: no right turn is recognized.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source supplies no lane ordinals or counts (st.lane_adjacency absent).

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in permit, but within r the subject drifts so that its footprint overlaps both lanes for several scenes before the exit.

onset.words: the operation of vehicles within a roundabout
onset.justification: The act begins at the subject's entry into the roundabout: the observation at which rel.occupies(subject, r) rose, the onset the concept declares.

occasion.recognition: who intends to exit a roundabout

under_way.justification: Inside the act the subject's heading change since its entry into r (headingSince, integrated from kin.yaw_rate "rate of change of heading") is defined and its footprint overlaps r; before the entry it is not.

param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: turning-movement classification in intersection geometric design practice (AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets)

segmentation.text: No vehicle
shall at any time be driven
through or within a safety zone.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; claimed as the aggregate. Same mapping as the index's 'No vehicle'.

'be driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven. Moving is the negation of drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation ... its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance'). 'at any time' makes every observation a judged one.

'safety zone' (DEF-NRS-484B-057: 'the area officially set aside within a highway for the exclusive use of pedestrians and which is so plainly marked') is st.safety_zone, 'an area within the highway marked off for pedestrians only'; 'through or within' it is the vehicle's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (..., safety zone, ...)').

NRS_484B_110.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is moving at the observation: not drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance.
NRS_484B_110.obligation: At every such observation the subject's footprint overlaps no safety zone: for every region z of kind st.safety_zone, not rel.occupies(subject, z).

narrowings.why: 'be driven' is read through the vehicle's motion: a moving vehicle is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
A safety zone 'officially set aside' and 'plainly marked' is read by the presence of the marked st.safety_zone region.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car moving at 8 m/s crosses a marked safety zone: its footprint overlaps the zone at several observations.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car moving at 8 m/s passes beside the safety zone, its footprint never overlapping it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car stays at rest at the curb for the whole recording.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car moves past a safety zone; the source does not report which regions the car's footprint overlaps.

segmentation.text: It shall be unlawful for any person driving or operating, propelling or causing to be propelled, any vehicle,
to fail to stop not less than fifty feet from the nearest side of
a school pedestrian lane
where any signal device, flagman or other person is stationed, giving warning that children are about to cross or are crossing the street;

and it is further declared unlawful to proceed until such signal has stopped, raised, or been removed, or the flagman or person stationed at such pedestrian lane has given a signal to go, or has left the locality.

elements.justification: "any vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), one atom, never expanded. "any person driving or operating, propelling or causing to be propelled" names who controls the vehicle, read through its controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

"stop" here is a stop the law requires, so the definition whose own scope is "when required" (DEF-NRS-484A-255, "complete cessation from movement") is the one whose scope the words meet; drv.motion.complete_halt carries it ("The road user is at rest at the observation ... at or below a tolerance the caller sets for the source's speed resolution"). "not less than fifty feet from the nearest side of" the crossing: st.region_geometry "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)" is the distance from the vehicle's body to the nearest side of the crosswalk region, a distance the words themselves state (literal); it is not used for occupancy, so the "Not a stand-in for: occupancy" clause does not apply.

"a school pedestrian lane": st.crosswalk "marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection" — a lane for pedestrians to cross the street; not a sidewalk. Its school character is read through the warning of children crossing given there (observable_reading status). "the street" it crosses: st.on_way "the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on" ties the crosswalk to the highway (st.highway, "the entire public way between its boundary lines") on which the subject's governed travel region also lies; st.on_way is not nearness. The crosswalk is the one the subject approaches: prim.region_offset_along "the signed distance ... from a road user's reference point ... to a structure region ... measured along a carrier's designated direction" positive puts it ahead of the subject along its travel region's direction; the primitive establishes only the side, and the nearest side's distance is read from st.region_geometry, as its contract requires.

"any signal device ... giving warning that children are about to cross or are crossing": dev.crossing_warning_signal "a signal device at a pedestrian or school crossing that warns of persons crossing; active attribute" with active true. "flagman or other person is stationed, giving warning": dev.human_direction "a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}" of any role ("or other person"), indication stop, the warning that halts traffic. "stationed" at the crossing the subject approaches is read through dev.governs "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls" on the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"): a device governing the subject's travel region and a crosswalk ahead of it on the same way. dev.governs is not a position, and the halt place is read from the crosswalk, not from the device.

LVMC_11_46_030_o1.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The duty arises at an event: at the judged observation t the subject comes within fifty feet of a crosswalk at which a warning is given. Bind a travel region g (kind st.travel_region) with rel.occupies(subject, g); a device d with dev.governs(d, g) that gives warning at t: a dev.crossing_warning_signal whose active attribute holds, or a dev.human_direction of any role whose indication is stop; a highway w (st.highway) with st.on_way(g, w); a crosswalk c (st.crosswalk) with st.on_way(c, w), ahead of the subject along g (prim.region_offset_along(subject, c, g) > 0), and the nearest such crosswalk ahead (no other crosswalk on w has a smaller positive offset along g). The event: st_region_geometry_distance(subject, c) is below the literal fifty feet at t and was at or above it at the observation before (rises of the distance being below fifty feet).
LVMC_11_46_030_o1.obligation: Duty of rule 4c. Act: a halt of the subject (drv_motion_complete_halt(subject) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) at an observation at which the body distance st_region_geometry_distance(subject, c) is at or above the literal fifty feet, c is ahead of the subject along a travel region it occupies that d governs, and d gives warning. Search: back from t through observations at which d gives warning continuously and c stays ahead of the subject along a travel region it occupies that d governs. The search ends at the onset of d's warning (the observation at which d's warning rose: a halt before the warning began is no halt for it), at the previous occurrence of the same event for the same subject and crosswalk (an earlier rise of 'within fifty feet of c'), or at an observation at which c is not ahead. Written: since(warning(d) and ahead(c) and not earlier-event, halt(subject) and distance(subject, c) >= fifty feet and warning(d) and ahead(c)). Where the search finds the halt, compliant; where it reaches the warning's onset, the previous event or an observation with c not ahead without the halt, violated; where it reaches the start of the recording with d warning and c ahead at every observation and no halt found, unknown. A missing distance, governance or direction makes the duty unknown only where the verdict turns on it.

narrowings.why: "any person driving or operating, propelling or causing to be propelled" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle whoever or whatever controls it.
The crosswalk is a school pedestrian lane where the warning of children crossing is given there; the school designation is read through that warning, not through a separate designation.

"that children are about to cross or are crossing" is read through the warning given, not through children observed: the device's or person's warning (signal active, or a person's stop indication) is the evidence of the crossing it announces; the device stationed at the pedestrian lane is the one governing the subject's travel region with that lane the nearest crosswalk ahead on the same way.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A straight two-way street w (st.highway) with a lane g (st.lane, direction east, st.on_way w) and a marked crosswalk c across w ahead. A school crossing guard (dev.human_direction, role school_crossing_guard, indication stop) governs g from before the subject appears until after it passes. The subject, a passenger car (ru.motor_vehicle) in g, approaches from far upstream at a steady urban speed and, without halting, comes within fifty feet of c and passes through it; distances, speed and governance observed at every scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the subject halts (speed at or below the halt tolerance) while its body is farther than fifty feet from c and the guard still indicates stop; later the guard indicates proceed and the subject drives on through the crosswalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Same street and crosswalk, but no warning device and no person directing traffic is in the scene; the subject drives through c without halting.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source maps regions without outlines (st.region_geometry absent): the distance from the subject's body to c, and so the event, is unknown.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The guard indicates stop over g at every scene of the recording; the subject is in g with c ahead from its first observation, is moving at its first observation and comes within fifty feet of c later without any halt recorded; whether it halted for the warning before the recording began is not observed.
scenarios.boundary: the approach to c under the guard's warning before the recording's first scene: the warning's onset and the subject's conduct since then

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the warning is given by a dev.crossing_warning_signal governing g whose active attribute holds, and no person directs traffic.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject halts farther than fifty feet from c before any warning is given, the guard then steps out with the stop indication, and the subject moves on and comes within fifty feet of c without halting again while the warning lasts.
