segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter
within a business or residence district
entering into or emerging from an alley, driveway or building
shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to
driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway, driveway or building
yielding the right-of-way to any pedestrian
as may be necessary to avoid collision

elements.justification: Each term is admitted as its aggregate: 'bicycle' DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'electric bicycle' DEF-LVMC-11-02-082::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor'), 'electric scooter' DEF-LVMC-11-02-083::electric_scooter ('a device with handlebars and an electric motor'); the subject belongs to one of them (same words as the mapping index's 'Any person operating a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter'). 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion.

rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; st.alley: 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; st.driveway_or_alley_entrance: 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway' (its 'not a stand-in' clause, which of them meets the highway, does not matter: alley and driveway are both named); st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' — a road user that occupies no highway region is beyond the property line, where a building stands. Read at the entry onto the sidewalk: emerging = at the observation before the entry the subject occupies an alley or a driveway/alley entrance, or occupies no highway region; entering into = at the entry the subject occupies an alley or a driveway/alley entrance (the sidewalk area extending across it), or from the entry it occupies the sidewalk until it occupies no highway region (the movement into a building read by the movement itself).

Same words as the mapping index (LVMC_11_20_060_o1): drv.motion.complete_halt, whose definition DEF-NRS-484A-255 applies to 'Stop, when required' ('complete cessation from movement'); the stop is required here, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 (stopping when prohibited) does not apply. 'such vehicle' refers back to the device the subject operates; it is not a new class condition (the vehicle definition DEF-NRS-484A-320 excludes devices moved by human power, electric bicycles and electric scooters, so reading it as a class would empty the duty). 'immediately prior to' places the halt in the stopping zone just short of the sidewalk, read with e5.

Same atoms as the mapping index's 'driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway or driveway'. st.sidewalk: 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (not a crosswalk: none is meant); rel.occupies marks the event, the footprint coming to overlap the sidewalk; st.region_geometry: 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it' bounds the stopping zone outside the sidewalk. The sidewalk area across an alleyway, driveway or building is a part of a sidewalk region.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district or a residence district, as the map's reading classifies the area

LVMC_11_40_140_o1.applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter (any of the three aggregates). For a sidewalk region s, at the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap s (rel.occupies(subject, s) there and not at the observation before), asm.business_or_residence_district holds and the subject enters into or emerges from an alley, driveway or building: at that observation or the one before it occupies an st.alley or st.driveway_or_alley_entrance region; or at the observation before it occupies no st.highway region; or from that observation on it occupies s until it occupies no st.highway region.
LVMC_11_40_140_o1.obligation: Act before an event (rule 4c). Event: the entry onto sidewalk s defined in the applicability. Place: the stopping zone of s, the observations at which the subject does not occupy s and the ground distance from its body to s (st.region_geometry) is at most p.stop_point_tolerance. Act: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) at an observation in that zone. Search: from the observation before the event back through the observations at which the subject's body stays within p.stop_point_tolerance of s; it ends at the last observation before the event at which the subject is farther than p.stop_point_tolerance from s (the approach start) or at the last observation at which it occupied s (its previous entry onto s, whose halt does not count for this one). A halt found in the zone within the search: compliant. The search reaching either end without a halt: violated. Where it reaches neither end without a halt, because the recording begins inside the zone or the distance to s or the occupancy of s is unobserved at an observation the search crosses: unknown. A reverse, a lateral move or a speed fluctuation inside the zone begins no new approach. The halt is read on s itself, the sidewalk the event enters; no other sidewalk stands for it.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion: whoever or whatever controls it, the device's conduct is judged.

'immediately prior to' is read as a halt in the stopping zone of the sidewalk being entered, outside it and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it, during the approach that leads to the entry (the ontology's convention for an act due at a place before an event); a halt made farther back does not discharge the duty.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: In a declared residence district a bicycle rides out of a driveway entrance and onto the sidewalk without its speed falling to the halt tolerance while within the stopping zone; it was farther than the tolerance from the sidewalk earlier in the recording.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same bicycle halts just short of the sidewalk, within the stopping zone and outside the sidewalk, then rides onto it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides along the sidewalk from one sidewalk region into the next, coming from the sidewalk, not from an alley, a driveway or off the public way.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle emerges from a driveway onto the sidewalk with no halt recorded, and the source maps regions without their outline, so the stopping zone and the approach start cannot be read.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the electric bicycle already within the stopping zone, moving out of a driveway; it enters the sidewalk with no halt recorded, and the search reaches the start of the recording without reaching the approach start.
scenarios.boundary: the subject's approach to the sidewalk: the last observation at which it was farther than p.stop_point_tolerance from the sidewalk lies before the recording

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The same driveway exit without a halt, in a place the map's reading declares outside any business or residence district.

segmentation.text: Streets
other than truck routes
shall not be used as through routes
from one truck route to another
unless pick-up, delivery or essential use is required enroute

elements.justification: "Streets" (DEF-NRS-484A-265, "the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city"): st.highway "the entire public way between its boundary lines" at its whole extent, the city limit being the reading's scope for a city ordinance; rel.occupies anchors the subject on it. Same mapping as the index entry "upon a street".

"other than truck routes": a street stretch on which no travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) is governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign with code truck_route; the designation is marked by the sign, so the sign is the atom (ontology §9), its presence the evidence (observable_reading status).

"used as through routes": the subject travels the street stretch (rel.occupies of st.highway regions with no truck route governing, at every observation of the stretch) from leaving one truck route to entering another, read through its controlled motion; the stretch is bounded by the two truck-route occupancies, so the history read is the stretch itself, not the recording.

"truck route": the routes designated for trucks; the road users a through-route ban between truck routes concerns are trucks, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck ("every motor vehicle which is used for the transportation or delivery of goods with a body built and designed for that purpose"), one atom. "from one truck route to another": the subject occupied (rel.occupies) a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign with code truck_route, and now comes to occupy one so governed that lies on a different way: st.on_way "the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on" names the highway (st.highway) each lies on, and "another" is read as no highway in common between the two; st.on_way is not nearness.

"pick-up, delivery or essential use is required enroute": a purpose, read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading purpose): a halt on the stretch long enough to serve a stop, drv.motion.parked ("at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration") at some observation of the stretch, with min_duration the shortest pick-up or delivery dwell. A halt in traffic, shorter than that, is not such a stop.

LVMC_11_48_060.applicability: The subject is a truck (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck). Let onTR(g) = rel.occupies(subject, g) for a travel region g governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign with code truck_route. Trigger: at the judged observation t the subject comes onto a truck route: some travel region g2 with onTR(g2) at t, and the subject occupied no truck-route-governed travel region at the observation before. Exception: within the stretch defined in the obligation, drv_motion_parked(subject) held at some observation (speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration p.delivery_halt_min_duration); the exception reads the same stretch, re-bound with its full selection.
LVMC_11_48_060.obligation: The subject did not use streets as a through route from one truck route to another: it is not the case that, going back from the observation before t, the subject occupied at every observation a highway region (st.highway) and no truck-route-governed travel region, back to an observation s at which it occupied a truck-route-governed travel region g1 such that no highway w has both st.on_way(g1, w) and st.on_way(g2, w). Written at t with since: not since((not onTR-any and occupies some st.highway) or rises(onTR-any), exists g1 (onTR(g1) and forall w (on_way(g1, w) implies not on_way(g2, w)))). Unknown where the stretch reaches the start of the recording; a stretch that began on the same truck route's way, or not on a truck route, is no through route.

narrowings.why: "used as through routes" is read as a continuous stretch on streets off truck routes between leaving a truck-route region and entering one on a highway the first does not lie on; a stretch that returns to the same truck route's way is no through route.
Truck routes are read through the truck_route sign governing the travel region; its presence is the evidence of the designation.

"pick-up, delivery or essential use is required enroute" is read through a halt on the stretch at least as long as the shortest pick-up or delivery dwell; the requirement itself and an essential use without such a halt are not observable.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A truck (ru.truck) travels on lane A governed by a truck_route regulatory sign and lying on highway W1, turns onto residential street S (no truck_route sign governs its lanes), drives along S without halting, and comes onto lane B governed by a truck_route sign and lying on highway W2, which A does not lie on.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The truck leaves lane A on W1 for street S, drives along S, and comes back onto a truck-route lane lying on W1.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car (ru.motor_vehicle) makes the forbid trip from A over S to B.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe what signs govern (dev.governs absent): which regions are truck routes is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but on S the truck halts at the curb for longer than the delivery dwell before driving on to B.

segmentation.text: A vehicle
passing around a rotary traffic island
shall be driven only to the right of such island.

elements.justification: 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

A rotary traffic island is st.roundabout, 'a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches'; passing around it is the subject's footprint overlapping that region (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'), the same mapping the index gives 'within a roundabout' (LVMC_11_43_010_A). 'Traffic' here names the island, a structure, not road users the duty turns on, so the traffic aggregate is not claimed.

Passing with the island on the vehicle's left, i.e. to the right of it, is travel counter-clockwise about the island's centre seen from above; driving to its left is travel clockwise about it: drv.motion.circulating_clockwise_about(subject, r), 'the point lies to the right of a's direction of travel and a's velocity turns about it clockwise', on the roundabout r of s2, with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance and sin_tol = p.roundabout_clockwise_sin_tol, must not hold. Same concept the index maps for 'shall be in a counterclockwise direction' (LVMC_11_43_010_A).

NRS_484B_220_2.applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a roundabout region r (st.roundabout).
NRS_484B_220_2.obligation: At every such observation, for every roundabout r the subject occupies, drv.motion.circulating_clockwise_about(subject, r) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance and sin_tol = p.roundabout_clockwise_sin_tol does not hold.

narrowings.why: 'to the right of such island' is read as not travelling clockwise about the roundabout's reference point, taken as the centre of its central island; motion towards or away from the centre (entry, exit) is not a breach
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a st.roundabout whose reference point is at (0,0); at kin.position (0,-15) it moves with kin.velocity (-6,0) m/s: the centre is on its right and it turns clockwise.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: At kin.position (0,-15) in the roundabout the subject moves with kin.velocity (6,0) m/s: counter-clockwise, island on its left.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies no roundabout; it drives on a straight roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the roundabout but its kin.velocity is not observed.

segmentation.text: A person
shall not open the door of or board or alight from
the side of a vehicle which is closest to passing traffic
in such a manner as to interfere with
moving vehicular traffic.

elements.justification: The person who opens a door, boards or alights is not observable as such; the conduct is the door of a vehicle opening, so the rule judges the vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose door it is. Same words mapped to the vehicle aggregate by LVMC_11_22_010.
sig.door_open: 'a door open; side ∈ {traffic, curb}'. Opening the door, boarding and alighting through that side all show as the door on that side being open.
'the side of a vehicle which is closest to passing traffic' is the value side = traffic of sig.door_open; the vehicle is the subject (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle).

'vehicular traffic': road users that are traffic (admitted DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'vehicles and other conveyances … using any highway for purposes of travel') and vehicles (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); 'moving': not at rest, the negation of drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation').

operationalizations.standard: in such a manner as to interfere with
operationalizations.convention: While the traffic-side door is open, a moving vehicle of the traffic is interfered with where it touches the subject (rel.contact) or passes alongside it (rel.longitudinal_overlap: the two projections on the subject's heading share length) with a lateral body gap (rel.surface_gap, lateral component) no greater than the lateral reach of an open side door, p.door_swing_reach: it then drives through the space the open door takes.

NRS_484B_153_2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle and its door on the side closest to passing traffic is open (sig.door_open side traffic).
NRS_484B_153_2.obligation: No road user c that is traffic and a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) is in contact with the subject (rel.contact), or alongside it (rel.longitudinal_overlap: projections share length) with the lateral component of rel.surface_gap(subject, c) at most p.door_swing_reach; violated where one is.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who opens the door, boards or alights is read through the vehicle's traffic-side door being open: who is at the door is not observable.
Boarding and alighting are read through the open traffic-side door they pass through; boarding or alighting from a vehicle side that has no door is not read.
Interference is read as a moving vehicle touching the subject or passing alongside within the open door's reach; a moving vehicle that brakes or swerves earlier to avoid the door is not read.

scenarios.narrative: A car parked at the curb opens its traffic-side door; a moving car passes alongside it with a lateral body gap of 0.5 m.

segmentation.text: Whenever any vehicle is stopped at a marked crosswalk or at any unmarked crosswalk at an intersection to permit a pedestrian to cross the roadway
the driver of any other vehicle
approaching from the rear shall not overtake and pass such stopped vehicle

elements.justification: 'any vehicle' is a member b of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, quantified in the rule. 'is stopped' is drv.motion.complete_halt on b ('at rest at the observation', speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance). 'at a marked crosswalk or at any unmarked crosswalk at an intersection' is a crosswalk c: st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', which is the defined crosswalk in both of its branches; b is at c where its body occupies c (rel.occupies) or lies within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), and c lies ahead of or under b along the direction of a carrier b occupies (prim.region_offset_along not negative; carrier of kind st.travel_region): a vehicle halted beyond the crossing is not stopped at it. 'to permit a pedestrian to cross the roadway' is a purpose, read through the conduct it explains: a pedestrian (DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, 'a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair') occupies the crosswalk c (rel.occupies) at the same observation.

'the driver of any other vehicle' names the vehicle whose conduct is judged, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle other than b; same mapping as the index's 'The driver of a vehicle'. 'driver' is a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'approaching from the rear ... overtake and pass such stopped vehicle' is the manoeuvre of drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b): the subject, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it (approaching from the rear) to having b behind it. 'such stopped vehicle' is the same b bound by the trigger.

LVMC_11_30_030.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and some other vehicle b of the scene (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, not the subject) is, at the observation or at some observation of the p.overtake_window behind it, at a complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) at a crosswalk c (its body occupying c or within p.stop_point_tolerance of c, with c not behind it along the direction of a carrier it occupies) while a pedestrian occupies c.
LVMC_11_30_030.obligation: There is no other vehicle b such that, at the observation, the subject overtakes and passes b (drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b) with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos, at its recognition) and the trigger held for b at some observation of that act: from the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned, up to the observation itself, b was at a complete halt at a crosswalk c occupied by a pedestrian, as stated in the applicability.

narrowings.why: 'to permit a pedestrian to cross the roadway' is a purpose, read through the conduct it explains: the vehicle is halted at the crosswalk while a pedestrian occupies that crosswalk; a halt for a pedestrian still waiting on the curb is not read.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the overtaking vehicle whoever controls it.

The pass's observations are read from the one after the last observation at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned, up to the recognition: the language has no next-observation operator to single out that last aligned-ahead observation from the earlier ones of its run, so the act's first observation, at which b is still ahead of the subject with a gap between them, is not read for the trigger.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Car b halts 1 m before a marked crosswalk in the right lane while a pedestrian walks on the crosswalk; the subject car, coming up behind b in the same direction, moves to the left lane and passes b within 6 s while b is still halted and the pedestrian still on the crosswalk.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Car b halts before a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian on it; the subject car, behind b in the same direction, halts behind b and does not pass it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives along a street; no vehicle is halted at any crosswalk, and no other vehicle is in the scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Car b stands before a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian on it while the subject passes it, but the speed of b is not observed, so whether b is stopped is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_d1
scenarios.narrative: Car b is halted at an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection with a pedestrian on it during the first 3 s of the subject's pass; the pedestrian then reaches the far curb and b remains halted while the subject completes the pass 2 s later.

scenarios.name: occasion_d1_outside
scenarios.narrative: Car b halts at a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian on it while the subject waits behind; the pedestrian clears the crosswalk and b moves off before the subject begins to move out; the subject passes b, which is then moving, 8 s later, with no pedestrian on the crosswalk during the pass.

under_way.justification: An observation inside the pass is one at or after the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction within p.overtake_same_direction_cos), at which the subject is moving (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and before b is behind the subject: it is read from the subject's motion and the two road users' relative position, not from the region either occupies.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of road-user tracking in recorded and simulated traces

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 3B.16: stop lines placed at least 4 ft in advance of the nearest crosswalk line

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passing-manoeuvre model: passing times of about 4 to 11 s

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
param_proposals.source: heading angles of urban lane changes, typically below 20 degrees

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle:
Shall in every case yield
the right-of-way
to moving traffic and pedestrians.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency narrowing).

The line is subsection (3) of 'Limitations on backing': 'in every case' is every case of backing, drv.motion.moving_backward ('the component of a's velocity along a's heading ... below minus speed_tol'). To yield is to grant precedence: the backing vehicle does not keep backing into a danger of a crash with the road users of s4, and does not touch them (rel.contact: 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)').

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'): the scene condition 'using any highway' is carried beside it as rel.occupies of a st.highway; 'moving' is the negation of drv.motion.complete_halt. 'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; since traffic already contains moving pedestrians, the words add pedestrians whether moving or not.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: circumstances of direction, speed and proximity giving rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: direction, speed and proximity give rise to the danger of a crash where, under constant velocities, the two road users approach each other within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance)

NRS_484B_113_3.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is backing at the observation: drv.motion.moving_backward(subject) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance.
NRS_484B_113_3.obligation: At the observation, for every road user u other than the subject (not same) that is either moving traffic — ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, occupying a highway (rel.occupies, st.highway), and not drv.motion.complete_halt(u) with p.halt_speed_tolerance — or a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): not rel.contact(subject, u), and not [prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u, p.conflict_horizon) and prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u, p.conflict_horizon) < p.conflict_centre_clearance].

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

The duty is read on a backing vehicle: the line is a subsection of the section limiting backing, and 'in every case' covers every case of backing; yielding is read as backing into no danger of a crash and no contact with the road users the words name.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car backs out of a driveway at 2 m/s while a pedestrian walks behind it; their centres are on a closest approach 1 s ahead at 0.5 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car backs along an empty street at 2 m/s; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives forward past a pedestrian on the sidewalk; it never backs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source supplies no velocity for the car, so whether it is backing is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car backs toward a parked car at rest 6 m behind it, closing at 1 m/s; the parked car is not moving traffic and not a pedestrian.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car backs at 2 m/s toward a pedestrian standing still 2 m behind it: the closest approach is 1 s ahead at under 1 m.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; traffic-conflict technique TTC thresholds

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; passenger-car design dimensions

segmentation.text: Any pedestrian who is not wholly or partially blind
or any driver of any vehicle
who approaches or comes in contact with
a person wholly or partially blind, carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person
with wisdom
shall immediately
come to a full stop
and take such precautions before proceeding
as may be necessary to avoid an accident or injury to the person wholly or partially blind

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'). 'who is not wholly or partially blind' leaves out the pedestrians the law protects; blindness itself is no observable, and is read through the feature the same sentence names as its sign: the subject is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal ('pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'), which carries no exclusion of its own.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exclusions of devices moved by human power, electric bicycles, electric personal assistive mobility devices and electric scooters, which the reading classifies). 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is the role of who controls the vehicle, never membership: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Same atoms as 'The driver of a vehicle' (LVMC_11_20_060_o1).

'comes in contact with' is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', taken at the observation at which it begins; a near miss is not contact, its exclusion, and is read by 'approaches'. 'approaches' is the subject, while not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt), coming within a reach of the person: the centre-to-centre distance (rel.centre_distance, 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points') falls to p.blind_person_approach_reach. That atom is not read as a clearance between bodies or an order of arrival, its exclusions: only as how near the subject has come.

The person protected is identified by the features the words list: 'carrying a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted by a person' is ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, 'pedestrian carrying a white or white-and-red cane, accompanied by a guide animal, or led by another person'. 'a person wholly or partially blind' with those features is the pedestrian the class describes: the ontology's class for exactly this description, whose contract states no exclusion. The person is another road user than the subject, quantified in the applicability.

'before proceeding' refers to the full stop the sibling span requires after the approach or contact (o1): proceeding is the subject moving again (not drv.motion.complete_halt) after it has been at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, 'The road user is at rest at the observation — complete cessation from movement', DEF-NRS-484A-255, the definition scoped to a stop 'when required') since the latest approach or contact event with the same protected person. The referent keeps its subject (this subject), its object (that person), its event and its order (halt after the event, motion after the halt). 'take such precautions' is read through the outcome the precautions secure (observable_reading, perception), which the standard span bounds.

operationalizations.standard: such precautions ... as may be necessary to avoid an accident or injury to the person wholly or partially blind
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: while proceeding, the subject neither touches the protected person (rel.contact) nor is on a course whose closest approach of centres, under constant velocities, comes within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); an accident or injury is avoided when no such contact or conflict arises.

residues.why: 'with wisdom' qualifies the person assisting, not the person protected; that the person assisted is wholly or partially blind and is being assisted is what identifies the protected person, and a helper's wisdom, a state of mind no trace shows, does not change that identification, so the duty owed to the person assisted is the same whether or not the helper's wisdom holds.

LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2.applicability: The subject is either a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) that is not of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, or a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) read through its controlled motion; for some other road user b (not the same as the subject) of the class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, an approach or contact event (rel.contact beginning, or rel.centre_distance first falling to at most p.blind_person_approach_reach while the subject is not at rest) occurred at or before the judged observation; the subject has been at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) at some observation since the latest such event; and at the judged observation the subject is not at rest (proceeding).
LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2.obligation: At every such observation, for that b: the subject is not in contact with b (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the centres of the subject and b approach each other within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) with a closest-approach distance (prim.closest_approach_distance, same horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Either contact or such a conflict course is violated. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence for the standard, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'take such precautions' is a duty to make sure, read through the outcome it secures while the subject proceeds after its stop: no contact with and no conflict course toward the protected person.
'an accident or injury' is read only through contact between the bodies and a predicted closest approach of the centres below the clearance within the horizon; an injury without contact is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motor vehicle comes within the reach of a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal crossing ahead, halts, then moves off toward the pedestrian: prim.closest_approach_within holds over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle halts, waits until the pedestrian has left its path, then moves off; the centres do not approach below the clearance within the horizon and no rel.contact occurs.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle halts and moves off near an ordinary pedestrian; no ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal is in the scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle halts and moves off near a ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal; rel.centre_distance is not observed and no contact occurs, so whether an approach event occurred is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: After halting, the vehicle moves off and its body touches the white-cane pedestrian (rel.contact).

param_proposals.name: p.blind_person_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: the centre distance within which a moving road user has approached a pedestrian carrying a white cane or led by another person: the stopping distance from an urban approach speed of about 13 m/s with a 1 s perception-reaction time and a 4.5 m/s^2 deceleration
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping-sight-distance model

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed quantisation of the acquisition standard's scene graph

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hyden 1987); FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

segmentation.text: Drivers of vehicles proceeding in opposite directions
shall pass each other keeping to the right,
and
upon highways having width for not more than one line of traffic in each direction,
each driver shall give to the other at least one-half of the paved portion of the highway
as nearly as possible.

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, for the subject and the other. 'proceeding in opposite directions': rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing'; its exclusion concerns the direction of approach to an intersection, which these words do not name. 'proceeding': the subject is not at rest (negation of drv.motion.complete_halt). 'Drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion.

'highways having width for not more than one line of traffic in each direction': st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles', and st.lane_adjacency, 'the count of lanes in that direction', at most the stated figure, read on the lane the subject occupies (rel.occupies) on a highway (st.highway) it occupies.

'one-half of the paved portion of the highway': the half on the subject's side of st.centre_line, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', of the way the subject is on (st.on_way, 'the public way … a structure region lies on'). 'give to the other': the subject's body stays on its own half: prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line from the subject ('signed lateral offset … left positive') is at least half the subject's full width (kin.extent). 'the other' is the oncoming vehicle met: it closes on the subject within a horizon (prim.closest_approach_within, centres under constant velocities, not a contact or clearance) or is alongside (rel.longitudinal_overlap).

operationalizations.standard: as nearly as possible
operationalizations.convention: The subject gives the other half of the paved portion as nearly as possible where its body crosses the centre line by no more than a lateral positioning tolerance p.lateral_position_tolerance, or where its body is already within that tolerance of the road edge on its right (st.road_edge, ground distance through st.region_geometry, on the right per prim.region_lateral_offset), so that no more room is available to it.

NRS_484B_203_1_o2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle that is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), occupying a highway (rel.occupies, st.highway) and a lane (st.lane) whose lane count in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) is at most one.
NRS_484B_203_1_o2.obligation: For every road user c that is a vehicle, occupies the highway the subject occupies, is oncoming to the subject (rel.oncoming with p.oncoming_heading_cos) and is meeting it (prim.closest_approach_within(subject, c, p.meeting_horizon) or rel.longitudinal_overlap: projections share length), and for every centre line l lying on that highway (st.centre_line, st.on_way): prim.region_lateral_offset(l, subject) is at least half the subject's full width (kin.extent) less p.lateral_position_tolerance, or the subject's body is within p.lateral_position_tolerance of a road edge (st.road_edge, st.region_geometry distance) lying on its right (prim.region_lateral_offset negative). Violated where neither holds.

narrowings.why: 'Drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls them.

'the paved portion of the highway' is read as the roadway the centre line divides; a paved shoulder is not added to either half. Its half is given while the other vehicle approaches within p.meeting_horizon or is alongside.
'as nearly as possible' is read through the subject's room to its right road edge; obstacles on the subject's half are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Two-lane two-way road; the moving subject car straddles the centre line by 1 m while an oncoming car approaches 2 s away, with 2 m of room to its right road edge.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same road; the subject car keeps its body right of the centre line as the oncoming car passes.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives on a highway whose lane counts two lanes in its direction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Two-lane road with an oncoming car approaching; the source maps regions without their outline (st.region_geometry absent), so the offset from the centre line is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives over the centre line on a two-lane road with no other vehicle in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A very narrow paved road; the subject's body crosses the centre line by 0.5 m while its right side is at the road edge, as an oncoming car passes.

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
param_proposals.source: heading tolerance of road-geometry alignment; lane-change heading angles

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source

param_proposals.name: p.meeting_horizon
param_proposals.convention: the time ahead within which two vehicles closing head-on on a narrow two-way road count as meeting, so that each keeps to its half: the decision-and-steering time of a driver adjusting lateral position
param_proposals.source: AASHTO decision sight distance (avoidance manoeuvre times)

param_proposals.name: p.lateral_position_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the lateral margin within which a vehicle body counts as at a line or an edge: lane-keeping variability of a driven vehicle plus the source's position error
param_proposals.source: lane-keeping lateral deviation studies

segmentation.text: If a highway has two or more clearly marked lanes for traffic traveling in one direction,
vehicles must:
Not be moved from that lane until the driver has given the appropriate turn signal
and ascertained that such movement can be made with safety.

elements.justification: The subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles', and st.lane_adjacency gives 'the count of lanes in that direction', which is at least the literal two. Same mapping as the index's 'which has two or more clearly marked lanes for traveling in the same direction' (NRS_484B_208_1). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic whose direction the lanes serve. 'Clearly marked' is the lanes' presence on the road (observable_reading status); lane_adjacency's 'Not a stand-in for: the marking between two lanes' does not apply, since the count of lanes is what is read.
'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

A move from that lane is the subject, occupying the lane l1 of s1, coming to overlap its neighbouring lane of the same direction: drv.lane.entering_adjacent_lane(subject, l1, l2, side), read at the observation at which it holds, with side left or right. The appropriate signal is the one for the side of the move: sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}', showing that side, or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {..., left, right, ...}', meaning it; 'until ... has given' places it before the move: at the observation of the move and at the one before it. The indicator's exclusion (not the lane change itself) does not apply: the signal is read beside the move.

operationalizations.standard: such movement can be made with safety
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: at the observation the move begins, no other road user is in contact with the subject and none approaches the subject's centre, under constant velocities, within the conflict horizon to a centre distance below the conflict clearance

NRS_484B_223_1b.applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a lane l1 whose direction has at least two lanes (st.lane_adjacency count, literal 2), and at the observation it begins to move into the neighbouring lane l2 of the same direction on side s (drv.lane.entering_adjacent_lane(subject, l1, l2, s), s left or right).
NRS_484B_223_1b.obligation: At that observation and at the observation before it, the subject's turn indicator shows s or its hand signal means s; and at that observation no other road user is in contact with the subject (rel.contact) or has a closest approach to it within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'clearly marked' is read through the lanes' presence on the road
'the appropriate turn signal' is read as the indicator or arm signal of the side of the move, shown at the move and at the observation before it; its duration is not read here
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled conduct
'ascertained' is read through the outcome it secures: the movement made without a conflict

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a carriageway with two lanes in its direction the subject, in the right lane, comes to overlap the left lane while sig.turn_indicator is off and sig.hand_signal no_signal.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject's left indicator is on for 3 s before and during its move into the left lane; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a lane whose direction has one lane (st.lane_adjacency count 1) and keeps to it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves into the left neighbouring lane; sig.turn_indicator is not observed and sig.hand_signal reads no_signal; no other road user.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject signals left and moves into the left lane while a faster vehicle there has a closest approach to it in 1 s at a centre distance of 1 m.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique literature (Hyden 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width

segmentation.text: Any cab,
upon leaving any stand designated in accordance with the provisions of this Section,
shall execute a right-hand turn,
when a sign is posted giving notice of this requirement,
at the first street intersection after it leaves such stand.

elements.justification: No definition applies to 'cab' in this law (the definitions table lists none), so it is mapped like other words: ru.taxicab, 'passenger vehicle for hire, identifiable by its markings', is the class a cab is. No aggregate is admitted for the word here, so the class atom is the carrier.

The 'stand designated in accordance with the provisions of this Section' (a taxistand section) is the taxicab stand, st.curb_zone of kind taxicab_stand ('a signed or marked length of curb; kind ∈ {..., taxicab_stand, ...}'). The table resolves 'stand' to DEF-NRS-484A-250, which defines the act of halting; the noun here names the place, so the definition's words are not the carrier. 'leaving' is the event at which the cab's footprint ceases to overlap that curb zone (rel.occupies false, having been true at the previous observation). Designation is read by the stand's presence (status).

drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(a, r) denotes that 'Road user a has made a turn to the right through region r, recognized as it leaves r', with its heading change since entry in the right-turn band; it takes the intersection as its region argument, so the turn is judged at the intersection s5 singles out. kin.yaw_rate and rel.occupies are the atoms it reads.

The posted sign is a dev.regulatory_sign of code right_turn_only ('a point regulation by catalogue code, ... right_turn_only'), read where it governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region the cab occupies (rel.occupies) at the observation it leaves the stand, with its conditions holding for the cab (prim.conditions_hold: 'any occupancy or class condition is met'), so a notice limited to taxicabs is read as such. The sign is a condition, not the turn itself ('a prohibition sign is a condition').

'the first street intersection after it leaves such stand' is the intersection r (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet') whose exit the turn concept recognizes, such that since the observation the cab left 'such stand' — the same curb zone s2 binds — its footprint has overlapped no intersection other than r (rel.occupies). A city intersection is a street intersection within this ordinance's territorial scope.

LVMC_11_60_090.applicability: The subject is a taxicab (ru.taxicab). At the observation t its footprint ceases to overlap an intersection r (rel.occupies, st.intersection: false at t, true at t-1). Earlier, at an observation d, it left a taxicab_stand curb zone k (overlap of k true at d-1, false at d) while a regulatory sign of code right_turn_only whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold) governed (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupied at d; and at every observation from d to t its footprint overlapped no intersection other than r (written with since: [for every intersection q not the same as r, not rel.occupies(subject, q)] since [the departure from k with the sign condition]).
LVMC_11_60_090.obligation: At t, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(subject, r) holds, with step = p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min and u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min: the cab's passage through the first intersection after leaving the stand was a turn to the right.

narrowings.why: 'designated in accordance with the provisions of this Section' is read by the presence of the signed or marked taxicab_stand curb zone.

A sign 'giving notice of this requirement' is read as a posted right_turn_only regulatory sign that governs the travel region the cab occupies as it leaves the stand and whose conditions hold for the cab; its posting is read by its presence.

onset.words: the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r
onset.justification: The turn concept's act begins at the cab's entry into the intersection r, marked by rel.occupies rising on r.

occasion.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r.

under_way.justification: Inside the act the cab is within r since its entry and its heading is changing (kin.yaw_rate), which no observation before the entry shows; no span of this node is read while the act is under way.

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single center lane to be used only for turning by traffic moving in both directions,
the following rules apply:
A vehicle
may be driven in the center turn lane
only for the purpose of making a left-hand turn
onto or from the highway.

elements.justification: st.centre_turn_lane: 'a single centre lane used only for turning by traffic in both directions', the words' own configuration; 'center' (DEF-NRS-484A-040) places it on the line that indicates 'each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions'. The subject occupies it (rel.occupies). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic whose turns the lane serves. 'Designed to provide' is the lane's presence on the road (observable_reading status).
'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.
Driven in the centre turn lane: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the st.centre_turn_lane of s1.

'From the highway': the declared intention of s5 is taken at the place a left turn leaves the highway for, st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet') or st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'). 'Onto the highway': the left turn already made into the lane, read through conduct (observable_reading purpose): the subject has occupied the centre turn lane c at every observation since drv.motion.left_turn ('has completed a turn to the left') was recognized while it occupied c, and at some observation of the turn window behind that recognition it occupied no part of the highway h (st.highway) on which c lies (st.on_way, 'the public way a structure region lies on').

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

NRS_484B_223_3a.applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a centre turn lane c (st.centre_turn_lane).
NRS_484B_223_3a.obligation: At every such observation the subject's presence in c is excused, and otherwise violated, where either (from) the subject's declared intention int.left_turn at some intersection or driveway/alley entrance region holds at that observation, or (onto) the subject has occupied c at every observation since an observation at which drv.motion.left_turn(subject) (window = p.vehicle_turn_window, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol = p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) held while it occupied c, and at some observation of the window p.vehicle_turn_window behind that observation it occupied no part of the highway h on which c lies.

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'designed to provide' is read through the centre turn lane's presence on the road
a left-hand turn onto the highway is read through the turn the subject made into the lane from off the highway, which explains its presence there

segmentation.text: The driver of any truck or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,
which is following a truck, or combination of vehicles 80 inches or more in overall width,
shall, whenever conditions permit,
leave a space of 500 feet so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger,
but this shall not prevent a truck or combination of vehicles from overtaking and passing any vehicle or combination of vehicles.
This subsection does not apply to any vehicle or combination of vehicles while moving on a highway on which there are two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction.

elements.justification: 'truck' and 'combination of vehicles' are admitted aggregates (DEF-NRS-484A-305::truck, 'every motor vehicle which is used for the transportation or delivery of goods with a body built and designed for that purpose'; DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles, 'two or more vehicles coupled together'), claimed through ru.aggregate. '80 inches or more in overall width': kin.extent, 'the body's size along its axes … a formula reads the full length, width and height', the full width compared with the stated figure. 'Driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'following': rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction', the followed road user b ahead of the subject with no other road user between them in that lane (the one it immediately follows). b is a truck or a combination of vehicles (the admitted aggregates) whose full width (kin.extent) is at least the stated figure.

'leave a space of 500 feet': rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies … its longitudinal and lateral components', the longitudinal component to the followed vehicle at least the stated figure. The words 'so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger' state why the space is left; the duty is the stated space itself (narrowing).

'overtaking and passing any vehicle or combination of vehicles': drv.interaction.overtake_pass, 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear … comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it', with a the subject and b any road user that is a vehicle or a combination of vehicles (admitted aggregates). The pass is under way where its recognition falls within the window ahead of length p.overtake_window, the concept's own recognition window.

'a highway on which there are two or more lanes available for traffic moving in the same direction': st.lane_adjacency, 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction', read on the lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') the subject occupies (rel.occupies); the count is at least the stated figure. 'any vehicle or combination of vehicles' is the subject already bound by g1.

operationalizations.standard: whenever conditions permit
operationalizations.convention: Conditions permit the space where the followed vehicle has been the subject's immediate leader in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, no other road user between) and neither vehicle has been at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt) at every observation of the window behind of length p.truck_space_open_time: the time a heavy vehicle needs to open the space behind a leader by easing off a few miles per hour. A leader that has just come ahead of the subject, or a queue at rest, does not yet permit it.

NRS_484B_127_2.applicability: The subject is a truck or a combination of vehicles (either admitted aggregate) whose full width (kin.extent) is at least 80 inches, and the lane it occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane) does not count two or more lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count).
NRS_484B_127_2.obligation: For every road user b that is a truck or a combination of vehicles of full width at least 80 inches, ahead of the subject in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with no other road user ahead of the subject and behind b in that lane: either (i) conditions do not permit — it is not the case that, at every observation of the window behind of length p.truck_space_open_time, b was so the subject's immediate leader and neither the subject nor b was at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance); or (ii) the subject is overtaking and passing — within the window ahead of length p.overtake_window some road user c that is a vehicle or a combination of vehicles is overtaken and passed by the subject (drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, c) with p.overtake_window, p.overtake_same_direction_cos); or (iii) the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap(subject, b) is at least 500 feet. Violated where none holds.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the truck's or combination's conduct whoever controls it.
'so that an overtaking vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger' states the purpose of the space; the duty is the stated space, and whether an overtaking vehicle is present is not read.

'whenever conditions permit' is a catch-all read only through the leader having been the subject's immediate leader, both moving, for the window that opening the space takes; other conditions (grade, traffic behind) are not read.

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single center lane to be used only for turning by traffic moving in both directions,
the following rules apply:
A vehicle
must not travel more than 200 feet in a center turn lane
before making a left-hand turn from the highway.

elements.justification: st.centre_turn_lane: 'a single centre lane used only for turning by traffic in both directions'; 'center' (DEF-NRS-484A-040) places it on the line that indicates 'each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions'. Occupied by the subject (rel.occupies). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. 'Designed to provide' is the lane's presence (status).
'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

The travel in the lane is the distance the subject travelled while its footprint continuously overlapped (rel.occupies) the st.centre_turn_lane c, a distance along its path (kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path'), written with Term.distanceWhile; it is compared with the literal 200 ft.

The left-hand turn is drv.motion.left_turn, 'has completed a turn to the left', recognized at the observation its heading change settles; it is a turn from the highway made out of the centre turn lane: the subject occupied c (rel.occupies) at some observation of the turn window behind the recognition and no longer occupies c at it. The travel limit is read at the last observation of that window at which it occupied c.

NRS_484B_223_3b.applicability: drv.motion.left_turn(subject) (window = p.vehicle_turn_window, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol = p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) holds at the observation, and for a centre turn lane c the subject occupied c at some observation of the window p.vehicle_turn_window behind and does not occupy c at this observation.
NRS_484B_223_3b.obligation: At the last observation of that window at which the subject occupied c, the path length over which it had occupied c continuously (Term.distanceWhile subject (rel.occupies subject c)) is at most the literal 200 ft. Where that run in c began before the recording the distance is unknown.

narrowings.why: the travel limited is the continuous run in the centre turn lane ending at the left turn; a run before an earlier exit from the lane is not added
'travel' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single center lane to be used only for turning by traffic moving in both directions,
the following rules apply:
A vehicle
must not travel more than 50 feet in a center turn lane
after making a left-hand turn onto the highway
before merging with traffic.

elements.justification: st.centre_turn_lane: 'a single centre lane used only for turning by traffic in both directions'; 'center' (DEF-NRS-484A-040) places it on the line that indicates 'each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions'. Occupied by the subject (rel.occupies). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. 'Designed to provide' is the lane's presence (status).
'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

The travel in the lane after the turn is the distance along the subject's path (kin.path_length) over which it has stayed in the st.centre_turn_lane c (rel.occupies) since the turn, written with Term.distanceWhile; compared with the literal 50 ft.

The left-hand turn is drv.motion.left_turn, 'has completed a turn to the left', recognized while the subject occupies c; it is a turn onto the highway where, at some observation of the turn window behind the recognition, the subject occupied (rel.occupies) no part of the st.highway h on which c lies (st.on_way, 'the public way a structure region lies on'): it came from a driveway or another way.

Merging with traffic (the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic travelling in the through lanes) ends the counted travel: the subject's footprint ceases to overlap (rel.occupies) the centre turn lane c.

NRS_484B_223_3c.applicability: For a centre turn lane c lying on a highway h: the subject has occupied c at every observation since an observation at which drv.motion.left_turn(subject) (window = p.vehicle_turn_window, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol = p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) held while it occupied c, and at some observation of the window p.vehicle_turn_window behind that observation it occupied no part of h.
NRS_484B_223_3c.obligation: The path length over which that condition has held (Term.distanceWhile subject of it) is at most the literal 50 ft. The count ends when the subject's footprint leaves c (merging).

narrowings.why: the merge is read as complete when the footprint leaves the centre turn lane; distance travelled while straddling c and a through lane counts
'travel' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
