segmentation.text: Every driver of a vehicle
approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign

shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway
before entering the intersection.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; claimed as the aggregate. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) names who controls the vehicle, a relational role, not membership: read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency narrowing).

The approach is the carrier c the vehicle occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection r (st.lane_enters: 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'); the stop intersection is 'indicated by a stop sign' where a dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') governs c (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ...'). st.travel_region is the kind of c, st.intersection the kind of r. Same atoms as the index's 'approaching the intersection' plus the stop sign.

'stop' is required here, so DEF-NRS-484A-255 applies: 'complete cessation from movement', drv.motion.complete_halt. The three places are read through the approach carrier c, in the order the words list. (1) The crosswalk 'on the near side of the intersection' is the st.crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of: 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'); 'before entering' it is a halt with the footprint off it (rel.occupies), short of it along c's direction (prim.region_offset_along along st.lane_direction, positive) and within the stop-point tolerance (st.region_geometry ground distance). Distance never stands for belonging: the association is st.entrance_of. (2) 'if there is no crosswalk' holds where the crosswalks' entrance lists are observed and none marks c ('where the source observes a line's entrances its list is complete'); the st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device', recorded as marking c, is then the place: a halt not past it along c's direction, body within the tolerance; 'clearly marked' is read by the represented line (status). (3) 'if none': no stop line marks c either (lists observed); the point nearest the intersecting highway before entering the intersection is c's entrance end at r (st.intersection): a halt off r, short of r along c's direction, body within the tolerance of r — the ontology's approach convention reads the edge of the intersection as the carrier's entrance end, which is the point nearest the intersecting highway and the one with the widest view along it.

The event the halt precedes: the vehicle's footprint comes to overlap the intersection r (rel.occupies true at the observation, false at the previous one), r being the region st.lane_enters names for c.

NRS_484A_450_2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that enters an intersection r at the judged observation t — its footprint overlaps r at t and not at t-1 (rel.occupies) — having occupied at t-1 a carrier c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is r (st.lane_enters(c, r)), and a stop sign (dev.stop_sign) governs c (dev.governs).
NRS_484A_450_2.obligation: Duty of an act before an event (approach convention). Event: the entry into r at t through c; the duty is judged at t. Act: a halt of the subject (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance) at the governing place, read through c. Place, in the order the words list: (1) where a crosswalk x is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of(x, c)): a halt at which the footprint does not overlap x (rel.occupies), the subject is short of x along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along of x along st.lane_direction of c, positive) and the body-to-x ground distance (st.region_geometry) is at most p.stop_point_tolerance; (2) else, where the crosswalk lists are observed and none marks c, and a stop line l is recorded as marking c: a halt at which the subject is not past l along c's direction (offset not negative) and the body-to-l distance is at most p.stop_point_tolerance; (3) else, where the crosswalk and stop-line lists are observed and none marks c: a halt at which the footprint does not overlap r, the subject is short of r along c's direction, and the body-to-r distance is at most p.stop_point_tolerance. Where several marks of the governing kind mark c, a halt in the zone of any of them it has not passed counts. History bound: the search runs back from t-1 and ends at the approach start — the last observation before t at which the subject, on a carrier the governing mark is recorded as marking, is outside that mark's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it, farther than p.stop_point_tolerance; with several marks, outside and short of each) — or at the subject's previous entry into r, whichever is later. Nothing else ends it: not the start of the recording, a first observation, another intersection or mark, or a distance travelled. Crossing the mark, moving on toward r, a change of carrier or lateral move within the same entry, a reverse that stays within the zone and speed noise begin no new approach; only an observed exit from the zone upstream does, and the act is then owed again. Verdict: the act found → compliant; the search reaches the approach start or the previous entry without it → violated; it reaches neither (the recording begins first, or a speed or place in between is unobserved) without the act → unknown. Missing evidence: the entry is unknown, never absent, where t-1 does not show the subject on a mapped carrier with an observed association to r (no earlier observation, no mapped carrier, association unobserved); an unobserved dev.governs of c, or an unobserved association of a mark with c, makes the verdict unknown only where it turns on it — a halt found at a place known to govern, and an association the source excludes, are decided whatever the missing fact.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

The stop intersection 'indicated by a stop sign' is read by a stop sign the source records as governing the approach carrier c; a sign recorded only as governing the intersection itself is not read as facing c.
'clearly marked' is read by the represented stop line; the paint's clarity is not modelled.

The point nearest the intersecting highway 'where the driver has a view of approaching traffic' is read as c's entrance end, the edge of r, within p.stop_point_tolerance: no point nearer the intersecting highway lies before the intersection, and the view along it is widest there; the view itself (st.sight_along_way) is not compared with a bound.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car on lane c, governed by a stop sign, with a crosswalk recorded as marking c, approaches from 40 m at 10 m/s, rolls over the crosswalk at 4 m/s and enters the intersection without ever being at rest.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car comes to rest 1 m short of the crosswalk, off it, then proceeds and enters the intersection.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the intersection through a lane governed by a traffic signal and by no stop sign.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe which travel regions the stop sign governs.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No crosswalk marks c (lists observed); a stop line marks c; the car comes to rest 1 m short of the line and then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Neither a crosswalk nor a stop line marks c (lists observed); the car comes to rest 1 m short of the intersection's edge, off it, and then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A crosswalk marks c; the car comes to rest 20 m short of it, moves on and enters the intersection without halting again: the halt lies before the approach start.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the car already 1 m short of the crosswalk marking c, moving at 3 m/s; it enters the intersection without a recorded halt, and no recorded observation shows it outside the stopping zone upstream.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start: the observation at which the car was outside the crosswalk's stopping zone upstream lies before the recording, so whether it halted within the zone before the recording began is not observed

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_20_060_o1; MUTCD stop-line placement before a crosswalk

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning,
a vehicle must:
While being driven in the right turn lane,
not travel through an intersection.

elements.justification: st.turn_lane: 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}' — 'a single right lane to be used only for turning' is a turn lane of side right; rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors it to the lane the subject is in (bound with s3), so the configuration is the subject's own lane and not any turn lane of the scene. Same words, same atoms as NRS_484B_223_4a. 'A single right lane' is one lane, st.lane being 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles', of which st.turn_lane is a refinement: the words describe the lane the highway provides, a lane designated only for turning on the right. 'Highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, not an aggregate) is the way the lane lies on; the lane kind alone decides the configuration.

'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Not a stand-in for a named class: the words name none. Same mapping as 'a vehicle must:' in NRS_484B_223_4a.

'Being driven in the right turn lane' is the subject's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) the right turn lane L of s1; the intersection the duty concerns is the one L leads into: st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end — the carrier is an approach to that intersection' (a turn lane refines st.lane, a carrier the relation admits); st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'. Not a stand-in for the lane a lane leads into (st.lane_connectivity) or a device's governance: the relation is the source's entry topology. 'Driven' is read through the vehicle's motion (agency reading).

'Travel through an intersection' is a passage through X, from the subject's entry into X (its footprint comes to overlap X, rel.occupies) to its exit, that is not a turn: drv.motion.right_turn_through_region (proposed this iteration) 'has made a turn to the right through region r, recognized as it leaves r'; its not-denoted cases ('a passage through r whose heading change is above minus turn_min, such as one straight through or a turn to the left; a heading change of minus u_turn_min or less') are exactly the travel through that the turn-only lane forbids. The duty is therefore that, at the exit of a passage entered from the right turn lane, the concept holds.

NRS_484B_223_4b.applicability: At an observation at which the subject's footprint does not overlap an intersection X and overlapped it at the previous observation (its exit from X), where at some observation from its latest entry into X (the observation at which its footprint came to overlap X, having not overlapped it at the observation before) up to that exit, the subject's footprint overlapped a turn lane L of side right (st.turn_lane) that enters X (st.lane_enters L X): the passage was made while being driven in the right turn lane. At its entry the footprint overlaps both L and X.
NRS_484B_223_4b.obligation: At that exit, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(subject, X) holds, with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min p.turn_heading_min and u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min: the passage through X from its entry to its exit was a turn to the right. A passage straight through, a turn to the left or a reversal is travel through the intersection and violates the duty. Where the entry was not observed, an interval between observations since it exceeds the step, or a yaw rate since it is missing, the verdict is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'being driven' is read through the vehicle's motion in the lane, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Subject (ru.aggregate vehicle) occupies a st.turn_lane of side right that enters intersection X (st.lane_enters); it enters X from that lane and leaves X on the far side with its heading change since entry (from kin.yaw_rate) near zero: right_turn_through_region does not hold at the exit.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Subject enters X from the right turn lane and leaves X with a heading change since entry of about a quarter turn to the right: right_turn_through_region holds at the exit.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Subject enters X from an ordinary st.lane (no turn lane) and passes straight through; its footprint never overlaps a right turn lane entering X.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Subject enters X from the right turn lane and leaves it; kin.yaw_rate is absent on the source, so the heading change since entry, and right_turn_through_region, are unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3
scenarios.narrative: Subject's footprint overlaps the right turn lane L only at its entry into X (it overlaps L and X there), and only X afterwards; it passes straight through and exits: the condition held for part of the passage, and right_turn_through_region does not hold at the exit.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3_outside
scenarios.narrative: Subject occupied the right turn lane L earlier but moved into the adjacent through lane before reaching X; its footprint does not overlap L at its entry or afterwards; it passes straight through X: the condition held only before the passage began.

onset.justification: The concept's act begins 'at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation': the passage through the intersection begins at the entry.

occasion.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r.

under_way.words: the heading change of a since its entry into r, integrated from its yaw rate, while its footprint overlaps r
under_way.justification: An observation inside the passage is one since the entry at which the heading change is being integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading') while the footprint overlaps X; before the entry no integration runs.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading changes of a few degrees versus junction turns of about ninety degrees in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: midpoint between a right-angle turn and a full reversal of direction

segmentation.text: A vehicle
must not be driven to the left side of the highway at any time:
When approaching the crest of a grade
or upon a curve in the highway
where the driver’s view is obstructed
within such distance as to create a hazard in the event another vehicle might approach from the opposite direction.
Subsection 2 does not apply upon a one-way highway.

elements.justification: 'A vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole.

'the left side of the highway' is the side beyond its center (DEF-NRS-484A-040: 'to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions, and, if a line is not marked, it is an imaginary line in the highway equally distant from the edges'): an st.centre_line c, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions', lying (st.on_way) on the st.highway the subject occupies (rel.occupies), with prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) ('signed lateral offset (m, left positive)') negative: c lies to the right of the subject's reference point. 'at any time' places the duty at every observation. 'driven' is read through controlled motion (agency).

'the crest of a grade' is st.crest, 'the place on a roadway's longitudinal profile where the slope changes from rising to falling in the direction of travel ... so the ground distance from a road user to it is read through st.region_geometry'; not st.grade, whose contract says it is 'Not a stand-in for: the place of a crest'. 'approaching' is the subject's velocity (kin.velocity) pointing toward the crest's reference point from its position (kin.position): the dot product of the velocity with the vector from the position to that point is positive; the crest is anchored to the subject by its ground distance (st.region_geometry), bounded in s6.

'upon a curve in the highway': the subject occupies the st.highway (rel.occupies) and st.curvature, 'horizontal curvature of the roadway at a point, as a magnitude', at its point stands clear of zero by the source's resolution (p.curvature_resolution): a curve named without a size is its presence. Not kin.yaw_rate, which is 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature'.

'the driver's view is obstructed': st.sight_distance at the subject's point, 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... whether or not any road user is there', short of the distance of s6. What the driver could see is read through the sight distance of the place (observable_reading, perception), not rel.visible, since the other vehicle is hypothetical.
'upon a one-way highway': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'; there subsection 2 does not apply.

operationalizations.standard: within such distance as to create a hazard in the event another vehicle might approach from the opposite direction
operationalizations.convention: Passing sight distance: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance by prevailing speed (Table 3B-1), the warrant for a no-passing zone at a crest or curve, expressed as the time the subject's speed takes to cover it. The hazard distance is the subject's kin.speed times p.passing_sight_time; the view is obstructed within it where st.sight_distance at the subject's point is below it, and a crest is approached within it where its ground distance (st.region_geometry) is at most it. The bound moves with the subject's speed.

NRS_484B_213_2a.applicability: At an observation at which the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, occupies no st.one_way_roadway, st.sight_distance at its point is below the hazard distance (its kin.speed times p.passing_sight_time), and either (crest) for some st.crest k the subject's kin.velocity points toward k's reference point and the ground distance from the subject's body to k (st.region_geometry) is at most the hazard distance, or (curve) the subject occupies a highway and st.curvature at its point exceeds p.curvature_resolution.
NRS_484B_213_2a.obligation: The subject is not on the left side of the highway: for every st.centre_line c lying (st.on_way) on a highway the subject occupies, prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) is not negative. Where it is negative for some such c, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'driven to the left side of the highway' is read as the subject's reference point lying beyond the centre line to its left.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.
'the driver's view' is read through the sight distance of the subject's place, what could be seen from it, not through any driver's perception.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves toward an st.crest whose ground distance is below its speed times p.passing_sight_time; st.sight_distance at its point is below that distance; its reference point lies left of the centre line of the highway it occupies.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same approach to the crest with the subject right of the centre line (prim.region_lateral_offset to the line positive).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: On a straight, level two-way highway (curvature at resolution, no crest ahead, sight distance far above the bound), the subject drives left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject is left of the centre line approaching a crest; st.sight_distance is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: On a curve (st.curvature above p.curvature_resolution) with st.sight_distance below the subject's speed times p.passing_sight_time and no crest, the subject is left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches a crest with short sight distance on an st.one_way_roadway, left of the roadway's geometric centre.

param_proposals.name: p.passing_sight_time
param_proposals.convention: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance (Table 3B-1, the warrant for a no-passing zone) divided by the prevailing speed it is tabulated for: about eleven seconds of travel across 25 to 70 mph; the sight distance or the clear distance a pass needs is the subject's speed times this time
param_proposals.source: MUTCD 2009 Section 3B.02, Table 3B-1

param_proposals.name: p.curvature_resolution
param_proposals.convention: the horizontal curvature at or below which a mapped roadway reads as straight: the curvature resolution of map centrelines (a radius of about two kilometres)
param_proposals.source: map centreline curvature resolution of the acquisition source

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
approaching a yield sign
if required for safety to stop

shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection or, if there is no crosswalk, at a clearly marked stop line, or if none, then at the point nearest the intersecting highway where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency narrowing). Same mapping as the index's 'The driver of a vehicle'.

dev.yield_sign is the 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt'; the vehicle approaches it where it occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier c the sign governs (dev.governs) and whose entrance end is the intersection r (st.lane_enters). The intersection is named by 'the nearest side of the intersection'; st.travel_region is the kind of c.

'stop' is required here, so DEF-NRS-484A-255 applies: 'complete cessation from movement', drv.motion.complete_halt. The places are read through the approach carrier c, in the order listed. (1) The crosswalk 'on the nearest side of the intersection' is the st.crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of: 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'); 'before entering' it is a halt off it (rel.occupies), short of it along c's direction (prim.region_offset_along along st.lane_direction) and within the stop-point tolerance (st.region_geometry). (2) 'if there is no crosswalk' holds where the crosswalk lists are observed and none marks c; the st.stop_line recorded as marking c is then the place: a halt not past it, body within the tolerance; 'clearly marked' is read by the represented line (status). (3) 'if none': no stop line marks c either; the point nearest the intersecting highway before entering is c's entrance end at r (st.intersection): a halt off r, short of it along c's direction, body within the tolerance — the point nearest the intersecting highway and the one with the widest view along it. 'approaching traffic on the intersecting highway' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('using any highway for purposes of travel', carried as rel.occupies of a st.highway): the road users whose danger of a crash with the subject makes the stop 'required for safety' (operationalization of s3).

operationalizations.standard: required for safety to stop
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a stop is required for safety where, at some observation of the approach, some other road user of traffic (the traffic of s4, occupying a highway) and the subject approach each other within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), the envelope within which two bodies collide or nearly collide

NRS_484A_450_3.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that enters an intersection r at the judged observation t — its footprint overlaps r at t and not at t-1 (rel.occupies) — having occupied at t-1 a carrier c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is r (st.lane_enters(c, r)) and which a yield sign (dev.yield_sign) governs (dev.governs); and a stop was required for safety: at some observation from the approach start (as defined in the obligation) to t-1, some road user u other than the subject (not same) that is traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) occupying a highway (rel.occupies, st.highway) satisfies prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u, p.conflict_horizon) and prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u, p.conflict_horizon) < p.conflict_centre_clearance. Where no observation of that stretch shows such a road user, the duty does not arise.
NRS_484A_450_3.obligation: Duty of an act before an event (approach convention). Event: the entry into r at t through c; the duty is judged at t. Act: a halt of the subject (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance) at the governing place, read through c. Place, in the order the words list: (1) where a crosswalk x is recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of(x, c)): a halt at which the footprint does not overlap x (rel.occupies), the subject is short of x along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along of x along st.lane_direction of c, positive) and the body-to-x ground distance (st.region_geometry) is at most p.stop_point_tolerance; (2) else, where the crosswalk lists are observed and none marks c, and a stop line l is recorded as marking c: a halt at which the subject is not past l along c's direction and the body-to-l distance is at most p.stop_point_tolerance; (3) else, where the crosswalk and stop-line lists are observed and none marks c: a halt at which the footprint does not overlap r, the subject is short of r along c's direction, and the body-to-r distance is at most p.stop_point_tolerance. Where several marks of the governing kind mark c, a halt in the zone of any of them it has not passed counts. History bound: the search runs back from t-1 and ends at the approach start — the last observation before t at which the subject, on a carrier the governing mark is recorded as marking, is outside that mark's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it, farther than p.stop_point_tolerance; with several marks, outside and short of each) — or at the subject's previous entry into r, whichever is later. Nothing else ends it: not the start of the recording, a first observation, another intersection or mark, or a distance travelled. Crossing the mark, moving on toward r, a change of carrier or lateral move within the same entry, a reverse within the zone and speed noise begin no new approach; only an observed exit from the zone upstream does. Verdict: the act found → compliant; the search reaches the approach start or the previous entry without it → violated; it reaches neither without the act → unknown. Missing evidence: the entry is unknown, never absent, where t-1 does not show the subject on a mapped carrier with an observed association to r; an unobserved dev.governs of c, an unobserved association of a mark with c, or an unobserved closest approach makes the verdict unknown only where it turns on it — a halt found at a place known to govern is compliant whatever the conflict reading, and a duty that does not arise is decided whatever the missing fact.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'approaching a yield sign' is read through a yield sign the source records as governing the approach carrier c that enters r; a sign recorded only as governing the intersection itself is not read as facing c.
'clearly marked' is read by the represented stop line; the paint's clarity is not modelled.

The point nearest the intersecting highway 'where the driver has a view of approaching traffic' is read as c's entrance end, the edge of r, within p.stop_point_tolerance: no point nearer the intersecting highway lies before the intersection, and the view along it is widest there; the view itself (st.sight_along_way) is not compared with a bound.

The approach start that ends the search into the past is read with the subject on the approach carrier c itself (one of the carriers the governing mark is recorded as marking): an exit from the stopping zone upstream observed while the subject is on another carrier the same mark marks does not end the search, which then runs further back (to an approach start on c, an observation in r, or the recording's start, where it is unknown).

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car on lane c, governed by a yield sign, with a crosswalk marking c, approaches at 10 m/s while a car on the crossing highway is on a closest approach with it 2 s ahead at 1 m; the car never comes to rest and enters the intersection.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same conflict; the car comes to rest 1 m short of the crosswalk, off it, lets the crossing car pass, and enters.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car approaches the yield sign alone in the scene, no road user is ever on a closest approach with it, and it enters without halting: no stop was required for safety.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe which travel regions the yield sign governs.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No crosswalk marks c (lists observed); a stop line marks c; with the conflict present, the car comes to rest 1 m short of the line and then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Neither a crosswalk nor a stop line marks c (lists observed); with the conflict present, the car comes to rest 1 m short of the intersection's edge, off it, and then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A crosswalk marks c; the conflict is present on the approach; the car rests 20 m short of the crosswalk, moves on and enters without halting again.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the car already 1 m short of the crosswalk marking c, moving at 3 m/s, while a crossing car is on a closest approach with it 2 s ahead at 1 m; it enters without a recorded halt and no recorded observation shows it outside the stopping zone upstream.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start: the observation at which the car was outside the crosswalk's stopping zone upstream lies before the recording, so whether it halted within the zone before the recording began is not observed

param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
