segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate
a vehicle of any kind or character
at:
A rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.

elements.justification: Mapping index: 'It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate' maps to kin.speed. To drive or operate is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, and the prohibited driving is driving at a speed: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s.
Mapping index: 'a vehicle of any kind or character' maps to the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate', never expanded into classes.

operationalizations.standard: a rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions
operationalizations.convention: stopping-sight-distance model (perception-reaction distance plus braking distance at the friction-limited deceleration of the surface) held within the distance available ahead: the sight distance of the place, the visibility of the air and, in darkness, the low-beam reach; for traffic, the assured-clear-distance model against the road user ahead in the lane, whose own braking distance is credited; for curves, the side-friction model (speed squared times curvature within the lateral acceleration the surface allows); for width, the time-to-line-crossing model (lateral drift at the uncorrected heading error times the speed, within the lateral margin the lane leaves the vehicle, for at least the minimum time to line crossing)

NRS_484B_600_1a.applicability: The subject (vehicle aggregate) is moving: kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance.
NRS_484B_600_1a.obligation: With v the subject's speed, a the braking deceleration the surface allows (p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds; otherwise p.following_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds; otherwise p.following_decel_dry: a Term.cond selection), and S = v·p.driver_reaction_time + v·v/(2a): (i) S is at most st.sight_distance at the subject's place and at most env.visibility, and, where env.darkness holds, at most p.low_beam_sight_reach; (ii) for every road user u ahead of the subject in its lane, whatever its class (DEF-NRS-484A-285 'traffic' counts 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances' using the highway, so any road user ahead in the lane is traffic) (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), S is at most rel.surface_gap between them plus u's braking distance (u's speed squared over 2a); (iii) v·v·st.curvature at the subject's place is at most p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds and p.curve_lateral_accel_max otherwise; (iv) for every lane the subject's footprint overlaps, v·p.lane_keeping_heading_error·p.lane_departure_time_min is at most half of (st.lane_width of that lane minus the subject's width from kin.extent). No division reads a measured atom.

narrowings.why: 'drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it

the standard is the whole duty and is read through a policy model (surrogate): 'the traffic' only through the road users ahead in the subject's lane (crossing and adjacent traffic not read); 'surface' through wet and icy or snow-covered surface; 'width of the highway' through the width of the lane the subject occupies; 'the weather' through precipitation and visibility; the catch-all 'other highway conditions' only through sight distance, curvature and darkness, and no other condition
'at the subject's place' (st.sight_distance and st.curvature) is read at every lane the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), each of them bounding the speed
the surface gap to the road user ahead in the lane is read as the distance between the nearest points of the two bodies, not one of its components

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry daylight road, the subject moving on a straight lane wide enough for it, no road user ahead; its speed is such that v·p.driver_reaction_time + v·v/(2·p.following_decel_dry) exceeds st.sight_distance at its place (a blind crest ahead).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Dry daylight road, straight wide lane, no road user ahead, a long st.sight_distance and env.visibility; the subject moves at a speed whose stopping distance is within them and whose lateral drift bound holds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject stands at rest (kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but st.sight_distance is not observed on the source, and every other bound holds, so the verdict turns on the missing sight distance.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: env.ice_or_snow holds; the subject moves at a speed whose stopping distance on dry pavement would fit st.sight_distance but whose stopping distance with p.following_decel_ice exceeds it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Dry road, ample sight, but on a bend where v·v·st.curvature exceeds p.curve_lateral_accel_max.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A road user u is ahead in the subject's lane, nearly stopped, and the subject's stopping distance exceeds the surface gap plus u's braking distance.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.driver_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: perception-reaction time of an alert driver to an expected hazard in the stopping-distance model
param_proposals.source: Johansson and Rumar brake-reaction studies; AASHTO Green Book

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a dry paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.6)
param_proposals.source: tyre-pavement friction tables (AASHTO; accident-reconstruction handbooks)

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_wet
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a wet paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.4)
param_proposals.source: tyre-pavement friction tables (AASHTO; accident-reconstruction handbooks)

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.1)
param_proposals.source: tyre-pavement friction tables (AASHTO; accident-reconstruction handbooks)

param_proposals.name: p.curve_lateral_accel_max
param_proposals.convention: the lateral acceleration a passenger vehicle sustains on a curve within comfortable side friction on a dry or wet paved surface (about 0.3 g)
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book side-friction factors for horizontal curves

param_proposals.name: p.lane_keeping_heading_error
param_proposals.convention: the sine of the heading error (about 1.7 degrees) that a driver's lane keeping leaves uncorrected, so that the vehicle drifts laterally at that fraction of its speed
param_proposals.source: lane-keeping and time-to-line-crossing studies (Godthelp)

param_proposals.name: p.lane_departure_time_min
param_proposals.convention: the shortest time to line crossing a driver tolerates before correcting its lateral drift: the warning threshold of lane-departure warning systems
param_proposals.source: ISO 17361 lane departure warning systems

param_proposals.name: p.low_beam_sight_reach
param_proposals.convention: the distance ahead a passenger-car low beam lights the road in darkness enough to see an obstacle
param_proposals.source: UNECE R112 / SAE J1383 low-beam photometry

segmentation.text: When overtaking or passing
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
proceeding in the same direction,
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall exercise due care and:
If there is more than one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction,
move the vehicle to the lane to the immediate left,
if the lane is available and moving into the lane is reasonably safe.

elements.justification: 'overtaking or passing' a road user proceeding the same way is drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; it denotes the relative motion only and says nothing of lanes, which the words here do not name. The pass is under way while the bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero: 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)'; a projection, not a contact or a distance), within the window behind the pass's recognition.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels ...'), 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole; the overtaken road user is a member of any of them.

'proceeding' is the overtaken road user moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); 'in the same direction' is rel.same_direction ('headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance') between the subject and it, with the overtaking heading tolerance.

'a motor vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'). 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.standard: shall exercise due care
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the pass is made with due care where the subject's body never touches the overtaken rider's (rel.contact) and the rider is never made to brake harder than an evasive deceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal below its negative) while the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero); care is a state of mind, read only through this outcome

NRS_484B_270_2a_o1.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. At the observation, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r) rises, with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos, for some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, which at some observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window was moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, tolerance p.overtake_same_direction_cos).
NRS_484B_270_2a_o1.obligation: Surrogate. For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection): at every observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window, the subject is not in contact with r (rel.contact), and wherever the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) r's longitudinal acceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal) is not below the negative of p.rider_evasive_decel.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'due care' is read only through the pass's outcome for the rider: no contact and no evasive braking while side by side; other aspects of care are not observed and the rule is a surrogate

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle is ridden ahead of the subject car in the same direction; the subject car overtakes it and its side touches the bicycle while the two are side by side.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same pass, made without contact; the bicyclist keeps its speed.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car overtakes another car; no bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in permit, but the source does not observe contact between bodies.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car overtakes an electric scooter without touching it, but while they are side by side the rider brakes harder than the evasive deceleration.

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: overtaking-duration figures (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_30_030)

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading figures (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_30_030)

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: source speed resolution (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B)

param_proposals.name: p.rider_evasive_decel
param_proposals.convention: the longitudinal deceleration of a bicycle or scooter rider beyond which its braking counts as an evasive reaction to another road user rather than ordinary speed control: about 0.2 g, above comfortable bicycle braking
param_proposals.source: bicycle braking studies; traffic-conflict technique

segmentation.text: Every vehicle
driven upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section
or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn,
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.

elements.justification: 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. No named class stands in for it.

DEF-NRS-484A-070: 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section'. st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'; st.median_or_divider: 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'; st.on_way ties the divider to the highway h; rel.occupies anchors the subject on h. 'Driven' is read through the vehicle's motion.

'any left turn' is drv.motion.left_turn, 'Road user a has completed a turn to the left', a heading change to the left between turn_min and u_turn_min; 'U-turn' (DEF-NRS-484B-077, 'the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction') is drv.motion.u_turn, whose contract quotes that definition; a 'semicircular turn' is a turn through half a circle, a reversal of direction, which drv.motion.u_turn's band denotes. Both concepts read kin.yaw_rate through prim.heading_change and say nothing of the place, which the trigger and exceptions supply.

st.median_or_divider carries an 'opening attribute where a crossover exists': a turn 'through an opening' is one whose path overlaps (rel.occupies) a divider region of h that carries the opening attribute.

A crossover is a divider region with the opening attribute; an intersection is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; a turn 'at' it is one whose path overlaps it (rel.occupies). 'Established by a public authority' is a legal status read through the feature's presence.

NRS_484B_227_1_o3.applicability: At an observation at which drv.motion.left_turn(subject) or drv.motion.u_turn(subject) holds (the turn recognized; each holds at its recognition only), with window p.vehicle_turn_window, turn_min p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min and yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol, where at some observation of the window behind it of length p.vehicle_turn_window (the turn under way) the subject occupied a highway h on which a median_or_divider region lies (st.on_way).
NRS_484B_227_1_o3.obligation: The turn is made through an opening, a crossover or an intersection: at some observation of that same window the subject's footprint overlapped a median_or_divider region lying on h that carries the opening attribute, or an intersection lying on h. Where it overlapped none of them at any observation of the window, the turn violates the duty; where an overlap is unobserved and none is observed, unknown.

narrowings.why: 'semicircular turn' is read as a reversal of direction, the band of drv.motion.u_turn; a semicircle that does not reverse the heading is no semicircular turn.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's motion on the highway, whoever or whatever controls it.
'established by a public authority' is a legal status; the crossover or intersection present on the road is its evidence.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On highway h with a st.median_or_divider without opening, the subject makes a reversal of direction (drv.motion.u_turn rises) whose path crosses the divider away from any intersection and any region with the opening attribute.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: On h the subject makes a U-turn whose path overlaps a divider region carrying the opening attribute (a crossover).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject makes a left turn on a highway on which no st.median_or_divider lies.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject on divided highway h reverses direction across the divider; kin.yaw_rate is absent, so neither left_turn nor u_turn can be recognized.

scenarios.name: occasion_b
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies divided highway h during the first part of its left turn's window; the turn carries it across h's divider, where it has no opening, into a driveway beyond h: the trigger held for part of the turn and no opening or intersection was overlapped.

scenarios.name: occasion_b_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject left divided highway h before its turn window began and makes a U-turn on an undivided highway: the trigger held only before the turn.

scenarios.name: occasion_f
scenarios.narrative: The subject's U-turn on h overlaps a divider region carrying the opening attribute during part of its window.

scenarios.name: occasion_f_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject overlapped a divider opening on h only before its turn window began; the U-turn itself crosses the divider where it has no opening and overlaps no intersection.

scenarios.name: occasion_g
scenarios.narrative: The subject's left turn on h overlaps an intersection lying on h during part of its window.

scenarios.name: occasion_g_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupied an intersection on h only before its turn window began; it then makes a U-turn across the divider mid-block, overlapping no opening and no intersection.

under_way.words: its heading change over the window behind the observation
under_way.justification: The turn is under way within the window behind its recognition, over which prim.heading_change integrates kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading'): the road user's motion, not the region it occupies, tells the turn from what came before.

param_proposals.name: p.vehicle_turn_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of a turn by a motor vehicle at a junction or into or out of a driveway, from the start of its heading change to its end, including the crossing of opposing lanes
param_proposals.source: turning-movement durations at urban junctions in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading changes of a few degrees versus junction turns of about ninety degrees in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: midpoint between a right-angle turn and a full reversal of direction

param_proposals.name: p.turn_yaw_rate_tol
param_proposals.convention: the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which a road user's heading counts as no longer turning: the yaw-rate noise floor of the source
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate noise of vehicle inertial measurement

segmentation.text: A vehicle
must not be driven to the left side of the highway at any time:
When the view is obstructed
upon approaching within 100 feet of any bridge, viaduct or tunnel.
Subsection 2 does not apply upon a one-way highway.

elements.justification: 'A vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole.

'the left side of the highway' is the side beyond its center (DEF-NRS-484A-040: 'to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions, and, if a line is not marked, it is an imaginary line in the highway equally distant from the edges'): an st.centre_line c, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions', lying (st.on_way) on the st.highway the subject occupies (rel.occupies), with prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) ('signed lateral offset (m, left positive)') negative. 'at any time' places the duty at every observation. 'driven' is read through controlled motion (agency).

'any bridge, viaduct or tunnel' is st.elevated_structure, 'bridge, viaduct or tunnel carrying the roadway'. 'approaching within 100 feet': the ground distance from the subject's body to the structure (st.region_geometry) is at most the stated 100 feet and the subject's velocity (kin.velocity) points toward the structure's reference point from its position (kin.position).
'upon a one-way highway': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'; there subsection 2 does not apply.

operationalizations.standard: the view is obstructed
operationalizations.convention: Passing sight distance: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance by prevailing speed (Table 3B-1), the warrant for a no-passing zone where the view is restricted, expressed as the time the subject's speed takes to cover it. The view is obstructed where st.sight_distance at the subject's point, 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other', is below the subject's kin.speed times p.passing_sight_time; the bound moves with the subject's speed.

NRS_484B_213_2c.applicability: At an observation at which the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, occupies no st.one_way_roadway, st.sight_distance at its point is below its kin.speed times p.passing_sight_time, and for some st.elevated_structure x the ground distance from its body to x (st.region_geometry) is at most the stated 100 feet and the dot product of its kin.velocity with the vector from its kin.position to x's reference point is positive.
NRS_484B_213_2c.obligation: The subject is not on the left side of the highway: for every st.centre_line c lying (st.on_way) on a highway the subject occupies, prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) is not negative. Where it is negative for some such c, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'driven to the left side of the highway' is read as the subject's reference point lying beyond the centre line to its left.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.
'the view' is read through the sight distance of the subject's place, what could be seen from it, not through any driver's perception.

st.sight_distance 'at the subject's point' is read off the highway region the subject occupies (rel.occupies); the view is obstructed where it is below the subject's kin.speed times p.passing_sight_time for some such highway.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves toward an st.elevated_structure within the stated 100 feet, st.sight_distance at its point below its speed times p.passing_sight_time, its reference point left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same approach with the subject right of the centre line.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches a bridge within the stated distance with st.sight_distance far above the bound, left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches a bridge within the stated distance left of the centre line; st.sight_distance is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The same approach with short sight distance on an st.one_way_roadway.

param_proposals.name: p.passing_sight_time
param_proposals.convention: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance (Table 3B-1, the warrant for a no-passing zone) divided by the prevailing speed it is tabulated for: about eleven seconds of travel across 25 to 70 mph; the sight distance or the clear distance a pass needs is the subject's speed times this time
param_proposals.source: MUTCD 2009 Section 3B.02, Table 3B-1

segmentation.text: A vehicle
must not be driven to the left side of the highway at any time:
When approaching within 100 feet or traversing any intersection or railroad grade crossing.
Subsection 2 does not apply upon a one-way highway.

elements.justification: 'A vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole.

'the left side of the highway' is the side beyond its center (DEF-NRS-484A-040: 'to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions, and, if a line is not marked, it is an imaginary line in the highway equally distant from the edges'): an st.centre_line c, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions', lying (st.on_way) on the st.highway the subject occupies (rel.occupies), with prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) ('signed lateral offset (m, left positive)') negative. 'at any time' places the duty at every observation. 'driven' is read through controlled motion (agency).

'intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105) is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet', which excludes an alley junction as the definition's (3) does; 'railroad grade crossing' is st.railway_crossing, 'level crossing of a railway with the roadway' — a railroad (DEF-NRS-484A-200) is a carrier 'operated upon stationary rails' 'other than streetcars', and a streetcar line running in the street is no level crossing of a railway with the roadway. 'approaching within 100 feet': the ground distance from the subject's body to the region (st.region_geometry) is at most the stated 100 feet and the subject's velocity (kin.velocity) points toward the region's reference point from its position (kin.position). 'traversing': the subject's footprint overlaps the region (rel.occupies).
'upon a one-way highway': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'; there subsection 2 does not apply.

NRS_484B_213_2b.applicability: At an observation at which the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, occupies no st.one_way_roadway and, for some region x of kind st.intersection or st.railway_crossing, either the subject's footprint overlaps x (rel.occupies), or the ground distance from its body to x (st.region_geometry) is at most the stated 100 feet and the dot product of its kin.velocity with the vector from its kin.position to x's reference point is positive.
NRS_484B_213_2b.obligation: The subject is not on the left side of the highway: for every st.centre_line c lying (st.on_way) on a highway the subject occupies, prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) is not negative. Where it is negative for some such c, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'driven to the left side of the highway' is read as the subject's reference point lying beyond the centre line to its left.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves toward an st.intersection whose ground distance from its body is below the stated 100 feet, with its reference point left of the centre line of the highway it occupies.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same approach with the subject right of the centre line.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is left of the centre line far from any intersection or railway crossing.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves toward an intersection with st.region_geometry not observed: its distance to the intersection and its offset from the centre line are unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint overlaps an st.railway_crossing while its reference point is left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches an intersection within the stated distance on an st.one_way_roadway.

segmentation.text: When overtaking or passing
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
proceeding in the same direction,
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall exercise due care and:
If there is more than one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction,
move the vehicle to the lane to the immediate left,
if the lane is available and moving into the lane is reasonably safe.

elements.justification: 'overtaking or passing' a road user proceeding the same way is drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; it denotes the relative motion only, the lanes being read by a6 and a7. The pass is under way while the bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero; a projection, not a contact or a distance), within the window behind the pass's recognition.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole.

'proceeding' is the overtaken road user moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); 'in the same direction' is rel.same_direction ('headings aligned') between the subject and it, with the overtaking heading tolerance.
'a motor vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'). 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'more than one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction' is the count of lanes in the direction of a lane the overtaken road user occupies (st.lane_adjacency, 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction'; not the marking between lanes) being more than the stated one, read on a lane (st.lane) the rider occupies (rel.occupies). 'traffic' names the users of those lanes; no membership is read, the direction being the lanes' own.

'the vehicle' is the subject (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', of which the motor vehicle is a member). 'the lane to the immediate left' is the left neighbouring lane of the same direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction') of a lane (st.lane) the overtaken rider occupies (rel.occupies); 'move ... to' it is the subject's footprint overlapping that lane and not overlapping the rider's lane while the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), i.e. while it passes.

operationalizations.standard: if the lane is available and moving into the lane is reasonably safe
operationalizations.convention: gap acceptance at the start of the pass: at the last observation of the window behind at which the rider was ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, no shared length) with aligned headings, the lane to the rider's lane's immediate left exists (st.lane_adjacency), no temporary traffic control device governs it (available), and no road user other than the subject and the rider occupying it is nearer the subject's body (rel.surface_gap) than the subject's speed times the following headway for the surface: ice or snow, else wet road or precipitation, else dry (reasonably safe)

NRS_484B_270_2a_o2.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. At the observation, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r) rises, with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos, for some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, which at some observation of that window was moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos); and at some observation of that window at which the two were side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), r occupied a st.lane whose count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) is more than the literal one.
NRS_484B_270_2a_o2.obligation: For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection), unless the left lane was unavailable or unsafe at the pass's start: at every observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window at which the subject and r are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), the subject occupies (rel.occupies) the left neighbour (st.lane_adjacency) of a st.lane r occupies, and occupies no lane r occupies. The pass's start is the last observation of the window at which r was ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with headings aligned (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos); there the left lane is unavailable or unsafe where r's lane has no left neighbour, or a dev.temporary_traffic_control governs (dev.governs) that neighbour, or some road user u other than the subject and r occupying it has a rel.surface_gap to the subject below the subject's kin.speed × the headway (p.following_headway_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'move the vehicle to the lane' is read as the subject wholly in the left lane, overlapping none of the rider's lanes, at every observation at which it is side by side with the rider
'available' and 'reasonably safe' are read at the pass's start only, through closure by temporary traffic control and the time-headway gap to road users occupying the left lane

'the lane' to the rider's lane's immediate left is read beside some lane the rider occupies at the pass's start: the left lane is missing, unavailable or unsafe where it is so beside some lane the rider occupies

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry road with two lanes in one direction; a bicycle rides in the right lane; the left lane is open and empty. The subject car overtakes the bicycle staying in the right lane, side by side with it.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject car moves wholly into the left lane before drawing alongside and stays there until the bicycle is behind it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car overtakes another car on a two-lane carriageway; no bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe lane adjacency, so neither the lane count nor the left neighbour is known.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but at the pass's start a car occupies the left lane beside the subject, nearer than the subject's speed times the dry headway: the lane is not reasonably safe and the subject passes in the right lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The road has a single lane in the subject's direction; the subject passes a bicycle.

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: overtaking-duration figures (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_30_030)

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading figures (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_30_030)

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: source speed resolution (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B)

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_dry
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a dry surface: the two-second rule of driver manuals
param_proposals.source: driver manuals (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_wet
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a wet surface or in rain: the two-second rule lengthened by a second
param_proposals.source: driver manuals (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_ice
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on an icy or snow-covered surface: the tripled following time driver manuals advise
param_proposals.source: driver manuals (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)

segmentation.text: Pedestrians
shall move
whenever practicable
upon the right half of crosswalks.

elements.justification: 'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', claimed by its admitted id and never expanded into class atoms.

'shall move' places the duty on the pedestrian's movement: it is read at observations at which the pedestrian moves, i.e. where drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation ... its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance the caller sets for the source's speed resolution') does not hold with p.halt_speed_tolerance. A pedestrian at rest does not move, and the words place on it no duty of position.

'crosswalks' is st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'), carrying both limbs of DEF-NRS-484A-065 (the connection of the sidewalk lines at an intersection; a portion distinctly indicated for crossing by markings); the pedestrian's own crosswalk is anchored by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). 'the right half' is read about the crosswalk's reference point (st.region_geometry: 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame'; its not-a-stand-in clause excludes occupancy, which rel.occupies reads) and the pedestrian's own direction of movement (kin.velocity 'velocity vector', kin.position 'position of the body's reference point', kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity'): the pedestrian is on the right half where the crosswalk's reference point does not lie to the right of its direction of movement by more than p.pedestrian_lateral_tolerance, i.e. v_x(r_y-p_y) - v_y(r_x-p_x) is at least minus that tolerance times its speed.

operationalizations.standard: whenever practicable
operationalizations.convention: pedestrian stride and shy distance: keeping to the right half is impracticable where the right half ahead of the pedestrian is taken up within about two strides, by another road user occupying the same crosswalk ahead on its right (rel.bearing: positive longitudinal and negative lateral component; rel.surface_gap at or below the reach) or by an obstruction on its right (prim.region_lateral_offset below zero; st.region_geometry distance at or below the reach)

NRS_484B_293.applicability: The subject, a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), occupies a crosswalk x (rel.occupies(subject, x), x of kind st.crosswalk) and moves: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) does not hold.
NRS_484B_293.obligation: For every crosswalk x the subject occupies (re-bound with the same selection), either (a) it moves on the right half of x: with v its velocity, p its position and r the reference point of x, v_x*(r_y - p_y) - v_y*(r_x - p_x) is at least minus p.pedestrian_lateral_tolerance times its speed (kin.speed), so that x's reference point does not lie to its right by more than the tolerance; or (b) keeping to the right half is not practicable: some other road user u (not the subject) occupying x lies ahead of the subject on its right (rel.bearing(subject, u) with longitudinal component above zero and lateral component below zero) at a surface gap (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.pedestrian_near_reach, or some region o of kind st.obstruction lies on the subject's right (prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, o) below zero) at a ground distance (st.region_geometry) at or below p.pedestrian_near_reach.

narrowings.why: The halves of a crosswalk are read about its mapped reference point, taken as its centre, and the side is read relative to the pedestrian's own direction of movement (its velocity), which on a crossing runs along the crosswalk's length; a pedestrian within p.pedestrian_lateral_tolerance of the centre counts as on the right half.

The words name no factor of practicability; the catch-all is read only through the occupation of the right side ahead by another road user in the crosswalk or by an obstruction within p.pedestrian_near_reach; any other reason the right half may be impracticable is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian (ru.aggregate pedestrian) walks across a marked crosswalk it occupies (rel.occupies st.crosswalk) at 1.3 m/s (kin.speed); the crosswalk's reference point (st.region_geometry) lies 1.5 m to the right of its velocity; no other road user and no st.obstruction is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same pedestrian walks across the crosswalk with its reference point 1.5 m to the left of its velocity: it moves on the right half.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks along a st.sidewalk and occupies no st.crosswalk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian moving in a crosswalk at 1.3 m/s whose velocity is not observed: which half it moves on cannot be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian moves on the left half of the crosswalk while three other pedestrians occupying the crosswalk lie ahead of it on its right (rel.bearing longitudinal positive, lateral negative) at a surface gap of 1.5 m: the right half is not practicable.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian stands at rest (kin.speed 0) on the left half of the crosswalk: it does not move.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracked-object kinematics in driving datasets and simulators

param_proposals.name: p.pedestrian_lateral_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the lateral margin within which a pedestrian's reference point counts as on a line that divides a region or a way: half a pedestrian's shoulder breadth plus the source's position error for a pedestrian
param_proposals.source: Highway Capacity Manual pedestrian body ellipse (about 0.6 m shoulder breadth) and pedestrian tracking position error

param_proposals.name: p.pedestrian_near_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a pedestrian's body to a place, a region or a vehicle within which the pedestrian is near it: about two walking strides plus a curb step
param_proposals.source: pedestrian stride length (about 0.75 m) and curb step conventions of pedestrian facility design

segmentation.text: When a vehicle
enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered,
but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle

shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver shall proceed cautiously,
yielding
to vehicles which have previously completed a stop
or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'.

The entry is the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap the intersection X (rel.occupies; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet'), having at the previous observation occupied a carrier c that enters X: st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; st.travel_region is the kind of c. The carrier is the source's record, never read from distance or velocity.

dev.traffic_signal: 'a signal head; ... uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered' — 'installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered'. 'Controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself': the signal governs c or X. Not a stand-in for a position: governance, not the head's location, decides.

dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication' — exactly 'installed ... uncovered, but is inoperative'; read at the entry observation, 'at the time the vehicle enters the intersection'.

'The driver of the vehicle' is the vehicle's controlled motion (DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle'), read through the vehicle of the admitted aggregate.

Proceeding 'as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance' requires, at the subject's own entrance (its carrier c with st.lane_enters c X), the stop a stop sign requires before entering X (rel.occupies); the stop is DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement' (the definition whose scope is a stop 'when required'; DEF-NRS-484A-260 concerns stopping when prohibited), carried by drv.motion.complete_halt. Its place, in the words' order: st.stop_line ('the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') tied to c by st.entrance_of ('the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'), its side along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction) given by prim.region_offset_along and the body-to-line distance by st.region_geometry; else st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') marking c's entrance, 'before entering' being a footprint not overlapping it; else c's entrance end, the footprint not overlapping X and the body within the stop-point tolerance of it. Distance never stands for the association, which st.entrance_of records. 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway'): the view of its approaching members is a perception read through the place it describes.

NRS_484B_250_4_o1.applicability: At the subject's entry into an intersection X: the observation at which its footprint overlaps X and did not at the previous observation, where at that previous observation it occupied a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, X); and where at the entry observation a traffic signal d governs c or X (dev.governs) and d is inoperative (dev.inoperative).
NRS_484B_250_4_o1.obligation: Search for the stop: the subject made a complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) while occupying c at the place for c, in the words' order: (1) where a stop line marks c's entrance (st.entrance_of(line, c)), a halt with the line ahead of or at the subject's reference point along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along at or above zero) and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of the line (st.region_geometry distance); (2) where no stop line marks c (every line's entrance list is observed and excludes c), a halt with the footprint not overlapping the crosswalk marking c's entrance, that crosswalk ahead along c's direction (prim.region_offset_along above zero) and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of it; (3) where neither marks c, a halt with the footprint not overlapping X and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of X. History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start — the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the place marks, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it along c's direction, and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance; where several marks of that kind mark c, outside and short of each) — or at the subject's previous entry into X, whichever comes later. A halt found: compliant; either end reached without one: violated; neither end reached (the recording begins with the subject inside the zone): unknown. Each entry owes its own halt; only an observed exit from the zone upstream begins a new approach. The entry is unknown where the previous observation does not show the subject on a mapped carrier; where a mark's association with c is unobserved and the verdict turns on it, unknown. No bound is taken from the recording's start, a first observation or a cumulative distance.

narrowings.why: 'clearly marked' is read as the stop line the scene represents; the paint's clarity is not modelled.

'the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway' is read as c's entrance end into X, the point nearest the intersection outside it: the view is a perception read through the place the words describe, and no sight distance is measured. At an intersection with an inoperative signal the 'through highway' is each other way meeting there.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.traffic_signal governs carrier c, which enters X; at the subject's entry into X it is dev.inoperative. A st.stop_line marks c's entrance; the subject crosses it and enters X at a kin.speed well above p.halt_speed_tolerance, never halting since it was upstream of the line's stopping zone.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject halts (kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance) on c with the stop line just ahead within p.stop_point_tolerance, then enters X.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing c shows circular_green at the subject's entry into X: not inoperative.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A traffic signal governs c; dev.inoperative is absent on the source, so whether the signal is inoperative at the entry is unknown.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: Inoperative signal governing c; the recording begins with the subject already within p.stop_point_tolerance of the stop line, moving slowly; no halt is recorded before it enters X.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start: the subject's last observation outside the stop line's stopping zone upstream on c lies before the recording

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No stop line and no crosswalk mark c (entrance lists observed, excluding c); the subject halts with its footprint outside X and its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of X, then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A stop line marks c; the subject passes it without halting and halts only at the crosswalk beyond it, then enters X: the halt is not at the governing place.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: MUTCD stop line placement in advance of a crosswalk

segmentation.text: Any pedestrian
crossing a roadway
at a point where a pedestrian tunnel or overhead pedestrian crossing has been provided
shall yield
the right-of-way
to all vehicles upon the roadway
The foregoing rules in this Section shall have no application under the conditions stated in Section 11.30.070
when pedestrians are prohibited from crossing at certain designated places

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); one atom.

Same words and reading as LVMC_11_30_060_A's 'crossing a roadway': the pedestrian occupies a roadway r (rel.occupies; st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') and moves across a carrier k it occupies (st.lane or the roadway): drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos.

st.pedestrian_grade_separation, 'a pedestrian tunnel or overpass at a point on the highway', is exactly 'a pedestrian tunnel or overhead pedestrian crossing'; 'has been provided' is its presence. 'at a point where' places the pedestrian's crossing at that facility: st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)', at most p.grade_separation_reach, the reach within which a crossing is made at the point the facility serves; the distance relates the pedestrian, a road user, to the region.

Same words and meaning as the index's 'shall yield' -> kin.speed, rel.contact: not proceeding (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) into a conflict, and no collision (rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap').

'all vehicles' are members v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, quantified in the obligation; 'upon the roadway' is the roadway r the pedestrian crosses, re-bound in the obligation with its selection, and v occupies it (rel.occupies; st.roadway).

A place where pedestrians are prohibited from crossing is shown on the road by a posted prohibition: dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code', code pedestrians_prohibited, governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the roadway r the pedestrian crosses. 'designated' is legal status, read through the sign's presence.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where direction, speed and proximity give rise to the danger of a crash
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the defined right-of-way arises between road users 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash'; that danger is read as the two centres approaching under constant velocities within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

residues.why: Section 11.30.070 is no node of this run's library, neither accepted nor planned, so no rule can be composed; the condition under which it suspends this section is stated in this text's own words, 'when pedestrians are prohibited from crossing at certain designated places', carried by g8. Conditions of 11.30.070 those words do not state are not read; reported to the operator.

LVMC_11_30_060_B.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; it occupies a roadway r and moves across a carrier k it occupies (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos); some pedestrian tunnel or overpass g (st.pedestrian_grade_separation) lies within p.grade_separation_reach of its body (st.region_geometry); and no dev.regulatory_sign of code pedestrians_prohibited governs (dev.governs) that roadway r.
LVMC_11_30_060_B.obligation: For every vehicle v (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that occupies the roadway the subject occupies and crosses (re-bound with the same selection): the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while the subject's and v's centres, under constant velocities, approach within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'shall yield' is read as not proceeding into a danger of a crash with a vehicle on the roadway: a pedestrian at rest yields, and one moving while no conflict is projected yields too.
the right-of-way's 'direction, speed and proximity' are read only through the constant-velocity closest approach of the two centres.
a place designated as one where pedestrians are prohibited from crossing is read through the presence of a pedestrians_prohibited regulatory sign governing the roadway crossed.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses a roadway 10 m from a pedestrian overpass, walking at 1.4 m/s into the path of a car on that roadway whose projected closest approach is 1 m in 2 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses the roadway 10 m from the overpass at 1.4 m/s; no vehicle is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses a roadway 300 m from any pedestrian tunnel or overpass.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses the roadway near an overpass while a car approaches, but the source maps the overpass without its outline, so the distance to it is unknown.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of road-user tracking in recorded and simulated traces

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: geometric convention separating walking along a roadway from crossing it, from pedestrian heading resolution

param_proposals.name: p.grade_separation_reach
param_proposals.convention: ground distance from a pedestrian's body to a pedestrian tunnel or overpass within which a roadway crossing is made at the point that facility serves: the facility's width plus the stair or ramp landings at either end
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Planning, Design and Operation of Pedestrian Facilities: overpass stairs and ramps landing within about 30 m of the crossing line

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique (Swedish TCT, Hydén 1987): time-to-collision thresholds of 1.5 to 3 s

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (about 5.8 m by 2.1 m)

segmentation.text: Whenever signals are placed over the individual lanes of a highway,
the signals indicate, and apply to
drivers of vehicles,
as follows:
A red “X” symbol means
a driver facing the signal
must not enter or drive in any lane over which the red signal is shown.

elements.justification: 'signals ... placed over the individual lanes' is dev.lane_control_signal ('an overhead per-lane signal'), the lane it is over read by dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane ...'; not a stand-in for a position, and no halt position is read); 'lanes of a highway' is st.lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on a st.highway by st.on_way ('the public way ... a structure region lies on'). The lane is used as a lane, not as a half of the roadway.

'drivers of vehicles' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the subject is a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); 'driver' is not an aggregate.
'A red “X” symbol' is the state red_x of dev.lane_control_signal ('state ∈ {green_down_arrow, red_x, yellow_x, yellow_arrow(dir), dark}').

As the index maps 'pedestrians facing the signal' (NRS_484B_283_1d1): facing is read from the head's location (dev.position 'location of the device head / sign face'; not a stand-in for a stop line or crossing, none is read) and the subject's kin.position and kin.heading ('direction the body points'): the head lies ahead of the subject, the dot product of the vector from the subject to the head with its heading being positive. No atom carries the orientation of a signal face; a head ahead of the driver is the head it faces.

'enter ... any lane' is the rise of the subject's footprint overlap with the lane (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'); 'drive in' is the overlap while the subject moves (drv.motion.complete_halt — 'at rest at the observation' — not holding with p.halt_speed_tolerance); 'over which the red signal is shown' is the lane governed (dev.governs) by the lane-control signal displaying red_x.

NRS_484B_307_12b.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), and some lane l (st.lane) lying on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway) has a lane-control signal d placed over it (dev.lane_control_signal d, dev.governs(d, l)) that displays red_x and faces the subject: the dot product of (dev.position of d minus kin.position of the subject) with the subject's kin.heading is above zero.
NRS_484B_307_12b.obligation: For every lane l and lane-control signal d so selected (re-bound with the whole selection: d governs l, displays red_x and faces the subject): the subject does not enter l — rel.occupies(subject, l) does not rise at the observation — and does not drive in l — it does not occupy l while drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) fails.

narrowings.why: A vehicle that occupies a red-X lane while at rest (already in the lane when the indication appeared, halted) neither enters nor drives in it at that observation.
'drivers' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever is at its controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle (ru.aggregate vehicle) moving at 15 m/s changes into a st.lane over which a dev.lane_control_signal 80 m ahead (dev.position ahead along kin.heading) displays red_x: rel.occupies of that lane rises. No other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle keeps to its own lane, whose signal displays green_down_arrow, while the signal over the adjacent lane displays red_x; it never occupies the red-X lane.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No lane-control signal in the scene displays red_x.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle drives on a road whose lane-control signals are not observed by the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle already occupies a lane when its overhead signal ahead turns to red_x and keeps driving in it at 12 m/s.

param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution

segmentation.text: Whenever signals are placed over the individual lanes of a highway,
the signals indicate, and apply to
drivers of vehicles,
as follows:
A downward-pointing green arrow means that
a driver facing the signal
may drive in any lane over which the green signal is shown.

elements.justification: 'signals ... placed over the individual lanes' is dev.lane_control_signal ('an overhead per-lane signal'), the lane it is over read by dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane ...'; not a stand-in for a position, and no halt position is read); 'lanes of a highway' is st.lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on a st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') by st.on_way ('the public way ... a structure region lies on'). The lane is used as a lane, not as a half of the roadway.

'drivers of vehicles' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the subject is a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', its exclusions decided by the reading); 'driver' is not an aggregate.

'A downward-pointing green arrow' is the state green_down_arrow of dev.lane_control_signal ('state ∈ {green_down_arrow, red_x, yellow_x, yellow_arrow(dir), dark}') displayed by a head placed over a lane (dev.governs, st.lane).

As the index maps 'pedestrians facing the signal' (NRS_484B_283_1d1): facing is read from the head's location (dev.position 'location of the device head / sign face'; not a stand-in for a stop line or a crossing, none is read) and the subject's position and heading (kin.position, kin.heading 'direction the body points'): the head lies ahead of the subject, the dot product of the vector from the subject to the head with the subject's heading being positive. No atom carries the orientation of a signal face; a head ahead of the driver is the head it faces.

'drive in any lane' is the subject's footprint overlapping a lane (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', st.lane) while it moves (drv.motion.complete_halt does not hold: 'at rest at the observation ... speed at or below a tolerance'); 'over which the green signal is shown' is the lane-control signal (dev.lane_control_signal) placed over that lane (dev.governs) displaying green_down_arrow.

NRS_484B_307_12a.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); some lane l (st.lane) lying on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway) has a lane-control signal d placed over it (dev.lane_control_signal d, dev.governs(d, l)) that displays green_down_arrow and faces the subject: the dot product of (dev.position of d minus kin.position of the subject) with the subject's kin.heading is above zero; and the subject drives in a lane l2 (rel.occupies(subject, l2), st.lane) over which a lane-control signal d2 is placed (dev.governs(d2, l2)) that displays a state other than dark and faces the subject in the same way, while drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) does not hold.
NRS_484B_307_12a.obligation: For every lane l2 and lane-control signal d2 so selected (re-bound with the whole selection: the subject occupies l2 while moving, d2 governs l2, is lit and faces the subject): d2 displays green_down_arrow — the lane the subject drives in is one over which the green signal is shown, the scope of the permission the words grant to a driver facing a green arrow.

narrowings.why: The words grant a permission and impose no duty of their own. The permission is read as its scope: a driver facing a green downward arrow, driving in a signalled lane under a lit head that faces it, is within the permission where the green arrow is shown over that lane; driving in a signalled lane under any other lit indication is outside it and is reported as a violation of this rule. Whether that conduct is also forbidden is decided by the rules of the other indications (NRS 484B.307(12)(b) and the following paragraphs).
'drivers' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving in the lane is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever is at its controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle (ru.aggregate vehicle) drives at 15 m/s in a st.lane over which a dev.lane_control_signal 80 m ahead (dev.position ahead along kin.heading, dev.governs that lane) displays yellow_x, while the signal over the adjacent lane, also ahead, displays green_down_arrow. No other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same vehicle drives in the lane whose overhead lane-control signal ahead displays green_down_arrow.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle drives on a road over whose lanes no lane-control signal is placed (no dev.governs from any dev.lane_control_signal).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle drives in a lane of a road whose lane-control signals are not observed by the source: whether a signal is over the lane and what it shows cannot be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Every lane-control signal over the lanes ahead of the vehicle displays red_x: the driver faces no green arrow.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer
or a traffic-control signal:
When proper signs have been erected,
the driver of a vehicle

shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped,
the driver shall yield
the right-of-way
to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway
or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway'), of which the subject is a member. 'Being controlled by a police officer' (DEF-NRS-484A-180 'every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic') is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic ... role ∈ {police_officer, ...}', of role police_officer governing (dev.governs) the subject's carrier c or X (st.travel_region), read at the subject's entry.

'Being controlled by ... a traffic-control signal' (DEF-NRS-484A-290 'by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed'): a dev.traffic_signal governing c or X (dev.governs) that is not dev.inoperative ('installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'): a dark signal directs nothing.

'Proper signs' are a dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') or dev.yield_sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') governing (dev.governs) the carrier c the subject occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is X (st.lane_enters), or X itself. Governance, not the sign's position, ties it to the approach.
Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Stop' is DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement' (the definition whose scope is a stop 'when required'; DEF-NRS-484A-260 applies when stopping is prohibited), carried by drv.motion.complete_halt; at a stop sign it is owed. 'Yield' at a yield sign is, in the words of the next sentence, 'slowed or stopped': the subject's kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') within the place's stopping zone is at or below the speed from which it still halts at the place (p.yield_line_speed_max), a halt included. The place, in the words' order: st.stop_line ('the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') tied to c by st.entrance_of, its side along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction) given by prim.region_offset_along, the body-to-line distance by st.region_geometry; else st.crosswalk marking c's entrance, 'before entering' being a footprint not overlapping it (rel.occupies); else c's entrance end into X (st.intersection), the footprint outside X. Distance never stands for the association. 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic; the view of its approaching members is a perception read through the place the words describe.

NRS_484B_257_1_o1.applicability: At the subject's entry into an intersection X: the observation at which its footprint overlaps X and did not at the previous observation, where at that previous observation it occupied a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, X); where at the entry observation a stop sign or a yield sign governs c or X (dev.governs); except where at that observation a police officer's direction (dev.human_direction of role police_officer) governs c or X, or a traffic signal that is not inoperative (dev.inoperative false) governs c or X.
NRS_484B_257_1_o1.obligation: Search for the act on the approach: where a stop sign governs c or X, a complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance); where only a yield sign does, an observation at which the subject's kin.speed is at or below p.yield_line_speed_max (a halt included) — in either case while occupying c within the stopping zone of the place for c, in the words' order: (1) where a stop line marks c's entrance (st.entrance_of(line, c)), the line ahead of or at the subject's reference point along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along at or above zero) and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of the line (st.region_geometry distance); (2) where no stop line marks c (every line's entrance list observed and excluding c), the footprint not overlapping the crosswalk marking c's entrance, that crosswalk ahead along c's direction and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of it; (3) where neither marks c, the footprint not overlapping X and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of X. History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start — the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the place marks, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it along c's direction and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance; where several marks of that kind mark c, outside and short of each) — or at the subject's previous entry into X, whichever is later. Act found: compliant; either end reached without it: violated; neither end reached (the recording begins inside the zone): unknown. Each entry owes its own act; only an observed exit from the zone upstream begins a new approach. The entry is unknown where the previous observation does not show the subject on a mapped carrier; where a mark's association with c is unobserved and the verdict turns on it, unknown. No bound is taken from the recording's start, a first observation or a cumulative distance.

narrowings.why: 'proper signs have been erected' is a legal status; a stop or yield sign present and governing the approach is its evidence.
'clearly marked' is read as the stop line the scene represents; the paint's clarity is not modelled.

'the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway' is read as c's entrance end into X, the point nearest the intersection outside it: the view is a perception read through the place the words describe; no sight distance is measured.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

The history bound 'the subject's previous entry into X' is written as the subject's observed exit from X following that entry (rises of not rel_occupies(subject, X)): a single since cannot tell the judged entry from an earlier one at the same intersection, so the search stops at the first observation off X after the earlier entry, and an act performed while the footprint still overlaps X after an earlier entry does not count toward the next entry.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.stop_sign governs carrier c entering X; a st.stop_line marks c; no officer or operating signal. The subject passes the line and enters X with kin.speed well above p.halt_speed_tolerance, never halting since it was upstream of the line's stopping zone.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject halts on c with the line just ahead within p.stop_point_tolerance, then enters X.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No stop or yield sign governs c or X; the subject enters X without halting.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Stop sign governing c; kin.speed is absent, so whether the subject halted within the line's stopping zone is unknown.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: Stop sign governing c; the recording begins with the subject already within p.stop_point_tolerance of the stop line, moving slowly; no halt is recorded before its entry into X.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start: the subject's last observation outside the stop line's stopping zone upstream on c lies before the recording

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Only a dev.yield_sign governs c; the subject passes the stop line's zone at kin.speed at or below p.yield_line_speed_max and enters X.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Only a yield sign governs c; the subject passes through the place's stopping zone with kin.speed well above p.yield_line_speed_max at every observation and enters X.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs c, but a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governs c at the subject's entry; it enters X without halting.
