param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: MUTCD stop line placement in advance of a crosswalk

param_proposals.name: p.yield_line_speed_max
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle at the place of a yield sign counts as having slowed: the speed from which a passenger car can still halt within the stop-point tolerance at a comfortable deceleration of about 4.5 m/s^2
param_proposals.source: AASHTO comfortable deceleration rate of the stopping sight distance model

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a green straight-through arrow alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
may proceed straight through, but must not turn right or left.
Such vehicular traffic
must yield
the right-of-way
to other vehicles
and to pedestrians
lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time the signal is exhibited.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., green_arrow(dir), ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once': a green straight-through arrow alone is the head displaying green_arrow(straight) and no other state. Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a and NRS_484B_307_4a_o1.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), both held, claimed as ru.aggregate and never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a travel region c (st.travel_region, the kinds 'a device can govern') whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; i of kind st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not read as a position, st.lane_enters not as presence in the intersection. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

The movement through intersection i (st.intersection) is the subject's passage from its entry (rel.occupies rising) to its exit. 'must not turn right or left': drv.motion.right_turn_through_region ('a turn to the right through region r, recognized as it leaves r') and drv.motion.left_turn_through_region ('a turn to the left through region r'); a reversal, drv.motion.u_turn_through_region ('turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction through region r'), is a turn to one hand carried past a right angle and is no movement 'straight through', so it is read with them (narrowing). 'may proceed straight through': a passage for which none of the three holds; the permission adds no duty. As the index maps the arrow movements of NRS_484B_307_4a_o1.

NRS_484B_307_5a_o1.applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, has entered intersection i from a travel region c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs): at the act's onset its footprint came to overlap i, having occupied c and not i at the observation before. At some observation of the passage, from that entry to the judged observation, s displayed a green straight-through arrow alone (green_arrow(straight) and no other state). The rule is judged at the passage's recognition: the observation at which the subject's footprint does not overlap i, having overlapped it at the previous observation.
NRS_484B_307_5a_o1.obligation: At that recognition none of drv.motion.left_turn_through_region, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region and drv.motion.u_turn_through_region holds for the subject and i (step = p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min): the passage was made straight through.

narrowings.why: 'turn right or left' is read as a passage through the intersection recognized as a right turn, a left turn or a reversal of direction (a U-turn turns to one hand beyond a right angle and is not straight through). A heading change below p.turn_heading_min, such as a lane change made inside the intersection, is read as straight through.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies lane c, recorded as entering intersection i and governed by head s displaying green_arrow(straight) alone; it enters i, its heading changes by +88 degrees inside i, and it leaves i while s still displays the arrow.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same arrow; the car passes through i with a heading change of 2 degrees and leaves it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: s displays circular_green alone from before the car's entry until after its exit; the car turns left through i.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source supplies no yaw rate for the car while it is inside i: which movement it made is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1
scenarios.narrative: s displays green_arrow(straight) alone at the car's entry into i and changes to circular_yellow alone while the car is turning left inside i; the car leaves i with a heading change of +90 degrees: the arrow was displayed for part of the passage only.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1_outside
scenarios.narrative: s displays green_arrow(straight) alone only while the car waits on c before its entry; from the entry to the exit s displays circular_green alone; the car turns left through i.

onset.words: the subject's entry into the intersection from its approach
onset.justification: The through-region acts begin, as their contracts state, 'at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r'.

occasion.recognition: the observation at which the subject's footprint does not overlap the intersection, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit, where the through-region acts are recognized

under_way.words: the subject inside the intersection it entered, turning or holding its heading, from its entry to its exit
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act is one from the entry on at which the subject still overlaps i and its heading change since the entry, integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading'), is being accumulated; before the entry the integration has not begun, so the motion, not the place alone, tells the act from what preceded it.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1; repeated unchanged

segmentation.text: A driver of a motor vehicle
shall: Exercise
proper caution
upon observing
a pedestrian:
(1) On or near a highway, street or road;
(2) At or near a bus stop or bench, shelter or transit stop for passengers of public mass transportation
or in the act of boarding
a bus or other public transportation vehicle;
or (3) In or near a school zone or a school crossing zone
marked in accordance with NRS 484B.363
or a marked or unmarked crosswalk.

elements.justification: The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.

What the driver must exercise shows in the vehicle's conduct toward the observed pedestrian: its motion, kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the duty read while it moves above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and the outcome caution exists to prevent, rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', which is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss'; the near miss is bounded by the operationalization of z2.

Observing is a perception; the ontology reads what was in an actual road user's line of sight as rel.visible, 'b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight from a's reference point to b's body' (observable_reading, perception). Its exclusions — a distance, the sight distance of a place, the clarity of the air, a lamp being lit — do not apply: the words name what the driver could see of an actual pedestrian.

'Pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate.

'Highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic'), 'street' (DEF-NRS-484A-265, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway inside the territorial limits of a city') and 'road' (DEF-NRS-484A-215, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway outside the territorial limits of a city') are all highways, and together every highway whatever the city limits: st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; it is 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway', and the words name the whole way. 'On' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; 'near' is st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)', at most p.pedestrian_near_reach. st.region_geometry is 'Not a stand-in for: occupancy', which is why rel.occupies carries 'on'.

'a bus stop or bench, shelter or transit stop for passengers of public mass transportation' is st.transit_stop, 'a bus stop, bench, shelter or platform for public transport passengers'. 'Stop' here is part of the place name 'bus stop' and 'transit stop', not the halt DEF-NRS-484A-255 or DEF-NRS-484A-260 defines. 'At' is rel.occupies of the stop's region and 'near' is its st.region_geometry ground distance at most p.pedestrian_near_reach, which also anchors the stop to the pedestrian.

Boarding is read through the conduct that shows it (observable_reading, purpose): the pedestrian within p.pedestrian_near_reach of the vehicle's body, rel.surface_gap 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', while the vehicle is at rest, drv.motion.complete_halt 'The road user is at rest at the observation', and has a door open, sig.door_open 'a door open'. The halt concept 'says nothing of how long the road user stays at rest, where it is, or why', which the reading does not need.

'Bus' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus ('a vehicle owned by the State, a political subdivision or a private school or nursery, designed for carrying more than 10 passengers ... or a vehicle, other than a taxicab, designed and used for the transportation of persons for compensation'), claimed as ru.aggregate. 'Other public transportation vehicle' is a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported ... upon a highway', excluding devices 'used exclusively upon stationary rails') that is in public transit service: ru.transit_bus, 'bus in public transit service, identifiable by its livery or route display', a class the words name on their own and no definition admits.

'School zone' (DEF-NRS-484B-063, 'those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property') and 'school crossing zone' (DEF-NRS-484B-060, 'those sections of streets not adjacent to school property that pupils cross while following a designated walking route to school') are administrative categories; the law takes them where they are 'marked', and the ontology makes the sign the atom where a category is marked on the road: dev.zone_sign, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}', with kind school or school_crossing and its end attribute false; the sections of street are the travel regions it governs, dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', of kind st.travel_region. dev.zone_sign is 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now', which the words do not ask: the zone, not its hours, places the pedestrian. 'In' is rel.occupies of such a region and 'near' its st.region_geometry ground distance at most p.pedestrian_near_reach.

'marked in accordance with NRS 484B.363' is the zone's marking: dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing. Its accordance with NRS 484B.363, a statute outside this corpus, is the legal status of a feature, read through the sign's presence (observable_reading, status).

'Crosswalk' (DEF-NRS-484A-065, '(1) That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface') is st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute', both values of the attribute read since the words name 'a marked or unmarked crosswalk'. 'In or near' (carried from z9) is rel.occupies of the crosswalk or its st.region_geometry ground distance at most p.pedestrian_near_reach.

operationalizations.standard: proper caution upon observing a pedestrian (a standard of the driver's care, a state of mind)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves, caution shows in its keeping no contact and no closest approach to the observed pedestrian, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

NRS_484B_280_1c.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven.
NRS_484B_280_1c.obligation: At every observation at which the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every road user p other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, visible from the subject at that observation (rel.visible), and at one of the places: (1) p's footprint overlaps a highway (st.highway) or its ground distance to one (st.region_geometry) is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach; (2) p's footprint overlaps a transit stop (st.transit_stop) or its ground distance to one is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach, or p's rel.surface_gap to a road user v that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus, or a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that is an ru.transit_bus, is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach while v is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) and has a door open (sig.door_open); (3) p's footprint overlaps, or its ground distance is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach to, a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing that begins a zone, or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk, marked or unmarked): the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of caution, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'A driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.
'upon observing' is read as the pedestrian being in the subject's line of sight at the observation judged; a pedestrian seen earlier and occluded now is not read.
'in the act of boarding' is read through the conduct that shows it: the pedestrian close to a halted bus or transit vehicle with a door open.
the marking's accordance with NRS 484B.363 is read through the presence of the school or school-crossing zone sign.

Proper caution, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome while the subject moves: no contact and no conflicting closest approach with the observed pedestrian; slowing, lookout and every other aspect of caution are read only through that outcome.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian visible from a moving car steps from the curb into a marked crosswalk; the car does not slow and their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car slows and halts short of the crosswalk while the visible pedestrian crosses; while it moves there is no contact and no conflicting closest approach.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is an electric scooter (not a member of the motor vehicle aggregate) passing a pedestrian at a crosswalk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A moving car closes on a pedestrian at a crosswalk with a conflicting closest approach; whether the pedestrian is in the car's line of sight is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A moving car drives on a street with no pedestrian in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian hidden behind a parked van (not visible from the car) steps into the roadway; the car's closest approach to it is in conflict but there is no contact: the duty arises only upon observing.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A visible pedestrian stands beside a halted transit bus whose door is open, boarding it; a moving car passes the bus with a conflicting closest approach to the pedestrian.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (time-to-collision thresholds)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (AASHTO)

param_proposals.name: p.pedestrian_near_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a pedestrian's body to a place, a region or a vehicle within which the pedestrian is near it: about two walking strides plus a curb step
param_proposals.source: pedestrian stride length (about 0.75 m) and curb heights (FHWA pedestrian facility guidance)

segmentation.text: A vehicle
must not be driven to the left side of the center of a two-lane, two-directional highway and overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction,
unless such left side is clearly visible
and is free of oncoming traffic

for a sufficient distance ahead to permit such overtaking and passing to be completely made without interfering with the safe operation of any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction or any vehicle overtaken.

elements.justification: 'A vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'), claimed whole.

'center' (DEF-NRS-484A-040) is 'a continuous or broken line marked upon the surface of a highway ... to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions, and, if a line is not marked, it is an imaginary line in the highway equally distant from the edges or curbs': st.centre_line, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', lying (st.on_way) on the st.highway the subject occupies (rel.occupies). 'to the left side of the center' is prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c), 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', being negative: the centre line lies to the right of the subject's reference point. 'two-directional highway' (DEF-NRS-484B-073) is 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions': the highway carries an st.centre_line, which divides 'the two directions of a two-way roadway', one roadway, so the way is undivided. 'two-lane': every st.lane lying on that highway (st.on_way) has an st.lane_adjacency 'count of the lanes in that direction' of a single lane, so the two directions carry the stated two lanes; the lane contract's exclusion ('lane ordinal equals roadway half only on a two-lane road') is met, the road being two-lane. 'overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction' is the act drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; b is of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'driven' is read through controlled motion (agency).

'such left side is clearly visible': st.sight_distance at the subject's point, 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... whether or not any road user is there'; what a driver could see is read through that place's sight distance (observable_reading, perception), not rel.visible, since no actual road user need be there. Its extent is bounded by the standard of s7.

'oncoming traffic': road users of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic whose heading is opposed and closing to the subject's (rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing'); 'free of' them for the distance of s7 is read on their rel.centre_distance to the subject, which is not used as a clearance between bodies but as the distance along the road ahead.

operationalizations.standard: for a sufficient distance ahead to permit such overtaking and passing to be completely made without interfering with the safe operation of any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction or any vehicle overtaken
operationalizations.convention: Passing sight distance: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance by prevailing speed (Table 3B-1), expressed as the time the subject's speed takes to cover it (p.passing_sight_time), so the required distance moves with the subject's speed; both the sight distance at the subject's point and the centre distance to every oncoming road user of traffic must reach it. Interference with the safe operation of an oncoming vehicle or the vehicle overtaken: the traffic-conflict technique, a contact or a closest approach under constant velocities within p.conflict_horizon closer than p.conflict_centre_clearance.

NRS_484B_213_1.applicability: The subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, overtakes and passes another road user b of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b) with p.overtake_window and p.overtake_same_direction_cos is recognized at the judged observation. b is quantified there, not a binder.
NRS_484B_213_1.obligation: At every observation of the act (from its beginning, the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead with aligned headings, to its recognition) at which the subject occupies a highway h on which an st.centre_line c lies (st.on_way) and every lane lying on h has a single lane in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) — the two-lane, two-directional highway — and prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) is negative for a centre line c lying on h (the subject on the left side of the center), all of the following hold; otherwise the duty is violated: st.sight_distance at the subject's point is at least the subject's kin.speed times p.passing_sight_time; every road user u of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic with rel.oncoming(subject, u) under p.oncoming_heading_cos is at a rel.centre_distance of at least that same distance; and neither b nor any road user u of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle oncoming to the subject is in rel.contact with the subject, or has prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'driven to the left side of the center' is read as the subject's reference point lying beyond the centre line to its left; a body that only straddles the line with its reference point on the right is not read.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.
'clearly visible' is read through the sight distance of the subject's place, what could be seen from it, not through any driver's perception.
The exception is read at the observations of the act at which the subject is on the left side of the center: visibility and freedom from oncoming traffic are required while the left side is used.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a highway with a centre line and one lane in each direction, the subject moves left of the centre line to pass b; a road user u of traffic is oncoming in that lane at a centre distance below the subject's speed times p.passing_sight_time, and its closest approach within p.conflict_horizon falls below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the pass is recognized.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same pass with st.sight_distance at the subject's point far above its speed times p.passing_sight_time at every observation of the act and no oncoming road user in the scene; the subject keeps clear of b.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject follows b on the two-lane highway without passing it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pass of permit with st.sight_distance not observed on the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on a highway with two lanes in each direction, using the other lane of its own direction, with an oncoming vehicle near on the far side of the centre line: the subject is never left of the centre of a two-lane highway.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5
scenarios.narrative: While the subject is left of the centre line, st.sight_distance at its point is above the subject's speed times p.passing_sight_time for the first part of the act and falls below it approaching a crest; no oncoming traffic.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5_outside
scenarios.narrative: st.sight_distance was below the bound before the act began and is above it at every observation of the act; no oncoming traffic.

scenarios.name: occasion_s6
scenarios.narrative: Sight distance is ample; an oncoming road user of traffic comes within the required distance during the second half of the act while the subject is still left of the centre line.

scenarios.name: occasion_s6_outside
scenarios.narrative: An oncoming road user passed the subject before the act began; during the act no oncoming road user is within the required distance.

under_way.words: overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act lies after its beginning, the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction), and at or before its recognition, while the subject's velocity (kin.velocity), exceeding b's along its heading, carries it up to and past b. These relations read the two road users' relative motion, never a place.

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: overtaking-manoeuvre durations in naturalistic driving studies

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading angles in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.passing_sight_time
param_proposals.convention: the MUTCD minimum passing sight distance (Table 3B-1, the warrant for a no-passing zone) divided by the prevailing speed it is tabulated for: about eleven seconds of travel across 25 to 70 mph; the sight distance or the clear distance a pass needs is the subject's speed times this time
param_proposals.source: MUTCD 2009 Section 3B.02, Table 3B-1

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
param_proposals.source: heading geometry of two-way traffic

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique; FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design-vehicle dimensions

segmentation.text: Said driver
having so yielded
may proceed
and
the drivers of all other vehicles
approaching the intersection
on the through highway
shall yield
right-of-way
to the vehicle about to enter or cross the through highway

elements.justification: 'Said driver' is the driver subsection (A) addresses: the driver of a vehicle (the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) at an entrance to the through highway, which DEF-NRS-484A-275 describes as one where 'vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield right-of-way to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to either an authorized stop sign or a yield sign, or other official traffic-control device'. Read: o occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier c2 (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(c2, j) for the intersection j the subject approaches, c2 governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign, a yield sign or a traffic signal showing flashing_red. dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply: governance is read. The role 'driver' is read through o's controlled motion, never as membership.

'having so yielded' requires the act itself, with its qualifications: o yielded right-of-way 'to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to' the device at its entrance (DEF-NRS-484A-275). Read over o's approach, from the last observation at which o's occupancy of c2 rose until its occupancy of j rose: where c2 is governed by a stop sign or flashing-red signal, o came to rest on c2 short of j (drv.motion.complete_halt, 'complete cessation from movement'); and o did not proceed (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while a vehicle on the through highway was in a danger of a crash with it, the right-of-way bound operationalized on s9 (prim.closest_approach_within / prim.closest_approach_distance with p.conflict_horizon and p.conflict_centre_clearance), nor touched one (rel.contact). The primitives' exclusion 'alone establishes none of [contact, clearance, danger]' is respected: the danger is the operationalization's bound. Subsection (A) itself is not in this plan nor accepted, so its words are carried by these observables, not by composition.

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Its exclusion 'a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle — never membership' does not apply: 'the drivers of' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading), and the aggregate only states the class. 'all other' = every vehicle other than the one about to enter: the subject is never the same road user as o.

st.lane_enters: 'a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection ... approaches through it whatever its motion'. The carrier c is quantified over st.travel_region (the abstract union of the carrier kinds lane_enters admits) and the intersection j over st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet'). Not a stand-in for the subject's presence in the intersection or for dev.governs: the relation read is entry topology, as its contract states.

DEF-NRS-484A-275: a through highway is one 'at the entrances to which vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield right-of-way to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to either an authorized stop sign or a yield sign, or other official traffic-control device'. Read on the devices: the subject's approach carrier c is governed (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by no stop sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt'), yield sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') or traffic signal showing flashing_red, while the entering vehicle's carrier c2 into the same j is governed by one of them. dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply: governance, not a halting place, is read.

To yield is to grant the other precedence: the subject does not proceed in conflict with it. kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells a subject still proceeding from one that has given way; rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)' marks precedence taken outright. rel.contact's exclusion 'a near miss' is respected: the near-conflict is bounded by the operationalization of s9, not by contact.

'the vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate, as on s5). 'about to enter or cross the through highway' is an imminent movement, read by the movement it leads to: o, coming from carrier c2 with st.lane_enters(c2, j), occupies j (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... intersection ...)') now or at an observation within p.conflict_horizon ahead; j is the intersection of the through highway the subject approaches (st.intersection).

operationalizations.standard: right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the centres of the two road users come within a centre clearance comparable to their half-extents inside a time-to-collision horizon; a road user whose speed is at or below the source's speed resolution has granted precedence

residues.why: a permission granted to the entering driver; it imposes no condition on the through-highway drivers beyond the entering vehicle's movement, which s10 carries, so the duty is the same whether or not the permission is read

LVMC_11_12_070_B.applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), occupies a carrier c (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(c, j) for an intersection j (st.intersection), and c is governed (dev.governs) by no stop sign, no yield sign and no traffic signal showing flashing_red; and some road user o, not the subject, is a vehicle (same aggregate) that came from a carrier c2 with st.lane_enters(c2, j) governed by a stop sign, a yield sign or a traffic signal showing flashing_red, and either occupies j (having occupied c2 or j at every observation since it last occupied c2) or occupies c2 and occupies j at some observation within p.conflict_horizon ahead; and o has so yielded: since the last observation at which o's occupancy of c2 rose, (i) where c2 is governed by a stop sign or a flashing-red signal, drv.motion.complete_halt(o; p.halt_speed_tolerance) held at some observation at which o occupied c2 and not j, and (ii) at every observation before o's occupancy of j rose, it is not the case that o's kin.speed exceeded p.halt_speed_tolerance while, for some vehicle v other than o that occupied j or a carrier entering j governed by no stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red signal, prim.closest_approach_within(o, v; p.conflict_horizon) held with prim.closest_approach_distance(o, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance, and o was in rel.contact with no such v; this is unknown where o's occupancy of c2 rose before the recording began.
LVMC_11_12_070_B.obligation: For every road user o selected as in the applicability (re-bound with the whole selection: a vehicle other than the subject, from a carrier c2 entering the same j governed by a stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red signal, entering j within p.conflict_horizon or already in j having come from c2, and having so yielded as the applicability states): it is not the case that the subject's kin.speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, o; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, o; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance; and rel.contact(subject, o) does not hold.

narrowings.why: 'drivers' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle approaching on the through highway, whoever or whatever controls it

the legal designation 'through highway' is read through the devices on the road that display it: a stop sign, a yield sign or a flashing-red signal governing the entering approach and none governing the subject's approach; 'other official traffic-control device' is read as the flashing-red signal, the remaining device that requires traffic from the intersecting highway to halt and yield
'about to enter or cross' is an imminent movement, read by the entry into the intersection it leads to (within p.conflict_horizon ahead) or by the vehicle already crossing

precedence is read as the subject not proceeding (speed above the halt tolerance) while a constant-velocity closest approach to the entering vehicle falls below the centre clearance within the horizon, and never touching it; how the subject gives way (slowing or halting) is not modelled

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Subject vehicle on a lane entering j with no device; o halts at the stop sign on the cross approach and starts into j when no through vehicle is within the conflict bound; the subject then arrives and the subject keeps its speed and the constant-velocity closest approach of centres is below p.conflict_centre_clearance within p.conflict_horizon.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject brakes to a halt short of j while o crosses; while the closest approach is below the clearance the subject's speed is at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance, and no contact occurs.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches j on the through approach, but no vehicle is on or entering from a stop-sign or yield-sign approach of j.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe which carriers the stop sign governs, so whether o's approach is an entrance to a through highway is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: All-way stop: the subject's own carrier is governed by a stop sign, so it is not on a through highway.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, except that o never comes to rest at its stop sign before entering j: it has not so yielded, and the duty does not arise.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, except that o halts and then pulls into j while the subject is already within the conflict bound of it: o has not so yielded.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hydén 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car dimensions (AASHTO design vehicle P: 5.8 m by 2.1 m)

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed noise floor of vehicle odometry and tracked-object estimates

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a green turn arrow alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
may proceed only in the direction indicated by the arrow signal so long as the arrow is illuminated,
but the traffic must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within the adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

elements.justification: 'a green turn arrow alone' is dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {... green_arrow(dir) ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once') displaying green_arrow(dir) for a turn direction (left, right or u_turn) and no other state: 'alone' excludes a circular green or any other state shown with it.

'Vehicular traffic' is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') that is a vehicle: 'vehicular' uses the defined word of DEF-NRS-484A-320, whose admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported') is claimed (see PLAN.md). 'facing the signal' is read through the approach: the subject's passage through the intersection (st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet') began from a carrier (st.travel_region) it occupied (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end') and which the signal governs (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a stand-in for a position).

'proceed only in the direction indicated by the arrow' is the passage through the intersection matching the arrow's direction, read at its recognition, the subject's exit from the intersection (rel.occupies of st.intersection ceasing): for green_arrow(left), drv.motion.left_turn_through_region ('Road user a has made a turn to the left through region r, recognized as it leaves r'); for green_arrow(right), drv.motion.right_turn_through_region ('has made a turn to the right through region r'); for green_arrow(u_turn), drv.motion.u_turn_through_region ('has turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction through region r'), each over the intersection the subject passes, with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min p.turn_heading_min and u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min. 'so long as the arrow is illuminated' is dev.traffic_signal displaying that arrow alone at some observation of the passage (the occasion of s1).

NRS_484B_307_4a_o1.applicability: At an observation at which the subject, a member of traffic and a vehicle, exits an intersection i (st.intersection): rel.occupies(subject, i) does not hold, having held at the previous observation; its passage through i began from a carrier c (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters(c, i)) that it occupied at its entry into i (the observation at which rel.occupies(subject, i) rose); a traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) governs c (dev.governs(d, c)); and at some observation from that entry to the exit, d displayed green_arrow(dir) and no other state, for some dir among left, right and u_turn.
NRS_484B_307_4a_o1.obligation: Re-binding i, c, d and dir with the whole selection of the applicability: the passage through i matches the arrow's direction at this exit: for dir left, drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(subject, i; p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, p.turn_heading_min, p.u_turn_heading_min) holds; for dir right, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(subject, i; p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, p.turn_heading_min, p.u_turn_heading_min) holds; for dir u_turn, drv.motion.u_turn_through_region(subject, i; p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, p.u_turn_heading_min) holds. Where arrows of several directions were displayed alone during the passage, matching any one of them complies.

narrowings.why: 'so long as the arrow is illuminated' is read as the arrow displayed alone at some observation of the subject's passage through the intersection, from its entry to its exit; a passage begun and ended while no such arrow is displayed is not judged. The direction is read on the whole passage, recognized at the exit.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle enters an intersection from an approach lane whose dev.traffic_signal displays green_arrow(left) alone and drives straight through: at its exit drv.motion.left_turn_through_region does not hold (heading change about 0 degrees). No other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same subject turns left through the intersection on the green left arrow alone: at its exit the heading change since its entry is about 90 degrees to the left.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing the subject's approach displays circular_green alone throughout its passage; the subject drives straight through.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes through the intersection on a green left arrow alone, but its yaw rate is not observed: the turn concepts cannot be decided at its exit.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1
scenarios.narrative: The signal displays green_arrow(left) alone when the subject enters the intersection and changes to yellow_arrow(left) while the subject is inside; the subject drives straight through: the arrow was displayed alone for part of the passage only.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1_outside
scenarios.narrative: The signal displays green_arrow(left) alone only before the subject enters the intersection and circular_red from its entry to its exit; the subject drives straight through: the arrow held only before the passage began.

onset.words: the subject's entry into the intersection: the observation at which its footprint came to overlap the intersection, having not overlapped it at the previous observation
onset.justification: The turn-through-region concepts state 'The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r'; the region is the intersection (st.intersection) the subject passes.

occasion.recognition: the observation at which the subject's footprint does not overlap the intersection, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit, at which the turn concepts are recognized

under_way.words: an observation from the subject's entry into the intersection up to its exit, at which its heading change since the entry is being integrated from its yaw rate
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act is one since the subject's entry into the intersection (rel.occupies rose) and before its exit, over which the concepts integrate the subject's motion, its heading change from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading'); before the entry no heading change of the passage is accumulated.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: intersection turn geometry: a lane change alters heading by a few degrees, a turn at a junction by about 90 degrees

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: intersection turn geometry: a left turn alters heading by about 90 degrees, a reversal by about 180 degrees

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red signal alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
may not proceed on or through any private or public property to enter the intersecting
street
where traffic is not facing a red signal
to avoid the red signal.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head; state in {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady red signal alone is the head displaying circular_red and no other state (no arrow, no flashing state). Same atom as the index maps these words to (NRS_484B_307_8d). It is a device, not a sign or a road feature, so no exclusion applies.

Reuses the index mapping of 'Vehicular traffic facing the signal' (NRS_484B_307_2a). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances'); 'vehicular' limits it to its vehicle members, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'). Facing the signal: the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a carrier c that runs into intersection i at its entrance end (st.lane_enters; c of kind st.travel_region, i of kind st.intersection), and the head governs c or i (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'); governance is control, not a position, as its exclusion requires.

st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; private or public property is ground no highway region covers, so proceeding on or through it is the subject's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) no st.highway region; the 'not a stand-in for the roadway' clause is respected, the test being against the whole way, so a sidewalk or shoulder is not property. The intersecting way is a highway h2 on which intersection i lies (st.on_way: 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there') and on which the approach carrier c does not lie; entering it is the subject's footprint coming to overlap h2 outside i, having overlapped no highway region at the previous observation.

The intersecting street's traffic not facing a red signal is read on that street's approaches into the same intersection: a traffic signal head that governs (dev.governs) a carrier k lying on h2 (st.on_way) and entering i (st.lane_enters; k of kind st.travel_region) displays a state other than circular_red (dev.traffic_signal). The words speak of the signal the street's traffic faces, so the condition reads the device and holds whether or not a road user is on h2.

The purpose 'to avoid the red signal' is read through the conduct it explains: having faced the red on c, the subject reaches h2 without having occupied i (rel.occupies, st.intersection) and without having stood on the property: drv.motion.parked is 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not', at rest throughout a window of min_duration; a road user that parks on the property is there for the property, not passing through it around the signal.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies within the territorial limits of an incorporated city, as the map's reading classifies the area

NRS_484B_307_8e.applicability: The subject is vehicular traffic (ru.aggregate traffic and ru.aggregate vehicle). There are an intersection i, a carrier c of kind st.travel_region that enters i (st.lane_enters c i), and a highway h2 on which i lies (st.on_way i h2) and on which c does not lie, such that: (a) at some observation up to the judged one, the subject occupied c while a traffic signal head governing c or i (dev.governs) displayed circular_red and no other state (steady red alone); (b) at the judged observation a traffic signal head governing some carrier k that lies on h2 and enters i displays a state other than circular_red (the intersecting street's traffic does not face a red signal); (c) the place lies within an incorporated city (asm.within_incorporated_city: the intersecting way is a street); (d) since the latest observation at which (a) held, the subject has at no observation occupied i and has at no observation been parked (drv.motion.parked with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.parking_min_duration): it is passing around the signal, not using the property (purpose read through conduct).
NRS_484B_307_8e.obligation: Re-binding i, c and h2 by the same selection and relations as the applicability (c enters i, i lies on h2, c does not lie on h2, the subject occupied c while a head governing c or i displayed circular_red alone, and has since neither occupied i nor been parked): it is not the case that at the judged observation the subject occupies h2 and does not occupy i while at the previous observation it occupied no st.highway region (it comes onto the intersecting street from private or public property off every public way).

narrowings.why: 'private or public property' is read as ground outside every highway's boundary lines: the subject's footprint overlaps no st.highway region at the observation before it comes onto the intersecting street. A cut across a sidewalk or shoulder alone, which is part of the highway, is not read as proceeding through property.

The purpose of avoiding the red signal is read through conduct: after facing the steady red on the approach, the subject reaches the intersecting street from off the way without having entered the intersection and without having parked on the property.
'Vehicular traffic' facing the signal is read through the vehicle's controlled motion on the approach, whoever or whatever is at the controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject (vehicle, traffic) occupies approach lane c entering intersection i; the head governing c displays circular_red alone; the head governing the cross street's approach lane k (on h2, entering i) displays circular_green. The subject turns right off c into a corner lot, its footprint overlapping no highway region for several observations while moving (never parked), and then comes to occupy h2 outside i. It never occupied i. The place is within an incorporated city.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene: the subject halts on c while its head displays circular_red alone, waits until circular_green, enters i and turns right onto h2 through i; at no observation does it come onto h2 from off the way.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head governing c displays circular_green throughout; the subject passes through i. It never occupied c facing a steady red alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the state of the head governing c is never observed (dev.traffic_signal absent); the subject cuts through the corner lot onto h2.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the subject parks in the corner lot (at rest for longer than the parking duration) before leaving onto h2; while it waited on c facing the red it complied, and after parking the cut-through condition no longer holds.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but every head governing an approach of h2 into i displays circular_red throughout (an all-red interval): the intersecting street's traffic faces red.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of automotive perception and simulator scene-graph sources

param_proposals.name: p.parking_min_duration
param_proposals.convention: the longest halt counted as temporary, as for loading or unloading: a common time limit of a passenger loading zone
param_proposals.source: municipal passenger loading zone time limits

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red signal alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal

must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection,
and,
except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (c) and (d) [(c) is appended below, NRS-484B-307-8d],
must remain stopped or standing until the green signal is shown.
After complying with the requirement to stop,
vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme right of the highway
may proceed into the intersection
for a right turn
only when the intersecting highway is two-directional or one-way to the right,
or vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme left of a one-way highway
may proceed into the intersection
for a left turn
only when the intersecting highway is one-way to the left,
but must yield
the right-of-way
to pedestrians and other traffic proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady red signal alone is circular_red and no other state (not flashing_red, and no arrow beside it). Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not the place of the halt, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'must stop': a stop required, DEF-NRS-484A-255, '"Stop," when required, means complete cessation from movement': drv.motion.complete_halt. 'before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection': the crosswalk (st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') recorded as marking the entrance of the subject's carrier c (st.entrance_of, 'the line or crossing a vehicle approaching through that carrier halts at or before'); 'where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made': the stop line (st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') recorded as marking c's entrance; 'or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection': c's entrance end at intersection i (st.intersection). 'before entering': the footprint does not yet overlap the region (rel.occupies); the side is read by the sign of prim.region_offset_along along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction), the distance to the place by st.region_geometry ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'). Not a stand-in: st.region_geometry is not occupancy, and prim.region_offset_along is read for the side only, never as the distance. Same mapping as the index for the stop words of NRS_484A_450_2 and NRS_484A_450_3.

NRS_484B_307_8a_o1.applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, enters intersection i at the judged observation: its footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies) there and did not at the previous observation, at which it occupied a travel region c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs); and s displays at the judged observation a steady red alone (circular_red and no other state).
NRS_484B_307_8a_o1.obligation: Rule 4c duty: an act at a place before an event. Event: the entry into i just described; each such entry is its own occurrence. Place: the stop line recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of) where one is; else the crosswalk recorded as marking c's entrance; else c's entrance end at the edge of i. Where a mark's association with c is not observed, whether it governs is unknown; where its list of entrances is observed and excludes c, it does not govern and the next place in that order is read. Act: a complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance) at an observation at which the subject occupies c, its footprint overlaps neither i nor the crosswalk marking c's entrance and it is not past the stop line where one is the place, it lies on the upstream side of the place along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction; the sign of prim.region_offset_along shows the place ahead, or zero on the line), and its body is within p.stop_point_tolerance of the place (st.region_geometry distance). History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start, the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on c, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream (off the place, short of it, and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance), or at the subject's previous entry into i from c, whichever is later; nothing else ends it: not the start of the recording, not the subject's first observation, not another intersection or mark, not a distance travelled. Only an observed exit from the zone upstream begins a new approach; a creep, a lateral move or a change of lane within the zone keeps a halt already made. A halt found: complied. Either end reached without a halt: violated. Neither end reached and no halt found (the recording begins with the subject inside the zone): unknown. Whether the entry occurred is unknown where the observation before does not show the subject on a mapped carrier whose association with the place is observed, or where there is no observation before.

narrowings.why: The place 'where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made' is read as the stop line the source records as marking the approach's entrance: a sign standing without a line indicates a place the ontology does not record (no regulatory sign code marks a stopping point), so where only such a sign indicates the place the duty is read at the crosswalk or the intersection's edge. The places are read in the order stop line, crosswalk, edge of the intersection, a halt before the first that marks the approach meeting the words for all of them.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies lane c, recorded as entering i and governed by head s displaying circular_red alone; a stop line marks c's entrance. The car passes the line at 12 m/s, its speed never at or below the halt tolerance, and its footprint comes to overlap i while s still displays circular_red alone; the search from the entry reaches the approach start (the car 40 m short of the line) without a halt.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same approach; the car halts with its body 1 m short of the stop line, footprint off the line and the crosswalk, waits, and then enters i for a right turn while s still displays circular_red alone: the halt lies within the approach.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car enters i while s displays circular_green alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source supplies no speed for the car at any observation of the approach: whether it halted is unknown.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the car already on c with its body 1.5 m short of the stop line, moving at 1 m/s; it enters i under circular_red alone without halting in the recording. The approach start and any earlier entry lie before the recording, so neither end of the search is reached.
scenarios.boundary: the car's approach on c before it came within the stop-point tolerance of the stop line

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No stop line or crosswalk marks c's entrance (every line's and crosswalk's list of entrances is observed and excludes c); the car halts with its body 1 m short of the edge of i and then enters i under circular_red alone: the place is the intersection's edge.

param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin

segmentation.text: A person,
except when stopping, standing or parking where no parking is permitted,
shall not start a vehicle which is stopped, standing or parked on a highway
nor enter upon a highway
unless and until such movement can be made with safety.

elements.justification: 'A person' who starts a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading), so the binder is the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same mapping as the index row 'A person'.

'stopping, standing or parking' (DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'; DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle'; DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle') together denote every halt, drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'), read at the observation before the start. 'where no parking is permitted' is a place a no-parking restriction marks: an st.curb_zone of kind no_parking, no_stopping or fire_lane or a curb painted red, which the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), or an st.travel_region it occupies that a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking, no_standing or no_stopping governs (dev.governs) with its conditions holding (prim.conditions_hold). The sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre (its not-a-stand-in clause does not apply); the posted or painted feature is the evidence of the restriction (status reading).

'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate. 'stopped, standing or parked' is every halt (the three definitions' union: DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily', DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle', DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle'; their exclusions -- conflict or device halts, passenger and loading halts -- intersect only on purposes no conduct shows), drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'start' is the observation at which complete_halt ceases to hold, having held at the previous one. 'on a highway' is rel.occupies of an st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines', matching DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines'), at the previous observation.

operationalizations.standard: such movement can be made with safety
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a movement is made with safety where, at its onset, no other road user's centre is predicted under constant velocities to come within the conflict centre clearance of the subject's centre within the time-to-collision horizon

NRS_484B_410_o1.applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation at which the subject starts: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) held at the previous observation while the subject occupied an st.highway region, and does not hold at this observation; and the exception does not hold: at the previous observation the subject did not occupy a place where no parking is permitted -- an st.curb_zone of kind no_parking, no_stopping or fire_lane, or one whose curb colour is red, or an st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking, no_standing or no_stopping whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold).
NRS_484B_410_o1.obligation: At that observation no other road user of the scene, of any class (same excludes the subject), satisfies prim.closest_approach_within(subject, other; p.conflict_horizon) with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, other; p.conflict_horizon) at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Where one does, violated.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who starts a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle, whoever or whatever controls it.

'where no parking is permitted' is read by the posted no-parking, no-standing or no-stopping sign whose conditions hold, or the marked or red-painted curb zone, the feature's presence being the evidence of the restriction.

'with safety' is read only as the absence, at the onset of the movement, of a predicted near-collision with another road user; 'unless and until' is read at the start observation, the start being withheld until then.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject car stands at the curb on a highway for 20 s, outside any no-parking zone, then starts (speed rises above the tolerance) while another car 12 m behind it in the same lane closes at 12 m/s, so their centres are predicted to meet within the horizon.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject car stands at the curb on a highway and starts; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives along the highway at 12 m/s throughout and never halts.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car stands at the curb and then moves off, but kin.speed is not observed on this source, so whether it was halted and started cannot be decided.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car halted in a curb zone of kind no_parking painted red starts while another car 12 m behind closes at 12 m/s: the exception holds.

param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracking sources

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique (Hyden; time-to-collision thresholds of 1.5 to 3 s)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car design dimensions (AASHTO design vehicle P)

segmentation.text: A person,
except when stopping, standing or parking where no parking is permitted,
shall not start a vehicle which is stopped, standing or parked on a highway
nor enter upon a highway
unless and until such movement can be made with safety.

elements.justification: 'A person' who enters upon a highway with a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the binder is the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same mapping as the index row 'A person'.

'stopping, standing or parking' (DEF-NRS-484A-260 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'; DEF-NRS-484A-250 'the halting of a vehicle'; DEF-NRS-484A-155 'the standing of a vehicle') together denote every halt, drv.motion.complete_halt, read at the observation before the entry. 'where no parking is permitted': an st.curb_zone of kind no_parking, no_stopping or fire_lane or a curb painted red that the footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), or an st.travel_region it occupies governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking, no_standing or no_stopping whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold); the posted or painted feature is the evidence (status reading).

'enter upon a highway' is the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') an st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines', DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way'), having overlapped no highway region at the previous observation. st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway: the words name the highway.

operationalizations.standard: such movement can be made with safety
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a movement is made with safety where, at its onset, no other road user's centre is predicted under constant velocities to come within the conflict centre clearance of the subject's centre within the time-to-collision horizon

NRS_484B_410_o2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation at which the subject enters upon a highway: it occupies an st.highway region here and occupied none at the previous observation; and the exception does not hold: at the previous observation the subject was not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) in a place where no parking is permitted -- an st.curb_zone of kind no_parking, no_stopping or fire_lane or whose curb colour is red, or an st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_parking, no_standing or no_stopping whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold).
NRS_484B_410_o2.obligation: At that observation no other road user of the scene, of any class (same excludes the subject), satisfies prim.closest_approach_within(subject, other; p.conflict_horizon) with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, other; p.conflict_horizon) at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Where one does, violated.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who enters upon a highway is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle, whoever or whatever controls it.

'where no parking is permitted' is read by the posted no-parking, no-standing or no-stopping sign whose conditions hold, or the marked or red-painted curb zone, the feature's presence being the evidence of the restriction.

'with safety' is read only as the absence, at the entry, of a predicted near-collision with another road user; 'unless and until' is read at the entry observation, the entry being withheld until then.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject car leaves a private parking lot and its footprint first overlaps the highway region while a car on the highway 10 m away closes on it at 13 m/s, so their centres are predicted to meet within the horizon.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject car leaves a private parking lot onto the highway; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car is on the highway at every observation of the trace and never enters it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves from a parking lot toward the highway, but rel.occupies is not observed on this source, so the entry cannot be decided.
