segmentation.text: Whenever an illuminated flashing red or yellow signal is used in conjunction with an official traffic-control device,
it shall require obedience by vehicular traffic as follows:
When a red lens is illuminated with rapid intermittent flashes,
drivers of vehicles
shall stop before entering the nearest crosswalk in an intersection or at a limit line when marked, or, if none, then before entering the intersection,
and the right to proceed shall be subject to the rules applicable after making a required stop.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal carries the states flashing_red and flashing_yellow of 'a signal head'; an illuminated flashing signal used as an official device is such a head present in the scene; its official status is read from its presence.

'Vehicular traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic limited to its vehicle members, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, as the index maps 'Such vehicular traffic' (NRS_484B_307_5a_o2).

A red lens with rapid intermittent flashes is dev.traffic_signal state flashing_red. It applies to the subject where the head governs (dev.governs) the carrier c (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies) and enters intersection i through (st.lane_enters), or governs i itself.
Reuses the index mapping of 'drivers of vehicles,' (NRS_484B_307_12a): the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; the driver role is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Reuses the index mapping of the parallel stop-before words (NRS_484B_307_8a_o1, NRS_484A_450_2). A stop is drv.motion.complete_halt ('complete cessation from movement', DEF-NRS-484A-255). The limit line is st.stop_line ('the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device'); the nearest crosswalk in the intersection is the st.crosswalk recorded as marking the subject's carrier's entrance (st.entrance_of, 'exactly that carrier's entrance'; the carrier enters i, st.lane_enters). The side of a mark is read along the carrier's direction (st.lane_direction, prim.region_offset_along); the distance through st.region_geometry; a halt overlapping the mark or i (rel.occupies) is not before entering it.

residues.why: The words subject the right to proceed after the stop to 'the rules applicable after making a required stop' without naming any rule of the corpus; this node judges the stop, and the proceeding is judged by those rules on their own terms.

NRS_484B_310_1.applicability: The subject is vehicular traffic (ru.aggregate traffic and vehicle). Judged at the observation at which the subject enters an intersection i (its footprint comes to overlap i, not having overlapped it at the previous observation) from a carrier c entering i (st.lane_enters) that it occupied at the previous observation, while a traffic signal head governing c or i (dev.governs) displays flashing_red at that entry observation.
NRS_484B_310_1.obligation: Act before an event (the ontology's approach convention). Event: the subject's entry into i through c. Place: where a stop line or a crosswalk is recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of), a halt (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) with the subject's body within p.stop_point_tolerance of such a mark (st.region_geometry), short of it along c's designated direction (sign of prim.region_offset_along along st.lane_direction) and not overlapping it nor i (rel.occupies); the crosswalk and the limit line are alternatives, and a halt at either discharges; where the marks' entrance lists are observed and neither a crosswalk nor a stop line marks c, a halt within p.stop_point_tolerance of i's edge at c's entrance end, not overlapping i. History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends only at the approach start (the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the mark marks, is outside the mark's stopping zone upstream: off it, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance; for several marks, outside the zone of each and short of each) or at the subject's previous entry into i; never at the recording's start or a distance travelled. A halt found discharges; either end reached without one violates; reaching neither is unknown. The entry is unknown where the observation before it is missing or does not place the subject on a mapped carrier; where a mark's association with c is unobserved, whether it governs is unknown, and the verdict is unknown only where it depends on it.

narrowings.why: 'before entering the nearest crosswalk ... or at a limit line when marked' is read as two alternative places, each marking the subject's approach carrier: a halt within the stop-point tolerance short of either discharges; 'if none' is read where the source's complete entrance lists show neither marks the carrier.
The official status of the flashing signal is read through the head's presence in the scene.
'drivers' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at the controls.

The record states the approach start that ends the search back only for marks; for the 'if none' alternative it is read the same way against the intersection's edge: the subject on a carrier entering the intersection, not overlapping it, short of it along the approach carrier's direction and farther from it than the stop-point tolerance.

scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the car halts with its body within the tolerance short of the stop line, not overlapping it, then enters i.

segmentation.text: A driver
shall not stop
or suddenly decrease the speed
of a vehicle
without first giving an appropriate signal
to the driver of any vehicle immediately to the rear.

elements.justification: 'A driver' is the relational role of DEF-NRS-484A-080, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the binder is the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same mapping as the index row 'a driver'.

'stop' is here a stopping the clause prohibits, so DEF-NRS-484A-260 applies ('when prohibited, any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle'): the onset of drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'), the observation at which it holds and did not at the previous one. The definition's exclusion, which the concept does not make, is carried beside it: 'except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' -- a road user ahead in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') within p.queue_halt_gap of body gap (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies'); 'or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' -- the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.stop_sign, a dev.yield_sign, a dev.traffic_signal showing a red indication, a dev.railway_signal_or_gate flashing or with gate lowering or down, or a dev.human_direction of role police_officer indicating stop. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position; it reads which device controls the region occupied.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the subject's class.

The signal of a stop or a decrease of speed is the brake lamp ('brake lamps lit') or the arm signal (sig.hand_signal, 'meaning ... stop_or_slow'). sig.brake_lamp is not a stand-in for a halt or a deceleration, and is not used as one: the halt and the deceleration are read from kinematics, the lamp only as the signal other road users see. 'first' is read as shown at the onset of the halt or the deceleration or at some observation of the window of length p.stop_signal_lead_window behind it.

'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, read on the other road user; 'immediately to the rear' is that road user behind the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction') with the gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.rear_signal_reach. rel.surface_gap is not a stand-in for an order of arrival; the order is read from rel.ahead_behind_in_lane. 'the driver of' is read through that vehicle (agency); no perception by that driver is read.

operationalizations.standard: suddenly
operationalizations.convention: a decrease of speed is sudden where the longitudinal deceleration exceeds the comfortable deceleration most drivers use when braking for an expected stop

NRS_484B_413_3.applicability: The subject is a vehicle. Engaged at an observation E at which either (a) drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) holds and did not hold at the previous observation, and that halt is not excused under DEF-NRS-484A-260: no road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with rel.surface_gap at most p.queue_halt_gap, and the subject occupies no st.travel_region governed (dev.governs) by a dev.stop_sign, a dev.yield_sign, a dev.traffic_signal showing circular_red, red_arrow or flashing_red, a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down, or a dev.human_direction of role police_officer indicating stop; or (b) the subject's kin.accel_longitudinal is at or below minus p.sudden_decel_min and was not at the previous observation; and at E some other road user of the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle is behind the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with rel.surface_gap at most p.rear_signal_reach.
NRS_484B_413_3.obligation: At E, or at some observation of the time window of length p.stop_signal_lead_window behind E, the subject showed sig.brake_lamp lit or a sig.hand_signal meaning stop_or_slow. Otherwise violated.

narrowings.why: 'A driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle, whoever or whatever controls it.
'an appropriate signal' is read as the brake lamps lit or the stop-or-slow arm signal; 'first' as shown at the onset or within the lead window behind it.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a flashing yellow turn arrow, displayed alone or in combination with another signal:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
is permitted to cautiously
enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by the arrow signal,
or other such movement as is permitted by other signal indications displayed at the same time.
Such vehicular traffic
must yield
the right-of-way
to pedestrians lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk
and yield
the right-of-way
to other traffic lawfully within the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., flashing_yellow_arrow(dir), ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once': a flashing yellow turn arrow is flashing_yellow_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn; 'displayed alone or in combination with another signal': whatever other states the head displays with it.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'enter the intersection': the passage through intersection i (st.intersection) from the entry (rel.occupies rising) to the exit. 'only to make the movement indicated by the arrow signal': the movement made, recognized at the exit, is a left turn (drv.motion.left_turn_through_region, 'a turn to the left through region r'), a right turn (drv.motion.right_turn_through_region), a reversal (drv.motion.u_turn_through_region, 'turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction through region r'), or straight through where none of them holds; it must be the movement the flashing yellow arrow's direction (dev.traffic_signal) indicates: a left arrow the turn to the left and the U-turn, a right arrow the right turn, a u_turn arrow the U-turn. As the index maps the arrow movements of NRS_484B_307_4a_o1.

'other signal indications displayed at the same time': the other states dev.traffic_signal displays ('several states may be displayed at once') at the same observation as the flashing yellow turn arrow. A movement they permit: circular_green, circular_yellow or flashing_yellow permit every movement; a green, yellow or flashing yellow arrow permits the movement of its direction (left: the left turn and the U-turn; right: the right turn; u_turn: the U-turn; straight: the straight movement).

operationalizations.standard: cautiously (the manner of the permitted entry)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: an entry is cautious where, at the observation of the entry, while the subject's speed is above the halt tolerance, no other road user's centre has a closest approach to the subject's centre, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance)

NRS_484B_307_7a_o1.applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, has entered intersection i from a travel region c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs): at the act's onset its footprint came to overlap i, having occupied c and not i at the observation before. At some observation of the passage, from that entry to the judged observation, s displayed a flashing yellow turn arrow (flashing_yellow_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn), alone or with other states. The rule is judged at the passage's recognition: the observation at which the subject's footprint does not overlap i, having overlapped it at the previous observation. The duty does not apply where, at such an observation of the passage at which s displayed the flashing yellow turn arrow, another state s displayed at the same observation permits the movement made (exception s5).
NRS_484B_307_7a_o1.obligation: At the recognition the movement made through i — a left turn, a right turn or a U-turn where drv.motion.left_turn_through_region, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region or drv.motion.u_turn_through_region holds for the subject and i (step = p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min = p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min = p.u_turn_heading_min), straight through where none holds — is the movement indicated by a flashing yellow turn arrow s displayed at an observation of the passage (left: the left turn or the U-turn; right: the right turn; u_turn: the U-turn); and the entry was cautious: at the entry observation, while the subject's speed was above p.halt_speed_tolerance, no other road user's closest approach to it (prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_horizon) was at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The movement is read from the passage through the intersection, recognized at the exit: a left turn, a right turn or a reversal by the turn concepts, straight through where none holds (a heading change below p.turn_heading_min). A left arrow is read as indicating the U-turn as well as the left turn, a U-turn being a turn to the left carried on.
'cautiously' names no factor; it is read only through the absence of a traffic conflict with any road user at the observation of entry, the time the words fix it to ('cautiously enter').

onset.words: the subject's entry into the intersection from its approach
onset.justification: The through-region acts begin, as their contracts state, 'at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r'.

occasion.recognition: the observation at which the subject's footprint does not overlap the intersection, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit, where the through-region acts are recognized and a straight passage is one none of them recognizes

under_way.justification: An observation inside the act is one from the entry on at which the subject still overlaps i and its heading change since the entry, integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading'), is being accumulated; before the entry the integration has not begun.

segmentation.text: A person
shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict
with other traffic
or in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer
or official traffic-control device,
in any of the following places:
Within 30 feet upon the approach to any official traffic-control signal
located at the side of a highway.

elements.justification: The words name the person who stops, stands or parks "a vehicle". Who controls a vehicle is not observable; the ontology reads the one who drives through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the road user judged is the vehicle (agency reading, disclosed). ru.aggregate is "membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id"; the admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle counts "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", its exceptions classified by the run's reading. Not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom (the words name none), nor for the relational role of who controls the vehicle: the atom states the class of the road user whose halts are judged.

"stop" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-260); "stand" is "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" other than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250); "park" is "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-155). Each is a halting, so forbidding all three forbids every halt of the vehicle at the place, however brief. drv.motion.complete_halt denotes that "The road user is at rest at the observation", observed as kin.speed at or below a tolerance, at each observation; what it does not denote ("a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance") is no halting. "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway").

"traffic" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"); "other" leaves out the subject itself. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ("a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction") places that traffic in the subject's path, and rel.surface_gap ("distance between the nearest points of two bodies") is the clearance to it that the operationalization of "necessary" bounds. Neither contract carries a not-a-stand-in clause this use touches; no centre distance and no order of arrival is read.

"in compliance with law" excuses a halt the law itself requires of the vehicle where it is. segmentation.text: A person

except when necessary to avoid conflict
with other traffic

or the directions of a police officer
or official traffic-control device,

Between a safety zone and the adjacent curb

"in compliance with law" excuses a halt the law itself requires of the vehicle where it is. A safety zone is "the area officially set aside within a highway for the exclusive use of pedestrians and which is so plainly marked or indicated by proper signs as to be plainly visible" (DEF-NRS-484B-057); st.safety_zone is "an area within the highway marked off for pedestrians only"; its official setting-aside and its marking are status, read from the zone's presence. The curb is st.road_edge ("curb or edge of the roadway"). The adjacent curb is the roadway edge nearest the zone, found from both regions' signed lateral offsets from the vehicle (prim.region_lateral_offset: "the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user"): the difference between that edge's offset and the zone's is no greater in magnitude than any other roadway edge's. scenarios.name: branch_2

segmentation.text: When a vehicle
enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered,
but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle

shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver shall proceed cautiously,
yielding
to vehicles which have previously completed a stop
or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'.

The entry is the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap X (rel.occupies, st.intersection), having occupied at the previous observation a carrier c that enters X (st.lane_enters: 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'); st.travel_region is c's kind.

dev.traffic_signal: 'a signal head; ... uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered'; 'controlled by' is dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection') on c or X.
dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the subject's entry observation, 'at the time the vehicle enters'.
'The driver of the vehicle' is the vehicle's controlled motion, read through the vehicle of the admitted aggregate.

'yielding' maps as in the index: the subject does not proceed in preference to the other vehicle — its kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') stays at or below the halt tolerance while the other is in conflict — and does not collide with it (rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'). kin.speed is not a stand-in for acceleration; contact is not a near miss, which the standard bounds.

'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate. 'Previously completed a stop' is another vehicle v's complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement') while occupying its own approach carrier c2 of X (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters) before entering X, its halt beginning before the subject's own halt on c: the order of stops at an intersection where every entrance is treated as stop-controlled.
'are within the intersection': v's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet').

operationalizations.standard: proceed cautiously: proceed without creating a danger of a crash with the vehicles the words name
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the subject proceeds (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while, under constant velocities, its centre and the other vehicle's approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance — a present danger of a crash

NRS_484B_250_4_o2.applicability: At every observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection X and has overlapped it continuously since its latest entry into X (the observation at which it came to overlap X, having occupied at the observation before a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, X)), where at that entry observation a traffic signal governing c or X (dev.governs) was inoperative (dev.inoperative), and where NRS_484B_250_4_o1 (binder subject ↦ subject) was complied with at that entry observation: 'After making such a stop' — the stop that rule searches for, read at the entry by a past operator.
NRS_484B_250_4_o2.obligation: Re-binding X and c as in the applicability: for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that either (a) occupies X, or (b) occupies a carrier c2 entering X (st.lane_enters c2 X), on which, without overlapping X, it came to a complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance) whose onset lies earlier than the onset of the subject's last halt on c before its entry (or the subject made none), having occupied c2 or X at every observation since: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'cautiously' is read only through the yielding the words join to it: proceeding without a present danger of a crash with the vehicles named; no further speed bound is read.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject halted at the stop line of c (inoperative dev.traffic_signal governing c) and entered X; vehicle v occupies X crossing from the subject's right; the subject moves on with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance and its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject stays at rest just inside X until v has cleared, then proceeds with no closest approach to v below p.conflict_centre_clearance within p.conflict_horizon.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing c showed circular_green at the subject's entry: not inoperative.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: After its stop the subject is in X with v crossing on a conflicting path; kin.speed is absent, so whether the subject proceeds into the conflict is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: After its stop the subject crosses X with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Vehicle v halted on its own approach after the subject's halt and still waits there; the subject crosses X and its closest approach to v is predicted below p.conflict_centre_clearance: v is not a vehicle that previously completed a stop and is not within X.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The subject entered X without halting at the stop line (NRS_484B_250_4_o1 violated at its entry), then crosses X in conflict with v: the yielding duty follows 'such a stop', which was not made; the omitted stop is judged by NRS_484B_250_4_o1.

segmentation.text: A person
shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict
with other traffic
or in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer
or official traffic-control device,
in any of the following places:
Within 20 feet of a driveway entrance to any fire station
and, on the side of a highway opposite the entrance to any fire station,
within 75 feet of that entrance.

elements.justification: The words name the person who stops, stands or parks "a vehicle". Who controls a vehicle is not observable; the ontology reads the one who drives through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the road user judged is the vehicle (agency reading, disclosed). ru.aggregate is "membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id"; the admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle counts "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", its exceptions classified by the run's reading. Not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom (the words name none), nor for the relational role of who controls the vehicle: the atom states the class of the road user whose halts are judged.

"stop" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-260); "stand" is "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" other than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250); "park" is "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-155). Each is a halting, so forbidding all three forbids every halt of the vehicle at the place, however brief. drv.motion.complete_halt denotes that "The road user is at rest at the observation", observed as kin.speed at or below a tolerance, at each observation; what it does not denote ("a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance") is no halting. "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway").

"traffic" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"); "other" leaves out the subject itself. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ("a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction") places that traffic in the subject's path, and rel.surface_gap ("distance between the nearest points of two bodies") is the clearance to it that the operationalization of "necessary" bounds. Neither contract carries a not-a-stand-in clause this use touches; no centre distance and no order of arrival is read.

"in compliance with law" excuses a halt the law itself requires of the vehicle where it is. Observably those are the halt a stop sign requires (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt") and the halt a traffic signal requires while it shows a red indication (dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head" with states circular_red, red_arrow(dir) and flashing_red), each on the traffic of a travel region the device governs (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") that the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"; st.travel_region is the kind that relation ranges over here). dev.governs is "Not a stand-in for: a position — the region a device governs is not where a halt is required": the governed region is not read as the place of a required halt; it reads only that a vehicle within the governed approach, while the device commands a halt, is held there in obedience to it.

dev.human_direction is "a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}". A police officer ("every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic", DEF-NRS-484A-180) is the role police_officer, and the direction a halt complies with is the indication stop, given to the travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region the kind). dev.governs is not read as the place a halt is required, only as the traffic the direction is given to. A flagger or a crossing guard is another role and is not read.

An official traffic-control device is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The devices whose directions a halt obeys are a stop sign (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign: "regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt", whose yield may require a halt), a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), and a level-crossing signal with its lights flashing or its gate lowering or down (dev.railway_signal_or_gate: "lights ∈ {flashing, dark}; gate ∈ {up, lowering, down, raising, none}"), each governing the travel region the vehicle occupies (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region). "official" is the device's legal status, read from its presence. dev.governs is not read as the position of a required halt, only as the traffic the device directs; no sign is read as a manoeuvre.

A driveway is "every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel by the owner and those having express or implied permission from the owner" (DEF-NRS-484A-190); st.fire_station_entrance is "the driveway entrance of a fire station", the very feature the words name. Ownership and permission are the way's legal status, which no feature on the road displays; the entrance's presence is read as that status. "Within 20 feet" is the ground distance from the vehicle's body to the entrance region (st.region_geometry: "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)") at most the literal 20 feet. st.region_geometry is "Not a stand-in for: occupancy" and no overlap is read from it.

The vehicle is on the side of the highway opposite the entrance where it stands beyond the middle of the way from the entrance: its footprint overlaps a highway (rel.occupies; st.highway: "the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders", as DEF-NRS-484A-095's "entire width between the boundary lines"), and among the roadway edges lying on that highway (st.road_edge: "curb or edge of the roadway"; st.on_way: "the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on") some edge lies between the vehicle and the fire station entrance (st.fire_station_entrance), in the vehicle's frame on the entrance's side and no farther than it (prim.region_lateral_offset: "the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user"), that is farther from the vehicle than every edge of that highway on the vehicle's other side: the vehicle is nearer the far side of the way than the near side. The test holds on a two-way, one-way or divided way alike, since it reads only the way's edges. st.on_way is "Not a stand-in for: nearness to a way" and is read only as the edge lying on the way; st.highway is not read as the roadway. "the entrance" is the same region the next span measures to.

"that entrance" is the fire station entrance (st.fire_station_entrance) the previous span singles out; the vehicle is within 75 feet of it where the ground distance from its body to that region (st.region_geometry: "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it") is at most the literal 75 feet. No occupancy is read from the distance.

operationalizations.standard: necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
operationalizations.convention: queue spacing of halted vehicles: a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within that gap between bodies is a halt the traffic ahead makes necessary

NRS_484B_450_1j.applicability: The subject is a road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the observation either the ground distance from its body to some fire station entrance (st.fire_station_entrance; st.region_geometry distance) is at most the literal 20 feet, or there are a fire station entrance f, a highway h whose footprint the subject's overlaps (rel.occupies) and a roadway edge e1 (st.road_edge) lying on h (st.on_way) such that, with lf and l1 the signed lateral offsets of f and e1 from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset), l1 is nonzero, of the sign of lf and of magnitude at most that of lf (e1 between the subject and the entrance), and every roadway edge e2 lying on h whose signed offset l2 is nonzero and of the sign opposite to lf has the magnitude of l2 less than that of l1 (the subject nearer the far side of the way than the near side), and the ground distance from the subject's body to that same f (st.region_geometry) is at most the literal 75 feet.
NRS_484B_450_1j.obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds, the subject is not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), unless at that observation one of the exceptions holds: (a) some road user other than the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; (b) a stop sign, or a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); (c) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs a travel region the subject occupies; (d) a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down governs a travel region the subject occupies. Violated where the subject is at rest there and no exception holds.

narrowings.why: The person who stops the vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the rule judges the vehicle's halts whoever or whatever controls it.

"necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic" is read only as a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within the queue gap; a halt to let crossing or oncoming traffic clear, with nothing ahead in the lane, is not read as necessary, so such a halt is judged without this exception.
"official" is the device's legal status, read from the device's presence in the scene.
The driveway definition's "private ownership" and the owner's permission are the way's legal status; the fire station entrance's presence in the scene is read as the driveway entrance the words name.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject, a ru.aggregate vehicle, is at rest (kin.speed zero) with its body 3 m from a st.fire_station_entrance (st.region_geometry); no other road user, no human direction and no device is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the subject moves past the entrance at kin.speed 8 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: On a two-way highway 12 m wide between its st.road_edge regions, the subject is at rest 2 m from the edge on the entrance's side, with its body 18 m from the entrance.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source maps the regions without their outlines, so every distance and lateral offset to them is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: On the same highway, the subject is at rest 1 m from the road edge on the side away from the entrance (the edge on the entrance's side 10 m from it, between it and the entrance), with its body 18 m from the entrance.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs the subject's lane.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The subject is at rest on the side of the highway away from the entrance, 1 m from the far road edge, with its body 30 m from the entrance.

segmentation.text: A person
shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict
with other traffic
or in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer
or official traffic-control device,

NRS_484B_450_1k.applicability: The subject is a road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the observation there is an obstruction o (st.obstruction, of any kind) lying on a highway h (st.on_way) whose footprint the subject's overlaps (rel.occupies), such that o's signed lateral offset from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset) is nonzero and the ground distance from the subject's body to o (st.region_geometry) is at most the magnitude of that offset (o to the subject's side, beside it or across the way), and a halt there would obstruct traffic: the ground distance from the subject's body to o is less than p.free_passage_width, and no roadway edge e (st.road_edge) whose signed lateral offset from the subject is of the sign opposite to o's lies at a ground distance from the subject's body of at least p.free_passage_width.
NRS_484B_450_1k.obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds, the subject is not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), unless at that observation one of the exceptions holds: (a) some road user other than the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; (b) a stop sign, or a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); (c) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs a travel region the subject occupies; (d) a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down governs a travel region the subject occupies. "official" is the device's legal status, read from the device's presence in the scene.

"would obstruct traffic" is read as the passage traffic needs, whether or not a member of traffic is present (the words state what the halt would do): the free width between the vehicle and the object and between the vehicle and the roadway edge on its other side. A passage beyond the far side of the object, away from the vehicle, is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A st.obstruction of kind excavation lies on the highway in the right lane; the subject, a ru.aggregate vehicle, is at rest (kin.speed zero) in the left lane alongside it, its body 0.3 m from the excavation and 0.5 m from the left st.road_edge; no other road user, no human direction and no device is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the subject moves past the excavation at kin.speed 6 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is at rest beside the excavation with its body 0.3 m from it and 4.5 m of roadway between its body and the road edge on its other side, so the halt leaves a passage.

scenarios.name: blind

segmentation.text: Unless otherwise provided by ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction,
a person
shall not: Stop, stand or park a vehicle
within an alley
in a business district
except for the expeditious loading or unloading of goods.

elements.justification: 'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stops, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. Who controls the vehicle is read through its controlled motion.

'Stop' prohibited takes DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; standing (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155) are halts as well, so the three verbs are read as the halting they all are. Halting is drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or another road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap). complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that.

'alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015: a highway 'Within a city block set apart for public use', 'Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; 'within' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... alley ...)'.

operationalizations.standard: expeditious loading or unloading of goods
operationalizations.convention: Loading or unloading is a purpose, read through the conduct it explains; 'expeditious' bounds how long that conduct may keep the vehicle standing. A halt counts as the expeditious loading or unloading the words except while the vehicle has not been at rest for longer than the temporary-halt bound of a loading zone (p.parking_min_duration): drv.motion.parked, at rest at every observation of that window behind, marks a halt beyond it.

assumptions.meaning: the alley at the place of the road user at the observation is one on which an ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction regulates stopping, standing or parking by provisions of its own, as the map's reading records
the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district, as the map's reading classifies the area

NRS_484B_477_1a.applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) an alley region (st.alley); asm.business_district holds at its place; and asm.local_alley_ordinance does not hold (where it holds the duty does not arise).
NRS_484B_477_1a.obligation: Violated where the subject is parked (drv.motion.parked with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.parking_min_duration: at rest at every observation of the window behind, so beyond an expeditious halt for loading or unloading) and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic: it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no road user is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap. Compliant otherwise.

narrowings.why: The three verbs are read as the halting they all are, with the stopping definition's exception read through the device the subject's region is governed by and a queue ahead within the queue spacing; standing's and parking's own exceptions add no further excuse.
The purpose of the halt is not observed: any halt no longer than the temporary-halt bound is read as the excepted loading or unloading, and a longer one as not excepted, whatever the vehicle does.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection and:
Both intersecting highways are two-directional:
After entering the intersection, the left turn must be made so as to leave the intersection to the right of the centerline of the highway being entered.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for 'vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power ...'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the aggregate carries only the class.

st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges' (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of two highways which join one another'); i is the target region of the declared intention and the region the left turn is made through: the subject's footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') from its entry to its exit. st.intersection is 'not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line': no halt place is read.

'two-directional' uses DEF-NRS-484B-073: 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions'. The intersecting highways are the highways i lies on (st.on_way: 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there'; st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'). 'undivided' is read with DEF-NRS-484A-070 ('divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section'): no st.median_or_divider ('physical barrier or dividing section between roadways') lies on h. 'allowed to proceed in opposite directions' is two carriers lying on h (lanes or roadway directed segments) whose designated directions (st.lane_direction) are opposed, the cosine at or below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos. 'Both' is every highway i lies on. st.on_way is 'not a stand-in for nearness to a way'.

drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(subject, i): 'Road user a has made a turn to the left through region r, recognized as it leaves r. The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies) ... its entry into r. The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r.' 'After entering the intersection, the left turn must be made so as to leave the intersection' is that act, begun at the entry and recognized at the exit. 'to the right of the centerline of the highway being entered': DEF-NRS-484A-040 makes the centerline the line 'to indicate each portion of a highway allocated to traffic proceeding in the two opposite directions', so the subject leaves to its right where, at the exit, it moves against the designated direction of no lane its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies over st.lane): drv.motion.moving_against_carrier(subject, l): 'part of its motion runs opposite to r's designated direction', with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, is false for every such lane l. The lanes the subject overlaps at the exit lie on the highway it enters. moving_against_carrier 'says nothing of whether a occupies r', which rel.occupies supplies.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

NRS_484B_400_2b.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation is the recognition of drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(subject, i; step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min) for an intersection i (st.intersection): the subject's exit from i after its entry, its heading change since the entry in the left-turn band. The act is under way from the entry into i (rel.occupies rising) up to the exit. int.left_turn(subject, i) is declared true at some observation while the act is under way (read behind the judged observation). i is the act's region and its kind is read at the recognition. Every highway h that i lies on (st.on_way i h) is two-directional, read at the recognition: no st.median_or_divider lies on h, and two lanes or roadway segments lying on h carry designated directions whose cosine is at or below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos.
NRS_484B_400_2b.obligation: At the recognition (the exit from i), for every st.lane l the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), drv.motion.moving_against_carrier(subject, l; speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) is false: the subject leaves the intersection in lanes allocated to its own direction, to the right of the centerline of the highway entered. A lane overlapped against its direction violates the duty; an unobserved lane direction or velocity makes it unknown where the verdict turns on it. Where the entry lies before the recording or a yaw rate since the entry is missing, the act is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

'to the right of the centerline of the highway being entered' is read through the lanes the subject overlaps as it leaves the intersection: none may carry a designated direction its motion runs against. A highway entered with no mapped lane is not read here.

onset.justification: drv.motion.left_turn_through_region: 'The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r.' r is the intersection i (st.intersection).

occasion.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r.

under_way.words: the observations from the subject's entry into the intersection up to its exit, at which it is moving through it and turning
under_way.justification: rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region': the subject did not overlap i before its entry, so overlap since the entry, together with the heading change integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading') since that entry, tells an observation inside the turn from one on the approach before it began.

scenarios.narrative: Two two-way undivided highways meet; the subject, with int.left_turn declared at the intersection, enters it, turns left (heading change in the band) and at its exit overlaps the receiving highway's lane whose designated direction its velocity runs against.

scenarios.narrative: Same layout and intention; at its exit the subject overlaps only the receiving lane whose designated direction its velocity runs along.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid, but the receiving highway is one-way (its lanes carry no opposed directions) or divided by a median: the condition fails.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid, but the source declares kin.yaw_rate absent, so the left turn through the intersection is not decided.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes straight through the intersection (heading change below the turn band) and exits into a lane against its direction: no left turn is recognized.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: int.left_turn is declared true at the entry and at the first observations inside the intersection, then false (the source's plan marks the turn completed) before the exit; the subject exits into an opposing lane: the intention held while the turn was under way.

scenarios.name: branch_3

segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are erected prohibiting parking upon a narrow highway,
a person
shall not park a vehicle
upon any such highway.

elements.justification: 'official traffic-control devices' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority') 'prohibiting parking upon a narrow highway' is the signed zone of kind narrow_highway (dev.zone_sign, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {..., narrow_highway, ...}'), whose legend's conditions hold at the observation (prim.conditions_hold; dev.zone_sign is 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold'), governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies). The narrowness of the highway is the posting's designation, read from the sign (status), not a width the rule measures.

'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person parks, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'park' is DEF-NRS-484A-155, 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading of merchandise or passengers', which drv.motion.parked denotes: at rest at every observation of the window behind of length min_duration, a shorter halt being the temporary one the definition leaves out (index: 'No person shall park' maps to drv.motion.parked).

'upon any such highway' is the subject's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a travel region (st.travel_region) of the highway the posting governs: the same region the trigger binds, the device's dev.governs relation fixing it.

NRS_484B_490.applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region r (st.travel_region) that a zone sign (dev.zone_sign) of kind narrow_highway governs (dev.governs), the sign's conditions holding at the observation for the subject (prim.conditions_hold).
NRS_484B_490.obligation: The subject is not parked: violated where drv.motion.parked holds for it (speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration p.parking_min_duration), compliant where it does not.

narrowings.why: Parking, a standing otherwise than temporarily for loading or unloading, is read through the halt's duration: a halt no longer than p.parking_min_duration is read as the temporary one.
The prohibition's legal status and the highway's designation as narrow are read from the posted narrow_highway zone sign.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

segmentation.text: A person
shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict
with other traffic
or in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer
or official traffic-control device,
in any of the following places:
At any place where official traffic-control devices prohibit stopping, standing or parking.

elements.justification: The words name the person who stops, stands or parks "a vehicle". Who controls a vehicle is not observable; the ontology reads the one who drives through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the road user judged is the vehicle (agency reading, disclosed). ru.aggregate is "membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id"; the admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle counts "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", its exceptions classified by the run's reading. Not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom (the words name none), nor for the relational role of who controls the vehicle: the atom states the class of the road user whose halts are judged.

"stop" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-260); "stand" is "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" other than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250); "park" is "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-155). Each is a halting; drv.motion.complete_halt denotes that "The road user is at rest at the observation", observed as kin.speed at or below a tolerance, at each observation; what it does not denote ("a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance") is no halting. Which of the three halts is forbidden at a place is the one the device there prohibits (next span). "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway").

"traffic" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"); "other" leaves out the subject itself. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ("a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction") places that traffic in the subject's path, and rel.surface_gap ("distance between the nearest points of two bodies") is the clearance to it that the operationalization of "necessary" bounds. Neither contract carries a not-a-stand-in clause this use touches; no centre distance and no order of arrival is read.

"in compliance with law" excuses a halt the law itself requires of the vehicle where it is. Observably those are the halt a stop sign requires (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt") and the halt a traffic signal requires while it shows a red indication (dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head" with states circular_red, red_arrow(dir) and flashing_red), each on the traffic of a travel region the device governs (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") that the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"; st.travel_region is the kind that relation ranges over here). dev.governs is "Not a stand-in for: a position — the region a device governs is not where a halt is required": the governed region is not read as the place of a required halt; it reads only that a vehicle within the governed approach, while the device commands a halt, is held there in obedience to it.

dev.human_direction is "a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}". A police officer ("every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic", DEF-NRS-484A-180) is the role police_officer, and the direction a halt complies with is the indication stop, given to the travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region the kind). dev.governs is not read as the place a halt is required, only as the traffic the direction is given to. A flagger or a crossing guard is another role and is not read.

An official traffic-control device is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The devices whose directions a halt obeys are a stop sign (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign: "regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt", whose yield may require a halt), a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), and a level-crossing signal with its lights flashing or its gate lowering or down (dev.railway_signal_or_gate: "lights ∈ {flashing, dark}; gate ∈ {up, lowering, down, raising, none}"), each governing the travel region the vehicle occupies (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region). "official" is the device's legal status, read from its presence. dev.governs is not read as the position of a required halt, only as the traffic the device directs; no sign is read as a manoeuvre.

An official traffic-control device is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The devices that prohibit stopping, standing or parking are the point regulations dev.regulatory_sign of code no_stopping, no_standing or no_parking ("a point regulation by catalogue code"), in effect for the vehicle where their stated conditions hold at the observation (prim.conditions_hold: "the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user"), governing a travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region); and the marked or signed lengths of curb st.curb_zone of kind no_stopping or no_parking ("a signed or marked length of curb") that the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies). Each prohibition reads the halt it names: "stopping" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily" (DEF-NRS-484A-260), drv.motion.complete_halt; "standing" is "the halting of a vehicle" otherwise than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and "parking" "the standing of a vehicle" otherwise than temporarily while loading or unloading (DEF-NRS-484A-155), each read through how long the vehicle has been at rest, drv.motion.parked ("at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration"), with p.standing_min_duration and p.parking_min_duration. dev.regulatory_sign is "Not a stand-in for: a manoeuvre or a road feature — a prohibition sign is a condition": it is read as exactly that condition. dev.governs is read as the traffic the sign regulates, not as a halt position.

operationalizations.standard: necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
operationalizations.convention: queue spacing of halted vehicles: a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within that gap between bodies is a halt the traffic ahead makes necessary

NRS_484B_450_1o.applicability: The subject is a road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the observation either a dev.regulatory_sign of code no_stopping, no_standing or no_parking whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold) governs (dev.governs) a travel region whose footprint the subject's overlaps (rel.occupies), or the subject's footprint overlaps a st.curb_zone of kind no_stopping or no_parking.
NRS_484B_450_1o.obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds, the subject is not engaged in the conduct a device there prohibits: where a no_stopping sign or curb zone applies, the subject is not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance); where a no_standing sign applies, it is not standing (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance and p.standing_min_duration); where a no_parking sign or curb zone applies, it is not parked (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance and p.parking_min_duration); unless at that observation one of the exceptions holds: (a) some road user other than the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; (b) a stop sign, or a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); (c) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs a travel region the subject occupies; (d) a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down governs a travel region the subject occupies. Violated where the subject engages in a prohibited halt there and no exception holds.

narrowings.why: The person who stops the vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the rule judges the vehicle's halts whoever or whatever controls it.

"necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic" is read only as a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within the queue gap; a halt to let crossing or oncoming traffic clear, with nothing ahead in the lane, is not read as necessary, so such a halt is judged without this exception.
"official" is the device's legal status, read from the device's presence in the scene.
"official" said of the prohibiting devices is their legal status, read from the sign's or the marked curb's presence in the scene.

Standing and parking are told from a halt by their purpose (receiving or discharging passengers, temporary loading or unloading), which is not observable; the purpose is read through how long the vehicle has been at rest.

The prohibition is read respectively to the place: where a device prohibits stopping, any halt is forbidden; where it prohibits standing, standing; where it prohibits parking, parking. A brief halt where a device prohibits only parking is not read as forbidden, since the device there permits it.

scenarios.name: forbid

scenarios.name: blind

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in this section [(2) and (3) appended below],
every vehicle
stopped or parked
upon a highway
where there are adjacent curbs
must be stopped or parked with the right-hand wheels of the vehicle parallel to and within 18 inches of the right-hand curb.
Local authorities may by ordinance permit parking
of vehicles with the left-hand wheels adjacent to and within 18 inches of the left-hand curb of a one-way highway.

Local authorities may by ordinance permit angle parking on any highway, except that angle parking must not be permitted on any highway constructed and maintained by the Department of Transportation under the authority granted by chapter 408 of NRS unless the Department has determined that the highway is of sufficient width to permit angle parking without interfering with the free movement of traffic.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the term DEF-NRS-484A-320 defines ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Its exclusion (not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom, or for a role) does not apply: the words name the defined aggregate itself.

'stopped or parked' is a vehicle brought to rest: drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation ... observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance' (a parked vehicle is at rest too, so the halt covers both words). The section regulates the position of a vehicle at rest at the side of the way, so a halt in the stream of traffic is not the stop it speaks of (the stopping definition DEF-NRS-484A-260 itself leaves out a halt 'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'). That halt is read through the conduct it names: the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given'), or it has a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the queue spacing. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: it is read only as the control of the region the subject occupies. complete_halt says nothing of why the vehicle halts; the device and queue atoms carry that.

'highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority') is st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; 'upon' is rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway: the words name the whole way, as the atom does.

A highway 'where there are adjacent curbs' is one along which a curb runs: st.lane_marking gives 'per side of a lane: type ∈ {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}', so a lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on the subject's highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') with a side of type curb shows the curbs. st.road_edge is not used for presence: its contract is 'curb or edge of the roadway' and does not tell a curb from an uncurbed edge. st.lane is not a stand-in for a lateral position here: it is read only for its side marking.

'parallel to ... the right-hand curb' with the right-hand wheels at it is a vehicle whose heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') lies along the designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') of the travel region it occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), within a parallelism tolerance, pointed with that direction (the right-hand curb is the curb on the right of the direction of travel, so its right side faces it only when headed with it). 'the right-hand curb' is a road edge (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway'; the highway's curbs are established by s5) lying on the same highway (st.on_way) on the vehicle's right: prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', below zero. 'within 18 inches' is the ground distance from the body outline to it (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)') at most the stated figure. st.region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy (it is read as a distance only); the lateral offset is read only for the side.

The permitted alternative position: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'a one-way highway' is the subject occupying (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'); 'the left-hand wheels adjacent to ... the left-hand curb' is the heading (kin.heading) along the roadway's designated direction (st.lane_direction) within the same parallelism tolerance, with a road edge (st.road_edge) on the same way (st.on_way) on the vehicle's left (prim.region_lateral_offset above zero); 'within 18 inches' is the body-to-edge ground distance (st.region_geometry) at most the stated figure. 'adjacent' is read as alongside, parallel to the curb, the same position as subsection 1 states for the right.

Angle parking permitted by the local authority shows on the road as an official traffic-control device: dev.regulatory_sign code 'angle_parking' governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), its 'structured conditions' holding (prim.conditions_hold), or a marked bay (st.parking_space, 'marked bay for standing or parking; angle attribute') whose angle stands clear of zero by the source's angle resolution. The presence of the device is the evidence of the permission and of its lawfulness, including the Department's determination for a highway it maintains (status reading): the words that limit where the authority may permit angle parking bind the authority, not the road user. A sign is not a stand-in for a manoeuvre: it is read only as the permission of the place.

assumptions.meaning: the one-way way at the place of the road user at the observation is one on which the local authority having jurisdiction permits vehicles to park with their left-hand wheels at the left-hand curb, as the map's reading records

residues.why: The provisions the words point to are subsections (2) and (3), which are segments s7-s9 of this same text and are carried there as the exceptions of this node; the words add nothing beyond them, so the duty is the same whether or not they are read.

NRS_484B_457_1.applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), is at rest at the observation (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance); it occupies (rel.occupies) a highway region h (st.highway) on which (st.on_way) some lane (st.lane) has a side whose marking type is curb (st.lane_marking); and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic: it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate, or person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no road user of the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap.
NRS_484B_457_1.obligation: At that observation, with h re-bound as in the applicability (a highway the subject occupies on which a lane has a curb-marked side), one of three holds; otherwise the duty is violated. (1) Right-hand curb: the subject occupies a travel region r lying on h whose designated direction d (st.lane_direction) has a dot product with the subject's heading (kin.heading) at or above p.parked_heading_cos, and some road edge region e (st.road_edge) lying on h (st.on_way) is on the subject's right (prim.region_lateral_offset of e below zero) at a ground distance from its body (st.region_geometry) of at most 18 inches (literal). (2) Left-hand curb of a one-way highway, where asm.left_curb_parking_permitted holds: the subject occupies a one-way roadway r (st.one_way_roadway) lying on h with heading·d at or above p.parked_heading_cos, and some road edge e lying on h is on its left (offset above zero) within 18 inches of its body. (3) Angle parking permitted: the subject occupies a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a regulatory sign of code angle_parking whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold), or it occupies a parking space (st.parking_space) whose angle exceeds p.parking_space_angle_resolution.

narrowings.why: The wheels are not observed: the body outline stands for them. The wheels lie inside the footprint, so the body-to-curb distance is at most the wheel-to-curb distance and the reading is lenient by the wheels' inset (a few centimetres). 'parallel' is read within the tolerance p.parked_heading_cos, headed with the designated direction, since the right-hand wheels face the right-hand curb only so.

Why a vehicle is stopped is not observed. The words speak of a vehicle stopped or parked to stand by the way (the stopping definition DEF-NRS-484A-260 itself leaves out a halt 'necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'); a halt made for traffic is read through the conduct that shows it: a halt in a region a signal, sign, railway device or person directing traffic governs, or a halt queued behind a member of traffic within the queue spacing. A halt mid-way through a parking manoeuvre is judged like any other halt.

The permission given by ordinance, and its validity on a highway the Department maintains, is read from the posted angle-parking sign or the angled bay marking: the presence of the device presumes the status.
The duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
