segmentation.text: If a laned roadway is restricted to one direction,
a person shall not stand or park a vehicle
upon the left-hand side of such one-way roadway
unless official traffic-control devices are erected permitting such standing or parking.

elements.justification: 'Roadway' is 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder' (DEF-NRS-484A-220); a roadway 'restricted to one direction' is st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction', which refines st.roadway, whose exclusion (not the sidewalk) does not touch a roadway. 'Laned' is read as a lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles'; not a stand-in for a half of the roadway, which is not how it is used here) lying on the public way (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines') on which the one-way roadway lies: the relation ties the lanes to the roadway's way, never distance.

'Stand' is 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers' (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and 'park' 'the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily ...' (DEF-NRS-484A-155): park is a kind of standing, so the two together are standing. drv.motion.parked denotes a road user 'at rest at every observation of the window behind the observation, of length min_duration', and leaves out 'a halt shorter than min_duration, which may be the temporary halt the definition leaves out': with min_duration p.standing_min_duration, a halt longer than a passenger pick-up dwell is standing, as the mapping index reads 'No person shall stand or park a vehicle'. 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'a person ... a vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Upon ... such one-way roadway': the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the same one-way roadway s1 selects, re-bound with s1's selection. 'The left-hand side' is read against the roadway's designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in ... a roadway, one-way roadway'), never the vehicle's heading alone: among the curbs or edges (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway') lying on the roadway's way (st.on_way, st.highway), the one nearest the subject lies on the left of that direction. Its side is read with prim.region_lateral_offset ('the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user ... perpendicular to the road user's heading'), whose sign is turned into the roadway's frame by the sign of the dot product of the subject's heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') with the roadway's direction: a parked vehicle may face either way. No 'not a stand-in' clause applies: the offset is used as a side, not as occupancy.

'Official traffic-control device' is 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic' (DEF-NRS-484A-145); a device 'permitting such standing or parking' is read through the devices of the vocabulary that permit it: a marked bay (st.parking_space, 'marked bay for standing or parking') the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); a regulatory sign of code angle_parking (dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code') or a zone sign of kind parking_restricted (dev.zone_sign, a signed zone with its 'conditions attribute') that governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; st.travel_region) a region the subject occupies, with its posted conditions holding for the subject (prim.conditions_hold, 'the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user'). dev.regulatory_sign's exclusion (a sign is not a manoeuvre or a road feature) is respected: the sign is read as the permission it posts.

NRS_484B_497.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway r (st.one_way_roadway) lying on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway) on which some lane (st.lane) also lies.
NRS_484B_497.obligation: For every one-way roadway r the subject occupies, selected again as in the applicability (lying on a highway h on which a lane lies), it is not the case that all of the following hold at the observation: (1) the subject is parked (drv.motion.parked with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and min_duration p.standing_min_duration); (2) the subject is on the left-hand side of r: of the road edges (st.road_edge) lying on h, the one with the smallest absolute lateral offset from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset) lies to the left of r's designated direction, that is its offset is positive where the dot product of the subject's heading (kin.heading) and r's direction (st.lane_direction) is positive, and negative where that dot product is negative; (3) no device permits standing or parking there: the subject's footprint overlaps no parking space (st.parking_space), and no regulatory sign of code angle_parking (dev.regulatory_sign) and no zone sign of kind parking_restricted (dev.zone_sign) whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold) governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies.

narrowings.why: 'A person shall not ... park a vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever is at its controls.
That a device is official and 'erected' is read from its presence on the road: a marked bay or a posted sign present in the scene is presumed official.

segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are erected giving notice thereof,
a person
shall not stand or park a vehicle
upon the left-hand side of a one-way
street.

elements.justification: 'official traffic-control devices' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority') 'giving notice thereof', notice that standing or parking is prohibited there, are a regulatory sign of code no_standing or no_parking (dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code') whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold) governing (dev.governs) the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), or a marked length of curb of kind no_parking or no_stopping (st.curb_zone, 'a signed or marked length of curb') the subject occupies. A sign is not a stand-in for a manoeuvre: it is read only as the notice of the place.

'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stands or parks, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'stand' is DEF-NRS-484A-250, 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers', and every parking (DEF-NRS-484A-155) is such a standing; the standing is drv.motion.parked with the passenger-dwell bound as its window, a shorter halt being read as the receiving or discharging of passengers the definition leaves out (index: 'No person shall stand or park a vehicle' maps to drv.motion.parked).

'a one-way' way is the subject occupying (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway r (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction') lying on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway). Its 'left-hand side' is the side to the left of r's designated direction (st.lane_direction): a road edge (st.road_edge) on h is on that side where its lateral offset from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset, 'left positive', relative to the subject's heading) times the sign of the dot product of the subject's heading (kin.heading) with r's direction is positive. The subject stands upon the left-hand side where it lies nearer such a left edge than every right edge, by ground distance from its body (st.region_geometry). The offset is read only for its side; the distance is not a stand-in for occupancy.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies within the territorial limits of an incorporated city, as the map's reading classifies the area

NRS_484B_493.applicability: The subject, a vehicle, is in a place given notice of the prohibition: it occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a regulatory sign of code no_standing or no_parking whose conditions hold (prim.conditions_hold), or a curb zone (st.curb_zone) of kind no_parking or no_stopping; it occupies a one-way roadway r (st.one_way_roadway) lying on a highway h (st.on_way, st.highway) inside an incorporated city (asm.within_incorporated_city, 'street' being a highway inside the territorial limits of a city, DEF-NRS-484A-265); and it is on r's left-hand side: with s the sign of kin.heading · d for r's designated direction d (st.lane_direction), some road edge eL (st.road_edge) lying on h with s times its lateral offset (prim.region_lateral_offset) positive lies nearer the subject's body (st.region_geometry) than every road edge eR lying on h with s times its offset negative.
NRS_484B_493.obligation: The subject is not standing: violated where drv.motion.parked holds for it (speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, min_duration p.standing_min_duration), compliant where it does not.

narrowings.why: Standing, a halt otherwise than for receiving or discharging passengers, is read through the halt's duration: a halt no longer than the passenger-dwell bound p.standing_min_duration is read as the excepted one.
Notice of the prohibition is read from the posted no_standing or no_parking sign or the no_parking or no_stopping curb marking at the subject's place.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are erected at hazardous or congested places,
a person shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle
in any such designated place.

elements.justification: 'Official traffic-control device' is 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic' (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The device erected at a hazardous place is dev.zone_sign of kind hazardous_place ('a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road'), a sign that begins a zone (its end attribute not set); the device erected at a congested place to keep it clear of halting vehicles is dev.regulatory_sign of code no_stopping ('a point regulation by catalogue code'). That the place is hazardous or congested is the authority's designation, evidenced by the sign; the sign is not read as the hazard it marks (dev.regulatory_sign: 'a warning sign is not the hazard it warns of'). The designation is in effect where the sign's posted conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold; dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now').

'Stop' when prohibited is 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-260, whose own scope 'when prohibited' these words meet); 'stand' is 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not' (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and 'park' 'the standing of a vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-155): the three verbs together forbid a halt, drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation ... its speed at or below a tolerance', p.halt_speed_tolerance), as the mapping index reads 'shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle'. The definition's exclusions, which the concept's contract does not make, are carried beside it: a halt with another road user ahead in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') within p.queue_halt_gap of the subject's body (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', not a centre distance) is a halt to avoid conflict with other traffic; a halt on a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') by a stop sign (dev.stop_sign), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign), a traffic signal showing a red or yellow indication (dev.traffic_signal), a railway signal with flashing lights or a gate not up (dev.railway_signal_or_gate), or a police officer's stop indication (dev.human_direction role police_officer, indication stop) is a halt in compliance with a device or an officer. 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'a person ... a vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Any such designated place' is the place the s1 device designates: a travel region (st.travel_region) the device governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a stand-in for a position, and it is not used as one) and the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies).

NRS_484B_500.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region r (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a designating device d whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold): a zone sign of kind hazardous_place that begins a zone (dev.zone_sign), or a regulatory sign of code no_stopping (dev.regulatory_sign).
NRS_484B_500.obligation: Wherever the subject occupies a travel region governed by such a designating device (selected again as in the applicability), the subject is not halted (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), except a halt that is (a) to avoid conflict with other traffic: some other road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; or (b) in compliance with a device or an officer: a travel region the subject occupies is governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign (dev.stop_sign), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign), a traffic signal displaying circular_red, circular_yellow, a red arrow, a yellow arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), a railway signal or gate with lights flashing or gate not up (dev.railway_signal_or_gate), or a person in the role police_officer giving the indication stop (dev.human_direction).

narrowings.why: 'A person shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever is at its controls.

That the place has been designated hazardous or congested by an authority, and the device erected there, are read from the device's presence on the road: the sign is presumed official and its designation presumed.

'Other traffic' in the stop definition's exclusion is read as any road user ahead in the same lane: the conflict avoided is read as a halt in a queue behind it, and a halt for a conflict with a road user crossing the lane is not read.

segmentation.text: Unless otherwise provided by ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction,
a person
shall not: Stop, stand or park a vehicle
in any other
alley
in such a manner, or under such conditions as to leave available less than 10 feet of the width of the alley for the free movement of vehicular traffic.

elements.justification: 'a person ... a vehicle': the duty binds the vehicle the person stops, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

'Stop' prohibited takes DEF-NRS-484A-260: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; standing and parking are halts as well, so the three verbs are read as the halting they all are: drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation'). The exception is read through its conduct: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or a person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), or a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within the queue spacing between bodies (rel.surface_gap).

'alley' (DEF-NRS-484A-015: a highway 'Within a city block set apart for public use', 'Which primarily services access to the rear entrance of abutting property') is st.alley, 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; the vehicle in it is rel.occupies.

The width of the alley left available beside the halted vehicle is measured on each side from its body: to the alley's edge, a road edge region (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway') on that side (prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive)', read for its sign only) at the ground distance from the body (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'); 'under such conditions' covers what else narrows that width beside it: an obstruction (st.obstruction, 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user') on that side within the width, or a member of traffic (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt) alongside (rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'the length the two footprints' projections ... share', at or above zero) on that side (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame') with a lateral gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, lateral component) inside it. The width available is the free width on one side, never the two sides added, since a vehicle moves past on one side. 'the free movement of vehicular traffic' (traffic of vehicles, DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) names whom the width serves: the duty binds whether or not a vehicle is present to use it. The region distance is not a stand-in for occupancy; the bearing and overlap are not a contact or distance and are read only for side and alongside.

assumptions.meaning: the alley at the place of the road user at the observation is one on which an ordinance of the local authority having jurisdiction regulates stopping, standing or parking by provisions of its own, as the map's reading records
the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district, as the map's reading classifies the area

NRS_484B_477_1b.applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies (rel.occupies) an alley region (st.alley); asm.business_district does not hold at its place ('any other' alley: one not in a business district, the alleys of paragraph (a) being those in one); asm.local_alley_ordinance does not hold; and its position leaves less than 10 feet (literal) of the alley's width free on either side: a side (left: prim.region_lateral_offset above zero, rel.bearing lateral component positive; right: below zero, negative) is free where some road edge region (st.road_edge) lies on that side, every road edge region on that side lies at a ground distance from the subject's body (st.region_geometry) of at least 10 feet, every obstruction (st.obstruction) on that side lies at least 10 feet from the body, and every other road user of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt) alongside the subject (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) on that side has a lateral gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap, lateral) of at least 10 feet; the condition holds where neither side is free.
NRS_484B_477_1b.obligation: The subject does not halt there: violated where it is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) and its halt is not one in the stream of traffic (it occupies no travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a traffic signal, stop sign, yield sign, railway signal or gate or person directing traffic (dev.human_direction), and no member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic is ahead of it in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.queue_halt_gap); compliant otherwise.

narrowings.why: The three verbs are read as the halting they all are, with the stopping definition's exception read through the device the subject's region is governed by and a queue ahead within the queue spacing.
The person is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:
When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,
to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping
due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing; or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.

As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.

elements.justification: "vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"; "driver" (DEF-NRS-484A-080, "every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle") is a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion, not membership.

Crossing at grade the track of a railroad: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.railway_crossing, "level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail". "Railroad" (DEF-NRS-484A-200) excludes streetcars; a streetcar line along a street forms no level crossing of a railway with the roadway, so the contract makes that exclusion. The crossing is under way from the observation the footprint overlaps the crossing until the subject has completely crossed (a5).

"without stopping": drv.motion.complete_halt, "The road user is at rest at the observation ... observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance the caller sets" (p.halt_speed_tolerance). Failing to completely cross without stopping is a halt at an observation of the crossing before the subject has completely crossed. The concept says nothing of where the road user is; the place is read from a2 and a5.

The causes the words name (no room beyond the crossing, the undercarriage hanging on the crossing) are why a vehicle comes to rest on the tracks; they are read through the conduct they explain, the halt before completely crossing (drv.motion.complete_halt), as the ontology reads a purpose by its conduct.

"the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail": st.region_geometry, "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)", from the subject's body to the st.railway_crossing whose outline carries "its nearest rail". While the subject has been within the literal 15 ft of the crossing at every observation since its footprint last overlapped it, its trailing end is not yet 15 ft past the rail; region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy, which a2 reads with rel.occupies.

NRS_484B_560_7a.applicability: The subject is a vehicle crossing a railroad crossing c and not yet completely across it: at this observation the ground distance from its body to c (st.region_geometry) is below the literal 15 ft, and has been below it at every observation since an observation (this one included) at which its footprint overlapped c (rel.occupies) — the past `since` of 'distance below 15 ft' over 'occupies c'.
NRS_484B_560_7a.obligation: At every such observation the subject is not halted: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance does not hold. A halt while it overlaps c, or after leaving c with its trailing end less than 15 ft past c, is a violation.

narrowings.why: "the driver" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; whoever or whatever controls it.

The causes of the halt (insufficient space beyond the crossing, insufficient undercarriage clearance) are not observed; they are read through the halt before completely crossing they explain, so any halt in that stretch is judged.

"completely cross", as the definition in this section states it, is read with the nearest rail as the outline of the mapped crossing region and the trailing end as the subject's body outline: the distance from body to crossing outline stands for the distance from the trailing end to the nearest rail.

scenarios.name: branch_1

segmentation.text: A vehicle
shall not be permitted to stand
unattended
upon any perceptible grade
without stopping the engine and effectively setting the brake thereon and turning the front wheels to the curb or side of the highway.

elements.justification: 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except ...'), claimed as one atom.

'Stand' is 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers' (DEF-NRS-484A-250): a halt, drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation ... its speed at or below a tolerance', p.halt_speed_tolerance). The definition's exclusion of passenger receiving is not carried: the duty reads only a vehicle with no person in it (s3), which no passenger is being received into while it stays so. 'Shall not be permitted' is read on the vehicle's conduct, whoever is in charge of it.

'Unattended': no person is in or on the vehicle to attend it, ru.occupant_count, 'the number of persons in or on a vehicle (an integer attribute of a road user)', equal to none. A source that observes arrivals but not a total declares it absent, and the rule is then unknown.

'Upon any perceptible grade': the subject is on a highway (rel.occupies; st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', which the words' 'side of the highway' names) at a place whose slope (st.grade, 'longitudinal slope of the roadway at a point'; not a stand-in for the place of a crest, which is not read) stands clear of zero: its magnitude exceeds p.grade_resolution. The words name the grade's presence, not a size: 'perceptible' is read as a slope the source resolves.

'Stopping the engine': kin.engine_running, 'the vehicle's engine or motor is running, so that propulsion is available', must be false; it is 'not a stand-in for motion or a halt', and the halt is read separately (s2). 'Setting the brake thereon' on an unattended vehicle is the parking brake: kin.parking_brake, 'the parking brake (hand brake) is set'; not a stand-in for the service brake or the brake lamp, neither of which is read, since no person presses a pedal in an unattended vehicle. 'Turning the front wheels to the curb or side of the highway': kin.steer_angle, 'front-wheel steering angle' (not a stand-in for a path or a manoeuvre, and it is read as the wheels' position only), turned beyond p.steer_angle_resolution toward the side on which the nearest curb or edge lies. The curb or side is the road edge (st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway') lying on the subject's highway (st.on_way, 'the public way a structure region lies on'; st.highway) nearest the subject, and its side is the sign of its lateral offset (prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user ... perpendicular to the road user's heading').

NRS_484B_533.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is halted (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), with no person in or on it (ru.occupant_count equal to none), whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a highway h (st.highway), and the magnitude of the grade at its place (st.grade) exceeds p.grade_resolution.
NRS_484B_533.obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds, with h selected again as there: the engine is not running (kin.engine_running false); the parking brake is set (kin.parking_brake); and the front wheels are turned toward the curb or side: of the road edges (st.road_edge) lying on h (st.on_way), the one with the smallest absolute lateral offset from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset) gives the side, and the steering angle (kin.steer_angle) exceeds p.steer_angle_resolution in magnitude and has the sign of that offset, both read left-positive.

narrowings.why: 'Shall not be permitted to stand' is read on the vehicle's conduct: the duty binds the standing vehicle whoever is in charge of it.
'Effectively setting the brake' is read as the parking brake set while the vehicle stays at rest; the brake's holding force is not observed.

The curb or side of the highway is read as the road edge nearest the vehicle, and the steering angle's sign is read left-positive, as kin.yaw_rate and prim.region_lateral_offset are; the direction the wheels should point for an uphill or downhill grade is not distinguished, the words not distinguishing it.
Where two road edges lying on the highway are equally nearest the vehicle, front wheels turned beyond the resolution toward the side of either comply.

scenarios.narrative: A car stands with no one in it on a clearly sloped street, its engine running, parking brake set, wheels turned toward the nearest curb.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car stands with no one in it on the same slope, engine off, parking brake set, front wheels turned toward the right-hand curb, which is the nearest road edge.

scenarios.name: idle

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car stands unattended on the slope, engine off, parking brake set, front wheels straight.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car stands on the slope with its driver inside.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer
or a traffic-control signal:
When proper signs have been erected,
the driver of a vehicle

shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped,
the driver shall yield
the right-of-way
to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway
or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, of which the subject is a member; 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction of role police_officer ('a person directing traffic ... role ∈ {police_officer, ...}') governing (dev.governs) the subject's approach carrier c or X (st.travel_region), read at the subject's entry.
A dev.traffic_signal governing c or X (dev.governs) that is not dev.inoperative ('installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'), read at the subject's entry.
'Proper signs': a dev.stop_sign or dev.yield_sign governing (dev.governs) the carrier c the subject entered X from (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters) or X itself.
Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.
Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) while the protected vehicle is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact).

'Other vehicles' are the admitted aggregate. 'Which have entered the intersection' is v's footprint overlapping X (rel.occupies) continuously since it occupied a carrier c2 entering X (st.lane_enters). 'Such through highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-275: 'every highway ... at the entrances to which vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield right-of-way to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to either an authorized stop sign or a yield sign') is a highway h_t that X lies on (st.on_way) on which c does not lie and none of whose carriers entering X is governed by a stop or yield sign (dev.governs); c2 lies on h_t.

'During the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection': the subject's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet') and its kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') is above the halt tolerance.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

operationalizations.standard: approaching so closely on the through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: v, occupying a carrier entering X that lies on the through highway, is an immediate hazard where, under constant velocities, its centre and the subject's approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance

NRS_484B_257_1_o2.applicability: At every observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection X and has overlapped it continuously since its latest entry into X (having occupied at the observation before a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, X)) and the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance): 'during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection'; where at that entry observation a stop sign or yield sign governed c or X, no police officer's direction governed c or X and no traffic signal that was not inoperative governed c or X; and where NRS_484B_257_1_o1 (binder subject ↦ subject) was complied with at that entry observation: 'After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped' — the act that rule searches for, read at the entry by a past operator.
NRS_484B_257_1_o2.obligation: Re-binding X and c as in the applicability: for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that, for some highway h_t that X lies on (st.on_way X h_t), on which c does not lie and none of whose carriers entering X is governed by a stop sign or a yield sign (dev.governs) — the through highway — either (a) overlaps X continuously since an observation at which it occupied a carrier c2 entering X and lying on h_t, or (b) occupies such a carrier c2 and its closest approach to the subject lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'proper signs have been erected' is a legal status; a stop or yield sign present and governing the approach is its evidence.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.stop_sign governs c; the subject halted at the stop line and entered X; v occupies X having entered from carrier c2 on a crossing highway whose carriers entering X carry no stop or yield sign; the subject moves across X with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance and its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; v has cleared X before the subject moves; no closest approach to any through-highway vehicle falls within the bound while the subject moves.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No stop or yield sign governs c or X when the subject enters X.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves within X while v crosses from another highway on a conflicting path; dev.governs is absent, so whether a sign governs c, and which highway is the through highway, are unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: After its stop the subject crosses X with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject entered X without halting at its stop sign (NRS_484B_257_1_o1 violated at its entry) and moves across X in conflict with v: the duty follows the stop the words name; the omitted stop is judged by NRS_484B_257_1_o1.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: After its stop the subject moves within X; v approaches on carrier c2 of the through highway, not yet in X, with its closest approach to the subject within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject keeps moving.

segmentation.text: The Department of Transportation, and local authorities with the approval of the Department of Transportation, may designate dangerous highway grade crossings of railroads
and erect official traffic-control devices at such crossings directing a stop.
When such stop signs are erected
the driver of any vehicle
shall stop within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest track of such a grade crossing
and afterward may proceed only
upon exercising due care.

elements.justification: A 'highway grade crossing of a railroad' ('railroad' is 'a carrier of persons or property upon cars ... operated upon stationary rails', DEF-NRS-484A-200) is st.railway_crossing, 'level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail', lying on a highway (st.on_way, 'the public way a structure region lies on'; st.highway). The authority's designation of it as dangerous is its legal status, evidenced by the stop sign erected for it (s2, s3).

'Official traffic-control devices ... directing a stop' ('every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad', DEF-NRS-484A-145) are stop signs: dev.stop_sign, 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt'; its presence is the evidence that it is official.

'When such stop signs are erected': the stop sign governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a stand-in for a position, and the place of the halt is read from the crossing, not from the sign) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies) on its approach, and that region lies on the same highway as the crossing (st.on_way): the chain of relations ties the sign to 'such crossings'.

'Driver' is 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-080), a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion; 'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

'Stop' when required means 'complete cessation from movement' (DEF-NRS-484A-255, whose own scope 'when required' these words meet): drv.motion.complete_halt, whose contract quotes it, with p.halt_speed_tolerance. The place of the halt: the ground distance from the subject's body to the crossing (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)'), the crossing being st.railway_crossing with 'its nearest rail', is at most the upper and at least the lower figure the span states (literals), and the subject's footprint does not yet overlap the crossing (rel.occupies). 'Such a grade crossing' is the crossing s1 to s3 select, re-bound with every relation that fixed it.

NRS_484B_557_o1.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), and the judged observation is an entry of the subject into a railway crossing x (st.railway_crossing): its footprint overlaps x (rel.occupies) and did not at the previous observation, and at that previous observation the subject occupied a travel region r (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign (dev.stop_sign), where r and x lie on the same highway h (st.on_way, st.highway).
NRS_484B_557_o1.obligation: Duty of an act before an event (rule 4c). Event: the entry of the applicability, for the crossing x and the governed region r it selects. Act and place: at some observation of the search the subject is halted (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), its footprint does not overlap x (rel.occupies), and the ground distance from its body to x (st.region_geometry) is at most the upper literal of s5 and at least its lower literal. Search: back from the observation before the entry, through observations at which the subject does not overlap x and its distance to x is at most the upper literal (the stopping zone). History bound: the search ends at the approach start, the last observation before the entry at which the subject does not overlap x and its distance to x exceeds the upper literal, or at the subject's previous exit from x (the observation at which it ceased to overlap x), the previous occurrence of the same event; nothing else ends it, not the start of the recording nor a first observation. Verdict: where the search finds the halt, the duty is met; where it reaches either end without the halt, the duty is violated; where it reaches the subject's first observation, inside the zone, with neither end found and no halt, the duty is unknown. A distance, an overlap or a speed unobserved at an observation of the search makes the search unknown from that point unless a halt in the zone was found nearer the entry. Whether the entry occurred is unknown where the previous observation does not show the subject's overlap with x, and whether the stop sign governs is unknown where governance of r is not observed.

narrowings.why: 'The driver of any vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion.
The designation of the crossing as dangerous by the Department or a local authority is read from the presence of a stop sign governing the approach to the crossing.
That the device is official and directs a stop is read from the presence of a stop sign.
The distance 'from the nearest track' is read as the distance from the vehicle's body to the crossing region, whose near boundary is its nearest rail.

The search's end at the subject's previous exit from the crossing is read as including the exit observation itself (the first observation at which it no longer overlaps the crossing): a halt there in the zone counts, and the search does not pass it.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car halts at a distance from the crossing between the two figures, then drives into it.

scenarios.name: idle

segmentation.text: A person shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle
for any purpose or period of time
except for the expeditious
loading or unloading of passengers
in any place marked as a passenger curb loading zone
during hours when the regulations applicable to such passenger curb loading zone are effective.

elements.justification: 'Stop' when prohibited is 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-260, whose own scope 'when prohibited' these words meet); 'stand' is 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not' (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and 'park' 'the standing of a vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-155): together a halt, drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation ... its speed at or below a tolerance', p.halt_speed_tolerance), as the mapping index reads 'shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle'. The definition's exclusions are carried beside it: a halt with another road user ahead in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') within p.queue_halt_gap of the body (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', not a centre distance) avoids conflict with other traffic; a halt on a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing red or yellow, a railway signal flashing or a gate not up, or a police officer's stop indication (dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.traffic_signal, dev.railway_signal_or_gate, dev.human_direction) complies with a device or an officer. 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

The purpose 'loading or unloading of passengers' is not observable and is read by the conduct it explains: during the halt (drv.motion.complete_halt) a door of the vehicle is open (sig.door_open, 'a door open; side in {traffic, curb}'), the act through which passengers board or alight. The passenger curb loading zone is 'reserved for the exclusive use of vehicles during the loading or unloading of passengers' (DEF-NRS-484B-033).

'Passenger curb loading zone' is 'an area adjacent to a curb or edge of a highway reserved for the exclusive use of vehicles during the loading or unloading of passengers' (DEF-NRS-484B-033): st.curb_zone of kind passenger_loading, 'a signed or marked length of curb', which the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... curb zone ...)'). The marking is the evidence of the designation.

The hours of a curb zone are those its posting states: a zone sign of kind parking_restricted (dev.zone_sign, whose 'conditions attribute' is 'a list of time windows ...'; 'a legend read with no restriction is the empty set (unconditional)') governing (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies); whether its hours hold now is prim.conditions_hold ('env.civil_time falls in one of its time windows'), never the sign itself (dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now').

operationalizations.standard: expeditious
operationalizations.convention: curbside passenger pick-up dwell: a halt counts as expeditious loading or unloading while it has not lasted as long as a passenger pick-up dwell at the curb, i.e. while the subject is not at rest at every observation of a window of length p.standing_min_duration behind the observation (drv.motion.parked)

residues.why: 'For any purpose or period of time' excludes no halt: every halt, whatever its purpose and length, is within the prohibition, so the duty is the same whether or not these words are read.

NRS_484B_503.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a curb zone z of kind passenger_loading (st.curb_zone), and the zone's regulations are effective: every zone sign of kind parking_restricted (dev.zone_sign) that governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies has its conditions holding for the subject at the observation (prim.conditions_hold); where no such sign governs, the marked zone is read as effective at all hours.
NRS_484B_503.obligation: Wherever the subject occupies such a zone with its regulations effective (selected again as in the applicability), the subject is not halted (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), except a halt that is (a) to avoid conflict with other traffic: some other road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; or (b) in compliance with a device or an officer: a travel region the subject occupies is governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal displaying a red or yellow indication or flashing_red, a railway signal or gate with lights flashing or gate not up, or a person in the role police_officer giving the indication stop; or (c) expeditious loading or unloading of passengers: the subject is not parked with min_duration p.standing_min_duration (drv.motion.parked with p.halt_speed_tolerance), and at some observation of the same halt, before or after the observation, a door of the subject is open (sig.door_open): the subject has stayed halted since an observation at which it was halted with a door open, or stays halted until an observation at which it is halted with a door open.

narrowings.why: 'A person shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion.
The purpose of loading or unloading passengers is read by the conduct it explains: a door of the halted vehicle open during the halt.
'Marked as' a passenger curb loading zone is read from the presence of the curb zone of that kind on the road.
'Other traffic' in the stop definition's exclusion is read as any road user ahead in the same lane, the conflict avoided being a halt in a queue.
A railway gate 'not up' is read as a gate observed lowering, down or raising; a crossing without a gate (gate state none) excuses a halt only through flashing lights.

A traffic signal's 'red or yellow indication' is read as circular red or yellow and red or yellow arrows of any direction (with flashing red); flashing yellow and flashing yellow arrows, which permit proceeding, are not included.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car halts inside a passenger_loading curb zone that no sign governs, for longer than the standing duration, no door open; no road user ahead and no stop control governs its lane.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car halts in the zone, opens its curb-side door, and moves off before the standing duration has elapsed.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car halts at a curb where there is no curb zone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car halts in the zone briefly, shorter than the standing duration, and the source does not observe its doors.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car halts in the zone while a parking_restricted zone sign governing its lane posts hours that do not include the observation's time of day.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car halts in the zone behind another car ahead in the same lane, within the queue gap, doors closed.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red signal alone:
After complying with
the requirement to stop,
vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme right of the highway
may proceed into the intersection
for a right turn
only when the intersecting highway is two-directional or one-way to the right,
or vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme left of a one-way highway
may proceed into the intersection
for a left turn
only when the intersecting highway is one-way to the left,
but must yield
the right-of-way
to pedestrians and other traffic proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady red signal alone is circular_red and no other state (not flashing_red, and no arrow beside it). Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'After complying with the requirement to stop' requires the halt itself (rule 5), with every qualification of the requirement it names, borrowed from NRS-484B-307-8a (reference s3): 'must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection'. A stop required is DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement': drv.motion.complete_halt. The place: the stop line (st.stop_line) recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of) of the subject's carrier c, else the crosswalk (st.crosswalk) marking it, else c's entrance end at the intersection (st.intersection); the footprint not overlapping the region (rel.occupies), on its upstream side along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction, sign of prim.region_offset_along) and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry distance), on the approach that ends in this entry, as NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 states the place, zone and history bound. Not compliance with that node, which a composed rule grants where it is not engaged; st.region_geometry is not occupancy.

'vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), claimed as ru.aggregate. 'facing such a signal': the steady red head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the carrier c (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies), whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection). 'situated on the extreme right of the highway': c is a lane (st.lane) whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane'). Not a stand-in: lane membership is read from the ordinal, never from a lateral offset; dev.governs is not a position.

'may proceed into the intersection': the subject's entry into intersection i (st.intersection), its footprint coming to overlap i (rel.occupies) having occupied at the observation before the travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters); the place at which the intention of s6 is declared. As the index maps 'may proceed straight through or turn right or left' (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'the intersecting highway': each highway region (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines') that i lies on (st.on_way, 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there') other than a highway c lies on. 'two-directional' (DEF-NRS-484B-073, 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions'): no median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways') lies on it, and two lanes (st.lane) lying on it carry designated directions (st.lane_direction) whose cosine is below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos. 'one-way to the right': at least one lane lies on it and every lane lying on it carries a designated direction to the right of c's designated direction, the cross product of c's direction with the lane's (d_x times l_y minus d_y times l_x) being below minus p.cross_direction_sin_min. Not a stand-in: st.on_way is the way a region lies on, not nearness; st.lane_direction is local to its carrier.

'vehicular traffic facing such a signal': as s4. 'situated on the extreme left': c is a lane (st.lane) of ordinal 1 (st.lane_adjacency, 'ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane'); 'of a one-way highway': the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'), as the index maps 'Upon a highway designated and signposted for one-way traffic' (NRS_484B_220_1). Not a stand-in: lane membership is read from the ordinal, never from an offset.
As s5: the subject's entry into i from c (rel.occupies rising; st.lane_enters; st.travel_region; st.intersection), the place at which the intention of s10 is declared.

'the intersecting highway': each highway region (st.highway) that i lies on (st.on_way) other than a highway c lies on. 'one-way to the left': at least one lane (st.lane) lies on it and every lane lying on it carries a designated direction (st.lane_direction) to the left of c's designated direction, the cross product of c's direction with the lane's being above p.cross_direction_sin_min. Not a stand-in: st.on_way is not nearness.

'must yield': kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') tells a subject that moves on toward the other road user from one that holds back, and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)') is the crash precedence exists to avoid; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s13 reads. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'pedestrians and other traffic': road users of the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian and DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than the subject. 'proceeding': moving, kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'as directed by the signal at the intersection': it overlaps (rel.occupies) intersection i (st.intersection) or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of) of a travel region that enters i (st.lane_enters, st.travel_region), or it occupies a travel region c' entering i that is governed (dev.governs) by a head displaying a green indication (dev.traffic_signal: circular_green or green_arrow). Not a stand-in: st.entrance_of is the recorded association, never a distance.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210, 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance); the subject grants precedence where, while its speed is above the halt tolerance (p.halt_speed_tolerance), no such approach to the other road user arises. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the constant-velocity extrapolation of both road users.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the right at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included
the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

compositions.quote: must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection
compositions.why: The words borrow the requirement's place and its order (the crosswalk on the nearest side, or the place a sign or pavement marking indicates, else the intersection's edge) and the meaning of stopping before it. The condition requires that the halt itself occurred there; a composition with NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 would not establish it, since a composed rule counts as complied with where it is not engaged. So the borrowed words are carried by the halt, the place and the approach on s2, and no rule of NRS-484B-307-8a need apply, hold or be complied with.

NRS_484B_307_8c.applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, approached intersection i through a travel region c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs), and entered i (its footprint came to overlap i, having occupied c and not i at the observation before) at an observation at which s displayed a steady red alone (circular_red, no other state), after halting at the place of the stop on that approach (s2 with s3: the place, zone and history bound NRS_484B_307_8a_o1 states); at that entry either (right) c is a lane whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction, int.right_turn is declared true for the subject at i, and every highway i lies on other than one c lies on is two-directional (no median or divider lies on it; two lanes on it with directions opposed within p.lane_opposed_direction_cos) or one-way to the right (every lane on it points to the right of c's direction by more than p.cross_direction_sin_min); or (left) c is a lane of ordinal 1, the subject's footprint overlaps a one-way roadway, int.left_turn is declared true for the subject at i, and every such highway is one-way to the left. Its footprint has overlapped i at every observation since that entry, the judged one included.
NRS_484B_307_8c.obligation: For every road user p other than the subject that is of the class pedestrian or of the class traffic and is proceeding as directed by the signal at i — its speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance, and either its footprint overlaps i or a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a travel region that enters i, or it occupies a travel region c' entering i governed by a head that displays circular_green or a green_arrow: it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while the closest approach of the two centres lies within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject's body does not touch p's (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection' is read through the signal state governing the other road user's approach (a green indication) where it approaches, and through its presence within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk where it is there; a road user that entered against its own red and is now within the intersection is yielded to as well.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car halts with its body 1 m short of the stop line of the rightmost lane c (ordinal 2 of 2), int.right_turn declared at i, the cross street undivided with lanes in both directions; it enters i under circular_red alone at 4 m/s while a car on the cross street, on a lane entering i governed by a head displaying circular_green, approaches from the left at 12 m/s, the closest approach of their centres 1.5 s ahead at 1 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same right turn on red with no other road user in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car halts in lane c and enters i only after s displays circular_green alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but lane ordinals and counts are not observed: whether the car is on the extreme right is unknown (c is on no one-way roadway, so the left branch is decided false).

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the car halted 15 m short of the stop line behind a queue and rolled into i without halting at the place: the halt the words require did not occur and the duty of this paragraph does not arise.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car halts at the stop line of the leftmost lane (ordinal 1) of a one-way roadway, int.left_turn declared at i, every lane of the cross street pointing to its left; it enters i under circular_red alone at 5 m/s while a pedestrian walking at 1.3 m/s in the crosswalk marking the entrance of a cross-street lane into i is closing on its path, the closest approach of their centres 1.2 s ahead at 0.7 m.

param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin

param_proposals.name: p.lane_opposed_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about twenty-five degrees) off exactly opposed at which the designated directions of two mapped lanes of one way count as opposite directions of travel: the direction noise of map lane segments along a gently curving way
param_proposals.source: map lane-direction tolerance, matching the catalogue's tolerance for opposed vehicle headings (p.oncoming_heading_cos)

param_proposals.name: p.cross_direction_sin_min
param_proposals.convention: sine of the smallest angle (thirty degrees) by which a way's designated direction lies to one side of an approach's designated direction for that way's traffic to count as flowing to that side: the legs of a junction meet at larger angles, and map direction noise is far smaller
param_proposals.source: intersection design guidance limiting the skew of junction legs
