segmentation.text: Whenever a vehicle is parked or stopped
upon the traveled portion of a highway or shoulder adjacent thereto,
whether attended or unattended
during the times mentioned
and there is insufficient light to reveal any person or object within a distance of 1,000 feet upon such highway or roadway,
such vehicle shall display lighted lamps
meeting the requirements of subsection 1 [(1) appended below].

Every vehicle shall be equipped with one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a white or amber light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle, and one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a red light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear of the vehicle.
The location of such lamps shall be such that at least one such lamp is installed as near as practicable to the side of the vehicle which is closest to passing traffic.

elements.justification: 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, one ru.aggregate atom. 'parked or stopped' is the vehicle at rest, drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation'), which covers a parked vehicle and one stopped for any time; as the index maps 'stopped or parked' (NRS_484B_450_1l).

'the traveled portion of a highway' is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder' (as the index maps 'the paved or main-traveled part of the highway'); 'shoulder adjacent thereto' is st.shoulder, 'the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic', lying on the same highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway its kind, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'). rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on either.

The times are borrowed from NRS-484D-100-1 (t5): '(a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise; (b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead;' read as env.darkness ('insufficient natural light; the boundary relative to sunset and sunrise is a reading parameter') or env.visibility ('visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)') below the same 1,000-foot figure as t6. The third circumstance of that line, a device directing lamps on, is not borrowed: the condition t6 joins by 'and' entails time (b), so the times hold wherever t6 holds, whatever that circumstance is.

Insufficient light to reveal a person or object within 1,000 feet: env.darkness ('insufficient natural light') or env.visibility ('visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)') below the law's figure, a literal; as the index maps the like words of LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2.

The lamps subsection 1 (t8) describes are borrowed from the appended text: 'one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a white or amber light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle, and one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a red light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear of the vehicle'. These are the parking lamps to the front and the tail lamps to the rear: sig.position_lamp, 'position, parking, cowl or tail lamps lit (the lamps a vehicle shows without its headlamps)'. Their colour, reach and location are residues (t9, t10).

compositions.why: The words borrow only the periods NRS 484D.100 names (darkness from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise; other times when insufficient light or atmospheric conditions make persons and vehicles not discernible at 1,000 feet) to say when this duty arises; nothing turns on whether that line's lamp duty applies to this vehicle or is complied with, and that line itself excepts parked vehicles, so composing it would read its exception, not its times.
compositions.quote: (a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise; (b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead;

compositions.why: The words borrow from the appended subsection 1 only its description of the lamps (front lamps showing white or amber, rear lamps showing red) to say which lamps the displayed lights are; the equipment duty of subsection 1 need not be complied with for this display duty to be judged, and it is no node of the corpus.
compositions.quote: one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a white or amber light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle, and one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a red light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear of the vehicle

residues.why: 'whether attended or unattended' covers both states: the duty is the same whether or not anyone attends the vehicle.

The equipment duty and the lamps' colour (white or amber to the front, red to the rear) and reach (visible from 500 feet) describe the lamps the obligation requires displayed; no atom carries a lamp's colour, reach or fitment, so the rule reads only that the position lamps are lit.
The location of the lamps (one as near as practicable to the side closest to passing traffic) is a fitment requirement no atom carries; the rule does not read it.

NRS_484D_165_3.applicability: The subject is a member of the vehicle aggregate, at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance), its footprint overlaps a roadway or a shoulder lying on the same highway as a roadway, and at the observation env.darkness holds or env.visibility is below the literal 1,000 ft.
NRS_484D_165_3.obligation: The subject's position lamps are lit (sig.position_lamp) at the observation.

narrowings.why: The lamps the appended subsection describes are read as the position (parking and tail) lamps lit; their colour, reach and location are not read (residues on t9 and t10).

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car of the vehicle aggregate stands at rest on the roadway at night (env.darkness true), position lamps off.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but its position lamps are lit.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car stands at rest on the roadway by day, visibility 5,000 m.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car stands at rest on the roadway at night; the source does not observe position lamps.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car stands at rest on the paved shoulder of the highway by day in fog, env.visibility 120 m, position lamps off.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: sensor speed resolution of the acquisition standard

segmentation.text: A person shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle
for any purpose or length of time
in any restricted parking zone
other than for the purpose to which parking in such zone is restricted,
except that a driver of a passenger vehicle
may stop temporarily
in such zone
for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading of passengers
when such stopping does not interfere with
any vehicle which is waiting to enter or about to enter the zone
for the purpose of parking in accordance with the purpose to which parking is restricted.

elements.justification: 'Stop' when prohibited is 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-260, the definition the table resolves for 'stopping' in this law); 'stand' is 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not' (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and 'park' 'the standing of a vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-155): together a halt, drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation ... its speed at or below a tolerance', p.halt_speed_tolerance). The definition's exclusions are carried beside it: a halt with another road user ahead in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within p.queue_halt_gap of the body (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', not a centre distance) avoids conflict with other traffic; a halt on a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing red or yellow, a railway signal flashing or a gate not up, or a police officer's stop indication (dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.traffic_signal, dev.railway_signal_or_gate, dev.human_direction) complies with a device or an officer. 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

A restricted parking zone is st.curb_zone of kind restricted_parking ('a signed or marked length of curb'), which the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... curb zone ...)').

The purpose to which parking is restricted is the restriction the zone's posting states: a zone sign of kind parking_restricted (dev.zone_sign, whose 'conditions attribute' carries 'a vehicle class' and time windows) governing (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies). A halt is for that purpose where the sign's conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold: 'any occupancy or class condition is met'); the sign is not read as the condition holding (dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now').

'Driver' is 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-080), read through the vehicle's controlled motion. 'Passenger vehicle' has no posted definition: it is read as a vehicle (the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) not built to carry goods or to be drawn: not ru.truck ('motor vehicle for carrying goods, with a body built for that purpose') and not ru.trailer_or_combination ('vehicle drawn by another, or the combination'). The class atoms are carried beside the aggregate, never in place of it.
'In such zone': the same restricted_parking curb zone (st.curb_zone) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), re-bound with the selection of s3.

The purpose of and engagement 'in loading or unloading of passengers' are read by the conduct: a door of the halted vehicle (drv.motion.complete_halt) open (sig.door_open, 'a door open') during the halt.

'Any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'waiting to enter or about to enter the zone' is read by the conduct: that vehicle does not overlap the zone (rel.occupies, st.curb_zone of s3) and is halted (drv.motion.complete_halt) with the ground distance from its body to the zone (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') within p.zone_entry_wait_reach.

Parking 'in accordance with the purpose to which parking is restricted' is read, for the waiting vehicle, as the conditions of the parking_restricted zone sign (dev.zone_sign) governing (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies holding for that vehicle (prim.conditions_hold, 'any occupancy or class condition is met').

operationalizations.standard: temporarily
operationalizations.convention: curbside passenger pick-up dwell: a stop counts as temporary while it has not lasted as long as a passenger pick-up dwell, i.e. while the subject is not at rest at every observation of a window of length p.standing_min_duration behind the observation (drv.motion.parked)

operationalizations.standard: does not interfere with
operationalizations.convention: queueing at a curb space: a stop interferes with a vehicle where, at some observation of the stop so far, that vehicle stands halted outside the zone within one passenger-car length plus a queue spacing of it (p.zone_entry_wait_reach), the place a vehicle waits to take the space

residues.why: 'For any purpose or length of time' excludes no halt: every halt is within the prohibition whatever its purpose and length, so the duty is the same whether or not these words are read.

NRS_484B_510.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a curb zone z of kind restricted_parking (st.curb_zone).
NRS_484B_510.obligation: Wherever the subject occupies such a zone z (selected again as in the applicability), the subject is not halted (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), except a halt that is (a) to avoid conflict with other traffic: some other road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; or (b) in compliance with a device or an officer: a travel region the subject occupies is governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal displaying a red or yellow indication or flashing_red, a railway signal or gate with lights flashing or gate not up, or a person in the role police_officer giving the indication stop; or (c) for the purpose to which parking is restricted: some zone sign of kind parking_restricted (dev.zone_sign) governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies has its conditions holding for the subject (prim.conditions_hold); or (d) a temporary stop of a passenger vehicle for passengers: the subject is neither a truck (ru.truck) nor a trailer or combination (ru.trailer_or_combination), it is not parked with min_duration p.standing_min_duration (drv.motion.parked), a door of the subject is open (sig.door_open) at some observation of the same halt, before or after the observation, and at no observation of the halt up to the judged one is there a vehicle other than the subject (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose footprint does not overlap z, which is halted (drv.motion.complete_halt), whose body's ground distance to z (st.region_geometry) is at most p.zone_entry_wait_reach, and for which the conditions of such a parking_restricted zone sign hold (prim.conditions_hold).

narrowings.why: 'A person shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion.
'A driver of a passenger vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion.

The purpose of a halt is read through the class, occupancy and time conditions of the zone's posted sign holding for the vehicle; a restriction to a purpose the sign's legend states as none of these is not read, and a halt outside the sign's posted hours is read as not for the restricted purpose.
The purpose of and engagement in loading or unloading passengers are read by a door of the halted vehicle open during the halt.
'Waiting to enter or about to enter' is read by a vehicle halted outside the zone within the waiting reach; one still moving toward the zone is not read as waiting.
The waiting vehicle's purpose of parking in accordance with the restriction is read by the posted sign's conditions holding for it.

'A traffic signal displaying a red or yellow indication or flashing_red' is read as a steady red or yellow indication (circular_red, circular_yellow, red_arrow, yellow_arrow) or flashing_red; flashing_yellow and flashing_yellow_arrow, cautionary indications that require no halt, are not read as a device's direction to halt.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car halts in a restricted_parking curb zone, governed by a parking_restricted zone sign whose class condition the car does not meet, for longer than the standing duration, doors closed.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle meeting the sign's class condition, at a time inside its posted hours, parks in the zone.

scenarios.name: idle

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.name: branch_1

scenarios.name: branch_2

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source (sensor or simulator specification)

param_proposals.name: p.queue_halt_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies to a road user ahead in the same lane within which a halt is a halt behind other traffic: the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue
param_proposals.source: HCM queue spacing of stopped vehicles

param_proposals.convention: the longest halt counted as receiving or discharging passengers or loading rather than standing: a passenger pick-up dwell at the curb

param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book design vehicle dimensions; HCM queue spacing

segmentation.text: Any lighted headlamps
upon a parked vehicle
shall be depressed or dimmed.

elements.justification: sig.headlamp, 'headlamp state in {off, low_beam, high_beam}': lighted headlamps are a state other than off.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, one ru.aggregate atom. 'parked' is drv.motion.parked, 'Road user a is parked: "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not", observed as a at rest at every observation of the window behind', as the index maps 'parked' (NRS_484B_473_2).
Depressed or dimmed headlamps are the low beam: sig.headlamp state low_beam, not high_beam; as the index maps 'such lights shall be depressed or dimmed' (NRS_484B_473_2).

NRS_484D_165_4.applicability: The subject is a member of the vehicle aggregate, drv.motion.parked holds for it (speed tolerance p.halt_speed_tolerance, duration p.parking_min_duration), and its headlamps are lit (sig.headlamp low_beam or high_beam) at the observation.
NRS_484D_165_4.obligation: The subject's headlamps are on low beam (sig.headlamp low_beam) at the observation.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the headlamps are on low beam.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car has stood at rest at the curb for five minutes with its headlamps off.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car has stood at rest at the curb for five minutes; the source does not observe headlamps.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car halts for twenty seconds in traffic with high beams on: a halt shorter than the parking duration is not parked.

param_proposals.source: sensor speed resolution of the acquisition standard

segmentation.text: The prima facie speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour
on all streets and highways
unless a different speed limit is posted as set forth in this Title

elements.justification: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s is the speed the limit bounds; its exclusion of acceleration does not apply. A speed limit binds the vehicle travelling there: the subject is a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle).

st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'; streets (DEF-NRS-484A-265, highways inside a city) and highways together are every highway, so the city limit, a legal region class, is not needed. The subject is on one where its footprint overlaps it (rel.occupies). st.highway 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' does not apply: the words name the whole way.

dev.speed_limit_sign 'sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit; kind ∈ {maximum, minimum, structure_maximum, zone}': a posted limit is a sign of kind maximum, structure_maximum or zone governing (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies. 'posted as set forth in this Title' is the legal status of the posting, read through the sign's presence. A minimum is no different speed limit in the sense of a maximum replacing the prima facie one.

LVMC_11_16_060.applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), occupies a highway region w (st.highway); and no speed limit sign of kind maximum, structure_maximum or zone governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies.
LVMC_11_16_060.obligation: The subject's kin.speed is at most twenty-five miles per hour.

narrowings.why: a prima facie limit is read as a maximum: a speed above it is reported violated; the rebuttal a court may admit is not modelled
'posted as set forth in this Title' is read through the presence of the posted speed limit sign governing the subject's travel region

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Subject on a street lane governed by no speed limit sign travels above twenty-five mph.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, at or below twenty-five mph.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject's lane is governed by a maximum speed limit sign (45 mph posting).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A speed limit sign is present but the source does not observe what it governs; subject above twenty-five mph.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:
To fail to obey an official traffic-control device or the directions of a police officer
at a railroad crossing.

elements.justification: "vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"; "driver" (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

"Official traffic-control device" (DEF-NRS-484A-145) is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic"; at a railroad crossing its members that direct the subject's entry are dev.railway_signal_or_gate ("the devices at a level crossing; lights in {flashing, dark}; gate in {up, lowering, down, raising, none}": obeyed by not entering while the lights flash or the gate is not up), dev.traffic_signal (circular_red: not entering), dev.stop_sign ("regulatory sign requiring a full halt": a halt, drv.motion.complete_halt, on the approach short of the crossing, within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach by st.region_geometry) and dev.yield_sign ("requiring yielding without a mandatory halt": not entering while a rail vehicle, ru.rail_vehicle, closes within the conflict horizon — prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance, which are "not a stand-in for contact" and are read only as the conflict bound). "Police officer" (DEF-NRS-484A-180, "every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic") is dev.human_direction of role police_officer; its indication stop is obeyed by not entering. Each device must govern (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies) at its entry; dev.governs is not a position, and the place of the halt is read from the distance to the crossing.

The device or direction is obeyed at a railroad crossing: the event judged is the subject's entry into a st.railway_crossing, "level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail", the observation at which its footprint comes to overlap it (rel.occupies) having not overlapped it at the previous one. "Railroad" (DEF-NRS-484A-200) excludes streetcars, which form no level crossing of a railway with the roadway.

NRS_484B_560_7b.applicability: The subject is a vehicle and enters a railroad crossing c at this observation: rises(rel.occupies(subject, c)) for some st.railway_crossing c.
NRS_484B_560_7b.obligation: At the entry observation, for every device d that governs (dev.governs) a travel region r the subject occupies at that observation: (i) d a dev.railway_signal_or_gate: its lights are not flashing and its gate is not lowering, down or raising; (ii) d a dev.traffic_signal: it does not display circular_red; (iii) d a dev.human_direction of role police_officer: its indication is not stop; (iv) d a dev.yield_sign: no rail vehicle q (ru.rail_vehicle) has prim.closest_approach_within(subject, q) over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance at most p.conflict_centre_clearance; (v) d a dev.stop_sign: the subject halted before this entry. For (v) the search runs back from the entry: a halt counts at an observation where drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) holds with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, the subject's footprint does not overlap c, and its body is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach of c (st.region_geometry). The search ends at the last observation before the entry at which the subject's body was farther from c than p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach (the approach start: only an observed exit from that zone begins a new approach), or at the previous entry of the subject into c. Finding the halt meets the duty; reaching either end without it violates it; where the recording begins with the subject already within the reach of c and no halt is observed since, or the distance to c is unobserved at an observation the search reads and no halt is found, the duty is unknown. Where no device governs a region the subject occupies at the entry, the duty is complied with.

narrowings.why: "the driver" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; whoever or whatever controls it.
That a device is official, placed by a public authority or railroad, is read from its presence.

Obedience is read at the subject's entry into the crossing, through the devices and directions that govern that entry (railway lights and gate, a red signal, a stop or yield sign, a police officer's stop); instructions that do not bear on entering the crossing, and a direction to proceed, are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Railway signal lights flashing, gate down, governing the subject's approach lane; the subject car drives around the gate and its footprint comes to overlap the railway crossing.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Railway signal lights dark, gate up, governing the subject's lane; the subject car enters the crossing.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives along a street with no railway crossing; it never overlaps one.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car enters a crossing; a railway signal with lights flashing stands at the crossing but the source does not observe which regions it governs.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the subject's lane at the crossing; the subject car approaches from 60 m, halts 6 m from the crossing (kin.speed 0), then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the subject's lane; the subject approaches from 60 m and enters the crossing at 8 m/s without halting.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A police officer (dev.human_direction role police_officer, indication stop) governs the subject's lane; the subject enters the crossing.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: The subject enters an unsignalled crossing with no device governing its lane; no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the subject's lane; the recording begins with the subject 10 m from the crossing moving at 3 m/s, no halt is observed, and it enters the crossing.
scenarios.boundary: the subject's approach to the crossing from beyond p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach, which lies before the recording's first observation

param_proposals.name: p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a vehicle's body to a railroad grade crossing within which the vehicle is at the crossing, on the stretch where a halt for the crossing is made: the 50-ft outer bound of the zone in which grade-crossing practice places the halt before the nearest rail
param_proposals.source: MUTCD Part 8 highway-rail grade crossing stop-line placement and the Uniform Vehicle Code grade-crossing stop zone

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of vehicle tracking sources

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car design dimensions

segmentation.text: It shall be unlawful for any person to operate
a bicycle
at a speed greater than
is reasonable and prudent under the conditions then existing

elements.justification: kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity'. To operate a bicycle is read through its controlled motion (ontology, what is not an atom: 'operates' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion): the rule applies while the bicycle moves, its speed above the halt tolerance.

'bicycle' is admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride ... except a moped'); ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. Claimed as the aggregate, never expanded into classes.
kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity', m/s; the speed the words compare with the reasonable and prudent bound. Not a stand-in for acceleration: none is read.

operationalizations.standard: a speed reasonable and prudent under the conditions then existing
operationalizations.convention: bicycle stopping-sight-distance model: the distance travelled during the perception-reaction time plus the braking distance at a deceleration set by the surface does not exceed the distance ahead the rider can see; the surface (dry, wet or precipitation, ice or snow) selects the deceleration, and darkness caps the distance seen at the reach of a bicycle headlamp

LVMC_11_40_130.applicability: The subject belongs to the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle and moves: its speed (kin.speed) is above p.halt_speed_tolerance.
LVMC_11_40_130.obligation: At each such observation the subject's stopping distance does not exceed the distance it can see ahead. Stopping distance: speed times p.bicycle_reaction_time plus speed squared over twice the deceleration, where the deceleration is p.bicycle_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.bicycle_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.bicycle_decel_dry (a selection among bounds, Term.cond). Distance seen: env.visibility, and where env.darkness holds the smaller of env.visibility and p.bicycle_lamp_reach. Written as a product bound (speed squared at most twice the deceleration times the distance seen minus the reaction distance), so no measured atom is a divisor. Surrogate: its verdict is evidence, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'any person to operate' is read through the bicycle's controlled motion: a bicycle moving on the road is taken to be operated, whoever rides it.

The catch-all 'the conditions then existing' is read only through the contracts the operationalization names: visibility, the wet, precipitation and ice states of the surface, and darkness. Other conditions (the sight distance a bend or a crest leaves, the presence and density of pedestrians and other traffic, grade, the bicycle's own condition) are not read, so a speed made unreasonable only by them is not detected.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides fast in dense fog: env.visibility is far shorter than the reaction distance plus the dry braking distance at its speed.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides at a moderate speed on a dry road in daylight with long visibility and sight distance, its stopping distance well inside both.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The bicycle stands at rest at a signal: its speed is at the halt tolerance.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The bicycle rides at a speed whose verdict depends on the visibility, which the source does not observe.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: On an icy road in light mist the bicycle rides at a speed whose stopping distance at the ice deceleration exceeds the visibility, though the dry stopping distance would not.

param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

param_proposals.name: p.bicycle_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: perception-reaction time of a bicyclist in the stopping-sight-distance model

param_proposals.name: p.bicycle_decel_wet

param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (2012), stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.bicycle_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.05)

segmentation.text: A person
shall not bring a vehicle to a complete stop
upon a roadway
so as to impede or block the normal and reasonable movement of
traffic
unless the stop is necessary
for safe operation
or in compliance with law.

elements.justification: Reuses the index mapping of 'A person' (LVMC_11_22_010): the person who brings a vehicle to a stop is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the class is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, 'membership of a legal aggregate', not the role of driving.

A complete stop is the concept drv.motion.complete_halt: 'The road user is at rest at the observation — "complete cessation from movement" — observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance the caller sets', filled with p.halt_speed_tolerance. Of the two stop definitions the run leaves ambiguous, DEF-NRS-484A-255 ('complete cessation from movement') and DEF-NRS-484A-260 ('any halting, even momentarily'), both denote this halt; the concept says nothing of how long the vehicle stays at rest, so a momentary halt is read too. 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

Upon a roadway: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', which is DEF-NRS-484A-220 ('improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder'); 'Not a stand-in for: the sidewalk' — a halt on the shoulder or in a bay is not on the roadway.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'); the traffic whose movement is impeded is a traffic road user behind the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) at a body gap (rel.surface_gap) the operationalization of x4 bounds.

Safe operation requires the stop where the subject halts behind a road user ahead of it in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within a queue gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap), or where some road user is predicted to come close to it (prim.closest_approach_within, prim.closest_approach_distance; 'Not a stand-in for ... the danger of a crash' alone, the bound being the operationalization of x6).

Extends the index mapping of 'or in compliance with law' (NRS_484B_450_1a: dev.governs, dev.stop_sign, dev.traffic_signal, rel.occupies, st.travel_region) with the other controls whose indication requires a halt, as the mapping of 'shall not: Stop, stand or park a vehicle' (NRS_484B_477_1a) reads them: a stop sign (dev.stop_sign, 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt'), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign, 'requiring yielding without a mandatory halt', where a halt is how the yield is given), a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), a person directing traffic with indication stop (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard or railroad_flagger), or railway lights flashing or a gate not up (dev.railway_signal_or_gate), governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position', and no position is read from it.

operationalizations.standard: so as to impede or block the normal and reasonable movement of traffic
operationalizations.convention: Queue convention: the halt impedes or blocks traffic where a traffic road user is behind the halted subject in the same lane with the gap between bodies within p.rear_signal_reach (immediately to the rear) and that road user is itself at rest (complete halt within p.halt_speed_tolerance: blocked) or decelerating at p.speed_decrease_decel_min or more (impeded).

operationalizations.standard: the stop is necessary for safe operation
operationalizations.convention: Queue spacing and the traffic-conflict technique: the stop is necessary where a road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane with the body gap within p.queue_halt_gap (the subject halts behind other traffic), or where some road user's centre is predicted to come within p.conflict_centre_clearance of the subject's within p.conflict_horizon.

NRS_484B_627_2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) occupying a roadway.
NRS_484B_627_2.obligation: Violated where the subject is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) and some traffic road user other than the subject is behind it in the same lane with the body gap within p.rear_signal_reach and is at rest or decelerating at p.speed_decrease_decel_min or more; except where (a) some road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane with the body gap within p.queue_halt_gap, or some road user's closest approach to the subject lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or (b) a control requiring a halt governs a travel region the subject occupies: a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, a person directing traffic with indication stop, or railway crossing lights flashing or a gate not up. A moving subject, or one halted with no traffic held behind it, complies.

narrowings.why: 'A person' who brings the vehicle to a stop is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
'the normal and reasonable movement of traffic' is read only through traffic behind the subject in its own lane, halted or decelerating; traffic in other lanes is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car halts mid-block in a roadway lane with no road user ahead, no road user in predicted conflict and no stop sign or signal; a car behind it in the same lane halts 4 m behind.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same halt, but a bus is halted 3 m ahead of the car in its lane: the car halts behind other traffic.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car halts in a parking space off the roadway with a car passing behind it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not supply the in-lane ahead/behind relation, so neither the follower held behind nor the absence of a vehicle ahead is observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a stop sign governs the lane the car occupies.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car halts in a roadway lane with no other road user in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.rear_signal_reach
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies within which a following vehicle in the same lane is immediately to the rear of a vehicle: two seconds of headway at an urban speed of about 15 m/s
param_proposals.source: two-second headway rule of driver manuals

param_proposals.name: p.speed_decrease_decel_min
param_proposals.convention: the longitudinal deceleration at or beyond which a sampled acceleration counts as a decrease of speed rather than noise or rolling resistance: the acceleration resolution of the source
param_proposals.source: IMU and trajectory acceleration resolution

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source

param_proposals.name: p.queue_halt_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies to a road user ahead in the same lane within which a halt is a halt behind other traffic: the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue
param_proposals.source: queue spacing of halted vehicles (jam density)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique (Hyden; time-to-collision thresholds)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger car design dimensions

segmentation.text: A person shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle
for any purpose or length of time
other than for the expeditious
unloading and delivery or pickup and loading of materials
in any place marked as a freight curb loading zone
during hours when the provisions applicable to such zones are in effect.
The driver of a vehicle
may stop temporarily
at a place marked as a freight curb loading zone
for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading passengers,
when such stopping does not interfere with
any motor vehicle used for the transportation of materials
which is waiting to enter or about to enter such zone.

elements.justification: 'Stop' when prohibited is 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-260, the definition the table resolves for 'stopping' in this law); 'stand' is 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not' (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and 'park' 'the standing of a vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-155): together a halt, drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation ... its speed at or below a tolerance', p.halt_speed_tolerance). The definition's exclusions are carried beside it: a halt with another road user ahead in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within p.queue_halt_gap of the body (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', not a centre distance) avoids conflict with other traffic; a halt on a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing red or yellow, a railway signal flashing or a gate not up, or a police officer's stop indication (dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.traffic_signal, dev.railway_signal_or_gate, dev.human_direction) complies with a device or an officer. 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

The purpose 'unloading and delivery or pickup and loading of materials' is read by the conduct it explains: a halt (drv.motion.complete_halt) during which a door of the vehicle is open (sig.door_open, 'a door open'), made by a vehicle built or licensed to carry goods (ru.truck, 'motor vehicle for carrying goods, with a body built for that purpose'; ru.commercial_motor_vehicle, 'vehicle over the jurisdiction's commercial mass class or marked as commercially licensed'), which tells the loading of materials from the loading of passengers that s10 excepts on its own terms. The freight zone is 'for the exclusive use of vehicles during the loading or unloading of freight' (DEF-NRS-484B-023).

'Freight curb loading zone' is 'a space adjacent to a curb for the exclusive use of vehicles during the loading or unloading of freight' (DEF-NRS-484B-023): st.curb_zone of kind freight_loading, 'a signed or marked length of curb', which the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies). The marking is the evidence of the designation.

The hours of the zone are those its posting states: a zone sign of kind parking_restricted (dev.zone_sign, with its 'conditions attribute ... a list of time windows'; an unrestricted legend is 'the empty set (unconditional)') governing (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies); whether its hours hold now is prim.conditions_hold, never the sign itself (dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now').

'Driver' is 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-080): a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion; 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. The driver is the subject's own vehicle.
The same freight_loading curb zone (st.curb_zone, 'a signed or marked length of curb') the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), re-bound with the selection of s5.

The purpose and engagement 'in loading or unloading passengers' are read by the conduct: a door of the halted vehicle (drv.motion.complete_halt) open (sig.door_open, 'a door open') during the halt, the act through which passengers board or alight.

'Motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'); a motor vehicle 'used for the transportation of materials' is the class whose contract is exactly that: ru.truck, 'motor vehicle for carrying goods, with a body built for that purpose', carried beside the aggregate, not in place of it.

'Waiting to enter or about to enter such zone' is read by the conduct: the goods vehicle does not overlap the zone (rel.occupies, st.curb_zone of kind freight_loading, the zone of s5) and is halted (drv.motion.complete_halt) with the ground distance from its body to the zone (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') within p.zone_entry_wait_reach. The relation is the distance the words imply ('waiting to enter'), not a belonging.

operationalizations.standard: expeditious
operationalizations.convention: commercial loading zone time limit: a halt counts as expeditious loading or unloading of materials while it has not lasted as long as the thirty-minute limit common to commercial loading zones, i.e. while the subject is not at rest at every observation of a window of length p.commercial_loading_max_halt behind the observation (drv.motion.parked)

operationalizations.standard: temporarily
operationalizations.convention: curbside passenger pick-up dwell: a stop counts as temporary while it has not lasted as long as a passenger pick-up dwell, i.e. while the subject is not at rest at every observation of a window of length p.standing_min_duration behind the observation (drv.motion.parked)

operationalizations.standard: does not interfere with
operationalizations.convention: queueing at a curb space: a stop interferes with a goods vehicle where, at some observation of the stop so far, that vehicle stands halted outside the zone within one passenger-car length plus a queue spacing of it (p.zone_entry_wait_reach), the place a vehicle waits to take the space

residues.why: 'For any purpose or length of time' excludes no halt: every halt is within the prohibition whatever its purpose and length, so the duty is the same whether or not these words are read.

NRS_484B_507_1.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a curb zone z of kind freight_loading (st.curb_zone), and the zone's provisions are in effect: every zone sign of kind parking_restricted (dev.zone_sign) that governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies has its conditions holding for the subject (prim.conditions_hold); where no such sign governs, the marked zone is read as in effect at all hours.
NRS_484B_507_1.obligation: Wherever the subject occupies such a zone z in effect (selected again as in the applicability), the subject is not halted (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), except a halt that is (a) to avoid conflict with other traffic: some other road user is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; or (b) in compliance with a device or an officer: a travel region the subject occupies is governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal displaying a red or yellow indication or flashing_red, a railway signal or gate with lights flashing or gate not up, or a person in the role police_officer giving the indication stop; or (c) expeditious loading of materials: the subject is a truck or a commercial motor vehicle (ru.truck or ru.commercial_motor_vehicle), it is not parked with min_duration p.commercial_loading_max_halt (drv.motion.parked), and a door of the subject is open (sig.door_open) at some observation of the same halt, before or after the observation; or (d) a temporary stop for passengers: the subject is not parked with min_duration p.standing_min_duration, a door of the subject is open at some observation of the same halt, before or after the observation, and at no observation of the halt up to the judged one is there a road user other than the subject that is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) and a truck (ru.truck), whose footprint does not overlap z, which is halted (drv.motion.complete_halt), and whose body's ground distance to z (st.region_geometry) is at most p.zone_entry_wait_reach.

narrowings.why: 'A person shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion.
'The driver of a vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion.

The loading or delivery of materials is read by the conduct it explains: a door open during the halt of a truck or a commercial motor vehicle; a delivery made from a passenger car is not told from a passenger pick-up and is judged under the passenger exception.
The purpose of and engagement in loading or unloading passengers are read by a door of the halted vehicle open during the halt.

'Waiting to enter or about to enter' is read by the conduct it leads to: a goods vehicle halted outside the zone within the waiting reach of it; one still moving toward the zone is not read as waiting.
'Marked as' a freight curb loading zone is read from the presence of the curb zone of that kind.

'A traffic signal displaying a red or yellow indication or flashing_red' is read as the circular indications circular_red and circular_yellow and flashing_red; a red or yellow arrow, which controls only the movement it points to, is not read as requiring the halt.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car halts inside a freight_loading curb zone that no sign governs, for longer than the standing duration, doors closed; no road user ahead and no stop control governs its lane.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A truck halts in the zone with its curb-side door open and moves off before the commercial loading duration has elapsed.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car halts at a curb where there is no curb zone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car halts in the zone briefly, shorter than the standing duration, and the source does not observe its doors.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car halts briefly in the zone with a door open while a truck stands halted just outside the zone, within the waiting reach of it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A passenger car halts briefly in the zone with a door open; no other road user is in the scene.

param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source (sensor or simulator specification)

param_proposals.name: p.queue_halt_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies to a road user ahead in the same lane within which a halt is a halt behind other traffic: the spacing of halted vehicles in a queue
param_proposals.source: HCM queue spacing of stopped vehicles

param_proposals.name: p.commercial_loading_max_halt
param_proposals.convention: the longest halt of a commercial vehicle counted as expeditious loading or unloading of goods or passengers: the thirty-minute limit common to commercial loading zones
param_proposals.source: municipal commercial loading zone time limits

segmentation.text: The Department of Transportation, and local authorities with the approval of the Department of Transportation, may designate dangerous highway grade crossings of railroads
and erect official traffic-control devices at such crossings directing a stop.
When such stop signs are erected
the driver of any vehicle
shall stop within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest track of such a grade crossing
and afterward may proceed only
upon exercising due care.

elements.justification: A 'highway grade crossing of a railroad' ('railroad' is 'a carrier of persons or property upon cars ... operated upon stationary rails', DEF-NRS-484A-200) is st.railway_crossing, 'level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail', lying on a highway (st.on_way, 'the public way a structure region lies on'; st.highway). The authority's designation of it as dangerous is evidenced by the stop sign erected for it.
'Official traffic-control devices ... directing a stop' (DEF-NRS-484A-145) are stop signs: dev.stop_sign, 'regulatory sign requiring a full halt'; its presence is the evidence that it is official.

'When such stop signs are erected': the stop sign governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a stand-in for a position) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies) on its approach, lying on the same highway as the crossing (st.on_way).

'Driver' is 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-080), read through the vehicle's controlled motion; 'any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

'Afterward' refers to the stop: 'complete cessation from movement' (DEF-NRS-484A-255), drv.motion.complete_halt, whose contract quotes it, with p.halt_speed_tolerance. The referent is carried in full: the halt itself, at the place the span states, not compliance with the stop rule. The place of that halt: the ground distance from the subject's body to the crossing (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), st.railway_crossing with 'its nearest rail', between the lower and the upper figure the span states (literals), the footprint not yet overlapping the crossing (rel.occupies).

'Proceed' after the halt is the subject's entry into the crossing: its footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the railway crossing (st.railway_crossing), and the duty runs while it occupies it.

operationalizations.standard: due care
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: proceeding across the crossing with due care is read by its outcome: from the entry and while the vehicle occupies the crossing, no rail vehicle (ru.rail_vehicle) approaches it within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within with p.conflict_horizon) to a centre distance below the collision clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance), and the vehicle's body touches no road user (rel.contact)

NRS_484B_557_o2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that has entered a railway crossing x (st.railway_crossing; its footprint overlaps x and did not at the previous observation) from a travel region r (st.travel_region) it occupied at the previous observation, governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign (dev.stop_sign), r and x lying on the same highway h (st.on_way, st.highway), and afterward: on that approach, searched back from the observation before the entry to the last observation at which it was farther than the upper literal of s5 from x or to its previous exit from x, it was halted (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance) at an observation at which it did not overlap x and its body's ground distance to x (st.region_geometry) lay between the lower and the upper literal of s5. The applicability holds at that entry and at every later observation while the subject occupies x without having left it; it is unknown where the search reaches the subject's first observation without a halt or either end.
NRS_484B_557_o2.obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds: no rail vehicle (ru.rail_vehicle) has a closest approach to the subject within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), and the subject is in contact (rel.contact) with no road user.

narrowings.why: 'The driver of any vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion.
The designation of the crossing as dangerous is read from the presence of a stop sign governing the approach to it.
That the device is official and directs a stop is read from the presence of a stop sign.

Due care, a standard about the driver's state of mind, is read only through the outcome of the crossing: no conflict with a rail vehicle and no contact with any road user while on the crossing; the rule is a surrogate and its verdicts are evidence, not a legal conclusion.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car on a lane governed by a stop sign halts between the two figures from the crossing, then enters it while a train closes on it so that their closest approach within the conflict horizon lies below the clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car halts between the two figures, then enters and clears the crossing; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The car enters a railway crossing from a lane that no stop sign governs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The car halts between the two figures and enters the crossing; no train is present, a pedestrian stands on the crossing near its path, and the source does not observe contact.

segmentation.text: No pedestrian
shall cross a roadway
at any place other than by a route at right angles to the curb or by the shortest route to the opposite curb
except in a crosswalk

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); one atom, never expanded.

Crossing a roadway is being on it and moving across it: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', on st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder' (the defined roadway; not the sidewalk or shoulder), and drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos on a carrier k the pedestrian occupies (a lane, st.lane, or the roadway itself), whose designated direction is the direction the curbs run: moving across, not along, the way. Walking along the roadway is not crossing it.

'a route at right angles to the curb' is motion at right angles to the direction the roadway's carriers run, which is the curb's direction: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with cos_max p.right_angle_crossing_cos, the tolerance of 'at right angles' on sampled headings. 'the shortest route to the opposite curb' between curbs that run parallel is the same perpendicular route.
st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', is the defined crosswalk; rel.occupies places the pedestrian in it. Not a sidewalk.

LVMC_11_30_050.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, occupies a roadway (st.roadway), does not occupy a crosswalk (st.crosswalk), and occupies a carrier k (a lane, st.lane, or a roadway) across which it moves: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos.
LVMC_11_30_050.obligation: For each such carrier k, the subject moves at right angles to it: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.right_angle_crossing_cos.

narrowings.why: 'at right angles to the curb' and 'the shortest route to the opposite curb' are read as motion perpendicular, within p.right_angle_crossing_cos, to the designated direction of the lane or roadway the pedestrian occupies, which runs along the curb; where the curbs are not parallel the shortest route may differ from that perpendicular, and a roadway carrying no designated direction (an unlaned two-way roadway) leaves the duty unknown.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses a laned roadway mid-block, away from any crosswalk, walking at 1.4 m/s at 40 degrees off perpendicular to the lane direction.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses the same roadway mid-block walking at 1.4 m/s at 5 degrees off perpendicular to the lane direction.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks along the sidewalk and never occupies the roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian occupies the roadway mid-block, but its velocity is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses diagonally at 40 degrees off perpendicular inside a marked crosswalk.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of road-user tracking in recorded and simulated traces

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: geometric convention separating walking along a roadway from crossing it, from pedestrian heading resolution

param_proposals.name: p.right_angle_crossing_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as at right angles to the curb: within about 15 degrees of perpendicular
param_proposals.source: pedestrian tracking heading resolution and path deviation observed in square crossings

segmentation.text: No pedestrian
shall cross a roadway
other than in a marked crosswalk or within an unmarked crosswalk
in any business district

elements.justification: 'Pedestrian' is admitted as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); ru.aggregate carries 'membership of a legal aggregate' and is claimed as one atom, never expanded into classes. Same words, same atoms as 'No pedestrian' in LVMC_11_30_050.

Same words, same mapping as LVMC_11_30_050. 'a roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; its exclusion (not the sidewalk) does not apply, since only the roadway is read. The pedestrian is on it by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). 'cross' is motion across the designated direction of travel of a lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') or of the roadway the pedestrian occupies: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier ('Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r'); that concept says nothing of occupancy, so occupancy is read beside it. st.lane is not used as a half of the roadway or a lateral position, as its exclusion forbids: only as a carrier of a direction.

'a marked crosswalk or ... an unmarked crosswalk' (DEF-NRS-484A-065: '(1) That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface') is st.crosswalk: 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection (st.intersection); marked attribute'. Both values of the marked attribute are admitted, so the definition's whole extent is kept. 'in' / 'within' is the footprint overlapping the crosswalk: rel.occupies. Same atoms as 'except in a crosswalk' (LVMC_11_30_050).

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district, as the map's reading classifies the area

LVMC_11_30_070_B.applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps a roadway (rel.occupies, st.roadway) at a place the reading declares to lie in a business district (asm.business_district), read at the judged observation.
LVMC_11_30_070_B.obligation: At every observation at which the subject occupies a roadway and moves across a lane or roadway it occupies (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos, on a region of kind st.lane or st.roadway the subject occupies), the subject's footprint overlaps a crosswalk (rel.occupies, st.crosswalk, marked or unmarked). Moving across the roadway while occupying no crosswalk is violated; standing on the roadway or moving along it is not a crossing and is compliant here.

narrowings.why: 'cross a roadway' is read at each observation as moving across the designated direction of a lane or roadway the pedestrian occupies (more than p.crossing_motion_cos from it, faster than p.halt_speed_tolerance); a pedestrian standing on the roadway or walking along it is not crossing and is not judged by this rule (LVMC_11_30_090 judges walking along).

segmentation.text: A person
shall
when operating a vehicle
give his full time and attention to the operation of the vehicle

elements.justification: The person is the one operating the vehicle, read through the vehicle's controlled motion; the vehicle is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and ru.aggregate's exclusion of 'who drives or controls a vehicle' is respected: the role is read through motion.

The duty's conduct is checked through its outcome: the vehicle's body does not touch another road user or a structure (rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users, or a road user and a structure, touch or overlap (a collision)'; its exclusion 'a near miss' is respected — the near conflict is the operationalization's bound).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'operating' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance.

operationalizations.standard: full time and attention to the operation of the vehicle
operationalizations.convention: surrogate safety measure for inattention: a driver who attends to the driving task neither collides nor closes on the road user ahead in its lane to a time-to-collision below the rear-end conflict threshold

LVMC_11_22_010.applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), is in motion: its kin.speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance.
LVMC_11_22_010.obligation: The subject is in contact (rel.contact) with no road user and no structure; and for every road user o ahead of the subject in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane): not (prim.closest_approach_within(subject, o; p.attention_ttc_min) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, o; p.attention_ttc_min) below p.conflict_centre_clearance).

narrowings.why: 'operating' is read through the vehicle's motion; a halted vehicle with its engine running is not judged
attention, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome on the road: no collision and no rear-end time-to-collision below the threshold; distraction that shows in no such outcome is not read
contact is read against every other road user only: Core's rel.contact relates two tracks, so the record's 'no structure' limb is not read

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject closes on a halted vehicle ahead in its lane at constant speed; the closest approach falls below the clearance within p.attention_ttc_min.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject follows a vehicle ahead at a steady gap, never closing within the threshold, and touches nothing.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is halted at a signal.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject's speed is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1

param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of a critical rear-end conflict
param_proposals.source: van der Horst (1990) rear-end TTC thresholds

param_proposals.source: passenger-car dimensions (AASHTO design vehicle P: 5.8 m by 2.1 m)

param_proposals.source: speed noise floor of vehicle odometry and tracked-object estimates

segmentation.text: The following regulations pertain to
the operation of vehicles
within a roundabout
The operator of a vehicle
entering a roundabout
shall yield
the right-of-way
to vehicles already in the roundabout
and wait
for a gap
in traffic
before entering

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'operation' read through controlled motion.
st.roundabout 'a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches'; rel.occupies anchors the subject: at its entry it occupies the roundabout.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'The operator' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
Entering is the event at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap the roundabout region (rel.occupies true and false at the observation before).

'wait ... before entering' is a condition on the entry: the subject's footprint comes to overlap the roundabout (rel.occupies of st.roundabout) only where the gap holds; waiting where none holds is staying out of it.

'traffic' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'); the traffic of the gap is the traffic in the roundabout the subject enters (rel.occupies of that st.roundabout region, crosswalks of its entering and exiting roadways included).
'before entering' fixes the moment: the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap the roundabout region, the same event as b5.

operationalizations.standard: a gap in traffic sufficient to enter
operationalizations.convention: gap-acceptance convention of roundabout entry capacity: an entering driver accepts a gap when no road user in the roundabout comes, under constant velocities, within the conflict clearance of it sooner than the critical headway

LVMC_11_43_010_B_o2.applicability: The subject belongs to DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the judged observation it enters an st.roundabout region r: rel.occupies(subject, r) holds there and not at the observation before.
LVMC_11_43_010_B_o2.obligation: At that entry, for every road user u of the scene other than the subject that belongs to DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and occupies r: the subject is not in contact with u (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u; p.roundabout_critical_gap) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u; p.roundabout_critical_gap) below p.conflict_centre_clearance. An entry with no such road user is compliant.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'wait for a gap' is read as entering only at a gap: where a gap is present when the subject arrives no halt is required, and an entry without a gap is the failure to wait.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the roundabout while a pedestrian on one of its crosswalks is on a course whose closest approach to the car comes within the clearance sooner than the critical gap.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car waits at the edge and enters once no road user in the roundabout comes within the clearance of it within the critical gap.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives on a street away from any roundabout.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car at the roundabout's edge beside circulating traffic, where the source does not observe which regions the road users occupy.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car enters an empty roundabout: no other road user is in the scene, and the duty is met.

param_proposals.name: p.roundabout_critical_gap
param_proposals.convention: critical headway of an entering driver at a single-lane roundabout: the shortest time to the next conflicting road user an entering driver accepts
param_proposals.source: Highway Capacity Manual, 6th edition, roundabouts chapter

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car design dimensions (AASHTO Green Book design vehicle)

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate
a vehicle of any kind or character
in a careless or imprudent manner
on any highway
in the City

elements.justification: 'drive or operate' names who controls the vehicle, which no atom observes; per the ontology's section on what is not an atom it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, 'a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven'. kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', tells the moving vehicle (speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) from one at rest; it is used for motion, not as a stand-in for acceleration or a manoeuvre. 'any person' is the one who drives: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.

'vehicle' is a defined term of this law with the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: '“Vehicle” means every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions (human-powered devices, electric bicycles, EPAMDs, electric scooters) made by the reading's classification. 'of any kind or character' adds no restriction and removes none beyond the definition; the aggregate is one atom and is not expanded.

Same words and meaning as the index's 'on a highway' -> rel.occupies, st.highway. st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', which is the defined 'entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority'; it is not the roadway, and the words do not narrow to the roadway. rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' anchors the subject on that highway.

operationalizations.standard: careless or imprudent manner
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: driving is read as careless or imprudent where, while the subject moves, it collides with another road user (rel.contact) or another road user's centre and the subject's, under constant velocities, approach within p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (a critical conflict). Care is a state of mind and the whole duty is this standard, so the rule is a surrogate.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies within the territorial limits of the incorporated city whose ordinances the reading applies, as the map's reading classifies the area

LVMC_11_22_020.applicability: The subject is a member of the vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, its footprint occupies a highway region (st.highway), asm.within_city_limits holds at the observation, and the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance).
LVMC_11_22_020.obligation: No other road user u of the scene (any class) is in contact with the subject (rel.contact), and no other road user u is such that, under constant velocities, the subject's and u's centres approach within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a closest-approach centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance). Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of carelessness, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a moving vehicle is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

'careless or imprudent' is read only through a collision or a critical conflict with another road user; careless conduct that produces neither (inattention, erratic lane keeping with no one near, harsh braking) is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves at 15 m/s on a highway inside the city (asm.within_city_limits declared true) toward a car halted ahead in its lane; at 2 s from the closest approach the projected centre distance is 1 m, and it does not brake.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves at 12 m/s alone on a city highway; no other road user is in the scene, so no contact and no conflict exist.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves in a private parking lot that is no highway region; it occupies no st.highway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves on a city street close behind a slower car with a projected conflict, but the source does not observe region occupancy, so whether it is on a highway is unknown.
