param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of road-user tracking in recorded and simulated traces

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique (Swedish TCT, Hydén 1987): time-to-collision thresholds of 1.5 to 3 s

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design vehicle dimensions (about 5.8 m by 2.1 m)

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red signal alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal

must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection,
and,
except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (c) and (d) [(c) is appended below, NRS-484B-307-8d],
must remain stopped or standing until the green signal is shown.
After complying with the requirement to stop,
vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme right of the highway
may proceed into the intersection
for a right turn
only when the intersecting highway is two-directional or one-way to the right,
or vehicular traffic facing such a signal and situated on the extreme left of a one-way highway
may proceed into the intersection
for a left turn
only when the intersecting highway is one-way to the left,
but must yield
the right-of-way
to pedestrians and other traffic proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady red signal alone is circular_red and no other state (not flashing_red, and no arrow beside it). Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'After complying with the requirement to stop' refers to s3 of this line and requires the halt itself with every qualification s3 states: 'must stop before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made, or in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, then before entering the intersection'. A complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt; DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement') at that place — the stop line (st.stop_line) recorded as marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of), else the crosswalk (st.crosswalk) marking it, else c's entrance end at i (st.intersection) — with the footprint not overlapping the region (rel.occupies), on its upstream side along c's direction (st.lane_direction, sign of prim.region_offset_along) and within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (st.region_geometry), on the approach that ends in this entry: the place, zone and history bound of NRS_484B_307_8a_o1. The halt itself, not compliance with that node, which a composed rule grants where it is not engaged.

'vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'facing such a signal': the steady red head governs (dev.governs) the carrier c the subject occupies (rel.occupies), whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters). 'situated on the extreme right of the highway': c is a lane (st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane'): the rightmost lane. Not a stand-in: lane membership is read from the ordinal, never from a lateral offset.

'may proceed into the intersection': the subject's entry into intersection i (st.intersection), its footprint coming to overlap i (rel.occupies) having occupied at the observation before the travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters); the place at which the intention of s10 is declared. As the index maps 'may proceed straight through or turn right or left' (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'the intersecting highway': each highway region (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines') that i lies on (st.on_way, 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there') other than a highway c lies on. 'two-directional' (DEF-NRS-484B-073, 'an undivided highway upon which vehicles are allowed to proceed in opposite directions'): no median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways') lies on it, and two lanes (st.lane) lying on it carry designated directions (st.lane_direction) whose cosine is below minus p.lane_opposed_direction_cos. 'one-way to the right': at least one lane lies on it and every lane lying on it carries a designated direction to the right of c's designated direction, the cross product of c's direction with the lane's (d_x times l_y minus d_y times l_x) being below minus p.cross_direction_sin_min. Not a stand-in: st.on_way is the way a region lies on, not nearness; st.lane_direction is local to its carrier.

'vehicular traffic facing such a signal': as s8. 'situated on the extreme left': c is a lane (st.lane) of ordinal 1 (st.lane_adjacency, 'ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane'); 'of a one-way highway': the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'), as the index maps 'Upon a highway designated and signposted for one-way traffic' (NRS_484B_220_1). Not a stand-in: lane membership is read from the ordinal, never from an offset.
As s9: the subject's entry into i from c (rel.occupies rising; st.lane_enters; st.travel_region; st.intersection), the place at which the intention of s14 is declared.

'the intersecting highway': each highway region (st.highway) that i lies on (st.on_way) other than a highway c lies on. 'one-way to the left': at least one lane (st.lane) lies on it and every lane lying on it carries a designated direction (st.lane_direction) to the left of c's designated direction, the cross product of c's direction with the lane's being above p.cross_direction_sin_min. Not a stand-in: st.on_way is not nearness.

'must yield': kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') tells a subject that moves on toward the other road user from one that holds back, and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)') is the crash precedence exists to avoid; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s17 reads. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'pedestrians and other traffic': road users of the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian and DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than the subject. 'proceeding': moving, kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'as directed by the signal at the intersection': it overlaps (rel.occupies) intersection i (st.intersection) or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of) of a travel region that enters i (st.lane_enters, st.travel_region), or it occupies a travel region c' entering i that is governed (dev.governs) by a head displaying a green indication (dev.traffic_signal: circular_green or green_arrow). Not a stand-in: st.entrance_of is the recorded association, never a distance.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210, 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance); the subject grants precedence where, while its speed is above the halt tolerance (p.halt_speed_tolerance), no such approach to the other road user arises. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the constant-velocity extrapolation of both road users.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the right at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included
the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

NRS_484B_307_8a_o3.applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, approached intersection i through a travel region c whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs), and entered i (its footprint came to overlap i, having occupied c and not i at the observation before) at an observation at which s displayed a steady red alone (circular_red, no other state), after halting at the place of the stop on that approach (s7: the place, zone and history bound of NRS_484B_307_8a_o1); at that entry either (right) c is a lane whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction, int.right_turn is declared true for the subject at i, and every highway i lies on other than one c lies on is two-directional (no median or divider lies on it; two lanes on it with directions opposed within p.lane_opposed_direction_cos) or one-way to the right (every lane on it points to the right of c's direction by more than p.cross_direction_sin_min); or (left) c is a lane of ordinal 1, the subject's footprint overlaps a one-way roadway, int.left_turn is declared true for the subject at i, and every such highway is one-way to the left. Its footprint has overlapped i at every observation since that entry, the judged one included.
NRS_484B_307_8a_o3.obligation: For every road user p other than the subject that is of the class pedestrian or of the class traffic and is proceeding as directed by the signal at i — its speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance, and either its footprint overlaps i or a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a travel region that enters i, or it occupies a travel region c' entering i governed by a head that displays circular_green or a green_arrow: it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while the closest approach of the two centres lies within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject's body does not touch p's (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'proceeding as directed by the signal at the intersection' is read through the signal state governing the other road user's approach (a green indication) where it approaches, and through its presence within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk where it is there; a road user that entered against its own red and is now within the intersection is yielded to as well.

segmentation.text: Persons riding bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
upon a roadway
shall not ride more than two abreast
except on paths or parts of roadways set aside for the exclusive use of bicycles, electric bicycles and electric scooters.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregates of the three defined terms, each one ru.aggregate atom ('membership of a legal aggregate'), never expanded; they class the subject and the other riders the obligation counts. 'riding' is read through the device's motion (agency reading).
st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', the extent of DEF-NRS-484A-220; rel.occupies anchors the subject. As the index maps 'upon a roadway'.

Riding abreast is riding side by side in a row: rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)', at or above zero; travelling the same way, rel.same_direction, 'headings aligned'; in one row, the body gap rel.surface_gap ('distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the spacing of riders side by side. Riding is moving: not drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation'). More than two abreast is the subject and two other riders of the s1 aggregates so placed. longitudinal_overlap is used as the projection it is, not as a contact or distance; surface_gap is the body gap itself.

'paths or parts of roadways set aside for the exclusive use of bicycles, electric bicycles and electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; rel.occupies anchors the subject on it: the riding the words except is the subject's own riding, on such a facility. The three device words name the users the facility is reserved for, the kind's own contract, not road users the duty counts.

NRS_484B_777_3.applicability: The subject is a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregate, is moving (not drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), its footprint overlaps a roadway, and it overlaps no bicycle lane or path at the observation.
NRS_484B_777_3.obligation: At the observation there are no two road users b and c, distinct from each other and from the subject, each a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregate and moving (not drv.motion.complete_halt), such that for each of the three pairs among subject, b and c the bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) with headings aligned (rel.same_direction, p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos), and at least two of the three pairs have a body gap (rel.surface_gap) at most p.abreast_gap_max.

narrowings.why: 'Persons riding' is read through the devices' controlled motion, whoever controls them.

Abreast is read as side by side, travelling the same way and in one row, the row being two of the three pairs within the riders' side-by-side spacing; riders side by side but lanes apart are not abreast.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within a business or residence district
emerging or entering an alley, driveway or building
shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to
driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway or driveway
yielding
the right-of-way
to any pedestrian
as may be necessary to avoid collision
and
upon entering the roadway
shall yield
the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on said roadway

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'The driver of' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

As LVMC_11_20_060_o1: st.driveway_or_alley_entrance 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway', st.alley 'a narrow way within a block'; a building's vehicle access is a driveway (DEF-NRS-484A-190 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel'); the subject occupies one (rel.occupies).

The yielding accompanies driving onto the sidewalk: the duty runs while the subject occupies the sidewalk region s (st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', whose exclusion 'a crosswalk' does not apply; rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... sidewalk ...)'). While it waits before the sidewalk it is halted, and the stop itself is LVMC_11_20_060_o1's duty.

To yield is not to proceed in preference: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells a subject still proceeding; rel.contact 'touch or overlap (a collision)' is precedence taken outright; its exclusion 'a near miss' is respected (the near conflict is bounded by the operationalizations).
'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'any' = every member present.

operationalizations.standard: right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: danger of a crash where the constant-velocity closest approach of centres is below a centre clearance within a time-to-collision horizon

operationalizations.standard: as may be necessary to avoid collision
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: yielding is necessary exactly where a collision would follow under constant velocities, a closest approach below the centre clearance within the horizon

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district or a residence district, as the map's reading classifies the area

LVMC_11_20_060_o2.applicability: asm.business_or_residence_district holds; the subject, a vehicle, occupies a driveway-or-alley-entrance region or an alley region d (st.driveway_or_alley_entrance or st.alley), and occupies a sidewalk region s (st.sidewalk).
LVMC_11_20_060_o2.obligation: For every road user p, other than the subject, that is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): not (the subject's kin.speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance), and not rel.contact(subject, p).

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
precedence is read as the subject not proceeding while a constant-velocity closest approach to the pedestrian falls below the centre clearance within the horizon, and never touching the pedestrian

segmentation.text: Upon a highway designated and signposted for one-way traffic
a vehicle
shall be driven only in the direction designated.

elements.justification: st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction', occupied by the subject (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'), as the index maps 'Upon any highway on which traffic is restricted to one direction of movement' (NRS_484B_210_1). 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel', whose direction the designation restricts. 'Designated and signposted' is legal status: the one-way roadway's presence on the road is its evidence (observable_reading status).

'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

'Only in the direction designated' forbids motion against the one-way roadway's designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — ... a roadway, one-way roadway'): drv.motion.moving_against_carrier(subject, r) on the one-way roadway r of s1, with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance. 'Driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

NRS_484B_220_1.applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a one-way roadway r (st.one_way_roadway).
NRS_484B_220_1.obligation: At every such observation, for every one-way roadway r the subject occupies, the subject is not moving against r's designated direction: drv.motion.moving_against_carrier(subject, r) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance does not hold.

'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it

'only in the direction designated' is read as no motion component against the designated direction beyond the speed resolution; motion across the roadway (entering or leaving it) is not read as a breach

segmentation.text: Every person operating a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
upon a roadway shall, except:
(a) When traveling at a lawful rate of speed
commensurate with the speed of
any nearby traffic;
(b) When preparing to turn left;
or
(c) When doing so would not be safe,
ride as near to the right side of the roadway
as practicable,
exercising due care
when passing a standing vehicle or one proceeding in the same direction.

For purposes of paragraph (c) of subsection 1, the conditions under which it is not safe to operate a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter as near to the right side of the roadway as practicable include, without limitation:
(a) When fixed or moving objects, parked or moving vehicles, bicycles, pedestrians, animals or surface hazards impede access to the right side of the roadway.
(b) When a lane is too narrow for a bicycle and a vehicle to travel safely side by side within the lane.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregates of the three defined terms, each one ru.aggregate atom ('membership of a legal aggregate'), never expanded; 'person operating' read through controlled motion (agency reading).

st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', is the extent of DEF-NRS-484A-220; rel.occupies anchors the subject ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'), as the index maps 'upon a roadway'. The exceptions 'except:' introduces qualify the keep-right duty (sibling spans, see PLAN).

'passing ... a vehicle' from the rear is drv.interaction.overtake_pass: 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; its contract 'says nothing of ... whether b moves', so it covers a standing and a moving b. 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'standing' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, not an aggregate): 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers', read as b at rest, drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation'), the passenger purpose being unobservable (observable_reading purpose). 'one proceeding in the same direction' is b moving (kin.speed above the tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, 'headings aligned').

operationalizations.standard: exercising due care when passing
operationalizations.convention: Due care is a standard of the rider's state of mind; it is bounded by the clearance kept while passing. At every observation of the pass at which the two bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) the bodies do not touch (rel.contact) and the lateral component of their body gap (rel.surface_gap) is at least p.door_swing_reach where the passed vehicle is at rest (the reach of a door opened into the rider's path) and at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap where it moves (the bicyclist's operating-space sway beyond its body width); the bound is selected by the passed vehicle's motion at each such observation.

NRS_484B_777_1_o2.applicability: The subject is a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregate, and at the observation drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b) is recognized (window p.overtake_window, heading tolerance p.overtake_same_direction_cos) for some road user b of the vehicle aggregate, the subject's footprint having overlapped a roadway at some observation since the act began.
NRS_484B_777_1_o2.obligation: For each such b: at every observation since the act began (the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned) up to the recognition at which the two bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), rel.contact between the subject and b is false and the lateral component of rel.surface_gap is at least the clearance selected there: p.door_swing_reach where b is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance), p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap where b moves with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos). Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of care, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'person operating' is read through the device's controlled motion, whoever controls it.
'standing' is read as the passed vehicle at rest: the definition's exclusion of a halt for receiving or discharging passengers turns on a purpose no atom observes, so every halt is read as standing.
Due care, the whole obligation, is read only as the clearance kept and the absence of contact while alongside the passed vehicle; the rider's attention and its speed while passing are not read.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not follow another vehicle
more closely than is reasonable and prudent, having due regard for the speed of such vehicles and the traffic upon and the condition of the highway.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'; 'vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'Driver' is a relational role the contract excludes from membership; it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Same words as 'The driver of a vehicle' (LVMC_11_20_060_o1).

'follow another vehicle': rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction', with the other road user ahead of the subject; the other is a vehicle, ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, never a class list.

operationalizations.standard: more closely than is reasonable and prudent, having due regard for the speed of such vehicles and the traffic upon and the condition of the highway
operationalizations.convention: Car-following stopping-distance convention: the longitudinal component of the body gap to each vehicle ahead in the lane (rel.surface_gap) is at least the subject's speed times a time headway, plus the difference of the two vehicles' braking distances (subject speed squared minus the followed vehicle's speed squared, over twice a braking deceleration). The speeds of both vehicles enter the bound by degree; the condition of the highway selects the headway and the deceleration: icy or snow-covered surface (env.ice_or_snow) the _ice pair, else a wet surface or falling rain (env.wet_road or env.precipitation) the _wet pair, else the _dry pair. Headways from the driver-manual following-time rules; decelerations from tyre-road friction tables.

NRS_484B_127_1.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle).
NRS_484B_127_1.obligation: For every road user b that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane): the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap(subject, b) is at least speed(subject) × H + (speed(subject)² − speed(b)²) / (2 × D), where H and D are p.following_headway_ice and p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet and p.following_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry and p.following_decel_dry (written with Term.cond). Violated at an observation where some such b is closer.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'the traffic upon … the highway' is read only through the followed vehicle and its speed, the part of the traffic the following distance answers to; the density of other traffic is not read. 'the condition of the highway' is read only through its surface (wet, icy or snow-covered, or rain falling); grade, curvature and surface damage are not read.

segmentation.text: Every vehicle
driven upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section
or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn,
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.

elements.justification: 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. No named class stands in for it.

DEF-NRS-484A-070: 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section'. st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'; st.median_or_divider: 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'; st.on_way: 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, shoulder, crosswalk, stop line, median or any other part of it' ties the divider to the highway h; rel.occupies anchors the subject on h ('on a highway' maps the same way in the index). The definition's 'constructed so as to impede the conflict' states the divider's purpose and is read through its presence. 'Driven' is read through the vehicle's motion.

Each roadway of a divided highway carries one direction of travel (st.roadway: 'separate roadways of a divided highway are separate'); the right-hand roadway is the one whose designated direction the vehicle travels with. Being driven on a roadway of h (rel.occupies, st.on_way) other than the right-hand one is moving against that roadway's designated direction: drv.motion.moving_against_carrier 'Road user a moves against the designated direction of travel of carrier region r' (proposed this iteration), with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance. The concept reads st.lane_direction and kin.velocity; it is not a stand-in for heading, so a vehicle pointing either way is judged by its motion.

st.median_or_divider carries an 'opening attribute where a crossover exists': 'through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space' is the subject's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a divider region of h that carries the opening attribute.

A crossover is a divider region with the opening attribute ('opening attribute where a crossover exists'); an intersection is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; rel.occupies places the subject at it. 'Established by a public authority' (DEF-NRS-484A-195) is a legal status read through the feature's presence.

NRS_484B_227_1_o1.applicability: At every observation at which the subject occupies a highway h (st.highway) on which a median_or_divider region lies (st.on_way), except where the subject's footprint overlaps a divider region lying on h that carries the opening attribute (an opening or a crossover), or an intersection lying on h.
NRS_484B_227_1_o1.obligation: Re-binding h as in the applicability: for every roadway r lying on h (st.on_way) that the subject's footprint overlaps, drv.motion.moving_against_carrier(subject, r) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance does not hold: the subject is not driven on a roadway of the divided highway against its designated direction. Unknown where r carries no designated direction or the subject's velocity is unobserved.

narrowings.why: 'the right-hand roadway' is read through the designated direction of the roadway the vehicle is on: it is driven on the right-hand roadway where it does not move against that roadway's direction. A source that records no direction on a divider's roadways leaves the duty unknown.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's motion on the highway, whoever or whatever controls it.
'established by a public authority' is a legal status; the crossover or intersection present on the road is its evidence.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A st.median_or_divider lies on highway h; the subject occupies the roadway r of h on the far side of the divider and its kin.velocity runs against r's st.lane_direction: moving_against_carrier holds.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the roadway of h whose st.lane_direction its velocity follows; moving_against_carrier does not hold for any roadway it overlaps.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives against a roadway's direction on a highway on which no st.median_or_divider lies: no divided highway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a roadway of the divided highway h; st.lane_direction is absent on the source, so moving_against_carrier is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject crosses the opposing roadway's edge while its footprint overlaps an intersection lying on h: the exception for an intersection holds.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle:
Shall not back into an intersection, on or over a crosswalk, or around a street corner.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is a defined term whose admitted aggregate is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency narrowing).

'back' is moving backward, drv.motion.moving_backward ('the component of a's velocity along a's heading ... below minus speed_tol'), read from kinematics as kin.gear's contract requires. 'into an intersection' is the footprint coming to overlap an intersection r (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; rel.occupies true at the observation, false at the previous one) while backing; the crosswalk and the stop line are not stand-ins for it, as st.intersection's contract says. 'on or over a crosswalk' is the backing vehicle's footprint overlapping a st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'). 'around a street corner': the corner is where two streets meet; backing around it carries the vehicle through the area 'embraced within the prolongation ... of the lateral curb lines' of the meeting ways (DEF-NRS-484A-105), the st.intersection region, while its heading turns — read as backing with the footprint overlapping r, the heading having changed by at least the turn threshold since the backing within r began (Term.headingSince, integrated from kin.yaw_rate).

NRS_484B_113_2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is backing at the observation: drv.motion.moving_backward(subject) with speed_tol = p.halt_speed_tolerance.
NRS_484B_113_2.obligation: At the observation, none of: (a) for some intersection r (st.intersection), the subject's footprint overlaps r and did not at the previous observation (rel.occupies) — it backs into r; (b) for some crosswalk x (st.crosswalk), the footprint overlaps x (rel.occupies); (c) for some intersection r, the footprint overlaps r and the magnitude of Term.headingSince(subject, p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, ψ) is at least p.turn_heading_min, where ψ = drv.motion.moving_backward(subject) and rel.occupies(subject, r): since it last began backing within r its heading has turned at least by the turn threshold — it backs around the corner.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'back into an intersection' is read as the entry into the intersection while backing; backing straight out of an intersection the vehicle is already in is not backing into it.

'around a street corner' is read through the intersection region the corner bounds, with a heading change of at least p.turn_heading_min while backing within it; the city-limit qualifier of 'street' (DEF-NRS-484A-265) is not read, every intersection's corners being treated as street corners.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car backs at 2 m/s along a street and its footprint comes to overlap the intersection while backing.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car backs at 2 m/s mid-block, away from any intersection or crosswalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives forward through an intersection and over its crosswalks without ever backing.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car's footprint comes to overlap an intersection while the source supplies no velocity, so whether it was backing is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car backs over a marked mid-block crosswalk: its footprint overlaps the crosswalk while backing.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car that overshot into the intersection backs straight out of it, heading unchanged, on an approach with no crosswalk: it is not entering the intersection and its heading has not turned.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A car standing within the intersection backs around the corner into the cross street, its heading turning 80 degrees while its footprint still overlaps the intersection.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1; turning-movement classification in trajectory analysis

segmentation.text: The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to mark and maintain with yellow paint or road buttons crosswalks approximately twelve feet in width at intersections in the vicinity of schools where in the opinion of the City Traffic Engineer crossing the roadway by schoolchildren is unsafe.

The City Traffic Engineer, if necessary, is further authorized to mark and maintain with a distinguishing color or road buttons upon the pavement or by signs erected along the curb in a conspicuous manner, the words "School-Xing," not less than one hundred feet in advance of each crosswalk established
and
it shall be unlawful for the operator of any vehicle to drive into a crosswalk
where there is displayed a sign with the words "School-Xing,"
when there is in the crosswalk
upon the side of the roadway on which said vehicle is coming
any person
attempting to cross the street

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'the operator of' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency), never as membership. 'drive into a crosswalk' is the observation at which the subject's footprint begins to overlap (rel.occupies rises) a crosswalk cw (st.crosswalk 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'); 'Not a stand-in for' clauses of rel.occupies are none, and st.sidewalk's exclusion of crosswalks is not engaged.

dev.zone_sign 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}': the 'School-Xing' sign is kind school_crossing. It is the sign of that crosswalk: it governs (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the carrier c the subject occupies (rel.occupies), whose entrance into intersection j (st.lane_enters) the crosswalk marks (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'). dev.zone_sign's exclusion 'whether the condition holds now' is respected: no condition of the legend is read; dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply.
The person o is in the crosswalk cw the subject drives into: rel.occupies(o, cw) 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... crosswalk ...)'.

The side of the roadway the subject comes on is its side of the centre line (st.centre_line 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway') of the way w the crosswalk lies on (st.on_way(cw, w), st.on_way(cl, w), st.highway). With L = prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, cl) ('the signed lateral offset ... of a structure region from a road user', left positive) and y the lateral component of rel.bearing(subject, o) ('direction of b from a in a's frame'), o is on the subject's side where L > 0 and y < L, or L < 0 and y > L. Where the subject occupies a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'), the whole crosswalk is its side.

'any person' in a crosswalk crossing the street: a person on foot or in a wheelchair (ru.pedestrian 'a person on foot, in a wheelchair, or on a device the jurisdiction treats as on foot'; its exclusion 'a person on a bicycle or scooter' is why the riders are named beside it), or a person riding a bicycle (ru.bicycle), an electric bicycle (ru.electric_bicycle) or an electric scooter (ru.electric_scooter) across it.
'attempting to cross' is a purpose, read through the conduct it explains: the person's presence in the crosswalk (rel.occupies(o, cw), st.crosswalk), which lies across the street.

residues.why: an authority given to the City Traffic Engineer to mark school crosswalks; it imposes nothing on a road user, and the duty's own words select the crosswalk by the School-Xing sign displayed for it (k5), so the duty is the same whether or not these words are read

an authority given to the City Traffic Engineer to mark or sign 'School-Xing' in advance of a crosswalk; the duty's own words read the sign displayed (k5), whoever placed it and at whatever set-back, so the duty is the same whether or not these words are read

LVMC_11_18_020.applicability: The subject, a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), occupies a carrier c (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(c, j) for an intersection j; a zone sign of kind school_crossing (dev.zone_sign) governs c (dev.governs); a crosswalk cw (st.crosswalk) marks c's entrance (st.entrance_of(cw, c)); and some road user o, other than the subject, of class ru.pedestrian, ru.bicycle, ru.electric_bicycle or ru.electric_scooter, occupies cw on the subject's side of the roadway: with cl a centre line (st.centre_line) and cw both lying on one way w (st.on_way, st.highway), L = prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, cl) and y the lateral component of rel.bearing(subject, o), L > 0 and y < L, or L < 0 and y > L; or the subject occupies a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway).
LVMC_11_18_020.obligation: The subject's occupancy of cw does not rise at this observation (rel.occupies(subject, cw) does not hold here while it did not hold at the previous observation), for the cw bound in the applicability, re-bound with the same selection (crosswalk marking the entrance of the carrier c the subject occupies, c governed by the school_crossing sign, a person of the named classes in cw on the subject's side).

narrowings.why: 'the operator of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'displayed' is read through the sign's presence governing the subject's approach carrier; the crosswalk is the one recorded as marking that carrier's entrance
'attempting to cross the street' is read through the person's presence in the crosswalk

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A school_crossing sign governs the subject's lane; a child walks in the crosswalk on the subject's half of the roadway; the subject drives into the crosswalk.

scenarios.name: permit

scenarios.name: idle

segmentation.text: Every vehicle
driven upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section
or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn,
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.

elements.justification: 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. No named class stands in for it.

DEF-NRS-484A-070: 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section'. st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'; st.median_or_divider: 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'; st.on_way ties the divider to the highway h ('a median or any other part of it'); rel.occupies anchors the subject on h. 'Driven' is read through the vehicle's motion.

'driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section' is the subject's footprint overlapping a divider region: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... median ...)'; st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'. Over, across and within are all an overlap of the footprint with the divider region; no distance stands in for it.
st.median_or_divider carries an 'opening attribute where a crossover exists': 'through an opening' is the footprint overlapping a divider region of h that carries the opening attribute.

A crossover is a divider region with the opening attribute; an intersection is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; rel.occupies places the subject at it. 'Established by a public authority' is a legal status read through the feature's presence.

NRS_484B_227_1_o2.applicability: At every observation at which the subject occupies a highway h (st.highway) on which a median_or_divider region lies (st.on_way), except where the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection lying on h.
NRS_484B_227_1_o2.obligation: Re-binding h as in the applicability: for every median_or_divider region m lying on h, the subject's footprint does not overlap m (rel.occupies), unless m carries the opening attribute (an opening in the divider or a crossover).

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through the vehicle's motion on the highway, whoever or whatever controls it.
'established by a public authority' is a legal status; the crossover or intersection present on the road is its evidence.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A st.median_or_divider m without the opening attribute lies on highway h; the subject's footprint overlaps m as it drives across it away from any intersection.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives along its roadway of h; its footprint never overlaps the divider.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives over a painted island on a highway on which no st.median_or_divider lies.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives on h next to the divider; rel.occupies is absent on the source, so whether its footprint overlaps the divider is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject crosses the divider where the divider region it overlaps carries the opening attribute (a crossover).

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint overlaps the nose of the divider while it also overlaps an intersection lying on h.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
shall not: Intentionally
interfere with the movement
of a motor vehicle.

elements.justification: The three admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle and DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, claimed as ru.aggregate with their ids as the index maps 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'; 'the operator' is read through the device's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role'.

'Motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'), claimed as ru.aggregate, as the index maps 'any motor vehicle'.

The movement of the motor vehicle is its motion: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the vehicle moving, above p.halt_speed_tolerance) and kin.accel_longitudinal 'acceleration along heading, signed', whose braking shows the movement disturbed; it is 'Not a stand-in for: speed', and it is read here as the change the interference forces, not as the speed. The rider interferes from in front of the vehicle's movement: rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame', with the rider's bearing in the vehicle's frame pointing ahead. No exclusion applies.

operationalizations.standard: intentionally interfere (intent, a state of mind, and the degree of interference)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: an interference with a vehicle's movement is a conflict in which the vehicle, with the rider ahead of it, brakes evasively — a deceleration beyond comfortable service braking while their closest approach lies within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance

NRS_484B_270_7a.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, read as operated.
NRS_484B_270_7a.obligation: At every observation, for every road user m other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle and moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), it is not the case that: the subject lies ahead of m (the longitudinal component of the subject's rel.bearing in m's frame is positive), m's kin.accel_longitudinal is at or below the negative of p.vehicle_evasive_decel, and prim.closest_approach_within(m, subject) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(m, subject) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion; who controls it is not observed.

Intent shows in no single observation: it is read only through the conduct that interferes — the rider ahead of a moving motor vehicle in a conflict that forces it to brake evasively — and a conflict the rider did not seek is not told apart; an interference that forces no evasive braking (a swerve only) is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle cuts in front of a moving car and slows; the car, with the bicycle ahead of it, brakes harder than p.vehicle_evasive_decel while their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides in a bicycle lane; a car passes it without braking and without a conflicting closest approach.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a car (not a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregates).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter swerves in front of a moving car with a conflicting closest approach; the car's longitudinal acceleration is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a path with no motor vehicle in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.vehicle_evasive_decel
param_proposals.convention: the longitudinal deceleration of a motor vehicle at or beyond which its braking counts as an evasive reaction to another road user rather than ordinary speed control: about 0.4 g, above the comfortable deceleration of about 3.4 m/s^2
param_proposals.source: AASHTO comfortable deceleration rate; traffic-conflict studies of evasive braking

segmentation.text: The prima facie speed limit shall be fifteen miles per hour
when traversing any intersection
or street or highway
if during the last one hundred feet of his approach to such intersection
the driver
does not have a clear and unobstructed view of such intersection
and of any traffic upon all of the streets or highways entering such intersection
for a distance of one hundred feet along all such streets or highways
except on a through street or highway
or at a traffic-controlled intersection

elements.justification: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s is the speed the limit bounds; its exclusion of acceleration does not apply.

st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet' (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines'); traversing it is the subject's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies). Its exclusion 'a crosswalk or a stop line' does not apply: the region itself is read.

'the last one hundred feet of his approach' is a .path window, reading kin.path_length 'distance travelled along the body's path', ending at the observation at which the subject's occupancy of j (rel.occupies, st.intersection) rose; the window is the subject's own path before that entry.

'the driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is read through the controlled motion of the vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate's exclusion of 'who drives or controls a vehicle' is respected: the role is read through motion, the aggregate gives the class.

st.sight_distance 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... whether or not any road user is there': the view of the intersection is clear where the sight distance at the subject's point is at least the ground distance from its body to j (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'). Its exclusions (rel.visible, env.visibility) do not apply: the view of a place, not of an actual road user, is read.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic. The streets or highways entering j are the ways w (st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines') with st.on_way(j, w) ('an intersection lies on every way that meets there'). A view of any traffic upon them is, for every traffic member o occupying w (rel.occupies) whose ground distance to j (st.region_geometry) is within one hundred feet, rel.visible(subject, o) 'an unobstructed line of sight from a's reference point to b's body'; its exclusion of the sight distance of a place does not apply since d8 carries that.

st.sight_along_way 'the distance along a way, in each direction from the point of that way nearest a road user, within which another vehicle on that way could be seen from the road user's eye ...; the smaller of the two directions' is read for every way w with st.on_way(j, w) and compared with the literal one hundred feet; its exclusions (st.sight_distance, rel.visible) do not apply: the sight along each entering way is what the words measure.

DEF-NRS-484A-275 'at the entrances to which vehicular traffic from intersecting highways is required by law to yield right-of-way to vehicles on such through highway in obedience to either an authorized stop sign or a yield sign, or other official traffic-control device': the subject's approach carrier c (the carrier it occupied, st.lane_enters(c, j), at the last observation before its entry into j) is governed (dev.governs) by no stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red traffic signal, while another carrier entering j is governed by one of them. Same reading as LVMC_11_12_070_B s7. dev.governs 'Not a stand-in for: a position' does not apply.

A traffic-controlled intersection is one whose traffic a control device controls: a traffic signal ('a signal head') in a state other than dark, a stop sign or a yield sign governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection') j itself or a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, j). dev.governs 'no closure to the lanes that enter it' is respected by reading both the junction and the entering carriers explicitly.

residues.why: every intersection is, by DEF-NRS-484A-105, a junction of highways and streets; the words add no region beyond the intersection whose approach the condition measures, so the duty is the same whether or not they are read

LVMC_11_16_040.applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies an intersection j (st.intersection); and at some observation of the .path window of one hundred feet (kin.path_length) behind the observation at which its occupancy of j rose, the view was not clear: the subject's st.sight_distance was below its ground distance to j, or for some way w with st.on_way(j, w) its st.sight_along_way(w) was below one hundred feet, or some traffic member o (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) occupying such a w within one hundred feet of j (st.region_geometry distance) was not rel.visible from the subject; and not (d9) the subject's approach carrier at its entry into j was governed by no stop sign, yield sign or flashing-red signal while another carrier entering j was governed by one; and not (d10) a traffic signal in a state other than dark, a stop sign or a yield sign governs j or a carrier entering j.
LVMC_11_16_040.obligation: At every observation at which the subject occupies j, its kin.speed is at most fifteen miles per hour.

narrowings.why: a prima facie limit is read as a maximum: a speed above it is reported violated; the rebuttal a court may admit is not modelled
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
the legal designation 'through street or highway' is read through the devices on the road that display it (stop sign, yield sign, flashing-red signal governing the entering approaches)

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled intersection, hedges limit sight along the cross street to 20 m during the last 100 ft of the subject's approach; it traverses j above fifteen mph.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, traversing j at or below fifteen mph.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Same restricted view, but a traffic signal (circular_green) governs the subject's approach lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled intersection; the source does not supply sight along the ways, and the subject traverses above fifteen mph.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled intersection, no other road user in the scene; a wall limits sight along one cross way below one hundred feet during the last 100 ft of the approach; the subject traverses at or below fifteen mph. The traffic quantifier is empty and the verdict is still decided by the sight along the way.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within an intersection
intending to turn to the left
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction
which is within the intersection
or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver, having so yielded
and having given a signal when and as required,
may make such left turn
and the drivers of all other vehicles
approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
shall yield
the right-of-way
to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Within an intersection': the subject's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... intersection ...)'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet').
Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) while the protected vehicle is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact).

'Any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate. 'Approaching from the opposite direction', per rel.oncoming's not-a-stand-in clause, is read through the carrier v approaches through (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters c2 X) and its st.lane_direction, opposed to the direction of the carrier c1 the subject entered X from, within p.oncoming_heading_cos — never from current headings, which the subject's turn changes.
'Which is within the intersection': v's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies), having come from c2.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

operationalizations.standard: so close to the intersection as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a vehicle approaching on its carrier is an immediate hazard where, under constant velocities, its centre and the subject's approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

NRS_484B_253_o1.applicability: At every observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection X and the subject declares int.left_turn at X (intent subject X) at that observation.
NRS_484B_253_o1.obligation: Re-binding X as in the applicability, and c1 as the carrier entering X (st.lane_enters c1 X) the subject occupied when it last entered X (it has overlapped X continuously since an observation at which it occupied c1): for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle approaching from the opposite direction — v occupies a carrier c2 entering X, or overlaps X continuously since an observation at which it occupied such a c2, where the designated directions of c1 and c2 (st.lane_direction) have a dot product below minus p.oncoming_heading_cos — and that either overlaps X or, on c2, has its closest approach to the subject within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject overlaps X and declares int.left_turn at X; v approaches on c2, whose st.lane_direction is opposed to that of the subject's entry carrier c1; the subject moves into its turn with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance while its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject stays at rest in X until v has passed, then turns.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject crosses X with int.left_turn declared false at X (its plan goes straight).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Left-turning subject in X, opposing v in conflict; kin.speed is absent, so whether the subject proceeds into the conflict is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject turns left in X with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: v approaches from a cross street (its carrier's direction perpendicular to c1's) on a conflicting path; the subject turns: v does not approach from the opposite direction.

segmentation.text: The driver of a motor vehicle
shall: Exercise due care
to avoid a collision
with a person riding
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter.

elements.justification: Reuses the index mapping of 'The driver of a motor vehicle' (NRS_484B_270_1): the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.
A collision is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; it is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss', which the operationalization of w2 bounds separately.

'a person riding' is the rider's controlled motion of the device, read as the device moving: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance (observable_reading, agency), as the index maps 'a person lawfully riding' for NRS_484B_270_1.

Reuses the index mapping of 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter.' (NRS_484B_270_1): the three admitted aggregates, claimed as ru.aggregate with their ids, never expanded into class atoms.

operationalizations.standard: due care to avoid a collision (a standard of the driver's care, a state of mind)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves, care shows in its keeping no closest approach to the rider, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

NRS_484B_270_5a.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven.
NRS_484B_270_5a.obligation: At every observation at which the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every road user b other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter and moving with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance: the subject is not in contact with b (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, b) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, b) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of care, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.
'a person riding' is read as the device moving above the halt tolerance; a rider at rest is not read.

Due care, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome while the subject moves: no contact and no conflicting closest approach with a riding bicyclist or scooter rider; lookout, speed choice and every other aspect of care are read only through that outcome.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A moving car closes on a bicycle riding ahead in the same lane; their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance and the car does not slow.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car slows behind the moving bicycle and keeps a closest approach beyond p.conflict_centre_clearance, then passes with a wide berth; no contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is an electric scooter (not a member of the motor vehicle aggregate) riding near a bicycle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A moving car passes alongside a riding electric bicycle with no conflicting closest approach; contact between bodies is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A moving car drives on an empty street: no bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is in the scene.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter
within a business or residence district
entering into or emerging from an alley, driveway or building
shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to
driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway, driveway or building
yielding the right-of-way to any pedestrian
as may be necessary to avoid collision

elements.justification: Each term is admitted as its aggregate: 'bicycle' DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'electric bicycle' DEF-LVMC-11-02-082::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor'), 'electric scooter' DEF-LVMC-11-02-083::electric_scooter ('a device with handlebars and an electric motor'); the subject belongs to one of them.

As in LVMC_11_40_140_o1: rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; st.alley 'a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'; st.driveway_or_alley_entrance 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'; st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines' (occupying none of it: beyond the property line, where a building stands). Read at the subject's latest entry onto the sidewalk it occupies.

Same atoms as the mapping index for these words. st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; rel.occupies: the subject's footprint on that sidewalk since its entry; st.region_geometry is claimed with the words as mapped and reads the sidewalk's outline for the occupancy the source derives.

'yielding' as in the mapping index: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the subject proceeds only while it does not create a conflict) and rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the standard e7 bounds. 'pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'). The right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210) is 'the right ... to proceed ... in preference to another' approaching so as 'to give rise to the danger of a crash'.

operationalizations.standard: as may be necessary to avoid collision
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the subject moves, a pedestrian whose centre comes, under constant velocities, within the conflict clearance of the subject's centre within the conflict horizon is a danger of collision the subject must yield to

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district or a residence district, as the map's reading classifies the area

LVMC_11_40_140_o2.applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter. At an observation at which it occupies a sidewalk region s and has occupied s at every observation since its latest entry onto s (rel.occupies(subject, s) since the observation at which it rose), where at that entry asm.business_or_residence_district held and the subject entered into or emerged from an alley, driveway or building (as in LVMC_11_40_140_o1: at the entry or the observation before it occupied an st.alley or st.driveway_or_alley_entrance region; or at the observation before it occupied no st.highway region; or from the entry it occupies s until it occupies no st.highway region).
LVMC_11_40_140_o2.obligation: For every pedestrian p of the scene other than the subject (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance. A scene with no pedestrian is compliant.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion.
Yielding is read as not proceeding into a conflict and not colliding: the subject may move where no pedestrian is in conflict with it; where one is, it must be at rest.

scenarios.name: permit

scenarios.name: idle

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter emerges from an alley across the sidewalk with no pedestrian in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

segmentation.text: Upon approaching
an authorized emergency vehicle
or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency
which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Proceed
with caution.

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'approaching' the emergency vehicle: the subject moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) with the emergency vehicle ahead in its frame (rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component positive), within the centre distance (rel.centre_distance 'Euclidean ground-plane distance between reference points') at which its lamps engage the driver; rel.centre_distance is not used as a clearance or an order of arrival.

Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'; its conduct is carried by t4 and t6.

ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service ...; kind in {... regulatory_agency ...}', read with kind regulatory_agency; 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' respected.

'moving': the emergency vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance. 'preparing to move', as t12 defines it: sig.hand_signal 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {no_signal, ...}' other than no_signal, or sig.turn_indicator other than off (read as the indication, not the move it precedes), with the vehicle visible from the subject (rel.visible 'an unobstructed line of sight').

sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...', read as colour red, mode flashing, facing front from the quoted requirement 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front'; not a stand-in for an audible warning.
Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'any other' excludes the emergency vehicle itself; 'driver' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Mapping index: 'unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer' maps to dev.governs, dev.human_direction, rel.occupies, st.travel_region; read with role police_officer governing a travel region the subject occupies.
'Proceed': the subject continues to move, kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above the halt tolerance; the manner of proceeding is the standard t11.

The definition of 'preparing to move' used by t4: 'any indication that is visible to an approaching driver' (rel.visible) 'that ... is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle' (kin.speed) 'or (b) The use of hand signals' (sig.hand_signal); the open list also read through sig.turn_indicator.

operationalizations.standard: with caution
operationalizations.convention: caution is read through the conduct it secures toward the emergency vehicle: no traffic-conflict with it (closest approach of the centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision threshold below the collision clearance), no contact, and, while side by side with it, a gap between bodies of at least the lateral passing clearance

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

residues.why: illustrative: arriving at or leaving a scene are instances of moving or preparing to move, which t4 already reads; the duty is the same whether or not the vehicle is arriving at or leaving a scene

NRS_484B_267_2b.applicability: There is a road user e, not the subject, of the authorized-emergency-vehicle aggregate or an official vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, showing a lit warning lamp of colour red, mode flashing, facing front, that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) or preparing to move (visible from the subject, rel.visible, with a hand signal other than no_signal or a turn indicator other than off); the subject is approaching e: it moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), e lies ahead of it in its frame (rel.bearing longitudinal positive) or the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), and their centre distance is at most p.emergency_approach_reach. And no human_direction device of role police_officer governs a travel region the subject occupies.
NRS_484B_267_2b.obligation: For every such e: the subject and e are not in contact; it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; and where rel.longitudinal_overlap of the subject and e is at or above zero, rel.surface_gap between them is at least p.emergency_pass_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'preparing to move' is defined (t12) as an indication 'visible to an approaching driver': read as the emergency vehicle being visible from the subject (rel.visible) while it gives the indication
caution, a standard of the driver's care, is read only through the clearance the subject keeps from the emergency vehicle; its speed is judged by NRS_484B_267_2a

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Ambulance e, moving with a lit red flashing front lamp, is ahead of the moving subject within p.emergency_approach_reach; the subject passes alongside it with rel.surface_gap below p.emergency_pass_clearance while rel.longitudinal_overlap is at or above zero.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the subject passes with a gap of at least p.emergency_pass_clearance and no closest-approach conflict or contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: e's warning lamps are off as the subject approaches and passes.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but sig.warning_lamp is not observed, so whether the duty is engaged is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject closes on e from behind in its lane; their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: e stands at rest with its lamps flashing, no hand signal and no turn indicator: it is neither moving nor preparing to move.
