segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer
or a traffic-control signal:
The driver of a vehicle
shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or yield in compliance with a yield sign,
in compliance with the manner prescribed in subsection 1 [NRS-484B-257-1],
prior to entering an intersection
if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto
although not a part of a through highway
and shall proceed cautiously,
yielding
to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield
and which are within the intersection
or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, of which the subject is a member; 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction of role police_officer governing (dev.governs) the subject's approach carrier c or X (st.travel_region), read at the subject's entry.
A dev.traffic_signal governing c or X (dev.governs) that is not dev.inoperative ('installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'), read at the subject's entry.
Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Such driver' is the one so obliged: a dev.stop_sign or dev.yield_sign governs (dev.governs) the carrier c (st.lane_enters c X) the subject occupied (rel.occupies) when it entered X, or X itself — one of the 'one or more entrances' the words name.
Same mapping as 'yielding' in the index: the subject does not proceed (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) while the protected vehicle is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact).

'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate. 'Not so obligated to stop or yield' is v whose approach carrier c2 of X (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters) is governed (dev.governs) by no stop sign and no yield sign, nor is X.
'Which are within the intersection': v's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies), continuously since it occupied c2.
'During the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection': the subject's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies) and its kin.speed is above the halt tolerance.

operationalizations.standard: proceed cautiously: proceed without creating a danger of a crash with the vehicles the words name
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the subject proceeds (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while, under constant velocities, its centre and the other vehicle's approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance — a present danger of a crash

operationalizations.standard: approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: v approaching on its carrier is an immediate hazard where, under constant velocities, its centre and the subject's approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance

residues.why: 'although' is concessive: the duty reaches signed entrances whether or not the intersection is part of a through highway, and the yielding owed by a driver entering through a signed entrance is the same in both cases; the words withhold the duty nowhere.

NRS_484B_257_2_o2.applicability: At every observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection X and has overlapped it continuously since its latest entry into X (having occupied at the observation before a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, X)) and the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance); where at that entry observation a stop sign or a yield sign governed c or X (dev.governs), no police officer's direction (dev.human_direction of role police_officer) governed c or X, and no traffic signal that was not inoperative governed c or X.
NRS_484B_257_2_o2.obligation: Re-binding X and c as in the applicability: for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle not so obligated — v occupies a carrier c2 entering X, or overlaps X continuously since an observation at which it occupied such a c2, where no stop sign and no yield sign governs c2 or X (dev.governs) — and that either overlaps X or, on c2, has its closest approach to the subject within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'cautiously' is read only through the yielding the words join to it: proceeding without a present danger of a crash with the vehicles named; no further speed bound is read.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.yield_sign governs c; the subject entered X and moves across it with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance; v occupies X having entered from c2, which no stop or yield sign governs; their closest approach lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject waits at rest until v has cleared, then moves across X with no closest approach to v within the bound.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No stop or yield sign governs c or X when the subject enters X.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Subject moving across X in conflict with v; dev.governs is absent, so whether a sign governs c, and whether v is so obligated, are unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves across X with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: At an all-way stop, v entered X from c2, which a stop sign governs; the subject moves in conflict with v: v is itself obligated to stop, and this duty does not protect it.

segmentation.text: A driver of a motor vehicle
shall: Exercise due care
to avoid a collision
with a pedestrian.

elements.justification: The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as ru.aggregate; 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role such as who drives'.
A collision is rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; it is 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss', which the operationalization of x2 bounds separately.

'Pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate as the index maps 'A pedestrian'.

operationalizations.standard: due care to avoid a collision (a standard of the driver's care, a state of mind)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves, care shows in its keeping no closest approach to the pedestrian, under constant velocities, within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance of about a car's half-length plus half a body width

NRS_484B_280_1a.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read as driven.
NRS_484B_280_1a.obligation: At every observation at which the subject's kin.speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, for every road user p other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of care, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'A driver' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion; who or what is at the controls is not observed.

Due care, a state of mind, is read only through its outcome while the subject moves: no contact and no conflicting closest approach with a pedestrian; lookout, speed choice and every other aspect of care are read only through that outcome.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A moving car approaches a pedestrian crossing the roadway ahead and does not slow; their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car slows and halts short of the crossing pedestrian, keeping its closest approach beyond p.conflict_centre_clearance while it moves; no contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a bicycle (not a member of the motor vehicle aggregate) passing a pedestrian.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A moving car passes a pedestrian on the sidewalk with no conflicting closest approach; contact between bodies is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A moving car drives on a street with no pedestrian in the scene.

segmentation.text: When the signal is circular green alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
may proceed straight through or turn right or left
unless another device at the place prohibits either or both such turns.
Such vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or left,
must yield
the right-of-way
to other vehicles
and to pedestrians
lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time the signal is exhibited.

elements.justification: 'the signal is circular green alone' is dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, ... green_arrow(dir) ...}; several states may be displayed at once') displaying circular_green and no other state: 'alone' excludes a green arrow or any other state shown with it.

'Vehicular traffic' is a member of the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'), both claimed as ru.aggregate and never expanded. 'facing the signal' is read through the approach: the subject occupies (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a carrier (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet'), and the signal governs that carrier (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a stand-in for a position, none is read). The intersection is fixed by the carrier's entry topology, never by motion or distance.

'may proceed straight through or turn' names the traffic proceeding on its approach into and through the intersection, as the index maps 'approaching the intersection' (LVMC_11_12_070_B): the subject occupies the approach carrier entering the intersection (st.lane_enters), or occupies the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection) having been on that carrier continuously since; the movement it makes (straight or a turn) does not change the duty.

'Such vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or left' refers back to the subject (traffic aggregate and vehicle aggregate, 'membership of a legal aggregate'); the inclusion of turning vehicles adds no restriction: the duty binds the subject whichever movement it makes.

As the index maps 'shall yield the right-of-way' (NRS_484B_263_o1): to yield is to grant precedence — the subject does not move (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while the danger of a crash with a protected party exists, and does not move into contact with it (rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s7 reads).

'other vehicles' are road users other than the subject that are members of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('membership of a legal aggregate'; 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'): the parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'pedestrians' are members of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'): the parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'within the intersection' is the party's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the intersection the subject approaches or occupies (st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet'; not a stand-in for a crosswalk, which is read separately); 'an adjacent crosswalk' is a st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') tied to that intersection by relation atoms: it marks the entrance (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks') of some carrier (st.travel_region) entering that intersection (st.lane_enters); distance is not read for belonging. 'at the time the signal is exhibited' reads the party's presence at the same observation as dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_green alone ('several states may be displayed at once'). 'lawfully' is read as the operationalization of s7 discloses.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other')
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash with a party exists where, under constant velocities, the centres of the subject and the party approach within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), which reads the direction, the speed and the proximity of both together

residues.why: The words limit the permission to turn, not the duty to yield: traffic facing the circular green must yield whether or not another device prohibits a turn, and whether it makes the turn or not; the duty is the same either way.

NRS_484B_307_2a.applicability: There are an intersection i (st.intersection), a carrier c (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters(c, i)) and a traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) governing c (dev.governs(d, c)) such that d displays circular_green and no other state at the observation, and the subject, a member of traffic and a vehicle, either occupies c (rel.occupies(subject, c)) or occupies i and has occupied i continuously since an observation at which it occupied c (rel.occupies(subject, i) since rel.occupies(subject, c)).
NRS_484B_307_2a.obligation: Re-binding i, c and d with the whole selection of the applicability: for every road user u other than the subject that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) or a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) and that occupies i, or occupies a crosswalk x (st.crosswalk) marking the entrance (st.entrance_of(x, c2)) of some carrier c2 entering i (st.lane_enters(c2, i)): it is not the case that the subject moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while either prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or rel.contact(subject, u) holds.

narrowings.why: The right-of-way is owed to the parties s8 to s10 name; their 'lawfully' is not read: the words name no rule whose verdict decides a party's lawfulness, so every vehicle or pedestrian within is owed it; the rule never excuses a failure to yield to a lawful party and reaches further only where a party's presence is unlawful. 'an adjacent crosswalk' is any crosswalk that marks the entrance of a carrier into the same intersection; 'at the time the signal is exhibited' is every observation at which the circular green is displayed alone. Direction, speed and proximity are read together through the constant-velocity closest approach of the centres; a change of speed or direction ahead is not anticipated.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle occupies an approach lane entering an intersection whose dev.traffic_signal (dev.governs the lane) displays circular_green alone; it turns left into the intersection at 6 m/s while a pedestrian (ru.aggregate pedestrian) walks in the crosswalk that marks the entrance of the cross street's approach (st.entrance_of); prim.closest_approach_within holds with a closest centre distance of 1.0 m in 1.5 s, and the subject keeps moving.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same subject halts (kin.speed 0) inside the intersection until the pedestrian has crossed, then completes its turn with no closest approach below the clearance within the horizon.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing the subject's approach displays circular_red.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives through a signalized intersection whose signal states are not observed by the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject proceeds straight through on circular green alone; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing the subject's approach displays circular_green together with green_arrow(left): the green is not alone.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: On circular green alone, the subject turns left at 7 m/s across the path of an oncoming vehicle already within the intersection; prim.closest_approach_within holds with a closest centre distance of 1.5 m in 1.2 s.

segmentation.text: A person shall not drive a motor vehicle
at a speed in excess of 15 miles per hour
in an area designated as a school zone
except:
(a) On a day on which school is not in session;
(b) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(c) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or (d) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

As used in this section, “speed limit beacon” means a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit in a school zone or school crossing zone is in effect.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle for 'motor vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-130: 'every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); it is claimed as the aggregate and never expanded into classes. 'A person shall not drive' names no class: who drives is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency), so the exclusion 'a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle — never membership' does not apply: the aggregate carries only the vehicle's class.

kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity' (m/s). 'at a speed in excess of' compares the subject's speed with the figure the law states, carried as a literal (s2); the speed is a state at each observation, so the comparison is read at the judged observation. No 'not a stand-in for' clause of the contract applies.

dev.zone_sign: 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}; end attribute'. Ontology §9: 'Where the same category is also marked on the road by a sign (dev.zone_sign), the sign is the atom and the category is not.' The school zone (DEF-NRS-484B-063: 'those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property') is that category; 'an area designated as a school zone' is the stretch a zone sign z of kind school, not an end sign, governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'), read over st.travel_region, the kind dev.governs ranges over; the subject is in it where its footprint overlaps such a region r (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold', which this node reads only in exception (d); dev.governs is 'not a stand-in for a position' and no halt place is read from it. 'designated' is the legal status of the sign, read by its presence (observable_reading status).

dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect', the device the section defines (s12). The zone is designated by a beacon b where b governs the zone's region r (dev.governs over st.travel_region). 'operational' is read as b not inoperative: dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', applies to the beacon's head of lamps, so a beacon present and not inoperative is operational. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position: no place is read from it.

dev.speed_limit_beacon carries a 'flashing attribute': its lamps flash 'alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. 'the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect' is that attribute false for every operational beacon that governs r (the beacon of exception (c)).

The negation of s7: no dev.speed_limit_beacon ('a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign') that governs r (dev.governs, over st.travel_region) is present and not inoperative (dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'). An inoperative beacon leaves the zone 'not designated by an operational speed limit beacon'.

dev.zone_sign's 'conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend — a list of time windows ...; a legend read with no restriction is the empty set (unconditional), a legend not read is absent (every condition unknown)'. prim.conditions_hold: 'the structured conditions of a device (dev.zone_sign, dev.regulatory_sign) hold at the observation for a road user'. 'the sign designating the school zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect' is prim.conditions_hold false for z, the sign of s3, and the subject. dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold', which is why the primitive is read; its input env.civil_time is the primitive's own.

The section's definition of 'speed limit beacon' ('a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit ... is in effect') is the contract of dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. It adds no condition beyond the atom's, and the beacon is read as that atom in s7, s9 and s10.

assumptions.meaning: the date of the observation is a day on which the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place is in session, as the reading declares from that school's calendar

the time of the observation lies in the period from a half hour after the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place ceased operation to a half hour before that school next begins operation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule
the pupils of the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place are in class at the time of the observation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule

NRS_484B_363_1.applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle). At the judged observation its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region r that a dev.zone_sign z of kind school, not an end sign, governs (dev.governs); and, for that z and r, none of these holds at the judged observation: (a) asm.school_in_session_day is false; (b) asm.school_outside_operation_margin holds; (c) some dev.speed_limit_beacon governs r and is not dev.inoperative, asm.pupils_in_class holds, and no dev.speed_limit_beacon that governs r and is not inoperative is flashing; (d) no dev.speed_limit_beacon that governs r is present and not inoperative, and prim.conditions_hold for z and the subject is false. Where several such z and r hold, the duty applies if it applies for any of them. An undeclared assumption leaves the exception, and so the verdict where the speed exceeds the figure, unknown.
NRS_484B_363_1.obligation: The subject's kin.speed at the judged observation is at most the literal 15 mph of s2; a speed above it violates the duty.

narrowings.why: 'drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a motor vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
'designated' is the legal status of the zone: the zone sign governing the subject's region is the evidence, and the school property the zone adjoins is not read.

segmentation.text: A person shall not drive a motor vehicle
at a speed in excess of 25 miles per hour
in an area designated as a school crossing zone
except:
(a) On a day on which school is not in session;
(b) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(c) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or (d) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

As used in this section, “speed limit beacon” means a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit in a school zone or school crossing zone is in effect.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle for 'motor vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-130: 'every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); it is claimed as the aggregate and never expanded into classes. 'A person shall not drive' names no class: who drives is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency), so the exclusion 'a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle — never membership' does not apply.

kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity' (m/s). 'at a speed in excess of' compares the subject's speed with the figure the law states, carried as a literal (s2), at the judged observation. No 'not a stand-in for' clause of the contract applies.

dev.zone_sign: 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}; end attribute'. Ontology §9: 'Where the same category is also marked on the road by a sign (dev.zone_sign), the sign is the atom and the category is not.' The school crossing zone (DEF-NRS-484B-060: 'those sections of streets not adjacent to school property that pupils cross while following a designated walking route to school') is that category; 'an area designated as a school crossing zone' is the stretch a zone sign z of kind school_crossing, not an end sign, governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'), read over st.travel_region; the subject is in it where its footprint overlaps such a region r (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold', read only in exception (d); dev.governs is 'not a stand-in for a position'. 'designated' is the sign's legal status, read by its presence (observable_reading status).

dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect', the device the section defines (s12). The zone is designated by a beacon b where b governs the zone's region r (dev.governs over st.travel_region). 'operational' is read as b not inoperative: dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', applies to the beacon's head of lamps. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position.

dev.speed_limit_beacon carries a 'flashing attribute': its lamps flash 'alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. 'not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect' is that attribute false for every operational beacon that governs r.

The negation of s7: no dev.speed_limit_beacon ('a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign') that governs r (dev.governs, over st.travel_region) is present and not inoperative (dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication').

dev.zone_sign's 'conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend' and prim.conditions_hold: 'the structured conditions of a device (dev.zone_sign, dev.regulatory_sign) hold at the observation for a road user'. The sign indicates 'that the speed limit is not in effect' where prim.conditions_hold is false for z and the subject. 'the sign designating the school zone' is read as z, the sign designating the zone of this duty (the school crossing zone of s3): the subsection speaks of no other zone, and a school-kind sign need not exist at a crossing zone (disclosed in PLAN.md). dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold'; env.civil_time is the primitive's own input.

The section's definition of 'speed limit beacon' ('a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit ... is in effect') is the contract of dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. It adds no condition beyond the atom's.

assumptions.meaning: the date of the observation is a day on which the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place is in session, as the reading declares from that school's calendar

the time of the observation lies in the period from a half hour after the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place ceased operation to a half hour before that school next begins operation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule
the pupils of the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place are in class at the time of the observation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule

Where several such z and r hold, the duty applies if it applies for any of them.
NRS_484B_363_2.obligation: The subject's kin.speed at the judged observation is at most the literal 25 mph of s2; a speed above it violates the duty.

'designated' is the legal status of the zone: the zone sign governing the subject's region is the evidence, and the walking route the zone serves is not read.

scenarios.narrative: A motor vehicle's footprint overlaps a lane governed by a dev.zone_sign of kind school_crossing (not an end sign) whose conditions hold now; asm.school_in_session_day true, asm.school_outside_operation_margin false; no dev.speed_limit_beacon governs the lane; kin.speed is well above the stated 25 miles per hour.

scenarios.narrative: A dev.speed_limit_beacon that is not inoperative governs the zone's lane; asm.pupils_in_class true; the beacon is not flashing; the motor vehicle exceeds the stated figure: exception (c) holds.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Same as branch_1 but the beacon is flashing: exceptions (c) and (d) fail; the motor vehicle exceeds the stated figure.

scenarios.narrative: No beacon governs the zone's lane; prim.conditions_hold is false for the school crossing zone sign; the motor vehicle exceeds the stated figure: exception (d) holds.

segmentation.text: Upon the immediate approach of
an authorized emergency vehicle
or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency,
making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of every other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph,
immediately
drive to a position parallel to, and
as close as possible to, the right-hand edge or, if applicable, curb of a highway
and clear of any intersection.
The driver shall not drive to and stop in a position on a paved shoulder of a highway
where lawfully placed signage allows a vehicle described in paragraphs (a) to (f), inclusive, of subsection 4 of NRS 484B.210 [list appended below] to drive on the shoulder.

The provisions of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (c) of subsection 1 do not apply to: (a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus, that is being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The conduct the words require of it is carried by u4 and u1, not by the class.

ru.official_vehicle 'a vehicle in official or contracted road service ...; kind in {... regulatory_agency ...}', read with kind regulatory_agency; 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' respected.

sig.warning_lamp 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...', read as colour red, mode flashing, facing front from the quoted requirement 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front'; not a stand-in for an audible warning, which is not required.
Admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'every other' excludes the approaching vehicle; 'driver' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Mapping index: 'unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer' maps to dev.governs, dev.human_direction, rel.occupies, st.travel_region; dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic ...; role in {police_officer, ...}' read with role police_officer, governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

'Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph' refers to the paragraph's own provision that the driver 'shall not drive to and stop in a position on a paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows' listed vehicles 'to drive on the shoulder': the position this node requires excludes such a shoulder. st.shoulder 'the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic; paved attribute', read paved; dev.regulatory_sign 'a point regulation by catalogue code ... shoulder_use_permitted', governing (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or shoulder') that shoulder; rel.occupies anchors the subject's footprint.

'a position parallel to' the edge: the subject's heading (kin.heading 'direction the body points') is parallel, in either sense, to the designated direction (st.lane_direction 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') of a travel region (st.travel_region) its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); the carrier's direction runs along its edge. st.travel_region's exclusion of the highway's extent is respected: it only selects the carrier the subject is on.

'clear of any intersection': the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) no st.intersection region ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'; DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines'). Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk or a stop line' is respected.

operationalizations.standard: the immediate approach of the emergency or regulatory vehicle
operationalizations.convention: the vehicle moves with the subject ahead of it in its own frame, within the centre distance a vehicle at an urban response speed covers in the time a driver needs to perceive its lamps and begin clearing the way

operationalizations.standard: immediately
operationalizations.convention: the position is reached within a perception-reaction time plus the lane changes a pull-over takes, counted from the onset of the immediate approach; the duty to clear the way ends once the approaching vehicle has passed the subject (the subject behind it in its frame, their projections sharing no length)

operationalizations.standard: as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb of a highway
operationalizations.convention: curb-parking clearance: a vehicle pulled over to the edge stands with its body within the curb clearance of a parked car plus lane-keeping variability of the right-hand curb or roadway edge, or on an unsigned paved shoulder beyond it

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

NRS_484B_267_1b_o1.applicability: For some road user e, not the subject, the trigger rises at this observation (it holds here and did not at the previous observation): e is of the authorized-emergency-vehicle aggregate or an official vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, shows a lit warning lamp of colour red, mode flashing, facing front, moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with the subject ahead of it in its frame (rel.bearing longitudinal positive), within centre distance p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach. And no human_direction device of role police_officer governs a travel region the subject occupies.
NRS_484B_267_1b_o1.obligation: For every e whose trigger rises here: at some observation within p.emergency_pullover_window ahead (formula 'within', time), either e has passed the subject (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from e to the subject negative and rel.longitudinal_overlap of e and the subject negative), or the subject is at the position: (a) for some travel region t its footprint overlaps, the absolute dot product of its heading and t's designated direction is at least p.curb_parallel_cos; (b) for some highway h on which a travel region the subject occupies lies, either there is a road_edge region g lying on h with the ground distance from the subject's body to g (st.region_geometry) at most p.pullover_edge_gap and prim.region_lateral_offset of g from the subject at most zero (the edge on its right or under it), or the subject's footprint overlaps a paved shoulder lying on h; (c) its footprint overlaps no intersection region; (d) its footprint overlaps no paved shoulder governed by a regulatory sign of code shoulder_use_permitted.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

the duty is judged at the onset of the immediate approach; it is met once the position is reached within the window or the approaching vehicle has passed the subject first, since the paragraph's purpose, clearing its way, is then spent

'the right-hand edge ... of a highway' is read as the curb or roadway edge (st.road_edge) on the subject's right or a paved shoulder beyond it, not the outer boundary of the public way beyond the sidewalk; 'as close as possible' is read through a fixed gap, so what makes the edge unreachable (parked vehicles, obstructions) is not read
'parallel' is read with the heading in either sense along the occupied carrier's designated direction

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The trigger rises: ambulance e with a lit red flashing front lamp comes within p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach behind the moving subject. Over the next p.emergency_pullover_window the subject stays in the left lane, far from any road_edge region, and e does not pass it.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: At the trigger's rise the subject moves right and, within p.emergency_pullover_window, its body is within p.pullover_edge_gap of the right road_edge (prim.region_lateral_offset negative), heading parallel to its lane's direction within p.curb_parallel_cos, overlapping no intersection and no signed shoulder.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: e approaches with its warning lamps off: the trigger never rises.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but sig.warning_lamp is not observed, so whether the trigger rose is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Within the window the subject reaches the right edge, parallel, but its footprint overlaps an intersection region at every such observation, and e has not passed.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: e overtakes and passes the subject (the subject behind e, no longitudinal overlap) before the subject reaches the edge, within p.emergency_pullover_window.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: Within the window the subject moves onto a paved shoulder governed by a shoulder_use_permitted regulatory sign and stays there; it is never at the roadway edge off that shoulder, and e has not passed.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_immediate_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which an emergency or enforcement vehicle closing on a road user with its warning lamps flashing is in immediate approach: about five seconds of travel at an urban response speed of 20 m/s, the time a driver needs to perceive the lamps and begin to clear the way
param_proposals.source: driver-response studies of emergency-vehicle encounters (perception-reaction time plus lane-change time)

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_pullover_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest time from the onset of an emergency vehicle's immediate approach until a driver has moved to the right-hand edge: a perception-reaction time of about 1.5 s plus one or two lane changes of about 4 s each
param_proposals.source: AASHTO perception-reaction time; naturalistic lane-change duration studies

param_proposals.name: p.pullover_edge_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between a vehicle body and the right-hand curb or roadway edge within which a vehicle pulled over to clear the way counts as as close to the edge as it can be placed: the curb clearance of a parallel-parked car (about 0.3 m) plus lane-keeping variability and an edge margin
param_proposals.source: curb-parking clearance conventions of municipal codes and driver manuals

param_proposals.name: p.curb_parallel_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about fourteen degrees) between a stopped bus's heading and its carrier's designated direction, in either sense, at which the bus counts as approximately parallel to the curb
param_proposals.source: heading resolution of parked-vehicle placement

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a flashing yellow turn arrow, displayed alone or in combination with another signal:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
is permitted to cautiously
enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by the arrow signal,
or other such movement as is permitted by other signal indications displayed at the same time.
Such vehicular traffic
must yield
the right-of-way
to pedestrians lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk
and yield
the right-of-way
to other traffic lawfully within the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., flashing_yellow_arrow(dir), ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a flashing yellow turn arrow is flashing_yellow_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn, with whatever other states the head displays ('alone or in combination with another signal').

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).
'Such vehicular traffic' refers back to s2: the same admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

'yield': kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') tells a subject that moves on toward the other road user from one that holds back, and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)') is the crash precedence exists to avoid; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s11 reads. As the index maps 'must yield' (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'other traffic': road users of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') other than the subject. 'within the intersection': its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) intersection i (st.intersection). As the index maps 'lawfully using the intersection.' (NRS_484B_307_4a_o2).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210, 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance); the subject grants precedence where, while its speed is above the halt tolerance (p.halt_speed_tolerance), no such approach to the other road user arises. Direction, speed and proximity enter by degree through the constant-velocity extrapolation of both road users.

NRS_484B_307_7a_o3.applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, faces traffic signal head s showing a flashing yellow turn arrow: either it occupies a travel region c whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters) and which s governs (dev.governs), and s displays flashing_yellow_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn (with or without other states) at the judged observation; or it occupies i, has occupied it at every observation since it entered i from such a c, and s displayed such an arrow at that entry.
NRS_484B_307_7a_o3.obligation: For every road user p other than the subject that is of the class traffic and whose footprint overlaps i at the judged observation: it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while the closest approach of the two centres lies within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject's body does not touch p's (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'lawfully within the intersection' is read through the other road user's presence within the intersection; whether its presence there is lawful is not judged, so the subject yields to every such road user.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Head s governing left-turn lane c displays circular_green with flashing_yellow_arrow(left); an oncoming car already inside i proceeds straight at 11 m/s; the car turns left across its path at 6 m/s, the closest approach of their centres 0.9 s ahead at 1.2 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same signal; no other road user is in the scene; the car turns left through i. The duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: s displays green_arrow(left) alone; the car turns left past an oncoming car.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source supplies no velocity-derived speed for the turning car: whether it moved on toward the oncoming car is unknown.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

segmentation.text: Where the signal is circular green with a green turn arrow:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
may proceed
to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow or such other movement as is permitted by the circular green signal,
but the traffic
must yield
the right-of-way
to pedestrians
lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk
and to other traffic
lawfully using the intersection
at the time the signal is exhibited.

Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow when displayed with the circular green are thereby advised that so long as a turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: 'circular green with a green turn arrow' is dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, ... green_arrow(dir) ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once') displaying circular_green together with green_arrow(dir) for a turn direction (left, right or u_turn; a straight arrow is no turn arrow).

'Vehicular traffic' is a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') that is a vehicle: 'vehicular' uses the defined word of DEF-NRS-484A-320, whose admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway') is claimed (see PLAN.md). 'facing the signal' is read through the approach: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet') and the signal governs that carrier (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a stand-in for a position).

'may proceed' names the traffic proceeding on its approach into and through the intersection, as the index maps 'approaching the intersection' (LVMC_11_12_070_B): the subject occupies the approach carrier entering the intersection (st.lane_enters), or occupies the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection) having been on that carrier continuously since.
'the traffic' refers back to the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('membership of a legal aggregate').

As the index maps 'shall yield the right-of-way' (NRS_484B_263_o1): the subject does not move (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while the danger of a crash with a protected party exists, and does not move into contact with it (rel.contact 'touch or overlap (a collision)'; not a stand-in for a near miss, which s7's operationalization reads).

'pedestrians' are members of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'): parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'within an adjacent crosswalk' is the pedestrian's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') tied to the intersection by relation atoms: it marks the entrance (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks') of some carrier (st.travel_region) entering that intersection (st.lane_enters); distance is not read for belonging. 'lawfully' is read as the narrowing on s7 discloses.

'other traffic' are road users other than the subject that are members of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'): parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'using the intersection' is the party's footprint overlapping the intersection the subject approaches or occupies (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet', not a stand-in for a crosswalk). 'lawfully' is read as the narrowing on s7 discloses.

'at the time the signal is exhibited' reads the parties' presence at the same observation as dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_green with a green turn arrow ('several states may be displayed at once').

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other')
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash with a party exists where, under constant velocities, the centres of the subject and the party approach within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), which reads the direction, the speed and the proximity of both together

residues.why: The words describe which movements the traffic may make (the arrow's movement or one the circular green permits); the duty to yield binds the traffic facing the signal whichever movement it makes, so the duty is the same whether or not the movement is one of those.

An advisory statement of the signal phasing for the driver's information (opposing traffic faces a steady red while the arrow is lit); it requires, permits or forbids nothing, and the duty to yield is the same whether or not it holds.

NRS_484B_307_3a.applicability: There are an intersection i (st.intersection), a carrier c (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters(c, i)) and a traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) governing c (dev.governs(d, c)) such that d displays circular_green together with green_arrow(dir) for some dir among left, right and u_turn at the observation, and the subject, a member of traffic and a vehicle, either occupies c (rel.occupies(subject, c)) or occupies i and has occupied i continuously since an observation at which it occupied c (rel.occupies(subject, i) since rel.occupies(subject, c)).
NRS_484B_307_3a.obligation: Re-binding i, c and d with the whole selection of the applicability: for every road user u other than the subject that either is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) occupying a crosswalk x (st.crosswalk) marking the entrance (st.entrance_of(x, c2)) of some carrier c2 entering i (st.lane_enters(c2, i)), or is a member of traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) occupying i: it is not the case that the subject moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while either prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or rel.contact(subject, u) holds.

narrowings.why: The right-of-way is owed to the parties s9 to s13 name; their 'lawfully' (twice) is not read: the words name no rule whose verdict decides a party's lawfulness, so every pedestrian within an adjacent crosswalk and every member of traffic within the intersection is owed it; the rule reaches further than the words only where that presence is unlawful. 'an adjacent crosswalk' is any crosswalk marking the entrance of a carrier into the same intersection; 'at the time the signal is exhibited' is every observation at which the circular green with a green turn arrow is displayed. Direction, speed and proximity are read together through the constant-velocity closest approach of the centres.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for a driver of a vehicle
to fail or refuse to comply with any signal
of an authorized flagger serving in a traffic control capacity
in a clearly marked area of highway construction or maintenance
or any other area which has been designated as a temporary traffic control zone.

elements.justification: 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion, as the index maps 'The driver of a vehicle' (LVMC_11_20_060_o1).

The flagger's signal is dev.human_direction's 'indication in {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}'. Compliance is read in the subject's motion relative to the flagger's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head', used here as the flagger's place, not as a stop line): the flagger lies ahead of the subject where the vector from kin.position to dev.position has a positive component along kin.heading; passing the flagger is that component turning from positive to not positive. Slowing is read from kin.accel_longitudinal ('acceleration along heading, signed'; not a stand-in for speed); a turn from the heading change integrated from kin.yaw_rate (Term.headingSince).

A flagger is dev.human_direction with role flagger ('a person directing traffic and the direction given'); serving in a traffic control capacity for the subject is the flagger governing (dev.governs) the travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). Governance is control, not a position.

dev.temporary_traffic_control: 'cones, barricades, temporary signs and flashers marking works, a closure or an obstruction'. The area of highway construction or maintenance is a travel region lying on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway) that such a device governs (dev.governs) and the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

dev.zone_sign kind temporary_traffic_control, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road', governing (dev.governs) the travel region the subject occupies: the designated temporary traffic control zone is read from its sign; a sign marking the zone's end ('end' attribute) does not designate it.

NRS_484B_330_1.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate vehicle). At the judged observation the subject occupies a travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.human_direction f with role flagger giving an indication, and r is governed by a dev.temporary_traffic_control device and lies on a highway, or is governed by a dev.zone_sign of kind temporary_traffic_control that does not mark the zone's end.
NRS_484B_330_1.obligation: Re-binding f by the same selection (the flagger governing the region the subject occupies, in such a zone), with 'ahead' meaning the vector from the subject's kin.position to f's dev.position has a positive component along the subject's kin.heading: (stop) it is not the case that f indicates stop at the judged and at the previous observation, f was ahead of the subject at the previous observation and is not ahead at the judged one (the subject passes a flagger showing stop); (slow) it is not the case that f indicates slow and is ahead of the subject while the subject's kin.accel_longitudinal is at or above p.speed_decrease_decel_min (the subject speeds up toward a flagger showing slow); (turn) it is not the case that the subject passes f (ahead at the previous observation, not ahead at the judged one) while f indicates turn(dir) and the subject's heading change since f's turn(dir) indication last rose (Term.headingSince with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is not a turn toward dir: for left at least p.turn_heading_min to the left, for right at least p.turn_heading_min to the right, for u_turn of magnitude at least p.u_turn_heading_min. A proceed indication requires no further act.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at the controls.
'authorized' and 'serving in a traffic control capacity' are the flagger's status and role, read through the flagger's presence directing the region the subject occupies.
'clearly marked' is read through the presence of temporary traffic control devices governing the region; their clarity is not modelled.
'designated' is read through the presence of a temporary traffic control zone sign governing the region.

Compliance is read per indication: stop as not passing the flagger while the stop holds; slow as not speeding up toward the flagger; turn(dir) as having turned toward dir by the time the subject passes the flagger; proceed as a permission whose non-use is not judged.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a flashing yellow turn arrow, displayed alone or in combination with another signal:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
is permitted to cautiously
enter the intersection only to make the movement indicated by the arrow signal,
or other such movement as is permitted by other signal indications displayed at the same time.
Such vehicular traffic
must yield
the right-of-way
to pedestrians lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk
and yield
the right-of-way
to other traffic lawfully within the intersection.

'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). 'Such vehicular traffic' refers back to s2: the same admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

'must yield': kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') tells a subject that moves on toward the pedestrian from one that holds back, and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)') is the crash precedence exists to avoid; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s8 reads. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'pedestrians': the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk': the pedestrian's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) intersection i (st.intersection) or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks') of a travel region (st.travel_region) that enters i (st.lane_enters). operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210, 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance); the subject grants precedence where, while its speed is above the halt tolerance (p.halt_speed_tolerance), no such approach to the pedestrian arises. NRS_484B_307_7a_o2.applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, faces traffic signal head s showing a flashing yellow turn arrow: either it occupies a travel region c whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters) and which s governs (dev.governs), and s displays flashing_yellow_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn (with or without other states) at the judged observation; or it occupies i, has occupied it at every observation since it entered i from such a c, and s displayed such an arrow at that entry.
NRS_484B_307_7a_o2.obligation: For every road user p other than the subject that is of the class pedestrian and whose footprint overlaps i or a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a travel region that enters i at the judged observation: it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while the closest approach of the two centres lies within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject's body does not touch p's (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'lawfully within' is read through the pedestrian's presence within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk; whether its presence there is lawful is not judged, so the subject yields to every such pedestrian.
