segmentation.text: Upon approaching an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency which is moving or preparing to move in any direction,
including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident,
and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of
subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3],
the driver of any other vehicle shall,
except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer:
If possible,
drive in a lane that is not adjacent to the lane in which the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle of a regulatory agency is moving,
unless roadway, traffic, weather or other conditions make doing so unsafe or impossible.

As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

elements.justification: 'an authorized emergency vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle ('a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'); its 'not a stand-in for' a responding role does not bite, since the conduct is read separately. 'an official vehicle of a regulatory agency' is ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, not an emergency vehicle. 'Upon approaching': the subject, moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance), has that vehicle ahead of it (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) within the approach reach (rel.centre_distance; no clearance read). 'which is moving': the vehicle's kin.speed above the halt tolerance; 'or preparing to move', as defined in s10: visible from the subject (rel.visible) with an arm signal (sig.hand_signal other than no_signal) or a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator: the signal, not the manoeuvre). 'in any direction' adds no restriction.

sig.warning_lamp: 'a warning lamp lit; colour ..., mode ..., facing ...'. The words borrowed from DEF-NRS-484A-480-3, 'at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front', fix the lights: a lamp lit of colour red, mode flashing, facing front. Not a stand-in for an audible warning: no siren is read.

'any other vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); exclusions are the reading's. 'other' excludes the approached vehicle. 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

dev.human_direction 'a person directing traffic ...; role ∈ {police_officer, ...}': a law enforcement officer is role police_officer; excepted where such a device governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies).

'drive in a lane' is the subject's footprint overlapping a lane (rel.occupies; st.lane, 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles'), the lane being the subject's own feature; 'the lane in which the ... vehicle ... is moving' is a lane the approached vehicle occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane). 'adjacent' is read in two ways the contracts carry: the left or right neighbouring lane of the same direction (st.lane_adjacency, 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction'; not the marking between the lanes), and, for a vehicle moving against the subject's direction, the two leftmost lanes of opposite directions — each of lane ordinal one (st.lane_adjacency ordinal, 'ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction'), their designated directions opposed (st.lane_direction) — on one and the same roadway that both road users occupy (st.roadway, 'separate roadways of a divided highway are separate', so a divided highway's opposing lanes are never adjacent). A lane is not adjacent to itself.

The section's definition of 'preparing to move', read as s1 reads it: visible from the subject (rel.visible); '(a) A movement of the vehicle' kin.speed above the halt tolerance; '(b) The use of hand signals' sig.hand_signal other than no_signal; 'including, without limitation' admits a lit turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator). 'about to move' is read through these indications.

operationalizations.standard: If possible
operationalizations.convention: lane-change time: moving away from the vehicle's lane is possible once the approach has lasted the time a driver needs to perceive the vehicle and change one lane, and only where the subject's way carries a candidate lane: a lane on the same highway as the subject's lane (st.on_way) whose designated direction points the subject's way (st.lane_direction, positive dot product with the subject's lane direction) and that is not adjacent to the vehicle's lane

operationalizations.standard: unless roadway, traffic, weather or other conditions make doing so unsafe or impossible
operationalizations.convention: gap acceptance and lane availability: a candidate lane is impossible (roadway) where a temporary traffic control device governs it, and unsafe (traffic) where a road user occupying it, other than the subject (any road user using the highway: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances', DEF-NRS-484A-285, read without exclusion), is nearer the subject's body (rel.surface_gap) than the subject's speed times the following headway for the surface (ice or snow, else wet road or precipitation, else dry); weather makes the move unsafe where the road is icy or snow-covered, or the visibility (env.visibility) is shorter than the distance the subject travels at its speed in the lane-change time

compositions.quote: at least one flashing red warning lamp visible from the front

residues.why: 'including, without limitation' lists examples of a vehicle moving or preparing to move; the duty is the same whether or not the vehicle is arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident

NRS_484B_267_2e.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance). Some road user e, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle or an ru.official_vehicle of kind regulatory_agency, shows a lit sig.warning_lamp red, flashing, facing front; e is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) or preparing to move (rel.visible from the subject and e's sig.hand_signal other than no_signal or sig.turn_indicator other than off); e lies ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive) within p.emergency_approach_reach (rel.centre_distance). Not applicable where a dev.human_direction of role police_officer governs (dev.governs) a st.travel_region the subject occupies (rel.occupies).
NRS_484B_267_2e.obligation: For every e selected as in the applicability for which that whole selection has held at every observation of the window behind of length p.emergency_lane_change_window, every st.lane Le that e occupies and every st.lane Ls that the subject occupies: Ls is not adjacent to Le, or the move is excused. Adjacent: Ls is the left or right neighbour of Le (st.lane_adjacency), or Ls and Le each have lane ordinal one (st.lane_adjacency ordinal) with designated directions (st.lane_direction) whose dot product is negative while some st.roadway is occupied (rel.occupies) by both the subject and e. Excused where env.ice_or_snow holds; or env.visibility is below the subject's kin.speed × p.emergency_lane_change_window; or no candidate lane is open and clear. A candidate lane C is a st.lane lying on (st.on_way) the same st.highway as Ls, whose designated direction has a positive dot product with Ls's, and which is not adjacent to Le in the sense above; C is open and clear where no dev.temporary_traffic_control governs it (dev.governs) and no road user u other than the subject occupying C has a rel.surface_gap to the subject below the subject's kin.speed × the headway (p.following_headway_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'preparing to move', defined as an indication that the vehicle is 'about to move', is read through the visible indications the definition lists and a lit turn indicator
'visible to an approaching driver' is read as the vehicle being in the subject's line of sight (rel.visible)

the catch-all 'other conditions' is read only through the contracts named: a closure by temporary traffic control, the gap to traffic occupying the candidate lane, ice or snow, a wet surface or precipitation, and visibility

adjacency across the centre of a two-way roadway is read only between the two leftmost lanes of opposite directions on one roadway; the vehicle's own lane is not adjacent to itself, so following it in its lane is not read as a breach of this paragraph

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry road, four lanes in the subject's direction. A police car (authorized emergency vehicle) with its red front lamp flashing moves in lane 1 ahead of the subject; the subject has been approaching it within the reach for longer than the lane-change window and stays in lane 2, the neighbour of lane 1, while lanes 3 and 4 are open and empty.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene, but the subject has moved to lane 3, which is not a neighbour of lane 1.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives in lane 2 of a four-lane carriageway; no emergency or regulatory-agency vehicle is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe lane adjacency, so whether the subject's lane neighbours the police car's lane, and which lanes are candidates, is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Two lanes in the subject's direction; the police car moves in lane 1 and the subject in lane 2. The only lane not adjacent to lane 1 is lane 1 itself, occupied by the police car within the headway gap, so no candidate lane is clear: excused.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the road is covered in snow (env.ice_or_snow): excused.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the approach has lasted less than the lane-change window when the subject is observed in lane 2.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: Undivided two-way roadway, two lanes each way. A regulatory-agency official vehicle with its red front lamp flashing moves against the subject in the leftmost lane of its direction; the subject, approaching it head-on, drives in the leftmost lane of its own direction, while the right lane of its direction is open and empty.

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: centre distance within which a driver approaching an emergency or enforcement vehicle that shows flashing warning lamps counts as approaching it: about the distance at which the lamps are conspicuous by day and a driver at an urban speed of 15 m/s has ten seconds to slow
param_proposals.source: warning-lamp conspicuity and perception-reaction figures (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_267_2a)

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: source speed resolution (as proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B)

param_proposals.name: p.emergency_lane_change_window
param_proposals.convention: the time from the onset of an approach to an emergency or enforcement vehicle until a driver has moved one lane over: a perception-reaction time of about 1.5 s plus one lane change of about 4 s
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book perception-reaction time; naturalistic lane-change duration studies

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_dry
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a dry surface: the two-second rule of driver manuals
param_proposals.source: driver manuals (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_wet
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a wet surface or in rain: the two-second rule lengthened by a second
param_proposals.source: driver manuals (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_ice
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on an icy or snow-covered surface: the tripled following time driver manuals advise
param_proposals.source: driver manuals (as proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_127_1)

segmentation.text: When stopping is required
at a railroad crossing
the driver
shall keep as far to the right of the highway
as possible
and
shall not form two lanes of traffic
unless the highway is marked for four or more lanes of traffic.

elements.justification: "Stopping" (DEF-NRS-484A-260) is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle"; that it is required is read through the devices in the scene that require a halt of the subject's traffic: dev.railway_signal_or_gate, "the devices at a level crossing; lights in {flashing, dark}; gate in {up, lowering, down, raising, none}", with lights flashing or the gate lowering or down; dev.stop_sign, "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"; dev.traffic_signal showing circular_red; dev.human_direction with indication stop and role police_officer or railroad_flagger. Each must govern (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"). dev.governs is "not a stand-in for a position": the place of the stop is not read from governance but from s2's distance to the crossing. dev.traffic_signal is not a sign; the signal's state is read, not a sign's.

st.railway_crossing: "level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail"; "railroad" (DEF-NRS-484A-200) is "a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails": a level crossing of a railway with the roadway is a railroad crossing, and a streetcar line laid along the street forms no level crossing of a railway with the roadway, so the definition's exclusion is already made by the contract. The subject is at the crossing where st.region_geometry, "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)", is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach; region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy, and no occupancy is read from it.

"Driver" (DEF-NRS-484A-080) means "every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle": the duty binds the conduct of a vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"); ru.aggregate is not a stand-in for the relational role of who drives, which is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

The right of the highway the subject is on: st.highway "the entire public way between its boundary lines" occupied by the subject (rel.occupies); st.road_edge "curb or edge of the roadway" lying on that way (st.on_way, "the public way a structure region lies on"); the edge is on the subject's right where prim.region_lateral_offset, "the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user", is negative. st.on_way is not nearness to a way: the edge's belonging to the way is read from the relation, not from distance.

operationalizations.standard: as far to the right of the highway as possible
operationalizations.convention: A vehicle kept as far right as it can be placed stands with its body within the curb clearance of a parallel-parked car plus lane-keeping variability and an edge margin of the right-hand edge of the roadway: the ground distance from its body to a road edge on its right (st.region_geometry, prim.region_lateral_offset negative) is at most p.pullover_edge_gap. A vehicle in any lane but the rightmost, or wandering left within the rightmost, is farther.

NRS_484B_560_3_o1.applicability: The subject is a vehicle; its body is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach of a railroad crossing c (st.railway_crossing, st.region_geometry); and some device d governs (dev.governs) a travel region r whose footprint the subject overlaps (rel.occupies) and requires a halt of r's traffic at this observation: a dev.railway_signal_or_gate whose lights are flashing or whose gate is lowering or down, a dev.stop_sign, a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, or a dev.human_direction of role police_officer or railroad_flagger with indication stop.
NRS_484B_560_3_o1.obligation: At every such observation, some st.road_edge e lies on a highway h the subject occupies (st.on_way(e, h), rel.occupies(subject, h)), lies to the subject's right (prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, e) < 0), and the ground distance from the subject's body to e (st.region_geometry) is at most p.pullover_edge_gap. Where no such edge is found the duty is violated; where the offset or the distance of every candidate edge is unobserved, unknown.

narrowings.why: "the driver" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; whoever or whatever controls it.
That a device is official, placed by a public authority or railroad, is read from its presence.
"the right of the highway" is read as the right-hand edge of the roadway; a shoulder beyond that edge is not a place the vehicle is required to move onto.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Railway signal lights flashing and gate down govern the two-lane approach of a one-way roadway; the subject car halts 8 m from the railway crossing in the left lane, its body 4.5 m from the right-hand road edge (prim.region_lateral_offset negative), farther than p.pullover_edge_gap.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the subject's lane 10 m from a railway crossing on a two-lane two-way highway; the subject car halts straddling the centre line, its body 2.5 m from the right-hand road edge.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same crossing and flashing lights; the subject car halts 8 m from the crossing in the rightmost lane, its body 0.4 m from the right-hand road edge.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car is 8 m from a railway crossing whose lights are dark and gate up; no stop sign, red signal or stop direction governs its lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Lights flashing govern the subject's lane near a crossing; the source maps regions without their outline, so the distance to the crossing and to the road edge is unobserved.

param_proposals.name: p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a vehicle's body to a railroad grade crossing within which the vehicle is at the crossing, on the stretch where a halt for the crossing is made: the 50-ft outer bound of the zone in which grade-crossing practice places the halt before the nearest rail
param_proposals.source: MUTCD Part 8 highway-rail grade crossing stop-line placement and the Uniform Vehicle Code grade-crossing stop zone

param_proposals.name: p.pullover_edge_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between a vehicle body and the right-hand curb or roadway edge within which a vehicle pulled over to clear the way counts as as close to the edge as it can be placed: the curb clearance of a parallel-parked car (about 0.3 m) plus lane-keeping variability and an edge margin
param_proposals.source: parallel-parking curb clearance and lane-keeping variability in naturalistic driving data

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady yellow signal alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
is thereby warned that the related green movement is being terminated or that a steady red indication will be exhibited immediately thereafter,
and
such vehicular traffic
must not enter the intersection
when the red signal is exhibited.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a steady yellow signal alone is circular_yellow and no other state (not flashing_yellow, a flashing indication, and no arrow beside it). Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).
'such vehicular traffic' refers back to s2: the same admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the traffic that faced the yellow.

'enter the intersection': the subject's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') intersection i (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'), having not overlapped it at the previous observation. Not a stand-in: st.intersection is not the crosswalk or the stop line. As the index maps 'shall not enter or proceed through an intersection' (NRS_484B_270_4).

'when the red signal is exhibited': at the observation of the entry the head s that governs c (dev.governs) displays the steady red indication the yellow announced (dev.traffic_signal state circular_red), with no green arrow and no flashing yellow arrow beside it (narrowing on s6).

residues.why: The words state what the steady yellow indication tells the traffic facing it. They impose no duty and set no condition of the duty in s6, which the rule carries in full.

NRS_484B_307_6a.applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, occupies at the judged observation, or occupied at the previous one, a travel region c whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters) and which a traffic signal head s governs (dev.governs); and s displayed a steady yellow alone (circular_yellow, no other state) at some observation since the subject has occupied c without interruption: it faced the yellow on this approach.
NRS_484B_307_6a.obligation: The subject does not enter i while the red is exhibited: it is not the case that its footprint overlaps i at the judged observation, did not overlap i at the previous observation, and s displays circular_red at the judged observation with no green arrow and no flashing yellow arrow.

narrowings.why: 'the red signal' is read as the steady red indication the yellow precedes (circular_red). Where s displays a green arrow or a flashing yellow arrow beside the red, an entry for that arrow's movement is the arrow's signal (paragraphs 4 and 7), and this duty is not read on it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies lane c, which enters i and is governed by head s; s displays circular_yellow alone while the car is 30 m short of i at 14 m/s; s changes to circular_red alone 3 s later, and the car's footprint comes to overlap i 0.5 s after the red appears.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same yellow; the car's footprint comes to overlap i while s still displays circular_yellow alone.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: s displays circular_green alone at every observation while the car occupies c; the car enters i.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not record which intersection lane c enters: whether the car faces a signal of this intersection is unknown.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a green straight-through arrow alone:
Vehicular traffic facing the signal
may proceed straight through, but must not turn right or left.
Such vehicular traffic
must yield
the right-of-way
to other vehicles
and to pedestrians
lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time the signal is exhibited.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., green_arrow(dir), ...}; several states may be displayed at once': a green straight-through arrow alone is green_arrow(straight) and no other state. Same atom as the index for the signal words of NRS_484B_307_2a.

'Vehicular traffic': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), claimed as ru.aggregate, never expanded. 'facing the signal': the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters; st.intersection) and which the head governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'). Not a stand-in: dev.governs is not a position, st.lane_enters not presence in i. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'Such vehicular traffic' refers back to s2: the same admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, as the index maps 'Such vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or left,' (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'must yield': kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') tells a subject that moves on toward the other road user from one that holds back, and rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)') is the crash precedence exists to avoid; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s6 reads by the closest approach. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).
'other vehicles': road users of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle other than the subject. Same words, same atom as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'pedestrians': the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'). Same words, same atom as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

'within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk': the other road user's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) intersection i (st.intersection) or a crosswalk (st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') recorded as marking the entrance (st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks') of a travel region (st.travel_region) that enters i (st.lane_enters): the crosswalks of i's approaches. 'at the time the signal is exhibited': at the latest observation at which the head's display (dev.traffic_signal) became the green straight-through arrow alone. Not a stand-in: st.entrance_of is the recorded association, never a distance. Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2a).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210, 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another vehicle or pedestrian approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a closest approach of the two centres, under constant velocities, within the time-to-collision horizon (p.conflict_horizon) at a centre distance below the conflict clearance (p.conflict_centre_clearance); the subject grants precedence where, while its speed is above the halt tolerance (p.halt_speed_tolerance), no such approach to the other road user arises. Direction, speed and proximity, the factors the definition names, enter by degree through the constant-velocity extrapolation of both road users.

NRS_484B_307_5a_o2.applicability: The subject, of the classes traffic and vehicle, faces traffic signal head s: it occupies a travel region c whose entrance end is intersection i (st.lane_enters) and which s governs (dev.governs), or it occupies i and has occupied it at every observation since it entered i from such a c; and s displays a green straight-through arrow alone (green_arrow(straight), no other state) at the judged observation.
NRS_484B_307_5a_o2.obligation: For every road user p other than the subject that is of the class vehicle or of the class pedestrian, whose footprint overlaps i or a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a travel region that enters i at the judged observation, and overlapped one of them at the latest observation at which s's display became the green straight-through arrow alone: it is not the case that the subject's speed is above p.halt_speed_tolerance while the closest approach of the two centres lies within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and the subject's body does not touch p's (rel.contact).

narrowings.why: 'lawfully within' is read through the other road user's presence within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time the arrow is exhibited; whether its presence there is lawful is not judged, so the subject yields to every such road user. 'within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time' qualifies both the vehicles and the pedestrians.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Head s governing lane c, which enters i, changes to green_arrow(straight) alone while a pedestrian walks at 1.2 m/s in the crosswalk marking the entrance of the far-side approach of i; the car leaves its halt and proceeds straight at 8 m/s, the closest approach of the two centres lying 1.2 s ahead at 0.5 m, while the pedestrian is still in that crosswalk.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same arrow; no other road user is in the scene; the car proceeds straight through i. The duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: s displays circular_green alone while the car proceeds through i.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not record which carriers' entrances the pedestrian's crosswalk marks: whether it is an adjacent crosswalk is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the pedestrian was on the sidewalk when s's arrow came on and stepped into the crosswalk afterwards: it was not within the crosswalk at the time the signal was exhibited, so no yield is owed to it under this paragraph and the subject complies.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_12_070_B; repeated unchanged

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate
a vehicle of any kind or character
at:
In any event,
a rate of speed greater than 80 miles per hour.

elements.justification: "drive or operate" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: kin.speed, "magnitude of velocity"; the same words map to kin.speed in the run's index.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within an intersection
intending to turn to the left
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction
which is within the intersection
or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver, having so yielded
and having given a signal when and as required,
may make such left turn
and the drivers of all other vehicles
approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
shall yield
the right-of-way
to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: The turning vehicle t: 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'); its driver is its controlled motion.
t 'within an intersection': t's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet').

'Having given a signal when and as required' of a left turn: sig.turn_indicator 'state ∈ {off, left, right}' at left, or sig.hand_signal 'meaning ∈ {..., left, ...}' at left — the two manners a signal of turning is given — at some observation since t came onto the carrier c1 it entered X from: the signal is required on the approach to the turn and through it, which is when the words look for it. The indicator is not a stand-in for the turn itself, which k reads separately.
'May make such left turn': t is making its turn, moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) within X (rel.occupies) since its current movement within X began, with its left-turn plan declared (c).
'The drivers of all other vehicles': the subject, of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, other than t; 'drivers' read through the vehicles' controlled motion.

'Approaching the intersection': the subject occupies a carrier c2 whose entrance end is X (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end') and does not yet overlap X; 'from the opposite direction', per rel.oncoming's not-a-stand-in clause, is c2's st.lane_direction opposed to that of the carrier c1 t entered X from, within p.oncoming_heading_cos.
Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) while t is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact).
'The vehicle making the left turn' is t, of the admitted aggregate, within X (rel.occupies) making the turn the conditions a, b, c, i, j, k describe.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

NRS_484B_253_o2.applicability: At every observation at which the subject occupies a carrier c2 that enters an intersection X (st.lane_enters c2 X) and does not overlap X, and some other road user t of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: overlaps X; declares int.left_turn at X at this observation; entered X (overlapping it continuously since) from a carrier c1 entering X whose designated direction has a dot product with c2's below minus p.oncoming_heading_cos; has been moving within X (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) at every observation since its current movement began — the later of its latest entry into X and its latest rise above p.halt_speed_tolerance while in X; showed a left signal (sig.turn_indicator left or sig.hand_signal left) at some observation since it came onto c1; and complied with NRS_484B_253_o1 (binder subject ↦ t) at the observation at which that current movement began: 'having so yielded'.
NRS_484B_253_o2.obligation: Re-binding X and c2, and quantifying every road user t as in the applicability: for every such t, the subject is not in contact with t (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, t; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, t; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique time-to-collision thresholds

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: design passenger-car dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection and:
The turn is a right turn,
both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane
if the highway has a right turn lane
as set forth in subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b],
or must be made from the extreme right lane.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for 'vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power ...'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the aggregate carries only the class.

st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges' (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of two highways which join one another'); i is the target region of the declared intention and the region whose entry ends the approach: the subject enters i at the observation e at which its footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') having not overlapped it at the observation before. Its approach is a carrier it occupies whose entrance end is i (st.lane_enters: 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'): a lane (st.lane) or, where no lane is mapped, a roadway the source records as a directed approach segment (st.roadway). st.intersection is 'not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line'; st.lane_enters is 'not a stand-in for ... the subject's presence in the intersection', which rel.occupies reads.

The words borrow subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223, which quotes: 'If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning'. In this node the alternative 'or must be made from the extreme right lane' governs where the highway has no such lane: no single st.turn_lane ('a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}') of side right enters i (st.lane_enters) with its designated direction (st.lane_direction) aligned with that of the carrier the subject occupies entering i, the cosine at or above p.approach_lane_same_direction_cos. 'single' is kept: two such lanes leave the highway without a lane 'as set forth' there.

st.lane_adjacency: 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction; lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction'. The extreme right lane of the approach is the lane c entering i (st.lane_enters) whose ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction; 'must be made from' it is the subject's footprint overlapping c (rel.occupies) at the observation before the entry into i. st.lane_adjacency is 'not a stand-in for the marking between two lanes', which is not read. Where the subject's approach is a roadway recorded as a directed approach segment and no lane entering i is mapped on it (st.roadway), that segment carries a single line of traffic and is itself the extreme right lane.

compositions.quote: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
compositions.why: 'as set forth in subsection 4' borrows only that subsection's description of the lane: a single right lane, provided by the highway's design, used only for turning (kept in s6 as exactly one right turn lane of the approach). Whether a right turn lane exists is a fact of the road, not a verdict: the lane is the right turn lane whether or not any vehicle in it complies with the subsection's duty to be driven there only to turn right, so that rule need not apply, hold or be complied with here.

Whether a right turn lane exists is a fact of the road, not a verdict: the lane is the right turn lane whether or not any vehicle in it complies with the subsection's duty not to travel through an intersection, so that rule need not apply, hold or be complied with here.

NRS_484B_400_1_o2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation e is one at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection i (rel.occupies) and did not at the observation before (its entry). int.right_turn(subject, i) is declared true at the observation before e (s2 and s4). At the observation before e the subject occupies a carrier c that enters i (st.lane_enters c i; a lane, or a roadway directed approach segment), and the highway has no right turn lane (s6 with s7): there is not exactly one st.turn_lane of side right entering i whose designated direction (st.lane_direction) makes with c's a cosine at or above p.approach_lane_same_direction_cos. Whether the event occurred is unknown where the observation before e does not show the subject's place.
NRS_484B_400_1_o2.obligation: At the observation before e, the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the extreme right lane of its approach: a lane c entering i whose st.lane_adjacency ordinal equals the count of lanes in its direction; or, where the subject occupies no lane entering i, a roadway directed approach segment entering i. Occupying only lanes entering i of lower ordinal violates the duty; an unobserved ordinal or count makes it unknown where the verdict turns on it.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

The approach and the turn 'made from the extreme right lane' are read at the observation before the entry into the intersection, where the approach ends and the turn begins; a lane change earlier on the approach is not a breach, and the turn is identified by the declared intention and the entry. An unlaned directed approach segment is read as a single line of traffic, itself the extreme right lane.

param_proposals.name: p.approach_lane_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about twenty-five degrees) between the designated directions of two mapped lanes entering one intersection at which they count as lanes of the same approach carrying traffic the same way: the direction noise of map lane segments along a gently curving way, far below the angle between the legs of a junction

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate
a vehicle of any kind or character
at:
A rate of speed greater than
that posted by a public authority
for the particular portion of highway being traversed.

elements.justification: "drive or operate" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: kin.speed, "magnitude of velocity", the motion the duty judges; the same words map to kin.speed in the run's index.

"a vehicle of any kind or character": the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", whatever its class.
The rate of speed is kin.speed, "magnitude of velocity" (m/s), compared strictly greater than the posted value.

The speed posted: dev.speed_limit_sign, "sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit", of kind maximum, structure_maximum or zone, read as the value dev_speed_limit_sign_value (m/s). "Public authority" (DEF-NRS-484A-195, "the Department of Transportation or the local authority having jurisdiction") is the sign's legal source, read from the sign's presence.

The particular portion of highway being traversed is the travel region (st.travel_region) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) that the sign governs (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"). dev.governs is "not a stand-in for a position": no halt place is read from it, only which portion the posting covers.

NRS_484B_600_1c.applicability: The subject is a vehicle whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.speed_limit_sign of kind maximum, structure_maximum or zone.
NRS_484B_600_1c.obligation: For every such sign d governing a travel region the subject occupies, kin.speed(subject) is not greater than dev_speed_limit_sign_value(d).

narrowings.why: "drive or operate" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
That the speed is posted by a public authority is read from the presence of the speed limit sign.

scenarios.narrative: A maximum speed limit sign of 20.1 m/s governs the lane the subject car occupies; kin.speed is 24 m/s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same sign; kin.speed is 19 m/s.

segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are erected giving notice thereof,
a person shall not drive a vehicle
onto or from any controlled-access highway
except at those entrances and exits which are indicated by such devices.

elements.justification: "Official traffic-control device" (DEF-NRS-484A-145) is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority"; the devices giving notice of where a controlled-access highway may be entered and left are dev.regulatory_sign, "a point regulation by catalogue code", with code entrance or exit; their erection is read from the presence of such a sign in the scene. A sign is "not a stand-in for a manoeuvre or a road feature": the sign is read, not the ramp.

"vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"; "a person ... drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

"Controlled-access highway" (DEF-NRS-484A-060) is "every highway to or from which ... persons have no legal right of access except at such points only": st.controlled_access, "a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes". Driving onto it is the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap it (rel.occupies, which lists the controlled-access lane among its regions) having not overlapped it at the previous one; driving from it is the observation at which it ceases to overlap it, having overlapped it at the previous one.

An entrance or exit indicated by such devices is a travel region (st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... a lane, ... roadway, ... shoulder") by a dev.regulatory_sign of code entrance (for driving onto) or exit (for driving from). The subject drives onto the highway at an indicated entrance where, at its entry, it occupies (rel.occupies) such an entrance-governed region; it drives from it at an indicated exit where, at the last observation it overlapped the highway, it occupied such an exit-governed region. dev.governs is never a controlled-access region itself, so the governed lane is read, and "not a stand-in for a position" is respected: no halt place is read from it.

NRS_484B_587_1.applicability: Some dev.regulatory_sign with code entrance or exit is present in the scene; the subject is a vehicle; and at this observation it enters a controlled-access highway ca (rises(rel.occupies(subject, ca))) or leaves it (rises(not rel.occupies(subject, ca))).
NRS_484B_587_1.obligation: At an entry into ca: the subject occupies some travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code entrance. At a departure from ca: at the previous observation the subject both occupied ca and occupied some travel region r governed by a dev.regulatory_sign of code exit; written as rises(not X) where X is 'occupies ca and occupies a region governed by an exit-coded regulatory sign', which at a departure (X false here) holds exactly when X held at the previous observation. Otherwise the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: "a person ... drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; whoever or whatever controls it.
That entrance and exit signs are official and give notice of the controlled access is read from their presence in the scene.
An entrance or exit indicated by the devices is read as a travel region an entrance- or exit-coded regulatory sign governs.

segmentation.text: If the driver of a vehicle
intends to turn
at an intersection and:
The turn is a right turn,
both the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane
if the highway has a right turn lane
as set forth in subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223 [NRS-484B-223-4a, NRS-484B-223-4b],
or must be made from the extreme right lane.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for 'vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power ...'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the aggregate carries only the class.

st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges' (DEF-NRS-484A-105 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of two highways which join one another'); the intersection i is the target region of the declared intention and the region whose entry ends the approach: the subject enters i at the observation e at which its footprint overlaps i (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') having not overlapped it at the observation before. Its approach is 'a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection' (st.lane_enters: 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), the carriers being lanes (st.lane) or the kinds refining them. st.intersection is 'not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line': no halt place is read. st.lane_enters is 'not a stand-in for ... the subject's presence in the intersection', which rel.occupies reads.

st.turn_lane: 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}'; the right turn lane of the approach is the turn lane t of side right that enters i (st.lane_enters) and that s6 selects. 'the approach for the right turn and the right turn must be made from the right turn lane': the approach ends and the turn begins at the subject's entry into i, and at the observation before that entry the subject's footprint overlaps t (rel.occupies). st.turn_lane refines st.lane, whose exclusion 'a half of the roadway or a lateral position within a lane' does not apply: lane membership is read by occupancy. The approach is read at its end and the turn at its start (narrowing disclosed): a lane change into t earlier on the approach is not a breach.

The words borrow subsection 4 of NRS 484B.223, which quotes: 'If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning'. The highway the subject approaches on has such a lane where exactly one st.turn_lane ('a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}') of side right enters i (st.lane_enters) and its designated direction (st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') is aligned with that of a lane the subject occupies entering i, the cosine of the angle between the two directions at or above p.approach_lane_same_direction_cos; turn lanes of other approaches to i point along other legs and are not the subject's highway's. 'single' is kept: a second such lane makes the condition false. 'used only for turning' is the turn lane's own kind. st.lane_direction is read normalised, as its contract says.
