scenarios.narrative: Same layout; the subject occupies the right turn lane at the observation before it enters the intersection, with int.right_turn declared.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject enters the intersection with int.right_turn declared, but no right turn lane enters the intersection from its approach (only through lanes).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid, but the source declares st.lane_direction absent, so whether the right turn lane belongs to the subject's approach is unknown and the subject is not in it.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A right turn lane enters the intersection on the subject's approach; the subject enters from the through lane with int.left_turn declared and no int.right_turn: the duty does not arise.

param_proposals.name: p.approach_lane_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about twenty-five degrees) between the designated directions of two mapped lanes entering one intersection at which they count as lanes of the same approach carrying traffic the same way: the direction noise of map lane segments along a gently curving way, far below the angle between the legs of a junction
param_proposals.source: map lane-direction noise; mirrors p.lane_opposed_direction_cos proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_307_8a_o2

segmentation.text: If an official traffic-control device indicates that a U-turn is prohibited,
the driver
shall obey the directions of the device.

elements.justification: 'official traffic-control device' uses DEF-NRS-484A-145: 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'. The law's own words 'indicates that a U-turn is prohibited' limit it to the members whose indication is that prohibition: dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code ... no_u_turn ...', with code no_u_turn; a signal's arrows indicate stop or go, not a U-turn prohibition, and no marking of the ontology states one (disclosed in PLAN.md). The sign's 'conditions attribute ... read as that row says (unconditional when empty, unknown when absent)' is read through prim.conditions_hold ('the structured conditions of a device (dev.zone_sign, dev.regulatory_sign) hold at the observation for a road user'): the sign indicates the prohibition while its conditions hold. The sign directs the traffic of the travel regions it governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', over st.travel_region): the subject is under it where its footprint overlaps such a region (rel.occupies), or overlaps an intersection (st.intersection) that a governed lane (st.lane) enters (st.lane_enters: 'a device governs a lane and the lane enters an intersection; which intersection a device controls is read through both') having entered that intersection from that lane. dev.regulatory_sign is 'not a stand-in for a manoeuvre': the U-turn is read by its concept (s3). 'official' is read by the sign's presence (observable_reading status).

'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the class it presupposes is the vehicle of that definition's words, carried by the run's admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'), claimed as the aggregate and never expanded. The exclusion 'a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle — never membership' does not apply: the aggregate carries the vehicle's class only.

drv.motion.u_turn (definition DEF-NRS-484B-077): 'Road user a has turned “so as to proceed in the opposite direction”: its heading has reversed, “whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not”'. The direction of a no-U-turn sign is that no U-turn be made under it: 'obey the directions of the device' is the subject making no U-turn (the concept not holding at its recognition) where the sign governs it while the U-turn is under way. The concept 'says nothing of the way on which a turns', which s1 supplies.

NRS_484B_403_2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation is one at which drv.motion.u_turn(subject; window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) holds, i.e. a U-turn's recognition; the U-turn is under way at the observations of the window behind at which the subject's kin.yaw_rate exceeds p.turn_yaw_rate_tol in magnitude. The duty applies where, at some observation while the U-turn is under way, a dev.regulatory_sign s of code no_u_turn whose conditions hold for the subject there (prim.conditions_hold) governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), or governs a lane l that enters (st.lane_enters) an intersection the subject's footprint overlaps, the subject having occupied l at the observation before it entered that intersection.
NRS_484B_403_2.obligation: drv.motion.u_turn(subject) with window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min and yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol does not hold at the judged observation: a U-turn made under a no-U-turn sign disobeys it. Where the window is truncated or a yaw rate in it is missing, the concept and its occasion are unknown.

narrowings.why: 'official' is the legal status of the sign: the no-U-turn sign present and governing the subject's region is the evidence.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
'obey the directions of the device' is read as making no U-turn under it: the only direction a no-U-turn sign gives.

under_way.words: the observations of the window behind the recognition at which the subject's heading is turning
under_way.justification: kin.yaw_rate: 'rate of change of heading'. drv.motion.u_turn is recognized where 'the heading has stopped turning'; the observations of its window at which the yaw-rate magnitude exceeds p.turn_yaw_rate_tol (the concept's own yaw_tol) are those at which the reversal is being made, which tells them from travel before it began; 'not a stand-in for road curvature — a vehicle yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres'.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.regulatory_sign of code no_u_turn with empty conditions governs the subject's approach lane; the subject begins turning in that lane, enters the intersection and reverses its heading (heading change in the reversal band, then yaw below tolerance).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same sign and lane; the subject drives straight through the intersection: no U-turn is recognized.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject makes a U-turn on a lane no no_u_turn sign governs; no sign governs the intersection or a lane entering it from which the subject came.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid, but the source declares kin.yaw_rate absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The no_u_turn sign's conditions state hours that do not include the time of the observation (prim.conditions_hold false throughout the U-turn); the subject makes the U-turn under it.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1
scenarios.narrative: The no_u_turn sign governs the lane the subject occupies as it begins turning; the subject completes the reversal on lanes the sign does not govern, so that the governed lane is overlapped only at the first observations while the U-turn is under way.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the governed lane only before it begins turning; it continues past the sign's governed stretch and makes the whole U-turn later on lanes and an intersection the sign does not govern and did not enter from a governed lane.

param_proposals.name: p.vehicle_turn_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of a turn by a motor vehicle at a junction or into or out of a driveway, from the start of its heading change to its end, including the crossing of opposing lanes
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_217_2

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1

param_proposals.name: p.turn_yaw_rate_tol
param_proposals.convention: the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which a road user's heading counts as no longer turning: the yaw-rate noise floor of the source
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive a vehicle
over any bridge or other elevated structure constituting a part of a highway
at a speed which is greater than the maximum speed which can be maintained with safety to the bridge or structure,
when such structure is signposted as provided in this section
[(3) appended below].

The Department of Transportation upon request from any local authority shall, or upon its own initiative may, conduct an investigation of any bridge or other elevated structure constituting a part of a highway constructed and maintained under the authority granted by chapter 408 of NRS,
and if it thereupon finds that such structure cannot with safety to itself withstand vehicles traveling at the speed otherwise permissible under chapters 484A to 484E, inclusive, of NRS,
the Department shall determine and declare the maximum speed of vehicles which such structure can safely withstand,
and shall cause or permit suitable signs stating such maximum speed to be erected and maintained
at a distance of 100 feet before each end of such structure.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'any person to drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Driving over a bridge or other elevated structure: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.elevated_structure, 'bridge, viaduct or tunnel carrying the roadway', that lies on a highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway) — the structure 'constituting a part of a highway'.

The maximum speed which can be maintained with safety to the structure is the one the sign states: the value of a dev.speed_limit_sign of kind structure_maximum ('sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit') governing (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) while on the structure; greater than is kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') above that value. The safety of the structure is the authority's determination (y8), not a judgement left to the driver, so the span is no standard.

Signposted: a dev.speed_limit_sign of kind structure_maximum governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) while on the structure; 'as provided in this section' is read from the sign's presence (observable_reading status). dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position', so the sign's distance from the structure is not read from it.

The suitable signs stating such maximum speed are dev.speed_limit_sign of kind structure_maximum, whose value is the declared maximum; their erection and maintenance are read from their presence and governance (dev.governs) of the structure's travel regions.

residues.why: The authority's investigation, on request or on its own initiative, of structures built under chapter 408 of NRS (outside the corpus) is the process behind the posting; the rule reads the posted sign as the evidence of it.

The authority's finding that the structure cannot withstand the otherwise permissible speeds (chapters 484A to 484E, no node of the corpus) is the reason for the posting; the rule reads the posted maximum, not the finding.
The authority's determination and declaration of the maximum speed is read through the value the posted sign states; the act of declaring is not observable.

The sign's placement before each end of the structure is the authority's duty; the rule reads the sign's governance of the structure's travel regions, not its distance from the ends, so the placement is not checked.

NRS_484B_633_2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) occupying an elevated structure that lies on a highway, and a speed limit sign of kind structure_maximum governs a travel region the subject occupies.
NRS_484B_633_2.obligation: Re-binding every speed limit sign of kind structure_maximum governing a travel region the subject occupies while it occupies an elevated structure on a highway, the subject's speed is at or below that sign's value. Otherwise violated.

narrowings.why: 'any person to drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

'signposted as provided in this section' is read from the presence of a structure-maximum speed sign governing the travel region the subject occupies on the structure; the authority's investigation, declaration and placement are presumed from it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A truck occupies a bridge lying on a highway; a structure_maximum speed sign of 11 m/s governs the bridge lane it occupies; its speed is 16 m/s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same truck on the same bridge at 10 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car on a bridge lying on a highway whose lanes no structure_maximum speed sign governs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe which regions the speed limit sign governs, so whether the bridge is signposted is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car at 16 m/s on an ordinary roadway lane, off any elevated structure, though a structure_maximum sign governs the lane ahead of the bridge.

segmentation.text: After the establishment of a speed zone and the installation of appropriate signs to control speed,
it is unlawful for any person to drive a motor vehicle
upon the road
and in the speed zone
in excess of the speed therein authorized.

elements.justification: The established speed zone and its installed signs are read by their presence: dev.zone_sign of kind speed_zone, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road', and dev.speed_limit_sign, 'sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit; kind ∈ {maximum, minimum, structure_maximum, zone}', both governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region). dev.zone_sign is 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now'; no posted conditions are read here, the zone sign's presence is the zone. The establishment by an authority is a status read from the signs (observable_reading status).

'motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails. The term does not include an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'any person to drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

In the speed zone: the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region (st.travel_region) that a dev.zone_sign of kind speed_zone, not marking the zone's end, governs (dev.governs) and that lies on a highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway): the road of DEF-NRS-484A-215 is 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway' outside a city, whose observable part is the highway.

The speed therein authorized is the value of a dev.speed_limit_sign of kind zone or maximum ('sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit') governing a travel region the subject occupies; in excess is kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity', m/s) above that value.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies within the territorial limits of an incorporated city, as the map's reading classifies the area

NRS_484B_620_2.applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle); its place is not within an incorporated city (the assumption asm.within_incorporated_city is declared false: a road is, by DEF-NRS-484A-215, a highway 'outside the territorial limits of a city'); and it occupies a travel region r lying on a highway that is governed by a zone sign of kind speed_zone (not an end sign) and by a speed limit sign of kind zone or maximum.
NRS_484B_620_2.obligation: Re-binding every travel region the subject occupies that lies on a highway and is governed by a zone sign of kind speed_zone (not an end sign), the subject's speed is at or below the value of every speed limit sign of kind zone or maximum governing that region. A speed above such a value is violated.

narrowings.why: The establishment of the zone and the installation of its signs by an authority are read from the presence of the speed-zone sign and the speed limit sign governing the subject's region.
'any person to drive' is read through the motor vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.
The speed 'therein authorized' is read as the value of a speed limit sign of kind zone or maximum governing the subject's region; a minimum speed sign authorizes no maximum and is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car outside any incorporated city (asm.within_incorporated_city false) occupies a lane on a highway governed by a speed_zone zone sign and a zone speed limit sign of 20 m/s; its speed is 25 m/s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same scene with the car at 18 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car outside any city on a highway lane that no speed_zone zone sign governs; only a general maximum speed sign is present.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not supply the car's speed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the reading declares the place within an incorporated city (asm.within_incorporated_city true): it is no road.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not make a U-turn
in a business district,
except at an intersection
or on a divided highway
where an appropriate opening or crossing place exists.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom; ru.aggregate 'true when the user carries an included class'. 'The driver of' is the relational role DEF-NRS-484A-080 defines ('every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle'), which the aggregate is not a stand-in for: it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading), so the binder is the vehicle whose conduct is judged. Same mapping as the index row 'The driver of a vehicle'.

drv.motion.u_turn denotes a road user that 'has turned "so as to proceed in the opposite direction": its heading has reversed, "whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not"', the definition DEF-NRS-484B-077 ('the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not'). The concept 'says nothing of the way on which a turns', so the definition's 'upon a highway' is carried beside it: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') of an st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines'); st.highway is not a stand-in for the roadway, and the definition names the highway, not the roadway. The index maps 'shall not make a U-turn' to drv.motion.u_turn alone; the highway anchor is added here because the defined word carries it (PLAN.md).

st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges; a junction where an alley meets another way ... is no intersection', matching DEF-NRS-484A-105 ('the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... The junction of an alley with a street, road or highway shall not constitute an intersection'). It is not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line, which the words do not name. rel.occupies anchors the subject's own intersection: 'at an intersection' is the reversal made with the footprint overlapping it.

DEF-NRS-484A-070: 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section'. st.median_or_divider is the 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'; st.on_way ties it to 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; rel.occupies anchors the subject on that st.highway. Same mapping as the index row 'driven upon a divided highway'. st.on_way is not a stand-in for nearness: the divider lies on the very way the subject occupies.

st.median_or_divider carries an 'opening attribute where a crossover exists': the opening or crossing place in the divider. rel.occupies of a divider region having that attribute is the reversal passing through the crossover. Same atoms as the index row 'except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space'. 'appropriate' is the legal status of a feature on the road: the opening's presence is its evidence (observable_reading, status).

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district, as the map's reading classifies the area

NRS_484B_403_3.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The rule is engaged at an observation where the reading declares asm.business_district for the subject's place there; for a reversal of direction, at the observation at which the reversal is recognized.
NRS_484B_403_3.obligation: At the observation at which drv.motion.u_turn(subject; window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) rises while the subject occupies (rel.occupies) an st.highway region, one of the exceptions holds, else violated: (a) at every observation while the reversal is under way the subject occupies an st.intersection region; or (b) at every observation while it is under way the subject occupies an st.highway region on which (st.on_way) an st.median_or_divider region lies, and at some observation while it is under way the subject's footprint overlaps an st.median_or_divider region on that highway having the opening attribute. Where no reversal is recognized the duty is complied with.

narrowings.why: 'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle whoever or whatever controls it.

'an appropriate opening or crossing place' is read by the presence of a divider region carrying the opening attribute on the divided highway the subject occupies; its legal suitability is presumed from that presence.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_district declared true; the subject vehicle on a two-way street mid-block, with no intersection and no divider anywhere near, reverses its heading by about 180 degrees within 8 s with its yaw rate observed throughout, occupying the highway region.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_district declared true; the subject vehicle reverses its heading by about 180 degrees while its footprint overlaps an intersection region at every observation of the turn.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_district declared false for every place of the trace; the subject vehicle makes a mid-block reversal of direction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_district declared true; the subject vehicle's heading reverses mid-block but kin.yaw_rate is not observed on this source, so neither the reversal nor its under-way observations can be decided.

scenarios.name: occasion_s4
scenarios.narrative: In the business district the subject begins the reversal inside an intersection region and completes it mid-block beyond the intersection, so it occupies the intersection for part of the turn only; no divider.

scenarios.name: occasion_s4_outside
scenarios.narrative: In the business district the subject approaches on a lane outside the intersection, enters it, and makes the whole reversal with its footprint overlapping the intersection at every observation while the turn is under way.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5
scenarios.narrative: In the business district the subject starts its reversal on a stretch whose way carries no divider and finishes it where a divider with an opening lies on the way, passing through the opening; it is on the divided highway for part of the turn only and occupies no intersection.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5_outside
scenarios.narrative: In the business district the subject, having driven on an undivided stretch before, makes the whole reversal on a highway on which a divider lies, passing through the divider's opening mid-turn.

scenarios.name: occasion_s6
scenarios.narrative: In the business district, on a divided highway throughout the reversal, the subject's footprint overlaps the divider region with the opening attribute during the middle part of the turn only.

scenarios.name: occasion_s6_outside
scenarios.narrative: In the business district, on a divided highway throughout, the subject drives through a divider opening region before beginning its reversal and then reverses within one roadway without overlapping any opening while the turn is under way; no intersection.

under_way.justification: kin.yaw_rate is the 'rate of change of heading'; its magnitude above p.turn_yaw_rate_tol tells an observation inside the reversal from one before it began, when the vehicle ran straight on the same region. It is a reading of the road user's motion, not of a place.

param_proposals.name: p.vehicle_turn_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of a turn by a motor vehicle at a junction or into or out of a driveway, from the start of its heading change to its end, including the crossing of opposing lanes
param_proposals.source: observed turning-manoeuvre durations of passenger cars at urban junctions

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: geometric convention separating a turn (about 90 degrees) from a reversal (about 180 degrees)

param_proposals.name: p.turn_yaw_rate_tol
param_proposals.convention: the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which a road user's heading counts as no longer turning: the yaw-rate noise floor of the source
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate noise of vehicle inertial and tracking sources

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for a person to:
Drive a vehicle
in willful or wanton disregard of the safety of persons or property
on a highway
or premises to which the public has access.

elements.justification: The forbidden driving is read through the vehicle's motion: kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') and kin.accel_longitudinal ('acceleration along heading, signed', 'Not a stand-in for: speed'), the magnitudes the operationalization of d3 bounds.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); 'Drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency), never as membership.

Reuses the index mapping of 'on a highway' (LVMC_11_16_090_A_o1): the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', which is DEF-NRS-484A-095's 'entire width between the boundary lines of every way'; 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway', so the whole highway is read.

operationalizations.standard: willful or wanton disregard of the safety of persons or property
operationalizations.convention: Exhibition-driving and traffic-conflict conventions: the driving shows disregard of the safety of persons or property where the vehicle travels at or above p.exhibition_speed_min (beyond any posted limit), or where it accelerates at p.exhibition_accel_min or more while another road user's centre is predicted to come within p.conflict_centre_clearance of its own within p.conflict_horizon (driving hard into a conflict).

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies on premises to which the public has access, as the map's reading classifies the area

NRS_484B_653_1a.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that occupies a highway, or whose place the reading declares to be premises to which the public has access (asm.public_access_premises).
NRS_484B_653_1a.obligation: Violated where the subject's speed is at or above p.exhibition_speed_min, or where its longitudinal acceleration is at or above p.exhibition_accel_min while some road user other than the subject has a closest approach to it within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance at or below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Otherwise compliant (a surrogate: its verdicts are evidence, not a legal conclusion on the driver's state of mind).

narrowings.why: 'Drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

'willful or wanton' is a state of mind and is read only through conduct (extreme speed, hard acceleration into a predicted conflict); 'persons or property' is read through other road users and the persons and property they carry; property that is no road user is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car on a highway travels at 50 m/s, above the exhibition speed.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car on a highway travels at 15 m/s with gentle acceleration; no road user is in predicted conflict with it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car on a private farm way, off any highway, with the reading declaring the place not premises to which the public has access.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car on a highway with no other road user in the scene, but the source does not supply its speed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car in a public parking lot (asm.public_access_premises true) accelerates at 5 m/s^2 toward a pedestrian whose centre is predicted to come within the conflict clearance within the conflict horizon.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car alone on a highway at 25 m/s: no other road user in the scene, speed below the exhibition speed.

param_proposals.name: p.exhibition_speed_min
param_proposals.convention: a speed of about 100 mph, beyond any posted limit in the jurisdiction
param_proposals.source: Nevada posted speed limits (maximum 80 mph)

param_proposals.name: p.exhibition_accel_min
param_proposals.convention: harsh-acceleration threshold: a longitudinal acceleration of about 0.4 g, beyond ordinary driving
param_proposals.source: naturalistic driving harsh-event thresholds

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique (Hyden; time-to-collision thresholds)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger car design dimensions

segmentation.text: A vehicle
shall not be turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction
upon any curve,
or upon the approach to or near the crest of a grade,
where such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, one atom; same mapping as the index row 'A vehicle'.

drv.motion.u_turn denotes a road user that 'has turned "so as to proceed in the opposite direction": its heading has reversed', the very words of the span; the reversal 'whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not' is denoted. 'be turned' by the one at the controls is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading).

st.curvature is the 'horizontal curvature of the roadway at a point, as a magnitude (1/m, never negative): a bend to either hand has the same value'; 'any curve' names the feature without a size, so it is read as the curvature at the subject's place standing clear of zero, above p.curvature_resolution, which names only the source's resolution. rel.occupies of an st.roadway region ('the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') anchors the curve to the way the subject is upon. st.curvature is the road's geometry, not the vehicle's yaw (kin.yaw_rate is 'not a stand-in for road curvature').

st.crest is 'the place on a roadway's longitudinal profile where the slope changes from rising to falling in the direction of travel, carried as a region with a reference point and a boundary, so the ground distance from a road user to it is read through st.region_geometry' -- 'the crest of a grade'. st.region_geometry gives 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'; the approach to or nearness to the crest is that distance at most p.crest_near_reach. st.crest is not a stand-in for the slope at a point (st.grade) nor for the view (st.sight_distance), which s5 reads on its own.

st.sight_distance is 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it, whether or not any road user is there': 'such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet' is that distance at the subject's place below 500 ft. It is not a stand-in for whether an actual road user saw another (rel.visible): the words state what could be seen at the place, whether or not another vehicle is present, so no other vehicle is quantified (perception reading).

NRS_484B_407.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The rule is engaged at an observation where, at that one observation, (i) the subject occupies an st.roadway region and st_curvature at its place exceeds p.curvature_resolution, or the ground distance (st.region_geometry) from its body to an st.crest region is at most p.crest_near_reach; and (ii) st.sight_distance at its place is below 500 ft. For a reversal of direction, it is engaged where (i) and (ii) hold together at some one observation while the reversal is under way (yaw rate magnitude above p.turn_yaw_rate_tol, within the act's window behind its recognition).
NRS_484B_407.obligation: drv.motion.u_turn(subject; window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) does not rise: a reversal recognized where the rule is engaged is a violation; otherwise complied with.

narrowings.why: 'be turned' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever is at the controls.

'cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction' is read through the sight distance of the subject's place (what could be seen at a place), not through any actual driver's perception.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle on a roadway bend (curvature well above the resolution) where st.sight_distance is 100 m reverses its heading by about 180 degrees within 8 s, yaw rate observed.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: On the same bend with st.sight_distance 80 m the subject drives through without reversing; no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject reverses direction on a straight, level roadway (curvature at or below the resolution) with no crest within the reach and st.sight_distance 400 m.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject reverses direction on a roadway bend; st.sight_distance is not observed on this source, so whether the condition holds is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3
scenarios.narrative: The subject begins its reversal on a straight stretch and the second half of the turn takes place where the roadway curves; sight distance is 100 m throughout; no crest near.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject is on the bend (sight distance 100 m) only before the reversal begins; it makes the whole reversal on the straight stretch beyond, where sight distance is 400 m; no crest near.

scenarios.name: occasion_s4
scenarios.narrative: On a straight roadway the subject begins its reversal farther than the reach from a crest and ends it within the reach, where sight distance is 90 m.

scenarios.name: occasion_s4_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes within the reach of a crest (sight 90 m) before the reversal begins and makes the whole reversal on a straight level stretch far beyond it, where sight distance is 400 m.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5
scenarios.narrative: On a bend the subject begins its reversal where sight distance is 200 m, and during the turn moves to where it is 120 m.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5_outside
scenarios.narrative: On a bend the subject passes a spot where sight distance is 120 m before the reversal begins, then makes the whole reversal where sight distance is 250 m.

under_way.words: be turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction
under_way.justification: kin.yaw_rate is the 'rate of change of heading'; its magnitude above p.turn_yaw_rate_tol tells an observation inside the reversal from one before it began, when the vehicle ran on the same bend or near the same crest without turning.

param_proposals.name: p.vehicle_turn_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of a turn by a motor vehicle at a junction or into or out of a driveway, from the start of its heading change to its end, including the crossing of opposing lanes
param_proposals.source: observed turning-manoeuvre durations of passenger cars at urban junctions

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: geometric convention separating a turn (about 90 degrees) from a reversal (about 180 degrees)

param_proposals.name: p.turn_yaw_rate_tol
param_proposals.convention: the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which a road user's heading counts as no longer turning: the yaw-rate noise floor of the source
param_proposals.source: yaw-rate noise of vehicle inertial and tracking sources

param_proposals.name: p.curvature_resolution
param_proposals.convention: the horizontal curvature at or below which a mapped roadway reads as straight: the curvature resolution of map centrelines (a radius of about two kilometres)
param_proposals.source: HD-map centreline curvature resolution

param_proposals.name: p.crest_near_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a road user's body to a crest within which the road user is on the approach to or near the crest: the length of a crest vertical curve over which forward sight is restricted, about the stopping sight distance at 90 km/h
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance and crest vertical curve design

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not make a U-turn
in an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone
except:
(a) When there are no children present;
(b) On a day on which school is not in session;
(c) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(d) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or (e) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

As used in this section, “speed limit beacon” means a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit in a school zone or school crossing zone is in effect.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for 'vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power ...'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency), so the exclusion 'a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle — never membership' does not apply: the aggregate carries only the vehicle's class.

drv.motion.u_turn (definition DEF-NRS-484B-077): 'Road user a has turned “so as to proceed in the opposite direction”: its heading has reversed, “whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not”', recognized when the heading change over the window lies in the reversal band and the heading has stopped turning. 'make a U-turn' is that act by the subject; 'shall not' forbids its recognition. DEF-NRS-484B-077 places the turning 'upon a highway': the zone's travel regions (s3) lie on highways, so no further condition is added. The concept 'says nothing of the way on which a turns', which s3 supplies.

dev.zone_sign: 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}; end attribute'. Ontology §9: 'Where the same category is also marked on the road by a sign (dev.zone_sign), the sign is the atom and the category is not.' The school zone (DEF-NRS-484B-063: 'those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property') and the school crossing zone (DEF-NRS-484B-060: 'those sections of streets not adjacent to school property that pupils cross while following a designated walking route to school') are those categories; the area designated as either is the stretch a zone sign z of kind school or school_crossing, not an end sign, governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', over st.travel_region); the subject makes the U-turn in it where, while the U-turn is under way, its footprint overlaps such a region r (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold', read only in exception (e); dev.governs is 'not a stand-in for a position'. 'designated' is read by the sign's presence (observable_reading status).

ru.child: 'pedestrian who is visibly a child'. Children are present in the zone where some child's body lies within p.pedestrian_near_reach of a travel region z governs (st.region_geometry: 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)'), so a child on the sidewalk beside the zone's lanes counts; 'there are no children present' is no such child. st.region_geometry is 'not a stand-in for occupancy': the reach reads presence in the area, not a footprint inside a lane. The reach relates a region to a road user, as a reach may. A child riding a device is not ru.child and is not counted (disclosed in PLAN.md).

dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect', the device the section defines (s13). The zone is designated by a beacon b where b governs the zone's region r (dev.governs over st.travel_region). 'operational' is read as b not inoperative: dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', applies to the beacon's head of lamps. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position.

dev.speed_limit_beacon carries a 'flashing attribute': its lamps flash 'alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. 'not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect' is that attribute false for every operational beacon that governs r.

The negation of s8: no dev.speed_limit_beacon ('a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign') that governs r (dev.governs, over st.travel_region) is present and not inoperative (dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication').

dev.zone_sign's 'conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend' and prim.conditions_hold: 'the structured conditions of a device (dev.zone_sign, dev.regulatory_sign) hold at the observation for a road user'. 'the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect' is prim.conditions_hold false for z, the sign of s3, and the subject. dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold'; env.civil_time is the primitive's own input.

The section's definition of 'speed limit beacon' ('a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit ... is in effect') is the contract of dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. It adds no condition beyond the atom's.

assumptions.meaning: the date of the observation is a day on which the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place is in session, as the reading declares from that school's calendar

the time of the observation lies in the period from a half hour after the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place ceased operation to a half hour before that school next begins operation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule
the pupils of the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place are in class at the time of the observation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule

NRS_484B_363_3.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation is one at which drv.motion.u_turn(subject; window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min, yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol) holds, i.e. the U-turn's recognition. The U-turn is under way at the observations of the window behind (p.vehicle_turn_window) at which the subject's kin.yaw_rate exceeds p.turn_yaw_rate_tol in magnitude. The duty applies where, at some observation while the U-turn is under way, the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.zone_sign z of kind school or school_crossing that is not an end sign, and, for that z and r, none of the exceptions holds at every observation while the U-turn is under way: (a) no ru.child lies within p.pedestrian_near_reach (st.region_geometry distance) of any travel region z governs; (b) asm.school_in_session_day is false; (c) asm.school_outside_operation_margin holds; (d) some dev.speed_limit_beacon governs r and is not dev.inoperative, asm.pupils_in_class holds, and no beacon that governs r and is not inoperative is flashing; (e) no beacon that governs r is present and not inoperative, and prim.conditions_hold for z and the subject is false. Each exception is read as a whole at each observation (its spans joined by 'and' at the same moment) and excuses the act only where it holds at every observation while the act is under way.
NRS_484B_363_3.obligation: drv.motion.u_turn(subject) with window p.vehicle_turn_window, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min and yaw_tol p.turn_yaw_rate_tol does not hold at the judged observation: a recognized U-turn in the zone violates the duty. Where the window behind is truncated or a yaw rate in it is missing, the concept and the occasion are unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver' and 'make' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
'designated' is the legal status of the zone: the zone sign governing the subject's region is the evidence.

under_way.words: the observations of the window behind the recognition at which the subject's heading is turning
under_way.justification: kin.yaw_rate: 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left'. drv.motion.u_turn is recognized where 'the heading has stopped turning'; the observations of its window at which the yaw rate magnitude exceeds p.turn_yaw_rate_tol (the concept's own yaw_tol) are those at which the reversal is being made, which tells them from the straight travel before the act began. 'Not a stand-in for road curvature — a vehicle yaws on a straight road whenever it manoeuvres' is the reason it marks the manoeuvre and not the road.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle on a lane governed by a dev.zone_sign of kind school (not an end sign, conditions holding) reverses its heading within the window (kin.yaw_rate integrated into the reversal band, then below tolerance); a ru.child stands on the sidewalk beside the lane, within the reach; asm.school_in_session_day true, asm.school_outside_operation_margin false; no beacon governs the lane.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same zone, child and declarations as forbid; the vehicle drives straight through the zone and makes no U-turn (heading change below the reversal band).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle makes a U-turn on a street no dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing governs; a ru.child stands nearby.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid, but the source declares kin.yaw_rate absent, so neither the U-turn nor the moment it is under way is decided.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid but no ru.child is within the reach of any region the zone sign governs at any observation while the U-turn is under way: exception (a) holds.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A school_crossing zone sign governs the lane; a beacon that is not inoperative governs it and is not flashing; asm.pupils_in_class true; a child is present; the vehicle makes a U-turn: exception (d) holds.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: No beacon governs the zone's lane; prim.conditions_hold is false for the zone sign throughout the U-turn; a child is present: exception (e) holds.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle begins its U-turn (yaw rate above tolerance) while its footprint overlaps a lane the school zone sign governs and completes it on a lane the sign does not govern; a child is present and no other exception holds.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3_outside
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle occupies the zone's lane only before it begins turning; it leaves the zone and makes the whole U-turn on regions no zone sign governs.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5
scenarios.narrative: A ru.child is within the reach of the zone's lane when the U-turn begins and has walked beyond the reach before it ends; no other exception holds: exception (a) does not hold throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s5_outside
scenarios.narrative: A ru.child is within the reach only before the U-turn begins; no child is within the reach at any observation while the U-turn is under way: exception (a) holds throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s8
scenarios.narrative: A beacon governs the zone's lane, not flashing, with asm.pupils_in_class true; it is not inoperative at the first turning observations and inoperative at the later ones, while the zone sign's conditions hold; a child is present: neither (d) nor (e) holds throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s8_outside
scenarios.narrative: The beacon is inoperative before the U-turn begins and operational, not flashing, at every observation while it is under way, with asm.pupils_in_class true: exception (d) holds throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s10
scenarios.narrative: An operational beacon governs the lane with asm.pupils_in_class true; it is not flashing at the first turning observations and flashing at the later ones; a child is present and no other exception holds.

scenarios.name: occasion_s10_outside
scenarios.narrative: The operational beacon is flashing before the U-turn begins and not flashing at every observation while it is under way, with asm.pupils_in_class true: exception (d) holds throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s11
scenarios.narrative: The beacon governing the lane is inoperative at the first turning observations and operational and flashing at the later ones; the zone sign's conditions do not hold throughout; a child is present: neither (d) nor (e) holds throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s11_outside
scenarios.narrative: The beacon governing the lane is operational before the U-turn begins and inoperative at every observation while it is under way; prim.conditions_hold is false for the zone sign throughout: exception (e) holds throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s12
scenarios.narrative: No beacon governs the lane; prim.conditions_hold for the zone sign is false at the first turning observations and true at the later ones (its posted window opens mid-turn); a child is present.

scenarios.name: occasion_s12_outside
scenarios.narrative: No beacon governs the lane; prim.conditions_hold is true before the U-turn begins and false at every observation while it is under way: exception (e) holds throughout.

param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_217_2; turning-manoeuvre durations of the traffic-engineering literature

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1

param_proposals.name: p.turn_yaw_rate_tol
param_proposals.convention: the yaw-rate magnitude at or below which a road user's heading counts as no longer turning: the yaw-rate noise floor of the source
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by LVMC_11_40_080_o1

param_proposals.name: p.pedestrian_near_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a pedestrian's body to a place, a region or a vehicle within which the pedestrian is near it: about two walking strides plus a curb step
