param_proposals.source: vehicle braking friction tables (accident reconstruction practice)

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.1)
param_proposals.source: vehicle braking friction tables (accident reconstruction practice)

param_proposals.name: p.curve_lateral_accel_max
param_proposals.convention: the lateral acceleration a passenger vehicle sustains on a curve within comfortable side friction on a dry or wet paved surface (about 0.3 g)
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book horizontal curve side-friction factors

param_proposals.name: p.curvature_resolution
param_proposals.convention: the horizontal curvature at or below which a mapped roadway reads as straight: the curvature resolution of map centrelines (a radius of about two kilometres)
param_proposals.source: HD map centreline accuracy

param_proposals.name: p.curve_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: the distance a road user travels ahead within which a bend it reaches counts as one it is approaching: about the stopping sight distance at 90 km/h, the distance over which a driver must already be slowing for the bend
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance and horizontal curve warning placement (MUTCD Table 2C-4)

param_proposals.name: p.crest_near_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a road user's body to a crest within which the road user is on the approach to or near the crest: the length of a crest vertical curve over which forward sight is restricted, about the stopping sight distance at 90 km/h
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book crest vertical curves and stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.narrow_lane_width
param_proposals.convention: the lane width at or below which a highway's lane counts as narrow: below the 3.3 to 3.6 m design lane width at which a passenger car and a truck meet with comfortable lateral clearance
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, lane width

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique (Hyden; time-to-collision thresholds)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger car design dimensions

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in an ordinance enacted pursuant to NRS 484A.469 [DEF-LVMC-11-40-185-A],
an electric scooter
may be operated:
On a roadway, bicycle lane, path or route
at a speed of not more than 15 miles per hour.

elements.justification: 'Electric scooter' is defined by DEF-NRS-484B-018 as 'a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on in an upright or seated position and propelled by its electric motor or by propulsion provided by the rider', within the jurisdiction's limits of weight (not more than 100 pounds) and maximum motor speed (not more than 20 miles per hour). The word names one road-user class, and the ontology carries that class with its own local atom ru.electric_scooter, 'a standing or seated electric scooter with handlebars', whose scope is the class as the target jurisdiction's own taxonomy names it, so the definition's weight and design-speed limits are the taxonomy that atom already labels. The ru.aggregate contract says it is 'not a stand-in for a named road-user class for which the applicable definitions ... permit its own class atom — that class's own atom'. The earlier claim ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter cannot be used by any faithful rule: the run's reading leaves the aggregate with no included class, so membership is never true and the subject's class never holds in any scene. That claim is therefore replaced by the class atom the rule reads.

'roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'. 'bicycle lane, path' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'. A 'route' for these devices runs on roadways and bicycle lanes or paths, so it adds no place beyond them. rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', anchors the scooter on the region of either kind; each region quantifier ranges over the claimed kind. 'bicycle' here names the kind of structure, not road users the duty counts.
kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity' (m/s), is compared with the law's own figure, 15 miles per hour, a literal. Its contract has no 'not a stand-in for' clause bearing on this quantity.

residues.why: The ordinance the words name is LVMC 11.40.185(A), posted as DEF-LVMC-11-40-185-A: 'an electric bicycle or an electric scooter may be operated on a public roadway or sidewalk, or a lane, path, or route designated for bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter use'. It provides where a scooter may be operated and states no speed. Nothing in it provides otherwise on the speed this line bounds, so the duty is the same whether or not the exception's words hold.

The permission to operate adds no restriction to the speed bound: a scooter at rest and one moving below the bound both meet it. The duty is therefore the same whether or not the scooter is being operated.

NRS_484B_785_1a.applicability: The subject is an electric scooter (ru.electric_scooter), and at the observation its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a roadway (st.roadway) or a bicycle lane or path (st.bicycle_lane_or_path).
NRS_484B_785_1a.obligation: The subject's speed (kin.speed) is at most the literal 15 mph at the observation.

narrowings.why: The permission 'may be operated ... at a speed of not more than 15 miles per hour' is read as its limit: operating in these places above the figure is outside what the line permits.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides on a roadway at 8 m/s, above 15 mph.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides in a bicycle lane at 5 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides on a sidewalk at 8 m/s and overlaps no roadway, bicycle lane or path.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides on a roadway, and the source does not observe its speed.

segmentation.text: It shall be unlawful for any person to ride
a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter
upon the sidewalks
on Fremont Street between Main Street and Seventh Street
This area shall be posted with signs indicating that the riding of bicycles, electric bicycles, or electric scooters on the sidewalk is prohibited

elements.justification: Riding is read through the device's controlled motion: a device ridden moves, so the duty is that the device be at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt: 'The road user is at rest at the observation ... its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance'), as the mapping index reads 'shall be ridden' (LVMC_11_38_030).

Each term is a defined word admitted as its aggregate, never expanded into a class list (DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle 'a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'; DEF-LVMC-11-02-082::electric_bicycle 'a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor which produces not more than seven hundred fifty watts'; DEF-LVMC-11-02-083::electric_scooter 'a device with handlebars and an electric motor ... must not weigh more than one hundred pounds without a rider and must have a maximum speed of not more than twenty miles per hour ... does not include a scooter that is designed ... primarily as an assistive device'); the subject belongs to one of them. Membership is decided by the run's reading of each definition under the ru.aggregate contract: where the reading leaves a class unresolved (as it does for the electric scooter, whose weight, design maximum speed and assistive purpose no atom observes), membership is unknown and the rule reports unknown for that device, never compliance or violation; the definition's limits are not dropped by substituting the class atom ru.electric_scooter, whose contract ('a standing or seated electric scooter with handlebars') states none of them.

st.sidewalk: 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line' (DEF-NRS-484A-240 'that portion of a highway between the curb lines ... and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians'); rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region' anchors the subject on it. Same atoms as the mapping index's 'upon any sidewalk'.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies on Fremont Street between Main Street and Seventh Street, as the map's reading records the named way and its limits

residues.why: The sentence directs the City to post signs; the riding prohibition of the first sentence holds whether or not the signs are posted, so the duty is the same either way.

LVMC_11_40_180_A.applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter, each as its admitted aggregate under the run's reading, that occupies an st.sidewalk region (rel.occupies) at a place where asm.fremont_street_main_to_seventh holds.
LVMC_11_40_180_A.obligation: At each such observation the subject is at rest: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance).

narrowings.why: 'any person to ride' is read through the device's controlled motion: a device moving on the sidewalk is read as ridden, so a device pushed by a person walking beside it is not told apart from one ridden (no rider posture is read).

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle moves along a sidewalk at a place the map's reading declares to be Fremont Street between Main Street and Seventh Street.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle stands at rest on that sidewalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on the roadway of Fremont Street within the declared stretch, never on the sidewalk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle on that sidewalk whose speed the source does not supply.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a sidewalk at a place the map's reading declares outside the named stretch.

segmentation.text: The following regulations pertain to
the operation of vehicles
within a roundabout
All vehicular travel
shall be in a counterclockwise direction

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions ('(1) Devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails; (2) Electric bicycles; (3) Electric personal assistive mobility devices ...; and (4) An electric scooter'). Under the ru.aggregate contract the run's reading classifies every road-user class under that id by the definition's words; the rule never expands or overrides that classification. Where the reading leaves a class unresolved (an electric scooter whose 100-pound weight and 20 mph speed limits from DEF-NRS-484A-082 are not observed may or may not be an 'electric scooter' in the defined sense), membership is unknown, as the contract states. 'operation' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

st.roundabout: 'a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches' — the roundabout of DEF-LVMC-11-02-130 ('an intersection characterized by a circulatory roadway, channelized approaches and yield control of entering traffic ... the area bounded by the outermost curb line ... and includes the crosswalks on any entering or exiting roadway'); 'within' places the subject in it, anchored by rel.occupies (the road user's footprint overlaps the region).

'vehicular' is the same aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, with the same definition words as a2; 'travel' is motion: the vehicle is not at rest, drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation ... observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance') being false.

drv.motion.circulating_clockwise_about: 'Road user a travels clockwise about the reference point of region r, as seen from above'; travel in a counterclockwise direction is its negation, the concept's contract leaving out 'one travelling counter-clockwise about the point' and 'one moving towards or away from the point within the angle sin_tol allows'. The concept takes the roundabout as its region argument r, the one the obligation binds. The circulatory roadway is the part of the roundabout 'used by vehicles to travel counterclockwise around a central island' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-040): the sense is judged about the roundabout's reference point.

LVMC_11_43_010_A.applicability: The subject belongs to DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate), its footprint occupies some st.roundabout region (rel.occupies), and it is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance)).
LVMC_11_43_010_A.obligation: For every st.roundabout region r whose area the subject's footprint occupies (rel.occupies(subject, r)), the roundabout selection of the applicability written again in full: not drv.motion.circulating_clockwise_about(subject, r; p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.roundabout_clockwise_sin_tol).

narrowings.why: Counterclockwise is judged about the reference point of the roundabout region, read as the centre of its central island; motion towards or away from that point within the tolerance (entering, leaving) is not clockwise and so is compliant.
'the operation of vehicles' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving in the roundabout is taken to be operated, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car in a roundabout circulates keeping the central island on its right, clockwise about the roundabout's reference point.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car circulates keeping the central island on its left, counterclockwise.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives on a straight street with no roundabout.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car circulates in a roundabout that the source maps without its reference point and outline.

segmentation.text: Except as provided in NRS 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B]:
A pedestrian
shall not cross an intersection diagonally
unless authorized by official traffic-control devices.

elements.justification: 'Pedestrian' is defined by DEF-NRS-484A-165 ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); the run admits it as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, claimed whole and never expanded into class atoms.

'intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105: 'The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines') is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'; the alley-junction exclusion of the definition's (3) is made by the atom's own contract. rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors the pedestrian in that intersection. 'diagonally' is a direction of the pedestrian's motion relative to the ways that meet there: the lanes that run into the intersection are read through st.lane_enters ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; kind st.lane), and drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, whose contract compares the road user's velocity with a carrier's designated direction, is read at two tolerances on every such lane: across it with the tolerance that tells across from along, and not across it with the right-angle tolerance, so the motion is oblique to both crossing ways. st.lane_enters is not used for the subject's presence (that is rel.occupies) nor for governance.

An 'official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-145) includes every 'marking ... placed or erected by a public authority ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'; the marking that authorizes a pedestrian crossing is a crosswalk 'distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface' (DEF-NRS-484A-065 (2)), carried by st.crosswalk ('marked crossing ...; marked attribute') read with its marked attribute; rel.occupies anchors the pedestrian inside that marked crossing. st.crosswalk 'Not a stand-in for' clauses do not concern this use.

NRS_484B_287_1d.applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps an intersection x (rel.occupies, st.intersection) into which at least one lane runs (st.lane_enters); the duty does not apply where LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject.
NRS_484B_287_1d.obligation: At each such observation: if the subject moves diagonally across x, that is, for every lane l with st.lane_enters(l, x), drv_motion_moving_across_carrier(subject, l) holds with parameters (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.crossing_motion_cos) and does not hold with parameters (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.right_angle_crossing_cos), then the subject's footprint overlaps a marked crosswalk (st.crosswalk with its marked attribute true). Otherwise compliant.

narrowings.why: 'cross ... diagonally' is read at each observation as the pedestrian, inside the intersection, moving oblique to every lane that runs into it (neither within the right-angle tolerance of across a lane nor along it); a crossing is judged by its motion at each observation, not as a corner-to-corner path.
'official' is read through the presence of the marking on the road: a marked crosswalk in the scene is presumed placed by a public authority.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Lanes running into intersection x run north-south and east-west; a pedestrian inside x walks north-east at 1.4 m/s, oblique to every entering lane, with no crosswalk under its footprint.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian inside x near its edge walks east at 1.4 m/s: across the north-south lanes at right angles, so the motion is not diagonal.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian walks along a sidewalk and its footprint overlaps no intersection.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian is inside x with no marked crosswalk under it, but its velocity is not observed, so whether it moves diagonally cannot be told.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian inside x walks north-east within a marked diagonal crosswalk.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability in naturalistic crossing studies

param_proposals.name: p.right_angle_crossing_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as at right angles to the curb: within about 15 degrees of perpendicular
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability in naturalistic crossing studies

segmentation.text: Drivers of vehicles proceeding in opposite directions
shall pass each other keeping to the right,
and
upon highways having width for not more than one line of traffic in each direction,
each driver shall give to the other at least one-half of the paved portion of the highway
as nearly as possible.

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with the definition's exclusions recorded by the run's reading of the aggregate), for the subject and for the other. 'proceeding in opposite directions': rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing', with its tolerance; its exclusion concerns 'the direction a road user approaches from' an intersection, which these words do not name: they name two vehicles meeting on a way. 'proceeding': the subject is not at rest (negation of drv.motion.complete_halt, 'complete cessation from movement'). 'Drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion.

'pass each other': the two are alongside, rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share'. 'keeping to the right': each keeps the other on its left, rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of" …)', its lateral component on the subject's left. Both occupy the same highway (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'), so a vehicle on another way is not met.

NRS_484B_203_1_o1.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance).
NRS_484B_203_1_o1.obligation: For every road user c that is a vehicle, occupies a highway region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.highway), is oncoming to the subject (rel.oncoming with p.oncoming_heading_cos) and is alongside it (rel.longitudinal_overlap: the projections share length): c lies on the subject's left (the lateral component of rel.bearing(subject, c) is to the left). Violated where such a c lies on the subject's right.

narrowings.why: 'Drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls them.
Passing each other is read as the two vehicles being alongside on the same highway; vehicles on different ways are not read as passing each other.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a two-way road, an oncoming car passes the moving subject car on the subject's right side.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: On a two-way road, an oncoming car passes the moving subject car on the subject's left side.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car is at rest at the curb while an oncoming car passes.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: An oncoming car passes the moving subject car on the subject's right side; the source declares rel.occupies and rel.bearing absent, so whether the two occupy the same highway is not observed (and the measured bearing is not supplied), and the duty is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives alone on the road: no vehicle meets it.

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
param_proposals.source: heading tolerance of road-geometry alignment; lane-change heading angles

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition source

segmentation.text: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously
during not less than the last 100 feet traveled
in a business or residential district
and not less than the last 300 feet traveled
in any other area
prior to changing the course
of a vehicle.
This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

elements.justification: 'A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn ... from a direct course' is the signal itself, not a declared intention: sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state in {off, left, right}', to the side of the course change, or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {..., left, right, ...}', to that side; the indicator's exclusion (not the turn or lane change itself) does not apply, the words naming the signal and not the manoeuvre. 'given continuously' is the signal holding at every observation of the window the next spans state. 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

'during not less than the last 100 feet traveled' is a .path window of the stated 100 feet of the subject's path behind the course change; the window reads kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path since the start of the trace'.
'not less than the last 300 feet traveled': a .path window of the stated 300 feet of the subject's path (kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path') behind the course change.

'changing the course' is the onset of the subject's turn from a direct course: the observation at which, for an st.lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') the subject occupies (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'), drv.lane.heading_left_of_carrier ('Road user a, moving, points to the left of the designated direction of travel of carrier region r by more than a tolerance') or the catalogued drv.lane.heading_right_of_carrier ('points to the right of the designated direction of travel of carrier region r by more than a tolerance') rises; the side of the departure is the side the signal must show. A turn, a lane change and a pull-out each begin so; following the lane's own direction is keeping the course. st.lane's exclusion (a half of the roadway or a lateral position) does not apply: the lane is the carrier whose direction is the course.
'of a vehicle': the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole: the subject is the vehicle whose course changes.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district or a residence district, as the map's reading classifies the area
the place of the road user at the observation lies in a business district or a residence district, as the map's reading classifies the area

residues.why: The words exclude the weather as a ground for any other duty; the duty is the same whatever the weather, so they add no restriction.

NRS_484B_413_2.applicability: The subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, changes course at the judged observation: for some st.lane l the subject occupies (rel.occupies), drv.lane.heading_left_of_carrier(subject, l) or drv.lane.heading_right_of_carrier(subject, l), each with p.course_departure_sin_tol and p.halt_speed_tolerance, holds here and did not at the previous observation (rises). The trigger is read only where the subject occupies some lane (definedWhen): where it occupies none, the course change is unknown.
NRS_484B_413_2.obligation: At that observation, for the side of the departure (left for heading_left_of_carrier, right for heading_right_of_carrier, read on the same lane l), the subject has shown sig.turn_indicator to that side or sig.hand_signal of meaning that side at every observation of the .path window of the subject's path behind it (holdsFor .path over kin.path_length). Written as two branches with constant window lengths: asm.business_or_residence_district holds at that observation and the signal holds over the stated 100 feet; or asm.business_or_residence_district does not hold and the signal holds over the stated 300 feet. It is unknown where the assumption is undeclared or the window reaches before the recording. Otherwise the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: The side of the signal is the side the heading departs to; a departure that later reverses is judged at its own onset.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_or_residence_district false; the subject moves in its lane with sig.turn_indicator off and sig.hand_signal no_signal, then its heading turns left of the lane's direction beyond p.course_departure_sin_tol (a lane change to the left).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_or_residence_district false; the subject shows sig.turn_indicator left at every observation over the last stated 300 feet of its path before its heading departs to the left of its lane.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject keeps its heading along its lane's designated direction throughout; no course change begins.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject's heading departs to the right of its lane; neither sig.turn_indicator nor sig.hand_signal is observed on the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_or_residence_district true; the subject shows sig.turn_indicator right over a stretch of its path longer than the stated 100 feet but shorter than the stated 300 feet before its heading departs to the right of its lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1 with asm.business_or_residence_district false: the indicator was not shown over the last stated 300 feet.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: asm.business_or_residence_district false; the subject shows sig.turn_indicator right over the last stated 300 feet and its heading departs to the left of its lane: the signal shows the wrong side.

segmentation.text: The following regulations pertain to
the operation of vehicles within a roundabout
The operator of a vehicle
who intends to exit a roundabout
Shall use the left lane to turn left or complete a U-turn

elements.justification: "vehicles" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"), claimed as one atom, never expanded; its exclusions are the reading's classification. "within a roundabout": st.roundabout "a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches" carries DEF-LVMC-11-02-130 ("an intersection characterized by a circulatory roadway", including the crosswalks on the entering and exiting roadways) at its whole extent; rel.occupies "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region" anchors the subject to that roundabout, so no other roundabout of the scene is read. Same mapping as the index for "the operation of vehicles" and "within a roundabout".

"a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; "The operator" names who controls it, a relational role and no aggregate, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency). Same mapping as the index entry "The operator of a vehicle".

The intention to exit is not observable; it is read through the exit it leads to (observable_reading intention): the observation at which the subject's footprint (rel.occupies "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region") ceases to overlap the roundabout r (st.roundabout) it occupied, which is the recognition of the turn concepts ("The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r"). No declared intention: the words state an intention to exit, which is read by the exit made, and the turn they name is read by the heading change the concepts measure.

"to turn left or complete a U-turn": drv.motion.left_turn_through_region ("a turn to the left through region r ... heading change ... from turn_min inclusive to u_turn_min exclusive") and drv.motion.u_turn_through_region ("so as to proceed in the opposite direction" through r), taking r = the roundabout the subject exits; a heading change measured from the entry into the roundabout to the exit is the turn the vehicle makes by the roundabout, whatever the circulation in between. "use the left lane": st.lane "a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles" with st.lane_adjacency "lane ordinal within the carriageway ... ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction": "the left lane" is the lane of ordinal 1, the count literal 1 declared on this span (literals), whose value is fixed by the atom's contract, not a reading parameter; rel.occupies anchors the lanes the subject's footprint overlaps. Not a stand-in exclusions: lane membership is read by footprint overlap and ordinal, never by a lateral offset from the edge, and the ordinal is not the marking between lanes.

LVMC_11_43_010_C1.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). Bind a region r of kind st.roundabout. At the judged observation the subject exits r having turned left or completed a U-turn through it: drv_motion_left_turn_through_region(subject, r) or drv_motion_u_turn_through_region(subject, r) rises, each with step .param p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph and turn_min p.turn_heading_min, u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min (the U-turn concept takes step and u_turn_min only). The intention to exit is read through this exit.
LVMC_11_43_010_C1.obligation: Re-bind the same roundabout: a region r of kind st.roundabout for which the same concept rises for the subject at the judged observation. The subject used the left lane within r: at every observation from its entry into r (the latest observation at which rel.occupies(subject, r) rose) up to the judged observation, wherever rel.occupies(subject, r) holds, every region l of kind st.lane with rel.occupies(subject, l) has st_lane_adjacency_ordinal(l) equal to the declared count literal 1 of s5 ("the left lane", the leftmost lane by st.lane_adjacency's contract). Written with since: since(phi, rises(occupies(subject, r)) and phi), phi = occupies(subject, r) implies forall lane l (occupies(subject, l) implies ordinal(l) = 1). Unknown where the entry lies before the recording or an ordinal of an occupied lane is unobserved.

narrowings.why: "The operator" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle whoever or whatever controls it.

"who intends to exit a roundabout" is read through the exit itself: the duty is judged at the observation at which the vehicle leaves the roundabout, the recognition of the turn; a vehicle that intends to exit but has not yet left is judged when it leaves.

"use the left lane" is read as occupying, within the roundabout, no lane other than the lane of ordinal 1 of its carriageway from the entry to the exit; a footprint straddling the left lane and another lane is not use of the left lane alone. A single-lane roundabout's only lane is ordinal 1.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A two-lane roundabout r (st.roundabout) whose circulatory and approach lanes carry st.lane_adjacency ordinals 1 (inner, leftmost) and 2 (outer). The subject, a passenger car (ru.motor_vehicle), enters r heading east in the lane of ordinal 2, circulates counter-clockwise in the outer lane and leaves r heading north: its yaw rate, observed at every scene at the sampling standard, integrates to a quarter turn to the left since the entry. At the exit the left turn through r is recognized; the subject occupied a lane of ordinal 2 within r.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout and the same left turn, but the subject enters and circulates in the lane of ordinal 1 only and leaves r heading north.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout; the subject enters heading east in the lane of ordinal 2 and leaves at the first exit heading south, a quarter turn to the right since the entry: no left turn or U-turn is recognized.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not supply lane ordinals (st.lane_adjacency absent): which lane the subject used is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout; the subject enters heading east in the lane of ordinal 2, circulates and leaves heading west, a half turn to the left since the entry: a U-turn through r made from the outer lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Same roundabout; the subject makes the U-turn of branch_1 in the lane of ordinal 1 throughout.

onset.words: the operation of vehicles within a roundabout
onset.justification: The act begins at the subject's entry into the roundabout: the observation at which rel.occupies(subject, r) rose, the onset the concepts declare ("its entry into r").

occasion.recognition: who intends to exit a roundabout

under_way.words: to turn left or complete a U-turn
under_way.justification: Inside the act the subject's heading change since its entry into r (headingSince, integrated from kin.yaw_rate "rate of change of heading") is defined and the subject's footprint overlaps r; before the entry it is not. The heading's integration reads the subject's motion, not the place alone.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: turning-movement classification in intersection geometric design practice (AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets)

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: turning-movement classification in intersection geometric design practice (AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets)

segmentation.text: The following regulations pertain to
the operation of vehicles
within a roundabout
The operator of a vehicle
entering a roundabout
shall yield
the right-of-way
to vehicles already in the roundabout
and wait
for a gap
in traffic
before entering

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', its exclusions decided by the reading's classification of the aggregate); 'operation' read through controlled motion.

st.roundabout 'a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-130's area, crosswalks of the entering and exiting roadways included); rel.occupies anchors the subject: at its entry it occupies the roundabout.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'The operator' read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Entering is the event at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap the roundabout (rel.occupies true at the judged observation and false at the observation before); st.roundabout is the region entered.

'shall yield' is judged at the entry by its outcome: the subject does not take the way from a vehicle already in the roundabout. rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)' decides the collision side; the danger of a crash short of contact is the b7 operationalization (prim.closest_approach_within / prim.closest_approach_distance). The obligation gives the subject's speed no role, so kin.speed is not claimed: no faithful rule over this obligation reads it.

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'already in the roundabout': each occupies (rel.occupies) the roundabout region r the subject enters, at the observation before the entry and at the entry.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: preference over another approaching 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a circulating vehicle whose centre comes, under constant velocities, within the conflict clearance of the entering vehicle's centre within the conflict horizon is approaching so as to give rise to the danger of a crash

LVMC_11_43_010_B_o1.applicability: The subject belongs to DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the judged observation it enters an st.roundabout region r: rel.occupies(subject, r) holds there and not at the observation before.
LVMC_11_43_010_B_o1.obligation: At that entry, for every st.roundabout region r the subject enters there, and for every road user v of the scene other than the subject that belongs to DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and occupies r at the observation before the entry and at the entry: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance. An entry with no such vehicle is compliant.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
Yielding is judged at the entry by its outcome: the subject enters only where no vehicle already in the roundabout is in contact or in conflict with it; the subject's speed is not itself judged.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the roundabout while a circulating car, already in it, is on a course whose closest approach to the entering car falls within the conflict horizon and below the clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the roundabout while the only circulating car is on the far side, its closest approach above the clearance.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car circulates inside the roundabout throughout the recording without entering it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car near the roundabout's edge beside a circulating car, where the source does not observe which regions the cars occupy.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car enters an empty roundabout: no other vehicle is in the scene, and the duty is met.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: Hydén, The development of a method for traffic safety evaluation: the Swedish Traffic Conflicts Technique (1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car design dimensions (AASHTO Green Book design vehicle)

segmentation.text: Every motorcycle or moped
when being driven on the highway
is entitled to full use of the traffic lane it is occupying,
and a person shall not drive another motor vehicle
in a manner which would deprive any such motorcycle or moped of such use.

elements.justification: 'motorcycle' and 'moped' are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or a saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels') and DEF-NRS-486-038::moped ('a motor-driven scooter, motor-driven cycle or similar vehicle that is propelled by a small engine'); each is claimed as the aggregate, not as the class atoms ru.motorcycle and ru.moped. The motorcycle or moped is a road user quantified in the obligation, not a binder.

st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders' is the defined highway (DEF-NRS-486-031: 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way maintained by a public authority'); its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' does not apply, the whole way being meant. rel.occupies anchors the motorcycle's footprint on it. 'being driven' is read through the motorcycle's presence and controlled motion on the way (agency): a motorcycle halted in a lane in traffic is still being driven.

st.lane: 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles' is 'the traffic lane'; its exclusions (a half of the roadway, a lateral position within a lane) do not apply, the lane being the strip itself. 'it is occupying' is rel.occupies of the motorcycle and that lane: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. 'traffic lane' is a lane; no road users of the traffic aggregate are read by the word.

'another motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'): the subject, a road user other than the motorcycle or moped. 'a person shall not drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

Depriving the motorcycle of full use of its lane is read as the subject sharing that lane beside it: the subject's footprint overlaps the same st.lane the motorcycle occupies (rel.occupies) while the two bodies are side by side, rel.longitudinal_overlap 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side): the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share' at or above zero. The overlap is 'a projection, so neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies', and it is read only as side-by-side position, not contact.

NRS_486_341.applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle).
NRS_486_341.obligation: At every observation, for every road user m other than the subject (not same) that is of DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle or DEF-NRS-486-038::moped and occupies a highway, and every lane L that m occupies: it is not the case that the subject occupies L and rel.longitudinal_overlap of the subject and m is at or above zero.

narrowings.why: Depriving of full use is read as the subject's footprint sharing the motorcycle's lane while side by side with it; a closeness from behind or from the next lane that leaves the motorcycle's lane free of the subject's footprint is not read.
'a person shall not drive' is read through the subject vehicle's controlled motion.
'being driven' is read through the motorcycle's presence and controlled motion on the highway, whoever is at its controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies lane L of a highway beside a motorcycle also occupying L; rel.longitudinal_overlap of car and motorcycle 2 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The car occupies lane L 20 m behind the motorcycle in L; rel.longitudinal_overlap negative.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a bicycle beside the motorcycle in L; a bicycle is not a motor vehicle.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car is side by side with a motorcycle on a highway (rel.longitudinal_overlap 2 m), both bodies within lane L; which lanes and which highway each footprint occupies is not observed, so whether the car shares the motorcycle's lane is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The car drives on the highway; no motorcycle or moped is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The car occupies the adjacent lane only, side by side with the motorcycle in L.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right
when such movement requires driving off the paved portion of the highway.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

'overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right' is the act drv.interaction.overtake_pass_on_right(subject, b), 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b on b's right'; b is of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

'driving off the paved portion of the highway': at some observation of the act the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') an st.shoulder whose paved attribute is unset ('the part of the highway beside the roadway ...; paved attribute'), or an st.road_edge whose paved attribute, 'for the surface beyond it', is unset, so that part of the body is at or beyond the edge of the pavement. 'requires' is read through the movement as made (reading). 'highway' keeps its extent: the paved portion is any paved part of it, so a paved shoulder or sidewalk is not 'off' it.

NRS_484B_210_3.applicability: The subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, overtakes and passes on its right another road user b of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: drv.interaction.overtake_pass_on_right(subject, b) with p.overtake_window and p.overtake_same_direction_cos is recognized at the judged observation; b is quantified there, not a binder.
NRS_484B_210_3.obligation: At no observation of the act, from its beginning (the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with aligned headings) to its recognition, does the subject's footprint overlap (rel.occupies) an st.shoulder whose paved attribute is unset or an st.road_edge whose paved attribute, for the surface beyond it, is unset; where it does at some such observation, the duty is violated.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on b's right with its footprint overlapping an st.shoulder whose paved attribute is unset during the side-by-side phase.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on b's right in the adjacent lane, its footprint overlapping no unpaved shoulder and no road edge with an unpaved surface beyond.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives along an unpaved shoulder with no road user ahead of it: no pass is recognized.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on its right; rel.occupies is not observed, so whether it overlapped an unpaved shoulder is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint overlaps an unpaved shoulder during the middle part of the pass only, the rest of the act on the roadway.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint overlapped an unpaved shoulder only before the act began; it returned to the roadway, and then passed b on its right on the pavement.

under_way.words: overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act lies after its beginning, the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction), and at or before its recognition, while the subject's velocity (kin.velocity), exceeding b's along its heading, carries it up to and past b; an unpaved shoulder occupied before that observation is outside the act. These relations read the two road users' relative motion, never a place.

param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: overtaking-manoeuvre durations in naturalistic driving studies

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos

param_proposals.source: lane-change heading angles in naturalistic driving data

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
shall yield the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield the right-of-way to that traffic
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exclusions classified by the run's reading); ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'Driver' is a relational role (ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for ... who drives or controls a vehicle'), read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Mapping index: 'The driver of a vehicle' maps to the same aggregate.

DEF-NRS-484A-060: a controlled-access highway is one 'to or from which owners or occupants of abutting lands and other persons have no legal right of access except at such points only'. st.controlled_access is 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes', and rel.occupies lists the 'controlled-access lane' among the regions a footprint overlaps. The entry is the observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps a controlled-access region c having not overlapped it at the previous observation; the exit, the observation at which it does not overlap c having overlapped it at the previous one. kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells the moving entry or exit. 'About to' is an imminent movement, read by the movement itself.

Mapping index: 'shall yield' maps to kin.speed, rel.contact. The subject yields while it moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)' is a failure to yield, and its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss' is respected: the near conflict is the operationalization of a5.

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'). 'on the highway' is the controlled-access highway the subject enters or exits: the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the same region c of st.controlled_access, re-bound with the selection of a2. 'approaching': the vehicle moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) and the subject lies ahead of it, rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame' with a positive longitudinal component.

operationalizations.standard: proximity that constitutes an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: under constant velocities the two centres reach their closest approach within the time-to-collision threshold at a centre distance below the collision clearance; a vehicle so placed is an immediate hazard

NRS_484B_263_o1.applicability: The subject (vehicle aggregate) is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and there is a controlled-access region c such that at this observation the subject's footprint overlaps c and did not at the previous observation (entry: rises of rel.occupies), or does not overlap c and did at the previous observation (exit: rises of its negation).
NRS_484B_263_o1.obligation: For every region c whose entry or exit occurs at this observation (re-bound with that selection): for every other road user v of the vehicle aggregate that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), whose footprint overlaps c, and in whose frame the subject lies ahead (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from v to the subject positive): the subject and v are not in contact, and it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

'about to enter or exit' is an imminent movement, read by the entry into or the exit from the controlled-access region as the source maps it: the duty is judged at the observation the subject's footprint comes onto or leaves that region; where the source maps the entrance and exit lanes inside the region, the entry is judged where those lanes begin, since the ontology carries no attribute telling an entrance lane from a through lane

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint comes to overlap controlled-access region c (it did not at the previous observation), kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance. Vehicle v moves on c with the subject ahead of it; prim.closest_approach_within holds over p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance is below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but v is far behind on c: the closest approach does not fall within p.conflict_horizon, and no contact occurs.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject travels within c throughout: its overlap with c neither begins nor ends during the trace.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, with every position, heading, speed, footprint and occupancy observed, but the source does not observe membership of the legal aggregate (ru.aggregate absent): whether the road users belong to DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and so whether v is a vehicle the subject must yield to, is unknown while v moves on c with the subject ahead of it in a closest-approach conflict.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject enters c and no other road user is in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject's footprint ceases to overlap c (exit) while a vehicle v moving on c, with the subject ahead of it, is in a closest-approach conflict with the subject.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or cross a highway
from a private way
shall yield
the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on such highway.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (definitions table); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', claimed by its id and never expanded. 'Driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is no aggregate: ru.aggregate is 'Not a stand-in for ... a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle', so the role is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency). Mapping index: 'The driver of a vehicle' maps to the same aggregate.

The entry onto or across the highway is where the subject's footprint comes onto its roadway: rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (roadway, ...)'; st.roadway 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on' ties that roadway to the highway; st.highway 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders' carries DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority'. st.highway's exclusion ('Not a stand-in for: the roadway') is respected: the roadway is its own atom, the highway only anchors it. kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' tells a moving entry from a vehicle standing at the edge. 'About to' is an imminent movement, read by the movement itself (ontology, what is not an atom).

DEF-NRS-484A-190: a private way is 'every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel by the owner'. st.driveway_or_alley_entrance is a 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: which of them meets the highway there' is why the rule adds st.alley ('a narrow way within a block serving the rear of properties'): an alley is a highway (DEF-NRS-484A-015 'Alley means a highway'), not a private way, so the subject must overlap the entrance and no alley region. rel.occupies anchors both to the subject's footprint.

Mapping index: 'shall yield' maps to kin.speed, rel.contact. The yield is judged while the subject moves (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above the halt tolerance): a subject at rest grants precedence. rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)' is a failure to yield; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a near miss' is respected, since the near conflict is the operationalization of s5.

'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'on such highway' singles out the highway the subject enters: the other vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region (st.travel_region, 'the union of the kinds a device can govern: a lane ..., a roadway ..., a shoulder, or an intersection') lying (st.on_way) on that same highway region, re-bound with the selection of s2. st.travel_region's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the extent of a highway' is respected: the highway is read through st.on_way, the travel region only locates the vehicle. 'approaching': the vehicle moves (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) and the subject lies ahead of it, rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame' with a positive longitudinal component.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: DEF-NRS-484A-210 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other'
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: under constant velocities (direction and speed of both), the two centres reach their closest approach within the time-to-collision threshold at a centre distance below the collision clearance; such a pair is in danger of a crash unless the subject grants precedence

NRS_484B_260.applicability: The subject (vehicle aggregate) is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) and its footprint overlaps both a roadway region r lying on a highway region h and a driveway_or_alley_entrance region e, and overlaps no alley region; its overlap with e has held at every observation since one at which it overlapped e and did not overlap r (the subject came onto the entrance from off the roadway: formula 'since').
NRS_484B_260.obligation: For every selection of h, r and e satisfying the applicability's conditions at this observation (re-bound in full): for every other road user v of the vehicle aggregate that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), whose footprint overlaps a travel region lying on h, and in whose frame the subject lies ahead (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from v to the subject positive): the subject and v are not in contact (rel.contact), and it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it

'about to enter or cross' is an imminent movement, read by the entering movement itself: the rule judges every observation at which the moving subject straddles the private way's entrance and a roadway of the highway, having come onto the entrance from off the roadway; the rest of a crossing is judged through the closest approach under constant velocities that each such observation predicts

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle rolls out of a driveway entrance region onto roadway r of highway h, kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance, overlapping no alley. Vehicle v moves in a lane on h with the subject ahead of it (rel.bearing longitudinal positive); prim.closest_approach_within holds over p.conflict_horizon and prim.closest_approach_distance is below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but v is far up the lane: their closest approach does not fall within p.conflict_horizon, and no contact occurs.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives along roadway r of h and its footprint never overlaps a driveway_or_alley_entrance region; v approaches from behind.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but st.on_way is not observed on the source: which highway the roadway r and v's lane lie on is unknown, so whether the subject is entering such a highway and whether v approaches on that same highway are unknown, while the subject straddles the entrance and the roadway and the closest approach is a conflict.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject rolls out of a driveway entrance onto roadway r of h and no other road user is in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject comes out of an alley: its footprint overlaps an st.alley region and the entrance region as it reaches roadway r, with v in conflict as in forbid. An alley is a highway, not a private way.

segmentation.text: The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
shall not: Overtake and pass a motor vehicle
unless the operator can do so safely without endangering himself or herself or the occupants of the motor vehicle.

elements.justification: The three admitted aggregates, claimed as ru.aggregate with their ids, as the index maps 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'; 'the operator' is read through the device's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency), ru.aggregate being 'Not a stand-in for: ... a relational role'.

'Overtake and pass' is drv.interaction.overtake_pass, whose contract is 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it', with a the subject and b the motor vehicle, as the index maps 'approaching from the rear shall not overtake and pass such stopped vehicle'; it 'says nothing of the lanes they occupy, of whether b moves', so a pass of a moving or a standing motor vehicle is covered alike. The concept holds at the recognition only, so the act's beginning, from which the standard of y3 is read, is located in the rule by the same definition the concept's contract gives it: 'The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction)', where 'b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame, the component along a's heading (kin.heading) of the vector from a's position to b's position (kin.position), is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative)'. These four atoms are claimed for that beginning: kin.position ('position of the body's reference point') and kin.heading ('direction the body points', read normalised) give the longitudinal component, rel.longitudinal_overlap ('the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share, negative for the gap between the projections') the absence of overlap, rel.same_direction ('the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance') the alignment, with p.overtake_same_direction_cos the same tolerance the concept is called with. 'A motor vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, claimed as ru.aggregate.

operationalizations.standard: safely, without endangering the operator or the occupants of the motor vehicle
operationalizations.convention: bicyclist operating space: a pass is safe where the gap between the rider's body and the passed vehicle's body stays at least the rider's operating-space sway and the bodies never touch; traffic-conflict technique: no other road user comes into a closest approach within a time-to-collision horizon and below a centre clearance during the pass

NRS_484B_270_7b.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, read as operated.
NRS_484B_270_7b.obligation: For every road user m other than the subject that is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle: at each observation at which drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, m) with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos holds (the pass's recognition), the pass was safe at every observation since its beginning, read with since. The beginning is the latest observation before the recognition at which m was ahead of the subject with headings aligned, as the concept's contract defines it: the component along the subject's heading (kin.heading) of the vector from the subject's position to m's position (kin.position) is positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap(subject, m) is negative, and rel.same_direction(subject, m) holds within p.overtake_same_direction_cos; the concept's recognition guarantees such an observation within the window behind. Safe at an observation: the subject is not in contact with m (rel.contact), its rel.surface_gap to m (the distance between the bodies) is at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap, and no road user u other than the subject and m has prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Where the pass is recognized and the pass was not safe at the beginning and at every observation after it up to the recognition, violated; an unobserved gap, contact, closest approach, position or heading that decides it leaves it unknown.

narrowings.why: 'The operator' is read through the device's controlled motion; who controls it is not observed.
'can do so safely' is the operator's judgement of the pass, read through the pass actually made: its clearance and the conflicts during it, from the act's beginning to its recognition.

Endangering the occupants of the motor vehicle is read through the clearance to and contact with its body, which carries them; endangering the operator is read through that clearance and through conflicting closest approaches with every other road user during the pass; other hazards (the surface, the operator's speed) are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle overtakes and passes a car moving slowly in the same direction, keeping a gap between bodies smaller than p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap while alongside.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle overtakes and passes a slow car with a gap of at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap throughout the pass, no contact and no conflicting closest approach with any other road user.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a moped (outside the bicycle, electric bicycle and electric scooter aggregates, each of which leaves a moped out) overtaking and passing a car.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle overtakes and passes a car with no conflict with other road users; the gap between bodies is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle begins the pass of a car with a wide gap, then closes to a gap below p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap while still alongside before clearing the car: the pass is safe for part of the act only.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle follows close behind a car with a small gap before the pass begins, then moves out and keeps a gap of at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap at every observation from the pass's beginning to its recognition.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a street with no motor vehicle in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle overtakes and passes a standing car with a wide gap, but during the pass an oncoming car comes into a closest approach with the bicycle within p.conflict_horizon and below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

segmentation.text: Every pedestrian
crossing a roadway
at any point other than within a marked crosswalk or within an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection
shall yield
the right-of-way
to all vehicles upon the roadway
The foregoing rules in this Section shall have no application under the conditions stated in Section 11.30.070
when pedestrians are prohibited from crossing at certain designated places

elements.justification: 'pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); one atom.

Same atoms and concept as LVMC_11_30_050's 'shall cross a roadway'. 'crossing a roadway' is a passage that lasts from the edge to the far side and does not end when the pedestrian pauses on the roadway: the pedestrian occupies a roadway r (rel.occupies; st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') and has occupied r at every observation since one, the judged observation included, at which it moved across a carrier it occupied (a lane, st.lane, or r itself): drv.motion.moving_across_carrier with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance and cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos, written with the past operator since (occupies r) since (moving across). A pedestrian who halts mid-crossing is thus still crossing, so the obligation's speed test (f4) can tell holding back from proceeding; one who has only walked along the roadway is not crossing. The roadway so bound is r.

st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', carries both the marked crosswalk and the unmarked crosswalk at an intersection (the defined crosswalk's two branches); the condition is that the pedestrian, at the judged observation, does not occupy one (rel.occupies).

Same words and meaning as the index's 'shall yield' -> kin.speed, rel.contact: the pedestrian grants precedence by not proceeding into a conflict; kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', tells whether the crossing pedestrian proceeds (above p.halt_speed_tolerance) or holds back, and rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)', is the crash the yield secures against. Not a near miss: the near conflict is the standard's (f5). Because the trigger (f2) keeps a pedestrian who has halted mid-crossing within the rule, the speed test is decided both ways where the rule applies.

'all vehicles' are members v of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, quantified in the obligation; 'upon the roadway' is 'the' roadway r the pedestrian crosses, re-bound in the obligation for every roadway with its whole selection (occupied by the subject, occupied since the subject moved across a carrier on it, and governed by no pedestrians_prohibited sign), and v occupies it (rel.occupies; st.roadway).

A place where pedestrians are prohibited from crossing is shown on the road by a posted prohibition: dev.regulatory_sign, 'a point regulation by catalogue code', code pedestrians_prohibited, governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') the roadway r the pedestrian crosses. 'designated' is legal status, read through the sign's presence. A prohibition sign is a condition, not a manoeuvre, as its contract says.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where direction, speed and proximity give rise to the danger of a crash
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the defined right-of-way arises between road users 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash'; that danger is read, from the two road users' directions, speeds and positions, as their centres approaching under constant velocities within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

residues.why: Section 11.30.070 is no node of this run's library, neither accepted nor planned, so no rule can be composed; the condition under which it suspends this section is stated in this text's own words, 'when pedestrians are prohibited from crossing at certain designated places', carried by f8. Conditions of 11.30.070 those words do not state are not read; reported to the operator.

LVMC_11_30_060_A.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; there is a roadway r such that: the subject occupies r, and (subject occupies r) since (the subject moves across a carrier it occupies: some lane k it occupies with drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, k), or r itself with drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, r); speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, cos_max p.crossing_motion_cos) — the strong past since, holding at the judged observation where the subject moves across there, and where it moved across at an earlier observation and has occupied r at every observation since; and no dev.regulatory_sign of code pedestrians_prohibited governs (dev.governs) r. Further, at the judged observation the subject occupies no crosswalk (st.crosswalk).
LVMC_11_30_060_A.obligation: For every roadway r selected again with the applicability's whole selection (the subject occupies r, has occupied r since it moved across a carrier as stated there, and no pedestrians_prohibited regulatory sign governs r), and for every vehicle v (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that occupies r: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while the subject's and v's centres, under constant velocities, approach within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'shall yield' is read as not proceeding into a danger of a crash with a vehicle on the roadway: a crossing pedestrian who holds back at rest yields, and one moving while no conflict with any vehicle is projected yields too.

the right-of-way's 'direction, speed and proximity' are read only through the constant-velocity closest approach of the two centres; a crash danger arising from acceleration within the horizon is not read.
a place designated as one where pedestrians are prohibited from crossing is read through the presence of a pedestrians_prohibited regulatory sign governing the roadway crossed.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses a laned roadway mid-block at 1.4 m/s; a car on that roadway at 12 m/s would come within 1 m of the pedestrian's centre in 2 s, and the pedestrian keeps walking.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses the roadway mid-block at 1.4 m/s; no vehicle is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses the roadway within a marked crosswalk while a car approaches.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian occupies the roadway mid-block while a car approaches, but the pedestrian's velocity is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks across a lane mid-block from the roadway edge, then halts in the lane while a car on that roadway approaches and passes with its centre about 2 m from the pedestrian's (a conflict is projected while the car approaches, but the pedestrian is at rest and the bodies do not touch); the pedestrian walks on once the car has gone.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks along the roadway mid-block, its velocity aligned with the lane's direction from the first observation on, while a car approaches behind it in the same lane: it never moves across a carrier, so it is not crossing.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks onto the roadway mid-block, halts in the lane, then walks on into the path of an approaching car whose centre would come within 1 m of the pedestrian's in 2 s.

segmentation.text: Except as provided in subsection 3,
a person shall not drive a motorcycle, moped or trimobile
abreast of or overtake or pass another vehicle within the same traffic lane.
Motorcycles and mopeds may,
with the consent of the drivers,
