be operated no more than two abreast in a single traffic lane.

elements.justification: 'motorcycle', 'moped' and 'trimobile' are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or a saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels'), DEF-NRS-486-038::moped ('a motor-driven scooter, motor-driven cycle or similar vehicle that is propelled by a small engine') and DEF-NRS-486-057::trimobile ('every motor vehicle equipped with handlebars and a saddle seat and designed to travel with three wheels'), each claimed as an aggregate, never expanded. 'a person shall not drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

'another vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'). 'within the same traffic lane': the subject and the other both occupy one st.lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles'; rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane'). 'abreast of': rel.longitudinal_overlap 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)' at or above zero; it is 'a projection, so neither a contact nor a distance', read only as side-by-side position. 'overtake or pass ... within the same traffic lane' is read through the same configuration: a pass made within one lane brings the two side by side within that lane, and the duty forbids the place of the pass, so it is judged at every observation the pass is made abreast in the lane; the act concept drv.interaction.overtake_pass, recognised only once the other is behind, would judge the pass after it may have left the lane. 'traffic lane' is a lane; the traffic aggregate is not read by the word.

'Motorcycles and mopeds' are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle and DEF-NRS-486-038::moped: the exception holds only where both the subject and the other vehicle are of one of them (a trimobile is not named).

The consent of both drivers is not observable; it shows in their conduct of riding together as a pair: rel.same_direction 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance', with tolerance p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos, while abreast within the lane. A pair met head-on in the lane shows no consent.

'no more than two abreast in a single traffic lane': no third road user occupies the same st.lane (rel.occupies) side by side with the subject (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero, 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)'). The figure two is a literal.

residues.why: Points to subsection 3, whose words are this line's second sentence and are carried by s4-s6; the duty is the same whether the pointer is read or not.

NRS_486_351_2.applicability: The subject is of DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle, DEF-NRS-486-038::moped or DEF-NRS-486-057::trimobile.
NRS_486_351_2.obligation: At every observation, for every road user v other than the subject of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and every lane L that both the subject and v occupy with rel.longitudinal_overlap of subject and v at or above zero, the pair is excused (s4-s6), else the duty is violated. The pair is excused where the subject and v are each of DEF-NRS-486-041::motorcycle or DEF-NRS-486-038::moped, rel.same_direction of subject and v holds with tolerance p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos (consent read), and no third road user w (other than the subject and v) of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle occupies L with rel.longitudinal_overlap of subject and w at or above zero (no more than two abreast).

narrowings.why: The drivers' consent is read through their conduct of riding side by side in the same direction within the lane; an unconsented same-direction pair cannot be told from a consented one and is excused.
'a person shall not drive' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
Overtaking or passing within the same lane is judged at the observations at which the subject is side by side with the other within that lane, not at the recognition of a completed pass.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle occupies lane L; a car travelling the opposite way also occupies L and comes abreast of it (rel.longitudinal_overlap 2 m at one observation): the car is of the vehicle aggregate, the headings are opposed so no consent shows (s5 fails) and the pair is not excused.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The motorcycle occupies L 15 m behind a car in L travelling the same way, overlap negative at every observation.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject is a bicycle (of none of the motorcycle, moped or trimobile aggregates) beside a car in L.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A road user and a second road user both occupy L side by side, headings aligned, no third road user beside them; the road-user classes are not observed, so whether the subject is a motorcycle, moped or trimobile and whether the pair is a motorcycle-or-moped pair is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Two motorcycles ride side by side in L with headings aligned; no third vehicle beside them.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Three motorcycles ride side by side in L with headings aligned.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The motorcycle rides alone in L; no other vehicle in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: Two motorcycles are abreast in L with opposed headings (met head-on): no consent shows and the pair is not excused.

segmentation.text: A person
shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle,
except when necessary to avoid conflict
with other traffic
or in compliance with law
or the directions of a police officer
or official traffic-control device,
in any of the following places:
On the highway side of any vehicle
stopped or parked
at the edge of or curb of a highway.

elements.justification: The words name the person who stops, stands or parks "a vehicle". Who controls a vehicle is not observable; the ontology reads the one who drives through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the road user judged is the vehicle (agency reading, disclosed). ru.aggregate is "membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id"; the admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle counts "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway", its exceptions classified by the run's reading. Not a stand-in for a named class with its own atom (the words name none), nor for the relational role of who controls the vehicle: the atom states the class of the road user whose halts are judged.

"stop" when prohibited is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-260); "stand" is "the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" other than while receiving or discharging passengers (DEF-NRS-484A-250); "park" is "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not" (DEF-NRS-484A-155). Each is a halting, so forbidding all three forbids every halt of the vehicle at the place, however brief. drv.motion.complete_halt denotes that "The road user is at rest at the observation", observed as kin.speed at or below a tolerance, at each observation; what it does not denote ("a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance") is no halting. "a vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway").

"traffic" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ("pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel"); "other" leaves out the subject itself. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ("a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction") places that traffic in the subject's path, and rel.surface_gap ("distance between the nearest points of two bodies") is the clearance to it that the operationalization of "necessary" bounds. Neither contract carries a not-a-stand-in clause this use touches; no centre distance and no order of arrival is read.

"in compliance with law" excuses a halt the law itself requires of the vehicle where it is. Observably those are the halt a stop sign requires (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt") and the halt a traffic signal requires while it shows a red indication (dev.traffic_signal: "a signal head" with states circular_red, red_arrow(dir) and flashing_red), each on the traffic of a travel region the device governs (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") that the vehicle's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies: "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"; st.travel_region is the kind that relation ranges over here). dev.governs is "Not a stand-in for: a position — the region a device governs is not where a halt is required": the governed region is not read as the place of a required halt; it reads only that a vehicle within the governed approach, while the device commands a halt, is held there in obedience to it.

dev.human_direction is "a person directing traffic and the direction given; role ∈ {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}; indication ∈ {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}". A police officer ("every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic", DEF-NRS-484A-180) is the role police_officer, and the direction a halt complies with is the indication stop, given to the travel region the vehicle's footprint overlaps (dev.governs: "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls"; rel.occupies; st.travel_region the kind). dev.governs is not read as the place a halt is required, only as the traffic the direction is given to. A flagger or a crossing guard is another role and is not read.

An official traffic-control device is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-145). The devices whose directions a halt obeys are a stop sign (dev.stop_sign: "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"), a yield sign (dev.yield_sign: "regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt", whose yield may require a halt), a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red (dev.traffic_signal), and a level-crossing signal with its lights flashing or its gate lowering or down (dev.railway_signal_or_gate: "lights ∈ {flashing, dark}; gate ∈ {up, lowering, down, raising, none}"), each governing the travel region the vehicle occupies (dev.governs, rel.occupies, st.travel_region). "official" is the device's legal status, read from its presence. dev.governs is not read as the position of a required halt, only as the traffic the device directs; no sign is read as a manoeuvre.

"any vehicle" is another road user, not the subject, of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate; "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"). Its highway side is its side away from the edge at which it stands: the subject is beside it (rel.longitudinal_overlap: "the length the two footprints' projections on that axis share", at least zero) and, in the subject's frame, the other vehicle and its edge lie on the same side of the subject (the lateral component of rel.bearing, "direction of b from a in a's frame", and the edge's prim.region_lateral_offset, "the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user", both strictly negative or both strictly positive). rel.longitudinal_overlap is "a projection, so neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies" and is read only as side by side; rel.bearing only as a direction. No distance to the other vehicle is required, since the words state none.

"stopped" is a halting of the other vehicle and "parked" its standing (DEF-NRS-484A-155: "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not"), itself a halting: either is the other vehicle at rest at the observation, drv.motion.complete_halt ("The road user is at rest at the observation"), applied to that vehicle; a slowing whose sampled speed stays above the tolerance is neither.

The edge or curb is st.road_edge ("curb or edge of the roadway") lying on a highway (st.on_way: "the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on"; st.highway, "the entire public way between its boundary lines", as DEF-NRS-484A-095 defines it); the other vehicle is at it where the ground distance from its body to the edge (st.region_geometry: "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it") is at most p.edge_standing_gap, a position tolerance. st.region_geometry is not read as occupancy; st.on_way not as nearness. A source that "maps regions without their outline declares it absent, and every such distance is then unknown": whether the other vehicle stands at the edge is then unknown.

operationalizations.standard: necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic
operationalizations.convention: queue spacing of halted vehicles: a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within that gap between bodies is a halt the traffic ahead makes necessary

NRS_484B_450_1l.applicability: The subject is a road user of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, and at the observation there are a road user b, not the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), and a roadway edge e (st.road_edge) lying on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway), such that the ground distance from b's body to e (st.region_geometry) is at most p.edge_standing_gap, the subject and b are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap of the subject and b at least zero), and the lateral component of b's bearing from the subject (rel.bearing) and e's signed lateral offset from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset) are both strictly negative or both strictly positive (b and its edge on the same side of the subject, so the subject is on b's highway side).
NRS_484B_450_1l.obligation: At every observation at which the applicability holds, the subject is not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), unless at that observation one of the exceptions holds: (a) some road user other than the subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; (b) a stop sign, or a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies); (c) a dev.human_direction of role police_officer with indication stop governs a travel region the subject occupies; (d) a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing circular_red, a red_arrow or flashing_red, or a dev.railway_signal_or_gate with lights flashing or gate lowering or down governs a travel region the subject occupies. Violated where the subject is at rest there and no exception holds.

narrowings.why: The person who stops the vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the rule judges the vehicle's halts whoever or whatever controls it.

"necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic" is read only as a halt with a member of traffic ahead in the same lane within the queue gap; a halt to let crossing or oncoming traffic clear, with nothing ahead in the lane, is not read as necessary, so such a halt is judged without this exception.
"official" is the device's legal status, read from the device's presence in the scene.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Another ru.aggregate vehicle b is at rest with its body 0.2 m from the right st.road_edge of the highway; the subject, a ru.aggregate vehicle, is at rest to b's left, side by side with it (rel.longitudinal_overlap positive, b's bearing to the subject's right, the edge to the subject's right); no road user is ahead of the subject in its lane, and no human direction or device is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the subject moves past b at kin.speed 7 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No other road user is in the scene; the subject is at rest in the middle of its lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source maps the regions without their outlines (st.region_geometry absent), so whether b's body stands at the road edge is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but b is moving at kin.speed 5 m/s.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but b is at rest with its body 2.5 m from the road edge.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but a dev.traffic_signal showing circular_red governs the subject's lane.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid mirrored: both vehicles stand heading the other way, so b and the edge lie to the subject's left; the subject is still on b's highway side.

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning,
a vehicle must:
Be driven in the right turn lane
only for the purpose of making a right turn.

elements.justification: st.turn_lane: 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}', with side right ('a single right lane to be used only for turning'), occupied by the subject (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). 'Designed to provide' is read through the lane's presence on the road (observable_reading, status).

'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exclusions classified by the reading); ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'.

'Be driven in the right turn lane': the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) the right turn lane t (st.turn_lane, side right) — the same lane s1 selects, re-bound with its whole selection. The right turn the lane is for, which s4's declared intention takes as its target region, is tied to that lane, never to any region of the scene: either the intersection t is an approach to (st.lane_enters: 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet'), or a driveway or alley entrance (st.driveway_or_alley_entrance: 'private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway') that lies on the same highway as t (st.on_way: 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'), so that a turn into a driveway or alley off that way also counts as the right turn the lane serves.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the right at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

NRS_484B_223_4a.applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies some turn lane t of side right (st.turn_lane, rel.occupies).
NRS_484B_223_4a.obligation: For every turn lane t of side right that the subject occupies (the whole s1 selection restated), at the judged observation the subject's declared intention int.right_turn is true either at the intersection r that t enters (st_lane_enters t r) or at some driveway or alley entrance r lying on a highway h on which t lies (st_on_way t h and st_on_way r h). Where it is declared false at every such region, or no such region exists, the subject's presence in t is violated; where it is undeclared at one such region and false at the others, it is unknown. The intention is read at the judged observation, never ahead.

narrowings.why: 'designed to provide' is read through the right turn lane's presence on the road
'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a st.turn_lane of side right that enters intersection X; int.right_turn is declared false at X and at the driveway entrance lying on the same highway as the lane (its plan goes straight).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the right turn lane and int.right_turn is declared true at the intersection the lane enters.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a through st.lane; no turn lane is occupied.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source labels lanes but cannot tell a turn lane; the subject occupies the rightmost lane with int.right_turn declared false at the intersection it enters and at the driveway entrance.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject in the right turn lane declares int.right_turn false at the intersection the lane enters and true at a driveway entrance lying on the same highway as the lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject in the right turn lane declares int.right_turn true only at another intersection of the scene, one the lane does not enter, and false at the intersection the lane enters and at the driveway entrance on its highway.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a turn lane of side left, its plan going straight: no right turn lane is occupied.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
shall yield the right-of-way
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield the right-of-way to that traffic
until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'Driver' is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Mapping index: 'The driver of a vehicle' maps to the same aggregate.

As in NRS_484B_263_o1: st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes' (DEF-NRS-484A-060 'no legal right of access except at such points only'); rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... controlled-access lane ...)'. The entry is the rise of the subject's overlap with region c, the exit the rise of its absence after overlap; kin.speed tells the subject still moves. 'About to' is read by the movement itself.

'that traffic' refers back to these words, so they keep their full qualification here: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; a footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) the same controlled-access region c; moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance), with the subject ahead in its frame (rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component positive).

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'); 'that traffic' is the approaching vehicles of a4, so a road user the duty concerns carries both aggregates. The continuing yield is read like the yield (mapping index 'shall yield': kin.speed, rel.contact): while the subject moves, no contact (rel.contact 'touch or overlap (a collision)', not a stand-in for a near miss, which a5 and a7 carry). 'continue' places the duty after the entry or exit, read on the clock (kin.time 'instant of observation') through the time since that event.

operationalizations.standard: proximity that constitutes an immediate hazard (the traffic the continuing yield concerns)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision threshold at a centre distance below the collision clearance

operationalizations.standard: until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety
operationalizations.convention: the subject may proceed with reasonable safety once no approaching vehicle of that traffic is in a traffic-conflict (closest approach within the time-to-collision threshold below the collision clearance); the continuing duty is read over the merge or diverge that follows the entry or exit, whose duration is the time an acceleration or deceleration lane is run

NRS_484B_263_o2.applicability: The subject (vehicle aggregate) is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and there is a controlled-access region c whose latest entry or exit by the subject (the latest rise of the subject's overlap with c, or of its non-overlap with c after overlapping it) lies strictly before this observation and no more than p.merge_window before it (Term.sinceRise of that event above zero and at most p.merge_window).
NRS_484B_263_o2.obligation: For every such region c (re-bound with that selection): for every other road user v of the traffic aggregate and of the vehicle aggregate that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), whose footprint overlaps c, and in whose frame the subject lies ahead (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from v to the subject positive): the subject and v are not in contact, and it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'about to enter or exit' is read by the entry into or exit from the controlled-access region as the source maps it, as in NRS_484B_263_o1

the continuing yield is judged at the observations that follow the entry or exit within the merge window; once that window has run the subject is taken to have merged or diverged, and its later conduct is judged by the following and lane rules, not by this one
'reasonable safety' is read through the same traffic-conflict bound as the immediate hazard: the subject may proceed once no approaching vehicle of that traffic is in such a conflict with it

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject entered controlled-access region c a short time ago (within p.merge_window, after the entry observation) and keeps moving; vehicle v (traffic and vehicle aggregates) moves on c with the subject ahead of it and their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but every vehicle on c is far behind: no closest approach within p.conflict_horizon, no contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject entered c long before, more than p.merge_window ago, and travels within it; v closes from behind.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid (velocities, positions and headings observed, so the closest approach is a conflict), but kin.speed is not observed: whether the subject is still moving and whether v is a moving vehicle approaching it are unknown while the conflict holds.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Within p.merge_window after its entry into c, the subject moves and no other road user is in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hyden; FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.merge_window
param_proposals.convention: the time an entering or exiting vehicle takes, after coming onto or leaving the controlled-access highway, to complete its merge into or diverge from the highway's traffic: an acceleration or deceleration lane of about 250 m run at about 25 m/s
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book acceleration and deceleration lane lengths

segmentation.text: When stopping is required
at a railroad crossing
the driver
shall keep as far to the right of the highway
as possible
and
shall not form two lanes of traffic
unless the highway is marked for four or more lanes of traffic.

elements.justification: "Stopping" (DEF-NRS-484A-260) is "any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle"; that it is required is read through the devices in the scene that require a halt of the subject's traffic: dev.railway_signal_or_gate, "the devices at a level crossing; lights in {flashing, dark}; gate in {up, lowering, down, raising, none}", with lights flashing or the gate lowering or down; dev.stop_sign, "regulatory sign requiring a full halt"; dev.traffic_signal showing circular_red; dev.human_direction with indication stop and role police_officer or railroad_flagger. Each must govern (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, "a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region"). dev.governs is "not a stand-in for a position": the place of the stop is not read from governance but from s2's distance to the crossing. dev.traffic_signal is not a sign; the signal's state is read, not a sign's.

st.railway_crossing: "level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail"; "railroad" (DEF-NRS-484A-200) is "a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails": a level crossing of a railway with the roadway is a railroad crossing, and a streetcar line laid along the street forms no level crossing of a railway with the roadway, so the definition's exclusion is already made by the contract. The subject is at the crossing where st.region_geometry, "the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)", is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach; region_geometry is not a stand-in for occupancy, and no occupancy is read from it.

"Driver" (DEF-NRS-484A-080) means "every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle": the duty binds the conduct of a vehicle, the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ("every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"); ru.aggregate is not a stand-in for the relational role of who drives, which is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

Two lanes of traffic are formed at the crossing where another member of "traffic" (DEF-NRS-484A-285, "pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel", the admitted aggregate) stands or moves beside the subject in a lane (st.lane, "a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles"; rel.occupies), so that two lines of traffic face the crossing side by side: rel.same_direction, "headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance", and rel.longitudinal_overlap positive, "the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)" — a projection, "neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies", and only side-by-side position is read from it. The other road user is at the same crossing c where its body is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach of c (st.region_geometry, claimed with s2). Requiring the other to occupy a lane leaves out a pedestrian on a sidewalk, which forms no lane of traffic.

The highway the subject occupies (st.highway, rel.occupies) is marked for four or more lanes where at least four distinct lanes (st.lane, "a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles") lie on it (st.on_way, "the public way a structure region lies on"), counted over both directions; st.lane is not a half of the roadway, and the count is of lane regions, not of lateral positions. The literal four is the text's figure.

NRS_484B_560_3_o2.applicability: The subject is a vehicle; its body is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach of a railroad crossing c (st.railway_crossing, st.region_geometry); and some device d governs (dev.governs) a travel region r whose footprint the subject overlaps (rel.occupies) and requires a halt of r's traffic at this observation: a dev.railway_signal_or_gate whose lights are flashing or whose gate is lowering or down, a dev.stop_sign, a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red, or a dev.human_direction of role police_officer or railroad_flagger with indication stop. Exception: the duty does not apply where the highway h the subject occupies has at least four pairwise distinct lanes lying on it (st.lane, st.on_way(l, h)).
NRS_484B_560_3_o2.obligation: At every such observation, no road user v other than the subject (not same(v, subject)), a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, occupying a lane (st.lane, rel.occupies), whose body is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach of the same crossing c, travels in the subject's direction (rel.same_direction with tolerance p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos) side by side with the subject (rel.longitudinal_overlap of subject and v positive). Where such a v exists the duty is violated; where none can exist it is complied with, also when the subject is alone.

narrowings.why: "the driver" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; whoever or whatever controls it.
That a device is official is read from its presence.

Forming two lanes is read as the subject standing or moving side by side with another road user in a lane, both at the crossing; which of the two came alongside the other is not told apart, so both are held to have formed the second line.
"marked" lanes are read from the mapped lane regions: a represented lane is read as a marked one.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Two-lane two-way highway (two lanes on the way); railway lights flashing govern the subject's lane; another car halts 10 m from the crossing in the right lane, and the subject car pulls up beside it in the opposing lane, same direction, longitudinal overlap 3 m.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same two-lane highway and flashing lights; the subject car halts in the right lane 8 m behind the other car (longitudinal overlap negative); no road user beside it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Lights dark and gate up at the crossing, no stop sign, red signal or stop direction governs the subject's lane; two cars pass side by side.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Two-lane highway; railway lights flashing at the crossing, but which travel regions the device governs is unobserved; no stop sign, signal or human direction; another car halts beside the subject at the crossing in the same direction, longitudinal overlap 3 m. Whether stopping is required of the subject's lane cannot be decided, so the duty's applicability, and the verdict, is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Four-lane highway (four lanes lie on the way, two per direction); flashing lights; the subject car halts in the left same-direction lane beside a car in the right lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Two-lane highway, flashing lights; the subject car halts alone at the crossing, no other road user in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a vehicle's body to a railroad grade crossing within which the vehicle is at the crossing, on the stretch where a halt for the crossing is made: the 50-ft outer bound of the zone in which grade-crossing practice places the halt before the nearest rail
param_proposals.source: MUTCD Part 8 highway-rail grade crossing stop-line placement and the Uniform Vehicle Code grade-crossing stop zone

param_proposals.name: p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two road users standing or moving side by side count as travelling the same way: the heading spread of vehicles queued in adjacent lanes
param_proposals.source: lane-change and queue heading variability in naturalistic driving data

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
approaching an intersection
shall yield
the right-of-way
to a vehicle which has entered the intersection
from a different highway.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion, not membership.

Same mapping as 'approaching the intersection' in the index: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier c1 whose entrance end is X — st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end — the carrier is an approach to that intersection'; st.travel_region is c1's kind, st.intersection X's. Never read from distance or velocity.

Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed — kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') above the halt tolerance — while the protected vehicle is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'). Contact is not a near miss; the near miss is the standard's bound.

'A vehicle' is the admitted aggregate; 'which has entered the intersection' is its footprint overlapping X (rel.occupies), continuously since the observation at which it came from its approach carrier (f).

'From a different highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way') is v's approach carrier c2 (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters c2 X) lying on a highway h2 (st.on_way: 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') on which the subject's carrier c1 does not lie. st.on_way is not nearness to a way: the relation is the map's.

Same mapping as 'or at a traffic-controlled intersection' in the index. DEF-NRS-484A-145: 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'; the intersection is controlled where a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering it (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection'; st.lane_enters ties the carrier to X).

'Vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions': per rel.oncoming's 'Not a stand-in for: the direction a road user approaches from — that is read through the carrier it approaches through ... and through that carrier's direction (st.lane_direction)'. The subject's carrier c1 and the carrier c2 v entered X from (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters) have designated directions opposed within p.oncoming_heading_cos. 'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate.

'Is making a left turn' is the turn under way in X: the vehicle's heading change since its entry into X (rel.occupies), integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left') by the formula language's heading-since term, lying to the left between p.turn_heading_min and p.u_turn_heading_min. kin.yaw_rate is not a stand-in for road curvature: it is the vehicle's own turning.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

NRS_484B_250_1.applicability: At every observation at which the subject occupies a carrier c1 that enters an intersection X (st.lane_enters c1 X): the subject approaching X; except where X is controlled — a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering X (dev.governs) — and except where NRS_484B_250_4_o1 or NRS_484B_250_4_o2 (binder subject ↦ subject) applies to the subject.
NRS_484B_250_1.obligation: Re-binding c1 and X as in the applicability: for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose footprint overlaps X and has overlapped it continuously since an observation at which v occupied a carrier c2 that enters X (st.lane_enters c2 X) and lies on a highway h2 (st.on_way c2 h2) on which c1 does not lie — excepting the pair where the designated directions of c1 and c2 (st.lane_direction) have a dot product below minus p.oncoming_heading_cos and either the subject or v declares int.left_turn at X at this observation, or v's heading change since its latest entry into X (heading-since over kin.yaw_rate, step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is a turn to the left of at least p.turn_heading_min and below p.u_turn_heading_min: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'official' is a legal status; the device present and governing is its evidence.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: No device governs X or its carriers. Vehicle v entered X from carrier c2 on highway h2, on which the subject's carrier c1 does not lie, and is crossing X. The subject on c1 keeps kin.speed well above p.halt_speed_tolerance and its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject comes to rest on c1 short of X until v has cleared, then proceeds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A dev.stop_sign governs c1: the intersection is controlled.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled X; v crossing X from a different highway on a conflicting path; kin.speed is absent, so whether the subject proceeds into the conflict is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches the uncontrolled X with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: v is approaching X on its own carrier and has not entered X; the subject's closest approach to v is in conflict, but v is not a vehicle which has entered the intersection.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: At a skewed junction v entered X from c2 on another highway whose designated direction is opposed to c1's within p.oncoming_heading_cos, and v declares int.left_turn at X; the subject proceeds in conflict with v: the pair is excepted.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique time-to-collision thresholds

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: design passenger-car dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.oncoming_heading_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as proceeding in opposite directions
param_proposals.source: skew tolerance of opposing intersection approaches

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading changes of a few degrees versus junction turns of about ninety degrees

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: midpoint between a right-angle turn and a full reversal of direction

segmentation.text: Except if required by an emergency
or as otherwise authorized by subsection 3
[(3) appended below],
a person shall not drive a vehicle
on a controlled-access highway:
Across any solid white line that separates an entrance or exit lane from a marked traffic lane.
A person driving a vehicle described in
paragraphs (a) to (f), inclusive, of subsection 4 of NRS 484B.210
may drive that vehicle on a paved shoulder of a controlled-access highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.
The provisions of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (c) of subsection 1 do not apply to:
(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480;
(b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490;
(c) A traffic incident management vehicle;
(d) A tow car;
(e) A coroner vehicle;
or (f) A public transit motor bus,
that is being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.

elements.justification: An emergency requiring the movement is not observable; it is read through the conduct that shows it: the subject's hazard lamps flashing (sig.hazard, "both indicators flashing together"), or the subject an emergency vehicle (ru.emergency_vehicle, "vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency") showing a lit warning lamp (sig.warning_lamp, "a warning lamp lit"). ru.emergency_vehicle is "not a stand-in for a responding emergency vehicle — the class alone is not responding": the class is read only together with its lit warning lamp.

Authorization by subsection 3 is the permission subsection 3 states (spans e7, e10, e12-e18): a shoulder-use permission posted by a dev.regulatory_sign, "a point regulation by catalogue code", of code shoulder_use_permitted; this span joins that permission to the duty as an exception.

"vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway". "drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the vehicle is moving, drv.motion.complete_halt not holding with p.halt_speed_tolerance.

"Controlled-access highway" (DEF-NRS-484A-060, "every highway to or from which ... persons have no legal right of access except at such points only"): st.controlled_access, "a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes", whose region the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies).

Driving across the line between two lanes is the subject's footprint first reaching from lane r1 into the neighbouring lane r2 on side s: drv.lane.entering_adjacent_lane, "Road user a, occupying lane r1, begins to move into lane r2, the neighbouring lane of the same direction on side s of r1". The line crossed is the marking on side s of r1: st.lane_marking, "per side of a lane: type ... colour", of type solid or double_solid and colour white. It separates an entrance or exit lane from a marked traffic lane where, of r1 and r2 (st.lane), one is governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code entrance or exit and the other is governed by no such sign. The regulatory sign is "not a stand-in for a road feature": the lane's role is read from the sign that indicates it, as subsection 1 reads entrances and exits.
The person driving a vehicle of the classes listed (e12-e17): the subject vehicle, admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; which vehicles are described is read from the list.

On a paved shoulder of a controlled-access highway: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a paved st.shoulder while it occupies the st.controlled_access region; the signage allowing that vehicle to use the shoulder is a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted governing that shoulder (dev.governs), whose conditions hold for the subject (prim.conditions_hold, "the structured conditions of a device ... hold at the observation for a road user").

"(a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480;": "authorized emergency vehicle" (DEF-NRS-484A-020, "a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law") names the class of vehicles the jurisdiction designates as emergency vehicles; its own class atom is ru.emergency_vehicle, "vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency", of any kind. ru.aggregate is "not a stand-in for a named road-user class for which ... its own class atom" exists, so the class atom carries it. The words "when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law" qualify the permission to depart from traffic laws, not membership of the class, and the permission this span confers is the shoulder use of e18, not emergency operation; so no responding conduct is read here, as the contract's "not a stand-in for a responding emergency vehicle" requires. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490;": a vehicle the jurisdiction, by its permit, designates to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-020, "a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws") is of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency: ru.emergency_vehicle, "vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency", the class atom that carries e12. The class alone is read; no conduct is required by these words. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(c) A traffic incident management vehicle;": ru.official_vehicle, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service", kind incident_management; not an emergency vehicle. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(d) A tow car;": "tow car" (DEF-NRS-484A-280, "a motor vehicle which has been altered or designed and equipped for and exclusively used in the business of towing vehicles ... or is otherwise exclusively used to render assistance to other vehicles") is a named road-user class with its own class atom: ru.official_vehicle, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment", of kind tow; ru.aggregate is "not a stand-in for a named road-user class for which ... its own class atom" exists. The definition's "a motor vehicle", which the official-vehicle contract ("a vehicle") does not already make, is carried beside it as ru.motor_vehicle, "a self-propelled vehicle other than a rail vehicle". The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"(e) A coroner vehicle;": ru.official_vehicle, "a vehicle in official or contracted road service", kind coroner; not an emergency vehicle. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

"or (f) A public transit motor bus,": a named road-user class with its own class atom, ru.transit_bus, "bus in public transit service, identifiable by its livery or route display"; ru.aggregate is "not a stand-in for a named road-user class for which ... its own class atom" exists. "Bus" (DEF-NRS-484A-030) includes it as "a vehicle owned by the State, a political subdivision ... designed for carrying more than 10 passengers and used for the transportation of persons, or a vehicle, other than a taxicab, designed and used for the transportation of persons for compensation"; its one exclusion, a taxicab, the transit-bus contract already makes, a transit bus being a bus. The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

Being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway: the listed vehicle occupies (rel.occupies) a paved st.shoulder lying on (st.on_way) the st.highway it is on, governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code shoulder_use_permitted whose conditions hold for it (prim.conditions_hold). The list borrowed through e8 from NRS 484B.210(4) reads, in part, "(c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;".

compositions.quote: (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle;
compositions.why: The reference borrows only the list of vehicle classes NRS 484B.210(4) sets forth (an authorized emergency vehicle, one under permit as such, a traffic incident management vehicle, a tow car, a coroner vehicle, a public transit motor bus) to name which vehicles subsection 3 permits on a signed paved shoulder; no rule of NRS 484B.210 (its passing on the right, or its exemption from it) needs to apply, hold or be complied with for this duty or its exception, and the list's words are appended in this line and carried by its own elements.

residues.why: Introduces the list of NRS 484B.210(4) as appended; the exemption from the passing rule of NRS 484B.210(1)(c)(1) it states is that section's, not this duty's, and is not read here.

NRS_484B_587_2b.applicability: The subject is a vehicle in motion (drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) with p.halt_speed_tolerance does not hold) whose footprint overlaps a controlled-access highway ca (rel.occupies, st.controlled_access). Exceptions: the duty does not apply where the subject's hazard lamps flash (sig.hazard) or it is an emergency vehicle with a lit warning lamp (ru.emergency_vehicle, sig.warning_lamp); nor where the subject, a listed vehicle (ru.emergency_vehicle for e12/e13; ru.official_vehicle of kind incident_management or coroner for e14/e16; ru.official_vehicle of kind tow that is ru.motor_vehicle for e15; ru.transit_bus for e17), occupies a paved shoulder lying on (st.on_way) a highway it occupies, which a shoulder_use_permitted dev.regulatory_sign governs (dev.governs) with its conditions holding for the subject (prim.conditions_hold).
NRS_484B_587_2b.obligation: At no such observation does drv.lane.entering_adjacent_lane(subject, r1, r2, s) hold, for lanes r1 and r2 and a side s in {left, right}, where the st.lane_marking on side s of r1 is of type solid or double_solid and colour white, and of r1 and r2 one is governed (dev.governs) by a dev.regulatory_sign of code entrance or exit and the other by no such sign.

narrowings.why: "a person shall not drive" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle in motion is driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
An emergency is read through the conduct that shows it: hazard lamps flashing, or an emergency vehicle showing a lit warning lamp.
An entrance or exit lane is read as a lane an entrance- or exit-coded regulatory sign governs, and a marked traffic lane as a mapped lane no such sign governs.

Driving across the line is read at the observation the footprint first reaches over it into the neighbouring lane; a solid_broken marking, whose solid side cannot be told from the per-side record, is not read as a solid line.
"lawfully placed" signage is read from the presence of a shoulder_use_permitted sign governing the shoulder.
"lawfully placed" signage is read from the presence of a shoulder_use_permitted sign governing the shoulder.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a controlled-access highway, the subject car in an entrance lane (governed by an entrance-coded sign) moves at 22 m/s and its footprint first reaches into the adjacent through lane across a solid white marking on that side.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject car in the entrance lane merges into the through lane where the marking between them on that side is broken white.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car changes lanes across a solid white line on a surface street; it never overlaps a controlled-access region.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car moves from the entrance lane into the through lane on a controlled-access highway; the source does not observe lane markings.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: An emergency vehicle with lit warning lamps crosses the solid white line from the through lane into an exit lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The subject car crosses a solid white line between two through lanes, neither governed by an entrance or exit sign.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: On a controlled-access highway, a public transit bus (no hazard or warning lamps) on a paved shoulder lying on the highway and governed by a shoulder_use_permitted sign with an unrestricted legend reaches from the entrance lane across a solid white line into the through lane.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: The scene of branch_3 with an ordinary car, of no listed class, in place of the transit bus: it reaches across the same solid white line from the shoulder-side entrance lane into the through lane.

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: The scene of branch_3 with a tow vehicle (an official vehicle of kind tow, a motor vehicle) in place of the transit bus.

scenarios.name: branch_6
scenarios.narrative: The scene of branch_3 with an emergency vehicle showing no warning lamp and no hazard lamps in place of the transit bus.

segmentation.text: A person shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle
other than a bus
in a bus stop,
or a taxicab
in a taxicab stand,
when such stop or stand has been officially designated and appropriately signed,
except that the driver of a passenger vehicle
may temporarily stop there
and for the purpose of and while actually engaged in
expeditiously
loading or unloading of passengers
when such stopping does not interfere with
any bus or taxicab
waiting to enter or about to enter such zone.

elements.justification: 'Stop' when prohibited is 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-260, the definition the table resolves for 'stopping' in this law); 'stand' is 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not' (DEF-NRS-484A-250) and 'park' 'the standing of a vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-155): together a halt, drv.motion.complete_halt ('at rest at the observation ... its speed at or below a tolerance', p.halt_speed_tolerance). The definition's exclusions are carried beside it: a halt with another road user ahead in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) within p.queue_halt_gap of the body (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', not a centre distance) avoids conflict with other traffic; a halt on a travel region the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.travel_region) governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal showing red or yellow, a railway signal flashing or a gate not up, or a police officer's stop indication (dev.stop_sign, dev.yield_sign, dev.traffic_signal, dev.railway_signal_or_gate, dev.human_direction) complies with a device or an officer. 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle.

'Bus' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus ('a vehicle owned by the State, a political subdivision or a private school or nursery, designed for carrying ... passengers and used for the transportation of persons, or a vehicle, other than a taxicab, designed and used for the transportation of persons for compensation'), claimed as one atom, never expanded; which classes it decides is the run's reading of the definition.

A bus stop at the curb is st.curb_zone of kind bus_stop ('a signed or marked length of curb'), which the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... curb zone ...)').

'Taxicab' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-270::taxicab ('a motor vehicle designed or constructed to accommodate and transport ... passengers, including the driver, and used to transport passengers for a charge or fee'), claimed as one atom; which classes it decides is the run's reading of the definition.

'Taxicab stand' is 'a fixed area in a highway parallel and adjacent to the curb or edge of the highway and set aside for taxicabs to stand for passengers' (DEF-NRS-484B-067): st.curb_zone of kind taxicab_stand ('a signed or marked length of curb'), which the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies).

That the stop or stand 'has been officially designated and appropriately signed' is its legal status, read from the feature's presence on the road: the curb zone of kind bus_stop or taxicab_stand the subject occupies (st.curb_zone, 'a signed or marked length of curb'; rel.occupies) is presumed designated and signed.

'Driver' is 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-080), read through the vehicle's controlled motion. 'Passenger vehicle' has no posted definition: it is read as a vehicle (the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) not built to carry goods or to be drawn: not ru.truck ('motor vehicle for carrying goods, with a body built for that purpose') and not ru.trailer_or_combination ('vehicle drawn by another, or the combination'), carried beside the aggregate.

'While actually engaged in' fixes the loading to the stop itself: the door of s11 is open at an observation of the same halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, 'at rest at the observation'); the purpose is read by that conduct.
The loading or unloading of passengers is read by the act through which passengers board or alight: a door of the vehicle open (sig.door_open, 'a door open; side in {traffic, curb}').

'Any bus or taxicab': the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus and DEF-NRS-484A-270::taxicab, each claimed as one atom; a road user the run's reading leaves unresolved under both makes this limb unknown, never decided.

'Waiting to enter or about to enter such zone' is read by the conduct, on the same zone z the subject occupies (st.curb_zone, rel.occupies): the bus or taxicab does not overlap z and the ground distance from its body to z (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') is within p.zone_entry_wait_reach; it is waiting where it is halted there (drv.motion.complete_halt), and about to enter where, read by the movement it leads to, it stays outside z within that reach until its footprint comes to overlap z (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.standard: temporarily
operationalizations.convention: curbside passenger pick-up dwell: a stop counts as temporary while it has not lasted as long as a passenger pick-up dwell, i.e. while the subject is not at rest at every observation of a window of length p.standing_min_duration behind the observation (drv.motion.parked)

operationalizations.standard: expeditiously
operationalizations.convention: curbside passenger pick-up dwell: loading or unloading counts as expeditious while the halt has not lasted as long as a passenger pick-up dwell (drv.motion.parked with min_duration p.standing_min_duration); the same bound as the temporary stop it qualifies

operationalizations.standard: does not interfere with
operationalizations.convention: queueing at a curb space: a stop interferes with a bus or taxicab where, at some observation of the stop so far, it is outside the zone within one passenger-car length plus a queue spacing of it (p.zone_entry_wait_reach), the place a vehicle waits to take the space, and is halted there or stays there until it comes onto the zone

NRS_484B_517.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) whose footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a curb zone z (st.curb_zone) that is of kind bus_stop while the subject is not a bus (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-030::bus false), or of kind taxicab_stand while the subject is not a taxicab (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-270::taxicab false).
NRS_484B_517.obligation: For every zone z the subject occupies that is selected as in the applicability (re-bound with its kind and the subject's class), the subject is not halted (drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), except a halt that is (a) to avoid conflict with other traffic: some road user other than the subject is ahead of the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with a gap between bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_halt_gap; or (b) in compliance with a device or an officer: a travel region the subject occupies is governed (dev.governs) by a stop sign, a yield sign, a traffic signal displaying a red or yellow indication or flashing_red, a railway signal or gate with lights flashing or gate not up, or a person in the role police_officer giving the indication stop; or (c) a temporary, expeditious stop of a passenger vehicle for passengers: the subject is neither a truck (ru.truck) nor a trailer or combination (ru.trailer_or_combination), it is not parked with min_duration p.standing_min_duration (drv.motion.parked), a door of the subject is open (sig.door_open) at some observation of the same halt, before or after the observation, and at no observation of the halt up to the judged one is there a road user w other than the subject that is a bus or a taxicab (the two admitted aggregates), whose footprint does not overlap z, whose body's ground distance to z (st.region_geometry) is at most p.zone_entry_wait_reach, and which either is halted there (drv.motion.complete_halt: waiting to enter) or, from that observation on, stays outside z within p.zone_entry_wait_reach of it until its footprint overlaps z (strong until, rel.occupies: about to enter).

narrowings.why: 'A person shall not stop, stand or park a vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion.
'The driver of a passenger vehicle' is read on the vehicle's controlled motion.
Official designation and appropriate signing are read from the presence of the curb zone of kind bus_stop or taxicab_stand on the road.
The purpose of loading or unloading passengers is read by a door of the halted vehicle open during the halt.

'Waiting to enter' is read by a bus or taxicab halted outside the zone within the waiting reach; 'about to enter', an imminent movement, is read by the movement it leads to: the bus or taxicab stays outside the zone within that reach until its footprint overlaps the zone.

'a traffic signal displaying a red or yellow indication': read as the steady red and yellow indications, circular and arrow (circular_red, circular_yellow, red_arrow(dir), yellow_arrow(dir)), with the record's flashing_red; flashing_yellow and flashing_yellow_arrow, which let traffic proceed with caution, are not taken as an indication a halt complies with
'a railway signal or gate with ... gate not up': read as a gate in the state lowering, down or raising; the state none (the device has no gate) is not a gate that is not up

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab-class passenger car halts in a bus_stop curb zone for longer than the standing duration, doors closed; no road user ahead and no stop control governs its lane.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab-class passenger car halts briefly in a bus_stop curb zone with its curb-side door open and moves off before the standing duration; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab-class passenger car halts in a passenger_loading curb zone, which is neither a bus stop nor a taxicab stand; no bus_stop or taxicab_stand zone is occupied.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab-class passenger car halts briefly in a bus_stop curb zone and the source does not observe its doors.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab-class passenger car halts briefly in a bus_stop curb zone and moves off before the standing duration, its doors closed throughout the halt: it is not loading or unloading passengers; no other road user is in the scene and no stop control governs its lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab-class passenger car halts in a bus_stop curb zone with its curb-side door open and stays halted longer than the standing duration: the stop is not temporary; no other road user is in the scene and no stop control governs its lane.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A taxicab-class passenger car halts in a bus_stop curb zone for longer than the standing duration, doors closed, a short queue gap behind a halted vehicle ahead in its lane: a halt to avoid conflict with other traffic.

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsection 2,
on a controlled-access highway
which has two or more clearly marked lanes for traveling in the same direction,
a driver may not continue to operate a motor vehicle in the extreme left lane
if the driver knows, or reasonably should know, that he or she is traveling at a rate of speed which is less than the posted speed limit for that portion of the controlled-access highway
and is being overtaken in that lane from the rear by a motor vehicle traveling at a higher rate of speed.
The requirements of subsection 1 do not apply: (a) To a driver operating a motor vehicle that is:
(1) Overtaking another vehicle proceeding in the same direction;
(2) Preparing for a left turn
at an intersection;
(3) Traveling in a lane designated for the use of high-occupancy vehicles pursuant to NRS 484A.460,
if the driver complies with the requirements to travel in such a lane
or (4) Engaged in the construction, maintenance or repair of the highway, including, without limitation, the removal of snow.
(b) When traffic conditions, inclement weather, obstructions or hazards
make it necessary to drive in the extreme left lane.
(c) When compliance with an official traffic control device or the directions given by a peace officer makes it necessary to drive in the extreme left lane.
(d) To the driver of an authorized emergency vehicle in the course of his or her official duties.
(e) To a driver operating a motor vehicle
within the geographical limits of a city or town.

elements.justification: st.controlled_access: 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes', DEF-NRS-484A-060's controlled-access highway; rel.occupies (which lists 'controlled-access lane') anchors it to the subject's footprint.

'two or more … lanes for traveling in the same direction': st.lane_adjacency, 'the count of lanes in that direction', at least the stated figure, read on the lane (st.lane) the subject occupies (rel.occupies). 'clearly marked': the lanes' presence on the map is the evidence (observable_reading status).

'a motor vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. 'in the extreme left lane': st.lane_adjacency, 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction … ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane, looking along the lane's direction', of the lane the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane): the lane with no left neighbour of the same direction. 'continue to operate' is the subject remaining there while the triggers hold, over the move-over window; 'driver' and 'operate' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'traveling at a rate of speed which is less than the posted speed limit for that portion': kin.speed below the value of a dev.speed_limit_sign ('sign stating a maximum or minimum speed, with value and unit'; kind maximum) that governs (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies): the limit of that portion. 'knows, or reasonably should know' is read through those facts themselves (observable_reading perception).

'being overtaken in that lane from the rear by a motor vehicle': a road user c other than the subject, a motor vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle), behind the subject in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane, 'a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction'); 'traveling at a higher rate of speed': kin.speed of c above the subject's, so that c, behind in that lane, closes on the subject from the rear.
'a driver operating a motor vehicle that is:' introduces the exceptions (1)-(4) for the subject, a motor vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle), carried by their own spans.

'Overtaking another vehicle proceeding in the same direction': drv.interaction.overtake_pass, 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it', with b a vehicle other than the subject (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); the overtaking is under way where its recognition falls within the window ahead of length p.overtake_window.

'at an intersection': st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet', DEF-NRS-484A-105's intersection, the target region of the declared intention int.left_turn (k10). The intersection the words place the preparation at is the one the subject is at: one its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, the turn's preparation carried into the intersection), or the one it approaches, which by st.lane_enters ('a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection') is the intersection a travel region (st.travel_region, the kind of the carrier the relation reads) the subject occupies runs into at its entrance end. No distance is read: the words state no size.

'a lane designated for the use of high-occupancy vehicles': st.reserved_lane, 'lane reserved for a class of vehicles; class ∈ {high_occupancy, …}', class high_occupancy, occupied by the subject (rel.occupies). 'high-occupancy vehicles' borrows DEF-NRS-484A-460-2: '(a) A vehicle that is transporting more than one person; (b) A motorcycle, regardless of the number of passengers; (c) A bus, regardless of the number of passengers; and (d) Any other vehicle designated by regulation.' — the class for which the lane is reserved. 'designated … pursuant to NRS 484A.460' is read through the reserved lane's presence (observable_reading status).

'the requirements to travel in such a lane' are, by DEF-NRS-484A-460-2, the conditions the Department determines ('(1) The number of occupants required per vehicle; and (2) The hours of the day that the use of the lane is restricted') and advises on signs; the class of road user the lane serves is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-460-2::high_occupancy_vehicle, which borrows '(a) A vehicle that is transporting more than one person; (b) A motorcycle, regardless of the number of passengers; (c) A bus, regardless of the number of passengers; and (d) Any other vehicle designated by regulation.' The posted conditions are a dev.zone_sign of kind high_occupancy_lane governing (dev.governs) the reserved lane, its 'conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend'; that they hold for the subject is prim.conditions_hold, 'the structured conditions of a device … hold at the observation for a road user'. The sign's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now' is met by reading prim.conditions_hold for it.

'Engaged in the construction, maintenance or repair of the highway, including … the removal of snow': the vehicle is in road service, ru.official_vehicle ('a vehicle in official or contracted road service, identifiable by livery or equipment'), kind highway_maintenance, and shows the conduct of a vehicle at work on the highway: an amber warning lamp lit, flashing or rotating (sig.warning_lamp, 'a warning lamp lit; colour ∈ {red, blue, amber, white}, mode ∈ {flashing, rotating, steady}'). Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: an audible warning' does not apply; the class's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: an emergency vehicle' does not apply.

'traffic conditions': road users other than the subject of the traffic (DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) occupying (rel.occupies) the lane to the right of the subject's (st.lane, st.lane_adjacency 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction'). 'inclement weather': env.precipitation ('rain or snow falling'), env.wet_road, env.ice_or_snow, env.visibility ('visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)'). 'obstructions or hazards': st.obstruction ('a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user'), located from the subject by its ground distance (st.region_geometry) and its side (prim.region_lateral_offset, 'left positive').

'compliance with an official traffic control device … makes it necessary': a device governing (dev.governs) the lane to the right of the lane the subject occupies (st.lane_adjacency) closes it: dev.lane_control_signal state red_x or yellow_x, dev.regulatory_sign code closed_to_traffic or do_not_enter, or dev.temporary_traffic_control ('cones, barricades … marking works, a closure'). 'the directions given by a peace officer': dev.human_direction role police_officer, indication stop, governing that lane. 'official' is read through the device's presence (observable_reading status).

'authorized emergency vehicle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle, carried by ru.aggregate; the class alone is no conduct, so being 'in the course of his or her official duties' is read through the conduct of a vehicle operated on duty as an emergency vehicle: a warning lamp of any colour lit, flashing or rotating (sig.warning_lamp, 'a warning lamp lit … mode ∈ {flashing, rotating, steady}') or a siren sounding (sig.siren, 'a siren, whistle or bell sounding'); the two are read separately, as sig.siren's contract requires. Like exceptions (a)-(c), it excuses the subject inside the obligation, so that another exception holding decides the verdict whatever the reading resolves of the class.
'a driver operating a motor vehicle': the subject, DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.standard: make it necessary to drive in the extreme left lane
