operationalizations.convention: Stopping-distance convention: S = speed(subject) × H + speed(subject)² / (2 × D), with H and D selected by the surface (_ice where env.ice_or_snow, _wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation, else _dry), as for following distance. The left lane is necessary where moving right cannot be done within S: a traffic member occupying the right neighbouring lane has a longitudinal body gap to the subject (rel.surface_gap) below S, or an obstruction lies within ground distance S of the subject on its right (st.region_geometry, prim.region_lateral_offset negative), or the visibility distance (env.visibility) is below S. Each factor enters by degree: the subject's speed and the surface move S; the gap, the distance and the visibility are compared with it.

assumptions.meaning: the place of the road user at the observation lies within the geographical limits of an incorporated city or of a town, as the map's reading classifies the area

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

compositions.quote: (a) A vehicle that is transporting more than one person; (b) A motorcycle, regardless of the number of passengers; (c) A bus, regardless of the number of passengers; and (d) Any other vehicle designated by regulation.

residues.why: Points to subsection 2, which is appended to this same law line and carried by its own exception spans k8-k20; the duty is the same whether or not these words are read.

NRS_484B_208_1.applicability: The subject is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) occupying a controlled-access highway (rel.occupies, st.controlled_access) and a lane (st.lane) that has no left neighbouring lane of the same direction (st.lane_adjacency: the leftmost) and whose count of lanes in its direction is at least two (st.lane_adjacency count); and the reading does not place it within the limits of a city or town (not asm.within_city_or_town_limits).
NRS_484B_208_1.obligation: Let S hold at an observation where: the subject occupies a controlled-access highway and the leftmost lane of two or more in its direction; its speed is below the value of some maximum dev.speed_limit_sign governing a travel region it occupies; and none of these holds: (1) within the window ahead of length p.overtake_window, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, c, p.overtake_window, p.overtake_same_direction_cos) for some vehicle c other than the subject (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); (2) for some intersection region ix that the subject occupies (rel.occupies) or that a travel region the subject occupies enters (st.lane_enters(carrier, ix)), intent int.left_turn of the subject at ix; (3) the subject occupies a reserved lane r of class high_occupancy, is a high-occupancy vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-460-2::high_occupancy_vehicle), and prim.conditions_hold(z, subject) for every dev.zone_sign z of kind high_occupancy_lane governing r; (4) the subject is an official vehicle of kind highway_maintenance showing an amber warning lamp, flashing or rotating (sig.warning_lamp); (b) with S_stop = speed × H + speed² / (2 × D) (H, D selected by surface as in the operationalization), some traffic member other than the subject occupies the lane to the right of the subject's lane with longitudinal surface gap below S_stop, or some obstruction lies within ground distance S_stop on the subject's right, or env.visibility is below S_stop; (c) a device governing the lane to the right closes it (lane control signal red_x or yellow_x, regulatory sign closed_to_traffic or do_not_enter, temporary traffic control, or police_officer direction stop); (d) the subject is an authorized emergency vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle) showing a warning lamp of any colour flashing or rotating (sig.warning_lamp) or sounding a siren (sig.siren). Let O hold where some motor vehicle c other than the subject is behind the subject in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) with speed above the subject's. Violated at an observation where, at every observation of the window behind of length p.left_lane_move_over_time, S has held at every observation since an observation at which O and S held together (holdsFor of since(S, O ∧ S)), and some motor vehicle other than the subject is behind the subject in its lane at the judged observation.

narrowings.why: 'clearly marked' lanes are read through the lanes the map represents; the paint's clarity is not modelled.

'continue to operate' is read as the subject remaining in the leftmost lane, slower than the limit and unexcused, for the window p.left_lane_move_over_time after a faster motor vehicle closed on it from behind, with a motor vehicle still behind it in that lane; 'driver' and 'operate' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'knows, or reasonably should know' is read through the facts known: the subject's own speed and the posted maximum governing where it is.
The lane's designation pursuant to NRS 484A.460 is read through the reserved lane of class high_occupancy the map represents.

Being engaged in construction, maintenance or repair of the highway is read through the conduct of a highway-maintenance vehicle at work: its amber warning lamp lit, flashing or rotating; such a vehicle driving with no warning lamp lit is not excused.

'traffic conditions' and 'hazards' are read only through road users in the right neighbouring lane and obstructions on the subject's right; inclement weather only through the surface condition, falling rain and the visibility distance.
An 'official' device is read through its presence on the road.

'in the course of his or her official duties' is read through the conduct of an emergency vehicle on duty: a warning lamp lit, flashing or rotating, or a siren sounding. An authorized emergency vehicle on duty that shows neither is not excused.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Three-lane controlled-access highway outside city limits (asm.within_city_or_town_limits false), dry; a maximum speed sign of 29 m/s governs the lanes. The subject car, showing no warning lamp and no siren, drives in the leftmost lane at 24 m/s; a car approaches from 80 m behind in the same lane at 32 m/s, closes and then follows at 24 m/s; the subject stays in the leftmost lane for 30 s with the middle lane empty.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject signals and moves to the middle lane 5 s after the faster car closes from behind.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives in the middle lane at 24 m/s with a faster car behind it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same scene as forbid; the source declares dev.speed_limit_sign absent, so whether the subject is below the posted limit is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Same scene with the reading placing the highway within city limits (asm.within_city_or_town_limits true).

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; a lane control signal showing red_x governs the middle lane throughout, closing it.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives in the leftmost lane at 24 m/s with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: Same scene as forbid; the subject is a highway-maintenance vehicle in road service with an amber warning lamp flashing throughout.

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the middle lane is occupied by a truck travelling alongside the subject at a body gap of 5 m throughout, so moving right is not possible.

scenarios.name: branch_6
scenarios.narrative: Same scene as forbid; the leftmost lane the subject occupies enters an intersection ahead, and the source declares the subject's plan to turn left at that intersection throughout.

scenarios.name: branch_7
scenarios.narrative: Same scene as branch_6, except that the intersection at which the source declares the subject's plan to turn left is one that no region the subject occupies enters and that the subject never occupies.

param_proposals.name: p.left_lane_move_over_time
param_proposals.convention: the time a driver needs, once a faster vehicle closes from behind, to check the mirrors, signal and move one lane to the right: a perception-reaction time, a few seconds of signal and the lane change
param_proposals.source: lane-change duration studies; driver manuals (signal at least 3 s before a lane change)

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: passing-manoeuvre durations, AASHTO passing sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading angles

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_dry
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a dry surface: the two-second rule of driver manuals
param_proposals.source: state driver handbooks

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_wet
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on a wet surface or in rain: the two-second rule lengthened by a second
param_proposals.source: state driver handbooks

param_proposals.name: p.following_headway_ice
param_proposals.convention: time headway a following driver keeps on an icy or snow-covered surface: the tripled following time driver manuals advise
param_proposals.source: state driver handbooks

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a dry paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.6)
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book; tyre-road friction tables

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_wet
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a wet paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.4)
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book; tyre-road friction tables

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.1)
param_proposals.source: tyre-road friction tables

segmentation.text: Whenever any person is riding a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter upon a sidewalk
such person shall yield
the right-of-way
to any pedestrian
and shall give audible signal
before overtaking and passing
such pedestrian

elements.justification: The three terms are admitted aggregates (DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle 'a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'; DEF-LVMC-11-02-082::electric_bicycle 'a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor which produces not more than seven hundred fifty watts'; DEF-LVMC-11-02-083::electric_scooter 'a device with handlebars and an electric motor ... must not weigh more than one hundred pounds ... maximum speed of not more than twenty miles per hour'), carried as aggregates and never expanded; which classes each includes is the run's reading, and where the reading leaves a class unresolved membership is unknown, which is the rule's faithful verdict, not a defect. 'riding' is read through controlled motion: the device is not at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt false; its contract 'observed as its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance'). 'upon a sidewalk': st.sidewalk 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', anchored by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... sidewalk ...)'); st.sidewalk's exclusion (a crosswalk) does not apply: the words name the sidewalk.

'shall yield' as in the mapping index: kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' (the subject does not proceed into a conflict; read through the closest-approach primitives, which compute from velocities) and rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; rel.contact's exclusion (a near miss) is respected: the near miss is the operationalization's closest-approach bound.
'pedestrian' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...'); same mapping as the index's 'to any pedestrian'.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: preference over another approaching 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a pedestrian whose centre comes, under constant velocities, within the conflict clearance of the moving subject's centre within the conflict horizon is approaching so as to give rise to the danger of a crash

LVMC_11_40_180_C_o1.applicability: The subject is a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter (membership of the three admitted aggregates, as the run's reading classifies them) that occupies an st.sidewalk region (rel.occupies) and is not at rest (not drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance)).
LVMC_11_40_180_C_o1.obligation: For every pedestrian p of the scene other than the subject (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian): the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, p; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance. A scene with no pedestrian is compliant.

narrowings.why: 'any person is riding' is read through the device's controlled motion: a device moving on the sidewalk is read as ridden.
Yielding is read as not proceeding into a conflict and not colliding: while riding, the subject keeps every pedestrian outside the conflict bound.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle (ru.bicycle) rides along the sidewalk toward a pedestrian walking toward it; their closest approach falls within the conflict horizon and below the clearance, and the bicycle keeps riding.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle (ru.bicycle) rides along the sidewalk; a pedestrian on it walks away on a diverging course whose closest approach stays above the clearance.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle (ru.bicycle) rides on the roadway beside the sidewalk where pedestrians walk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle moves near a pedestrian, and the source does not observe which regions the bicycle occupies.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle (ru.bicycle) rides along an empty sidewalk with no pedestrian in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: An electric bicycle (ru.electric_bicycle) rides along the sidewalk toward a pedestrian walking toward it; their closest approach falls within the conflict horizon and below the clearance.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: Hyden, The development of a method for traffic safety evaluation: the Swedish Traffic Conflicts Technique (1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: passenger-car design dimensions (AASHTO Green Book design vehicle)

segmentation.text: Except as provided in NRS 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B]:
When authorized to cross diagonally,
pedestrians
shall cross only in accordance with the official traffic-control devices pertaining to such crossing movements.

elements.justification: 'cross diagonally' is read as in NRS_484B_287_1d: the pedestrian's footprint overlaps an intersection (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') and its velocity is oblique to every lane that runs into it (st.lane_enters, kind st.lane), read through drv.motion.moving_across_carrier at the along/across tolerance and the right-angle tolerance. 'authorized' by official traffic-control devices (DEF-NRS-484A-145: every 'sign, signal, marking and device') is read through the marking that indicates the crossing: a marked crosswalk (st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing'; DEF-NRS-484A-065 (2) 'distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings') under the pedestrian's footprint. The crossing begins where the footprint comes to overlap the intersection.
'pedestrians' (DEF-NRS-484A-165: 'a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...') is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

'the official traffic-control devices' (DEF-NRS-484A-145: 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic', and traffic (DEF-NRS-484A-285) includes 'pedestrians') that regulate a pedestrian's crossing are pedestrian signal heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute when a timer is displayed'). 'pertaining to such crossing movements' ties the head to the crossing the words refer to ('such'): the diagonal crossing of the intersection the pedestrian enters. The head is tied to that intersection by dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself'), the intersection being re-bound in the obligation with the whole selection of s2 (st.intersection whose overlap by the subject's footprint, rel.occupies, rises at this observation, with every lane entering it, st.lane_enters, st.lane, crossed obliquely through drv.motion.moving_across_carrier). A head governing a different intersection, or none, does not pertain to the crossing. Among the heads governing that intersection, the one pertaining to the diagonal movement is the one the pedestrian faces across the crossing: its position (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') lies ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach; heads for the other crossings of the junction, beside or behind the pedestrian, are left out. dev.position is used as the head's location, not as a stop line or crossing, which its 'Not a stand-in for' clause excludes. 'in accordance with' is read through the indication shown when the crossing begins: walk, or a flashing indication with a countdown, accords; a steady don't-walk or a flashing one without countdown does not.

NRS_484B_287_1e.applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) beginning an authorized diagonal crossing: at this observation its footprint comes to overlap an intersection x (rel.occupies, st.intersection) that it did not overlap at the previous observation, its footprint overlaps a marked crosswalk (st.crosswalk, marked), and it moves diagonally across x: for every lane l with st.lane_enters(l, x) (at least one exists), drv_motion_moving_across_carrier(subject, l) holds with (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.crossing_motion_cos) and does not hold with (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.right_angle_crossing_cos). The duty does not apply where LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject.
NRS_484B_287_1e.obligation: For every intersection x re-bound with the whole selection of the applicability (rises(rel.occupies(subject, x)) at this observation; at least one lane l with st.lane_enters(l, x); for every lane l with st.lane_enters(l, x), drv_motion_moving_across_carrier(subject, l) with (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.crossing_motion_cos) and not with (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.right_angle_crossing_cos)), and for every pedestrian signal head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) with dev.governs(d, x) that the subject faces at this observation: d shows neither dont_walk_steady nor dont_walk_flashing without its countdown attribute. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from the subject's kin.position to d's dev.position and h the subject's kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where no head governing x is faced, compliant; where whether a faced head governs x is unobserved and its indication would forbid, unknown.

narrowings.why: 'official' is read through the presence of the signal head in the scene.

'the devices pertaining to such crossing movements' is read as the pedestrian signal heads that govern (dev.governs) the intersection whose diagonal crossing begins, and among them those the pedestrian faces across the crossing (ahead of it along its heading, within the facing cone and reach).

'cross only in accordance with the devices' is read at the start of the diagonal crossing (the entry into the intersection) through the indication of those heads: a steady don't-walk, or a flashing don't-walk with no countdown, forbids starting; conduct later in the crossing is not read, and devices other than pedestrian signal heads are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: At an intersection with a marked diagonal crosswalk, a pedestrian steps from the corner into the intersection walking north-east inside the marking while the pedestrian head governing that intersection, ahead of it 25 m away within the facing cone, shows dont_walk_steady.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same entry, while the faced head governing the intersection shows walk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian enters the intersection walking east, at right angles to the north-south lanes: no diagonal crossing begins.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same entry as forbid, but the state of the faced pedestrian head is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Same entry while the faced head governing the intersection shows dont_walk_flashing with its countdown displayed.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Same entry while the faced head governing the intersection shows dont_walk_flashing without a countdown.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: Same diagonal entry, but the scene has no pedestrian signal head at all.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: Same entry as forbid, and the faced head shows dont_walk_steady, but it is recorded as governing another intersection, not the one entered: it does not pertain to this crossing.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
may overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right only
under conditions permitting such movement in safety.

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'), claimed whole: DEF-NRS-484A-320 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exclusions classified by the run's reading. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency).

'overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right' is the act drv.interaction.overtake_pass_on_right(subject, b), 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b on b's right'; 'another vehicle' is b, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and not the subject. 'only' makes the act lawful only under the conditions of s3.

operationalizations.standard: under conditions permitting such movement in safety
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the movement is made in safety where, at every observation of the act, the subject is in contact (rel.contact) with no road user and no road user's closest approach to it under constant velocities (prim.closest_approach_within over p.conflict_horizon) comes closer than p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); the closest-approach distance is the measured magnitude the bound is compared with, so the verdict moves with how close the conflict is.

NRS_484B_210_2.applicability: The subject, of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, overtakes and passes on its right another road user b of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: drv.interaction.overtake_pass_on_right(subject, b) with p.overtake_window and p.overtake_same_direction_cos is recognized at the judged observation; b is quantified there, not a binder.
NRS_484B_210_2.obligation: For every b so selected, at every observation of the act within p.overtake_window behind the recognition, from the first observation after its beginning (the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with aligned headings) to its recognition, for every road user u other than the subject (b included): the subject is not in rel.contact with u, and it is not the case that prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u) over p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance. Otherwise the duty is violated. Surrogate: the verdict is evidence on the safety standard, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.

The catch-all 'conditions permitting such movement in safety' is read only through conflicts with road users: contact and closest approaches under constant velocities. Conditions of the road (surface, view) enter only through those conflicts.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on b's right and, while side by side, closes laterally on b so that their closest approach within p.conflict_horizon falls below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes b on b's right in the adjacent lane keeping its distance; no closest approach within p.conflict_horizon falls below p.conflict_centre_clearance and no contact occurs; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject follows b in the same lane at a steady gap and never passes it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject draws past b on its right, but the source observes no positions of road users (kin.position absent), so the relations the rule reads that are computed from positions (rel.bearing, rel.longitudinal_overlap, rel.contact) are unobserved too: whether a pass on the right occurred, and whether it was made without conflict, is unknown.

under_way.words: overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act lies after its beginning, the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction), and at or before its recognition, while the subject's velocity (kin.velocity), exceeding b's along the subject's own direction of travel, carries it up to and past b. These relations are computed from the two road users' kinematics, so the boundary reads their relative motion, never a place.

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind
param_proposals.source: overtaking-manoeuvre durations in naturalistic driving studies

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading angles in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique; FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design-vehicle dimensions

segmentation.text: Except as provided in NRS 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B]:
Between adjacent intersections
at which official traffic-control devices are in operation
pedestrians
shall not cross at any place
except in a marked crosswalk.

elements.justification: 'Intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105, 'The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of the roadways of two highways which join one another') is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet', alley junctions excluded as the definition's (3) excludes them. 'Adjacent intersections' are two intersections with none between them along the way; the pedestrian is between them where its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region c (st.travel_region) recorded as a directed approach to one of them, i1: st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end', the carrier being 'the stretch one direction of travel uses to reach one junction' — so nothing lies between c's stretch and i1 — and the other, i2 ≠ i1, is reached either through a second carrier the pedestrian also occupies that enters i2 (the opposing direction of a two-way way), or, where c is a lane (st.lane), through a lane that enters i2 and leads into c, directly or through one lane between (st.lane_connectivity, 'which lane a lane leads into'). The relation atoms tie both intersections to the pedestrian's own carriers; no distance stands for belonging. A pedestrian at either intersection is not between them: its footprint overlaps neither i1 nor i2, nor a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier it occupies (st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'). st.lane_enters is 'Not a stand-in for: ... the region a device governs', which v3 reads separately.

'Official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-145, 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'). The law's own words 'are in operation' qualify the devices and limit which members the duty reads: a device in operation is one that operates, displaying indications, so they leave out signs and markings, which are posted or painted but do not operate, and signal heads that are not operating — covered, dark, or inoperative. The members read are signal heads: dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {...}; uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered') with its uncovered attribute true and a state other than dark, and not dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'). The device is at the intersection where it governs it, dev.governs 'an intersection, read as control of the junction itself', or governs a carrier recorded as entering it (st.lane_enters), as the st.lane_enters contract directs: 'which intersection a device controls is read through both, or directly where the device governs the intersection'; dev.governs is 'Not a stand-in for: a position'. 'Official' is the device's legal status, read through its presence (observable_reading, status). Each of i1 and i2 must have such a device.

'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate as the index maps 'No pedestrian'.

To cross is to move across the way: drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, 'Road user a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r', with r the carrier c the pedestrian's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies, st.travel_region), as the index maps 'crossing a roadway' for LVMC_11_30_060_A. The concept 'says nothing of whether a occupies r', which rel.occupies supplies; a pedestrian at rest or walking along the carrier is not crossing, as the concept excludes.

'a marked crosswalk' is st.crosswalk with its marked attribute true ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute'), DEF-NRS-484A-065 (2) 'Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface'; 'in' it is rel.occupies of that crosswalk by the pedestrian, as the index maps 'except in a crosswalk'.

NRS_484B_287_1c.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian; neither LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 nor LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 applies to it (ruleApplies, subject mapped to subject; o1 applies at an observation at which, for some other road user of class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal, contact with the subject begins there, or their centre distance comes there to be at most p.blind_person_approach_reach having been above it at the previous observation while the subject is not at rest; o2 applies while the subject proceeds after having halted since such an event); and at the observation it is between adjacent controlled intersections: its footprint overlaps a travel region c (rel.occupies) recorded as entering an intersection i1 (st.lane_enters), and an intersection i2 other than i1 is found either because its footprint also overlaps a travel region recorded as entering i2, or because c is a lane and a lane that enters i2 leads into c (st.lane_connectivity) directly or through one lane between; each of i1 and i2 has a device in operation — a dev.traffic_signal that is uncovered, whose state is not dark and that is not dev.inoperative — that governs it (dev.governs) or governs a travel region recorded as entering it; and its footprint overlaps neither i1 nor i2 nor a crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of a carrier it occupies (st.entrance_of); and it is moving across c (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, c) with p.halt_speed_tolerance and p.crossing_motion_cos).
NRS_484B_287_1c.obligation: At that observation the subject's footprint overlaps a crosswalk (st.crosswalk) whose marked attribute is true (rel.occupies). Otherwise violated; where the crosswalk's occupancy or its marking is unobserved, unknown.

narrowings.why: 'official' is the devices' legal status, read through the presence of the signal heads.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Mid-block between two intersections each governed by an operating traffic signal, a pedestrian walks across both directional carriers of the roadway, outside any crosswalk.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Between the same two signalized intersections, a pedestrian walks across the roadway within a marked mid-block crosswalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks across a roadway mid-block between two intersections controlled only by stop signs, with no signal head at either.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses mid-block outside any crosswalk between two intersections with signal heads; which regions the signal heads govern is not observed on this source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian crosses at the unmarked crosswalk recorded as marking the entrance of the approach into a signalized intersection: it is at the intersection, not between.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian who is not blind walks across the roadway mid-block, outside any crosswalk, between two signalized intersections, toward a person carrying a white cane (class ru.pedestrian_with_white_cane_or_guide_animal) who at the first observations stands farther than p.blind_person_approach_reach (centre to centre) from it; the judged observation is the first at which the walking pedestrian's centre distance to the cane user is at most that reach, having been above it at the previous observation, so the approach event of LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 occurs there inside the recording and o1 applies to it at that observation.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: pedestrian crossing-path geometry

segmentation.text: When two vehicles
enter an intersection
from different highways
at approximately the same time,
the driver of the vehicle on the left
shall yield
the right-of-way
to the vehicle on the right.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: 'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'): the subject and the other vehicle v both.

Two vehicles 'enter' at approximately the same time when they reach its entrance together: a vehicle that yields at the edge never enters together with the other, so the entering the words time is each vehicle's arrival at X — occupying a carrier entering X (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), its body comes within the stop-point tolerance of X, the bound within which a vehicle is at a mark (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)'). Not a stand-in for occupancy: the distance reads arrival at the edge, the carrier fixes which intersection.

'From different highways' (DEF-NRS-484A-095): the two approach carriers c1, c2 (st.lane_enters) lie on ways (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') such that c2 lies on a highway on which c1 does not lie.
The subject is the vehicle on the left: the other vehicle lies on its right, rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of" ...)'. 'Driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.
Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) while v is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact).
'The vehicle on the right': v of the admitted aggregate whose bearing in the subject's frame (rel.bearing) has a negative lateral component (to the right) at the later of the two arrivals.

Same mapping as 'or at a traffic-controlled intersection' in the index: a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering X (dev.governs; DEF-NRS-484A-145 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic').

Per rel.oncoming's not-a-stand-in clause, the direction a road user approaches from is read through its approach carrier and that carrier's st.lane_direction: c1 and c2 have designated directions opposed within p.oncoming_heading_cos.

'Is making a left turn': the vehicle's heading change since its entry into X (rel.occupies), integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('positive when the heading turns to the left'), lies to the left between p.turn_heading_min and p.u_turn_heading_min.

operationalizations.standard: approximately the same time: the two arrivals at the intersection's edge are close enough in time that neither vehicle can clear before the other arrives
operationalizations.convention: arrival of each vehicle is the observation (kin.time) at which its body first comes within p.stop_point_tolerance of X on a carrier entering X; the two arrivals are at approximately the same time where their times differ by no more than p.same_time_arrival_window, a two-second headway

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

NRS_484B_250_2.applicability: At every observation at which the subject has arrived at an intersection X — its arrival: the latest observation at which, occupying a carrier c1 with st.lane_enters(c1, X), its body came within p.stop_point_tolerance of X (st.region_geometry distance) having not been within it at the observation before — and has occupied c1 or X at every observation since; except where X is controlled (a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering X), and except where NRS_484B_250_4_o1 or NRS_484B_250_4_o2 (binder subject ↦ subject) applies to the subject.
NRS_484B_250_2.obligation: Re-binding c1 and X as in the applicability: for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that arrived at X in the same way on a carrier c2 entering X, c2 lying on a highway (st.on_way) on which c1 does not lie, with the two arrivals no more than p.same_time_arrival_window apart (time since each arrival), v lying on the subject's right at the later of the two arrivals (rel.bearing lateral component negative), and v occupying c2 or X at every observation since its arrival — excepting the pair where c1's and c2's designated directions have a dot product below minus p.oncoming_heading_cos and the subject or v declares int.left_turn at X at this observation or v's heading change since its latest entry into X (heading-since over kin.yaw_rate, step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is a left turn of at least p.turn_heading_min and below p.u_turn_heading_min: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'official' is a legal status; the device present and governing is its evidence.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled X. The subject on c1 and v on c2 (on another highway) arrive within p.same_time_arrival_window of each other; v lies to the subject's right (rel.bearing). The subject proceeds with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance and its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same arrivals; the subject comes to rest at X's edge until v has crossed, then proceeds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A dev.yield_sign governs c1: X is controlled.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled X; simultaneous arrivals from different highways with v on the subject's right; the subject and v are not in contact and their centres' closest approach lies within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance; kin.speed is not observed, so whether the subject proceeds rather than holding at rest is unknown. (rel.bearing is computed from positions and headings and is not a mask that can blank which vehicle is on the right.)

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Simultaneous arrivals; v lies to the subject's left; the subject proceeds first in conflict with v: no vehicle on its right is owed the right-of-way.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: v on the subject's right arrives several times p.same_time_arrival_window after the subject; the subject proceeds: not approximately the same time.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The subject arrives at uncontrolled X with no other road user in the scene.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer
or a traffic-control signal:
The driver of a vehicle
shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or yield in compliance with a yield sign,
in compliance with the manner prescribed in subsection 1 [NRS-484B-257-1],
prior to entering an intersection
if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto
although not a part of a through highway
and shall proceed cautiously,
yielding
to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield
and which are within the intersection
or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, of which the subject is a member; 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction of role police_officer ('a person directing traffic') governing (dev.governs) the subject's approach carrier c or X (st.travel_region), read at the subject's entry.
A dev.traffic_signal governing c or X (dev.governs) that is not dev.inoperative ('installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'), read at the subject's entry.
Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Stop' is DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement' (drv.motion.complete_halt); 'in obedience to a stop sign' ties the halt to a dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') governing (dev.governs) the subject's approach carrier c or X. 'Yield in compliance with a yield sign' (dev.yield_sign, 'regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt'), in the manner subsection 1 prescribes ('in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped'), is the subject's kin.speed within the place's stopping zone at or below the speed from which it still halts at the place (p.yield_line_speed_max), a halt included. The act is owed at the place that manner names, which the act's own atoms read: the st.stop_line marking c (st.entrance_of), else the st.crosswalk marking c, else c's entrance end, the side along c's direction (st.lane_direction) given by prim.region_offset_along, the body-to-mark distance by st.region_geometry, the subject on c by rel.occupies.

'Prior to entering an intersection': the act is owed before the subject's entry into X - the observation at which its footprint comes to overlap X (rel.occupies), having occupied at the previous observation a carrier c entering X (st.lane_enters, st.travel_region).

'A stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto': a dev.stop_sign or dev.yield_sign governs (dev.governs) an approach carrier of X (st.lane_enters) or X; the sign the subject obeys is the one governing its own entrance c, which it occupies (rel.occupies).

residues.why: 'although' is concessive: the duty reaches signed entrances whether or not the intersection is part of a through highway, and the stop or yield owed at a signed entrance is the same in both cases (subsection 1 states the same act where it is part of one); the words withhold the duty nowhere.

NRS_484B_257_2_o1.applicability: At the subject's entry into an intersection X: the observation at which its footprint overlaps X and did not at the previous observation, where at that previous observation it occupied a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, X); where at the entry observation a stop sign or a yield sign governs c or X (dev.governs); except where at that observation a police officer's direction (dev.human_direction of role police_officer) governs c or X, or a traffic signal that is not inoperative governs c or X.
NRS_484B_257_2_o1.obligation: NRS_484B_257_1_o1 (binder subject to subject) is complied with at the entry - the manner subsection 1 prescribes - and the act it states is found on the approach: where a stop sign governs c or X, a complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance); where only a yield sign does, an observation at which kin.speed is at or below p.yield_line_speed_max (a halt included); in either case while occupying c within the stopping zone of the place for c, in subsection 1's order: (1) a stop line marking c's entrance (st.entrance_of), the line ahead of or at the reference point along c's direction (prim.region_offset_along at or above zero), the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of it; (2) where no stop line marks c (entrance lists observed and excluding c), the crosswalk marking c's entrance ahead, not overlapped, the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of it; (3) where neither marks c, the footprint outside X and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of X. History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start - the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the place marks, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it along c's direction and farther than p.stop_point_tolerance; where several marks of that kind mark c, outside and short of each) - or at the subject's previous entry into X, whichever is later. Act found: compliant; either end reached without it: violated; neither end reached (the recording begins inside the zone): unknown. Each entry owes its own act; only an observed exit from the zone upstream begins a new approach. The entry is unknown where the previous observation does not show the subject on a mapped carrier; where a mark's association with c is unobserved and the verdict turns on it, unknown. No bound is taken from the recording's start, a first observation or a cumulative distance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.stop_sign governs carrier c entering X; a st.stop_line marks c; no officer or operating signal. The subject passes the line and enters X with kin.speed well above p.halt_speed_tolerance, never halting since it was upstream of the line's stopping zone.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject halts on c with the line just ahead within p.stop_point_tolerance, then enters X.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No stop or yield sign governs c or X; the subject enters X without halting.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Stop sign governing c; kin.speed is absent, so whether the subject halted is unknown.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: Stop sign governing c; the recording begins with the subject already within p.stop_point_tolerance of the stop line, moving slowly; no halt is recorded before its entry into X.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start: the subject's last observation outside the stop line's stopping zone upstream on c lies before the recording

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Only a dev.yield_sign governs c; no stop line or crosswalk marks c; the subject reaches X's edge at kin.speed at or below p.yield_line_speed_max and enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs c, but an operating dev.traffic_signal (circular_red) also governs c at the subject's entry.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: MUTCD stop line placement in advance of a crosswalk

param_proposals.name: p.yield_line_speed_max
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle at the place of a yield sign counts as having slowed: the speed from which a passenger car can still halt within the stop-point tolerance at a comfortable deceleration of about 4.5 m/s^2
param_proposals.source: AASHTO comfortable deceleration rate of the stopping sight distance model

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not overtake and pass another vehicle traveling in the same direction
in an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone
except:
(a) On a day on which the school is not in session;
(b) During the period from a half hour after school is no longer in operation to a half hour before school is next in operation;
(c) If the zone is designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the hours when the pupils of the school are in class
and the yellow lights of the speed limit beacon are not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect;
or (d) If the zone is not designated by an operational speed limit beacon,
during the times when the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect.

As used in this section, “speed limit beacon” means a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit in a school zone or school crossing zone is in effect.

elements.justification: ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'. The definitions table admits DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle for 'vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, except: (1) Devices moved by human power ...'); claimed as the aggregate, never expanded. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency); the aggregate carries only the class.

drv.interaction.overtake_pass: 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it', recognized when b comes to be behind a after b was ahead with headings aligned within same_dir_cos. 'overtake and pass another vehicle traveling in the same direction' is that act with a the subject and b any other road user of the scene that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the admitted aggregate of 'vehicle', 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'); the concept's aligned headings carry 'in the same direction'. The concept 'says nothing ... of whether b moves', so 'traveling' is carried beside it: b's kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance at some observation while the pass is under way, so a pass of a vehicle at rest throughout is not this duty. b is quantified in the rule, not a binder. The concept reads kin.position, kin.heading and rel.longitudinal_overlap ('Where the positions of a and b are unobserved, it is unknown'); its call is expanded, so those atoms count as the rule's.

dev.zone_sign: 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind ∈ {school, school_crossing, ...}; end attribute'. Ontology §9: 'Where the same category is also marked on the road by a sign (dev.zone_sign), the sign is the atom and the category is not.' The school zone (DEF-NRS-484B-063: 'those sections of streets which are adjacent to school property') and the school crossing zone (DEF-NRS-484B-060: 'those sections of streets not adjacent to school property that pupils cross while following a designated walking route to school') are those categories; the area designated as either is the stretch a zone sign z of kind school or school_crossing, not an end sign, governs (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', over st.travel_region); the pass is made in it where, while the pass is under way, the subject's footprint overlaps such a region r (rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold', read only in exception (d); dev.governs is 'not a stand-in for a position'. 'designated' is read by the sign's presence (observable_reading status).

dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect', the device the section defines (s12). The zone is designated by a beacon b where b governs the zone's region r (dev.governs over st.travel_region). 'operational' is read as b not inoperative: dev.inoperative, 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', applies to the beacon's head of lamps. dev.governs is not a stand-in for a position.

dev.speed_limit_beacon carries a 'flashing attribute': its lamps flash 'alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. 'not flashing in the manner which indicates that the speed limit is in effect' is that attribute false for every operational beacon that governs r.

The negation of s7: no dev.speed_limit_beacon ('a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign') that governs r (dev.governs, over st.travel_region) is present and not inoperative (dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication').

dev.zone_sign's 'conditions attribute: a structured reading of the sign's legend' and prim.conditions_hold: 'the structured conditions of a device (dev.zone_sign, dev.regulatory_sign) hold at the observation for a road user'. 'the sign designating the school zone or school crossing zone indicates that the speed limit is not in effect' is prim.conditions_hold false for z, the sign of s3, and the subject. dev.zone_sign is 'not a stand-in for whether the condition holds now — that is prim.conditions_hold'; env.civil_time is the primitive's own input.

The section's definition of 'speed limit beacon' ('a device which is used in conjunction with a sign and equipped with two or more yellow lights that flash alternately to indicate when the speed limit ... is in effect') is the contract of dev.speed_limit_beacon: 'a pair or more of yellow lamps mounted with a speed sign, flashing alternately when the sign's limit is in effect'. It adds no condition beyond the atom's.

assumptions.meaning: the date of the observation is a day on which the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place is in session, as the reading declares from that school's calendar

the time of the observation lies in the period from a half hour after the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place ceased operation to a half hour before that school next begins operation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule
the pupils of the school served by the signed zone at the road user's place are in class at the time of the observation, as the reading declares from that school's schedule

NRS_484B_363_4.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). For each other road user b of the scene that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; same(b, subject) excluded), the pass of b is the act drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b; window p.overtake_window, same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos), recognized at the observation at which it holds; it is under way from the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, rel.same_direction within p.overtake_same_direction_cos) up to the recognition. The duty applies to that pass where b's kin.speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance at some observation while the pass is under way, and where, at some observation while the pass is under way, the subject's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a travel region r governed (dev.governs) by a dev.zone_sign z of kind school or school_crossing, not an end sign, and, for that z and r, none of the exceptions holds at every observation while the pass is under way: (a) asm.school_in_session_day is false; (b) asm.school_outside_operation_margin holds; (c) some dev.speed_limit_beacon governs r and is not dev.inoperative, asm.pupils_in_class holds, and no beacon that governs r and is not inoperative is flashing; (d) no beacon that governs r is present and not inoperative, and prim.conditions_hold for z and the subject is false. With no other vehicle in the scene the duty is met.
NRS_484B_363_4.obligation: For every such b, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b) with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos does not hold at the judged observation: a recognized pass of a travelling vehicle in the zone violates the duty. Where the window behind is truncated, or the overlap of the two bodies' projections (rel.longitudinal_overlap) or the positions of the subject or b are unobserved, the pass and its occasion are unknown.

narrowings.why: 'driver' and 'overtake' are read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
'designated' is the legal status of the zone: the zone sign governing the subject's region is the evidence.

under_way.words: from the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the moving subject with headings aligned, up to the recognition
under_way.justification: drv.interaction.overtake_pass: 'The act begins at the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of a with their headings aligned within same_dir_cos (rel.same_direction)', where 'b is ahead of a where the longitudinal component of b's bearing in a's frame (rel.bearing) is positive and the two bodies' projections on a's heading share no length (rel.longitudinal_overlap negative)'. The pass is under way from that observation to the recognition, while the subject moves (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity', above p.halt_speed_tolerance) and closes on b; the subject's motion and the relations it changes tell an observation inside the pass from one before it began, where the subject occupied the same lane, so no region alone could.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle, on a lane governed by a dev.zone_sign of kind school_crossing (not an end sign, conditions holding), comes up behind another moving vehicle with aligned headings and comes to have it behind (rel.bearing longitudinal negative, no overlap); asm.school_in_session_day true, asm.school_outside_operation_margin false; no beacon governs the lane. The recording begins well over p.overtake_window before the recognition.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same zone and declarations as forbid; the subject is the only vehicle in the scene and travels through the zone: no pass is recognized.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes another moving vehicle on a street no dev.zone_sign of kind school or school_crossing governs.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid, the recording beginning well over p.overtake_window before the pass and every position, heading, speed, bearing and occupancy observed, but the source declares rel.longitudinal_overlap absent: whether b was ahead of the subject and whether it comes to be behind it, which the pass concept reads through the overlap of the two bodies' projections, is not decided, so whether a pass of a travelling vehicle is made in the zone is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid, but the other vehicle is at rest (kin.speed at or below the halt tolerance) at every observation while the pass is under way: it is not a vehicle traveling.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: No beacon governs the zone's lane; prim.conditions_hold is false for the zone sign throughout the pass: exception (d) holds.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: An operational beacon governs the zone's lane and is not flashing; asm.pupils_in_class true throughout the pass: exception (c) holds.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3
scenarios.narrative: The pass begins while the subject's footprint overlaps a lane the school zone sign governs and is recognized after the subject has left the zone; no exception holds.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the zone's lane only before the pass begins (the other vehicle is not yet ahead with aligned headings), leaves the zone, and the whole pass takes place on regions no zone sign governs.

scenarios.name: occasion_s7
scenarios.narrative: A beacon governing the lane, not flashing, with asm.pupils_in_class true, is operational at the first observations of the pass and inoperative at the later ones, while the zone sign's conditions hold: neither (c) nor (d) holds throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s7_outside
scenarios.narrative: The beacon is inoperative before the pass begins and operational, not flashing, at every observation while it is under way, with asm.pupils_in_class true: exception (c) holds throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s9
scenarios.narrative: An operational beacon governs the lane with asm.pupils_in_class true; it is not flashing at the first observations of the pass and flashing at the later ones; no other exception holds.

scenarios.name: occasion_s9_outside
scenarios.narrative: The operational beacon is flashing before the pass begins and not flashing at every observation while it is under way, with asm.pupils_in_class true: exception (c) holds throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s10
scenarios.narrative: The beacon governing the lane is inoperative at the first observations of the pass and operational and flashing at the later ones; the zone sign's conditions do not hold throughout: neither (c) nor (d) holds throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s10_outside
scenarios.narrative: The beacon governing the lane is operational before the pass begins and inoperative at every observation while it is under way; prim.conditions_hold is false for the zone sign throughout: exception (d) holds throughout.

scenarios.name: occasion_s11
scenarios.narrative: No beacon governs the lane; prim.conditions_hold for the zone sign is false at the first observations of the pass and true at the later ones.

scenarios.name: occasion_s11_outside
scenarios.narrative: No beacon governs the lane; prim.conditions_hold is true before the pass begins and false at every observation while it is under way: exception (d) holds throughout.

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer,
a pedestrian
may not proceed to cross the highway,
but a pedestrian
who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1)
may continue to cross the highway
but must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone if one is provided or other place of safety before the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and steady.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute'). The signal that indicates to a pedestrian is the head that governs the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', traffic including pedestrians by DEF-NRS-484A-285; kinds st.roadway, st.lane) and that the pedestrian faces: dev.position ('location of the device head') ahead of kin.position along kin.heading ('direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is not used as a stop line or crossing.
'illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with no countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Entering the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) borrows (1)'s words: 'While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'. It is the pedestrian's latest step from a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) onto the roadway or lane r (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) made while the head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) governing r (dev.governs) showed walk and the pedestrian faced d (dev.position ahead of kin.position along kin.heading within the cone and reach).
Continuing to cross under this indication is the pedestrian's footprint still overlapping r (rel.occupies) at some observation while d shows the flashing indication without countdown.

Proceeding to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone or other place of safety is having left the roadway or lane crossed: the pedestrian's footprint no longer overlaps r (rel.occupies). Each place the words list (the curb's sidewalk, a safety zone, a median) lies off r. 'before the ... indication ... is illuminated and steady' fixes the moment: the observation at which d shows dont_walk_steady, having shown dont_walk_flashing without countdown at the previous one.

compositions.why: It borrows the circumstances of subparagraph (1)'s permission — the walk indication illuminated, the pedestrian facing the signal, proceeding across the highway in its direction — to qualify how the pedestrian entered. Subparagraph (1)'s rule is a duty on drivers to give the right-of-way; whether that duty applied to some vehicle, held, or was complied with says nothing of how this pedestrian entered, so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.
compositions.quote: While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

NRS_484B_283_1d3_o2.applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, with no vehicle v of the scene engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. The judged observation is the onset of the steady indication of a pedestrian head d governing (dev.governs) a roadway or lane r: d shows dont_walk_steady here and showed dont_walk_flashing without countdown at the previous observation. The subject's latest step from a sidewalk onto r (history bound: that step, searched back without other limit) was made while d showed walk and the subject faced d; and the subject's footprint overlapped r at some observation since d last began showing dont_walk_flashing without countdown. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where that step lies before the recording, applicability is unknown.
NRS_484B_283_1d3_o2.obligation: At the onset of the steady indication the subject's footprint does not overlap r (rel.occupies): it has reached a place of safety off the roadway.

narrowings.why: 'a curb, sidewalk, safety zone ... or other place of safety' is read as any place off the roadway or lane the head governs; the kind of place reached is not checked.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps from the sidewalk onto r facing d while d shows walk; d turns dont_walk_flashing without countdown while it is mid-crossing, then dont_walk_steady while it is still on r.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but the pedestrian reaches the far sidewalk, off r, before d turns steady.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian stepped onto r while d already showed dont_walk_flashing without countdown (no lawful entry under subparagraph (1)).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid but d's state is not observed.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the pedestrian already on r while d shows dont_walk_flashing without countdown; d turns steady while it is still on r; its step onto r is not recorded.
scenarios.boundary: the pedestrian's step from the sidewalk onto r, which lies before the recording

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated,
pedestrians facing the signal
may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal
and must be given
the right-of-way
by the drivers of all vehicles.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}'); 'in place' is a head present in the scene. 'such signals' regulate the crossing of the roadway they control: dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ... roadway'), traffic including pedestrians (DEF-NRS-484A-285: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles'), ties the head to the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (kinds st.roadway, st.lane). dev.governs is not used as a position.
'the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated' is the head's state walk (dev.pedestrian_signal state 'walk').

'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'facing the signal': the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') lies ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along the direction its body points (kin.heading, 'direction the body points'), within a cone and a reach. dev.position is used as the head's location, not as the place of a stop line or crossing, which its exclusion names.

'may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal' identifies the pedestrians the right-of-way is owed to: those on the roadway the head governs (rel.occupies of a st.roadway or st.lane region that head governs), facing the head, so moving toward it across the way. The highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines') is crossed by traversing its roadway; the sidewalk the words of the sibling subparagraphs call a place of safety is no part of the crossing.

Giving the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another') is observed as the vehicle not reaching the pedestrian (no rel.contact) with its speed (kin.speed) bounded as the standard sets, as the index maps 'Yield'.
'the drivers of all vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence where the two approach 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves (speed above the halt tolerance), a predicted closest approach of the two centres within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance is a danger of a crash in which the vehicle has not granted precedence

NRS_484B_283_1d1.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), not engaged by LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. There are a pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), a pedestrian signal head d showing walk, and a roadway or lane r governed by d (dev.governs), with p's footprint overlapping r (rel.occupies), p facing d, and p not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A or LVMC_11_30_060_B. p faces d where, with Δ the vector from p's kin.position to d's dev.position and h p's kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach².
NRS_484B_283_1d1.obligation: For every such pedestrian p: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and where the subject's speed (kin.speed) is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, it is not the case that the closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: 'the drivers' is read through the vehicles' controlled motion: the duty binds each vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
