segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer,
a pedestrian
may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal,
but must complete the crossing before the countdown timer gets to zero.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute when a timer is displayed'); 'such signals' regulate the crossing of the roadway they control, read through dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ... roadway'; traffic includes pedestrians, DEF-NRS-484A-285) on a roadway or lane (kinds st.roadway, st.lane).

'“Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

The pedestrian who proceeds across the highway under this indication is one whose footprint came onto the governed roadway or lane (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) while the head showed it, facing the head: the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head') ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach — the direction of the signal. dev.position is not used as a crossing or a stop line.

Completing the crossing is having left the roadway or lane crossed: the pedestrian's footprint no longer overlaps it (rel.occupies). The countdown timer gets to zero at the end of the flashing interval it times, where the head stops showing the flashing indication with a countdown and shows dont_walk_steady (dev.pedestrian_signal states dont_walk_flashing with countdown, then dont_walk_steady).

NRS_484B_283_1d2.applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, with no vehicle v of the scene engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. The judged observation is the countdown's end for a pedestrian head d governing (dev.governs) a roadway or lane r: d shows dont_walk_steady here and showed dont_walk_flashing with its countdown at the previous observation. The subject's latest entry onto r (the latest earlier observation at which its footprint came to overlap r, not overlapping it at the observation before; history bound: that entry, searched back without other limit) was made while d showed dont_walk_flashing with its countdown and the subject faced d, and d showed dont_walk_flashing with countdown at every observation from that entry to the previous one. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where the entry lies before the recording, applicability is unknown.
NRS_484B_283_1d2.obligation: At the countdown's end the subject's footprint does not overlap r (rel.occupies): it has completed the crossing.

narrowings.why: the countdown's reaching zero is read as the head's change from the flashing indication with countdown to the steady indication, which ends the interval the timer counts; the timer's displayed number is not read.
'complete the crossing' is read as the pedestrian's footprint having left the roadway or lane governed by the head; a pedestrian on a median or safety zone between roadways has left it.

scenarios.boundary: the pedestrian's entry onto r, which lies before the recording

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer,
a pedestrian
may not proceed to cross the highway,
but a pedestrian
who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1)
may continue to cross the highway
but must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone if one is provided or other place of safety before the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and steady.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute'). The signal that indicates to a pedestrian ('such signals') is the head that governs the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', traffic including pedestrians by DEF-NRS-484A-285; kinds st.roadway, st.lane) and that the pedestrian faces: the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head') ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is not used as a stop line or crossing.
'illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with no countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Proceeding to cross the highway is coming onto the roadway or lane the head governs: the pedestrian's footprint comes to overlap it (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane). The highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095) includes the sidewalk, but the sibling words 'must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone' place the sidewalk outside the crossing, so the crossing begins on the roadway.
'a pedestrian' (the one excepted) is the same admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Entering the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) borrows (1)'s words: 'While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'. It is the pedestrian's latest step from a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) onto a roadway or lane (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) made while a pedestrian head (dev.pedestrian_signal) governing that roadway or lane (dev.governs) showed walk and the pedestrian faced it (dev.position ahead of kin.position along kin.heading within the cone and reach).
Continuing to cross is not having returned to a sidewalk (rel.occupies of st.sidewalk) since that entry: the pedestrian is still in the crossing it began.

compositions.why: It borrows the circumstances of subparagraph (1)'s permission — the walk indication illuminated, the pedestrian facing the signal, proceeding across the highway in its direction — to qualify how the pedestrian entered. Subparagraph (1)'s rule is a duty on drivers to give the right-of-way; whether that duty applied to some vehicle, held, or was complied with says nothing of how this pedestrian entered, so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.
compositions.quote: While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

NRS_484B_283_1d3_o1.applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, with no vehicle v of the scene engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. There are a pedestrian head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) showing dont_walk_flashing without its countdown attribute and a roadway or lane r governed by d (dev.governs), the subject faces d, and the subject's footprint did not overlap r at the previous observation. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Excepted: the subject is continuing a crossing it began lawfully under subparagraph (1) — its latest step from a sidewalk onto a roadway or lane was made while a pedestrian head governing that roadway or lane showed walk and the subject faced that head, and its footprint has overlapped no sidewalk since.
NRS_484B_283_1d3_o1.obligation: The subject's footprint does not overlap r at this observation: it has not proceeded onto the roadway.

narrowings.why: 'proceed to cross the highway' is read as the pedestrian's footprint coming onto the roadway or lane the faced head governs; walking on the sidewalk is not crossing.

While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and steady
a pedestrian
may not proceed to cross the highway,
but a pedestrian
who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) or (2)
may continue to cross the highway
but must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone if one is provided or other place of safety
as soon as possible.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute'). The signal that indicates to a pedestrian is the head that governs the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', traffic including pedestrians by DEF-NRS-484A-285; kinds st.roadway, st.lane) and that the pedestrian faced when it stepped onto it: dev.position ('location of the device head') ahead of kin.position along kin.heading ('direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is not used as a stop line or crossing.
'illuminated and steady' is the head's state dont_walk_steady.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Entering the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) or (2) borrows their words: (1) 'While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'; (2) 'While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'. It is the pedestrian's latest step from a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) onto the roadway or lane r (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) made while the head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) governing r (dev.governs) showed walk, or dont_walk_flashing with its countdown, and the pedestrian faced d (dev.position ahead of kin.position along kin.heading within the cone and reach).
Continuing to cross is the pedestrian's footprint still overlapping r (rel.occupies) while d shows the steady indication.

Proceeding to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone or other place of safety is moving off the roadway or lane crossed: while the footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies), the pedestrian moves (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity'), at the pace the standard bounds. kin.speed is used as the magnitude of motion, not as acceleration.

operationalizations.standard: as soon as possible
operationalizations.convention: pedestrian clearance walking speed: a pedestrian still on the roadway after the steady indication proceeds as soon as possible where its speed is at least a floor well below the slow walking speed the clearance interval is timed for; lingering or halting on the roadway is below it

compositions.why: It borrows the circumstances of subparagraph (1)'s permission — the walk indication illuminated, the pedestrian facing the signal, proceeding across the highway in its direction — to qualify how the pedestrian entered. Subparagraph (1)'s rule is a duty on drivers to give the right-of-way; whether that duty applied to some vehicle, held, or was complied with says nothing of how this pedestrian entered, so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.
compositions.quote: While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

compositions.why: It borrows the circumstances of subparagraph (2)'s permission — the flashing don't-walk indication accompanied by a countdown timer, the pedestrian proceeding across the highway in the direction of the signal — to qualify how the pedestrian entered. Subparagraph (2)'s rule is the duty to complete the crossing before the countdown ends; lawful entry under (2) does not depend on that later duty being complied with (the entry precedes it), so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.
compositions.quote: While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

There are a pedestrian head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) showing dont_walk_steady and a roadway or lane r governed by d (dev.governs) such that the subject's footprint overlaps r here and the subject's latest step from a sidewalk onto r (history bound: that step, searched back without other limit) was made while d showed walk, or dont_walk_flashing with its countdown, and the subject faced d. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where that step lies before the recording, applicability is unknown.
NRS_484B_283_1d4_o2.obligation: The subject's speed (kin.speed) is at least p.pedestrian_clearing_speed_min: it keeps moving off the roadway rather than lingering on it.

narrowings.why: 'proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone ... or other place of safety' is read through the pedestrian's motion while still on the roadway; the direction it moves in (forward or back to the curb it left) is not read, and the kind of place reached is not checked.
'as soon as possible' is read as a speed floor at every observation on the roadway after the steady indication; the pedestrian's own ability (a slower walker) is not measured.

The signal that indicates to a pedestrian is the head that governs the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', traffic including pedestrians by DEF-NRS-484A-285; kinds st.roadway, st.lane) and that the pedestrian faces: dev.position ('location of the device head') ahead of kin.position along kin.heading ('direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is not used as a stop line or crossing.
'illuminated and steady' is the head's state dont_walk_steady.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Proceeding to cross the highway is coming onto the roadway or lane the head governs: the pedestrian's footprint comes to overlap it (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane). The highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095) includes the sidewalk, but the sibling words 'must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone' place the sidewalk outside the crossing, so the crossing begins on the roadway.
'a pedestrian' (the one excepted) is the same admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Entering the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) or (2) borrows their words: (1) 'While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'; (2) 'While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'. It is the pedestrian's latest step from a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) onto a roadway or lane (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) made while a pedestrian head (dev.pedestrian_signal) governing it (dev.governs) showed walk, or dont_walk_flashing with its countdown, and the pedestrian faced that head (dev.position ahead of kin.position along kin.heading within the cone and reach).
Continuing to cross is not having returned to a sidewalk (rel.occupies of st.sidewalk) since that entry.

compositions.why: It borrows the circumstances of subparagraph (1)'s permission — the walk indication illuminated, the pedestrian facing the signal, proceeding across the highway in its direction — to qualify how the pedestrian entered. Subparagraph (1)'s rule is a duty on drivers to give the right-of-way; whether that duty applied to some vehicle, held, or was complied with says nothing of how this pedestrian entered, so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.
compositions.quote: While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

compositions.why: It borrows the circumstances of subparagraph (2)'s permission — the flashing don't-walk indication accompanied by a countdown timer, the pedestrian proceeding across the highway in the direction of the signal — to qualify how the pedestrian entered. Subparagraph (2)'s rule is the duty to complete the crossing before the countdown ends; lawful entry under (2) does not depend on that later duty being complied with (the entry precedes it), so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.
compositions.quote: While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

NRS_484B_283_1d4_o1.applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, with no vehicle v of the scene engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. There are a pedestrian head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) showing dont_walk_steady and a roadway or lane r governed by d (dev.governs), the subject faces d, and the subject's footprint did not overlap r at the previous observation. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Excepted: the subject is continuing a crossing it began lawfully under subparagraph (1) or (2) — its latest step from a sidewalk onto a roadway or lane was made while a pedestrian head governing that roadway or lane showed walk, or dont_walk_flashing with its countdown, and the subject faced that head, and its footprint has overlapped no sidewalk since.
NRS_484B_283_1d4_o1.obligation: The subject's footprint does not overlap r at this observation: it has not proceeded onto the roadway.

narrowings.why: 'proceed to cross the highway' is read as the pedestrian's footprint coming onto the roadway or lane the faced head governs; walking on the sidewalk is not crossing.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: At the curb, the pedestrian faces a head 15 m away across roadway r that governs r and shows dont_walk_steady; at the next observation its footprint overlaps r.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same head and state; the pedestrian waits on the sidewalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The faced head shows walk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps onto r facing the head, but the head's state is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian stepped onto the first roadway while its head showed dont_walk_flashing with countdown, reached the median, and now steps onto the second roadway r while its faced head shows dont_walk_steady: it is continuing a lawful crossing.

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a pedestrian signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08 (pedestrian signal heads placed at the far end of the crossing, in the pedestrian's line of sight)

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a pedestrian signal head at which the head counts as the one across the crossing the pedestrian faces: a wide urban crossing (six lanes and a median, about 30 m) plus the head's set-back behind the far curb
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08; AASHTO Green Book urban cross-section widths

segmentation.text: Every person operating a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
upon a roadway shall, except:
(a) When traveling at a lawful rate of speed
commensurate with the speed of
any nearby traffic;
(b) When preparing to turn left;
or
(c) When doing so would not be safe,
ride as near to the right side of the roadway
as practicable,
exercising due care
when passing a standing vehicle or one proceeding in the same direction.

For purposes of paragraph (c) of subsection 1, the conditions under which it is not safe to operate a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter as near to the right side of the roadway as practicable include, without limitation:
(a) When fixed or moving objects, parked or moving vehicles, bicycles, pedestrians, animals or surface hazards impede access to the right side of the roadway.
(b) When a lane is too narrow for a bicycle and a vehicle to travel safely side by side within the lane.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregates of the three defined terms, each claimed as one ru.aggregate atom ('membership of a legal aggregate'), never expanded into classes; 'person operating' is read through the device's controlled motion (agency reading), not as a role atom, which the aggregate's 'not a stand-in for' clause excludes.

'upon a roadway': st.roadway is 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', the extent of DEF-NRS-484A-220 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder'; rel.occupies anchors the subject ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'), as the index maps 'upon a roadway shall, except:' (NRS_484B_777_1_o2). 'shall, except:' introduces the exceptions of this roadway duty, and the exceptions are read of the subject as it is upon that roadway. Exception (b) excuses the rider of this roadway who is preparing to turn left off it; a left turn off a roadway is made where that way meets another way, and such a place lies on the way the roadway belongs to: st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet'), which by st.on_way's contract 'lies on every way that meets there', and st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'), each tied to the subject as a region lying (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway its kind) on a highway on which a roadway the subject occupies lies. This is the referent of the words (the turn the rider upon this roadway prepares), not a place the words leave out: every intersection or entrance at which a rider can turn left off the roadway it is upon lies on that roadway's highway.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'), one ru.aggregate atom. 'any nearby traffic' is every road user of that aggregate, other than the subject, whose body gap to the subject (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') is within the nearby reach, whatever its direction of travel; where none is nearby the comparison holds vacuously ('any'). surface_gap is the body gap itself, not a centre distance.

The right side of the roadway is its right edge: st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway', lying on the same highway (st.on_way: 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway its kind) as the roadway the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.roadway). Nearness is the gap between the subject's body and that edge: prim.region_lateral_offset is 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', negative for an edge on the right, less half the subject's width from kin.extent ('a formula reads the full length, width and height'); st.region_geometry carries the edge's outline the primitive reads, and its 'not a stand-in for occupancy' clause does not apply, occupancy being read by rel.occupies.

Things that impede access to the right side: 'fixed or moving objects', 'animals' and 'surface hazards' are st.obstruction, 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user; kind in {debris, excavation, hose, barrier, stalled_vehicle_wreckage, sidewalk_fixture, mail_drop_box, other}' (an animal that is not ridden or herded is such an object, kind other); 'parked or moving vehicles', 'bicycles' and 'pedestrians' are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle and DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, whatever their motion. Impeding access is the thing lying in the rider's way on its right side: for an object, ahead of the subject along the designated direction of the roadway it occupies within the reach (prim.region_offset_along, 'the signed distance (m) from a road user's reference point to a structure region ... measured along a carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction)', from zero to the reach) and at or to the right of the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset at or below zero), its outline being st.region_geometry; for a road user, the body gap (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the reach, ahead and at or to the right of the subject (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame'). Neither atom is used for a clearance it excludes: surface_gap is the body gap itself; bearing is a direction only.

operationalizations.standard: a rate of speed commensurate with the speed of nearby traffic
operationalizations.convention: Traveling is the subject's speed (kin.speed) above the source's speed resolution (p.halt_speed_tolerance). The subject's speed is commensurate with the nearby traffic (s4b: traffic road users within p.nearby_traffic_reach, two seconds of headway at urban speed) where each such road user's speed exceeds the subject's by no more than p.commensurate_speed_margin, a speed differential within one traffic stream; the bound moves with both measured speeds.

operationalizations.standard: when doing so would not be safe
operationalizations.convention: Not safe is read through the two conditions subsection 2 names: (a) an object, vehicle, bicycle or pedestrian on the subject's right within p.right_side_impede_reach (s13), the distance within which a rider must steer around it; (b) the lane the subject occupies narrower than p.shared_lane_min_width (s14), the wide-outside-lane width of bicycle facility guidance below which a bicycle and a motor vehicle cannot share a lane side by side.

operationalizations.standard: as near to the right side of the roadway as practicable
operationalizations.convention: As near as practicable is a gap between the subject's body and the roadway's right edge of at most p.bicycle_keep_right_gap: a bicyclist's shy distance from a curb or edge plus the sway of its operating space and the source's position error (AASHTO bicycle operating space).

operationalizations.standard: the conditions under which it is not safe ... include, without limitation
operationalizations.convention: The catch-all 'include, without limitation' is read only through the contracts s13 and s14 read: obstructions and road users of the named aggregates on the subject's right within p.right_side_impede_reach, and a lane narrower than p.shared_lane_min_width.

operationalizations.standard: a lane too narrow for a bicycle and a vehicle to travel safely side by side within the lane
operationalizations.convention: The lane the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane) has a width (st.lane_width, 'width of a lane at a point') below p.shared_lane_min_width: 14 ft, the lane width below which bicycle facility guidance (AASHTO, MUTCD shared-lane guidance) holds that a bicycle and a motor vehicle cannot travel safely side by side within one lane; the bicycle and the vehicle are the design road users the width stands for, not road users present in the scene.

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

NRS_484B_777_1_o1.applicability: The subject is a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregate and its footprint overlaps a roadway at the observation, and none of the exceptions holds there (an exception that holds disengages the duty: the verdict is not applicable): (a) the subject is traveling (speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), complies with NRS_484B_785_1a (its lawful speed: the accepted record that an electric scooter on a roadway or bicycle lane or path travels at no more than its stated speed; a subject it does not engage complies), and every road user of the traffic aggregate other than the subject whose body gap to it is within p.nearby_traffic_reach has a speed no greater than the subject's plus p.commensurate_speed_margin (vacuously true where no such road user is nearby); (b) for some roadway r the subject occupies, some highway h on which r lies (st.on_way), and some intersection or driveway/alley entrance t lying on h (st.on_way), the source's declaration current at the observation states int.left_turn for the subject at t; (c) not safe: some obstruction o lies ahead of the subject within p.right_side_impede_reach along the designated direction of a roadway the subject occupies (prim.region_offset_along from zero to the reach, both inclusive) with a lateral offset from the subject at or below zero (on its right or overlapping its line), or some road user of the vehicle, bicycle or pedestrian aggregate other than the subject has a body gap to the subject within p.right_side_impede_reach and a bearing whose longitudinal component is positive and lateral component at or below zero, or the subject occupies a lane whose width is below p.shared_lane_min_width.
NRS_484B_777_1_o1.obligation: At the observation the subject rides as near the right side of the roadway as practicable: with r a roadway the subject occupies, for some road edge e lying on a highway on which r lies, with e's lateral offset from the subject negative (on its right), the magnitude of that offset less half the subject's width (kin.extent) is at most p.bicycle_keep_right_gap. Where no road edge on a highway of r lies on the subject's right in the scene, or the offset is unobserved, the verdict is unknown (definedWhen), never violated.

narrowings.why: 'person operating' is read through the device's controlled motion on the roadway, whoever controls it.

The catch-all 'include, without limitation' is read only through the contracts s13 and s14 read: obstructions, and road users of the vehicle, bicycle and pedestrian aggregates, in the rider's way on its right, and a lane narrower than the shared-lane width; other unsafe conditions, among them road users of no named aggregate (electric bicycles and electric scooters, which the vehicle and bicycle definitions leave out), are not read.
The right side is read relative to the subject's heading (the primitive's frame), and the edge is a mapped road edge on a highway the occupied roadway lies on.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides at 5 m/s on a roadway whose outside lane is 5.0 m wide, its body 2.5 m from the right road edge; a car of the vehicle and traffic aggregates travels the same way at 13 m/s with a body gap of 20 m behind it; no obstruction or other road user is on its right, no intersection or driveway entrance is in the scene, so no left turn is declared.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the bicycle rides with its body 0.6 m from the right road edge.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a sidewalk, its footprint overlapping no roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source maps regions without their outlines, so the road edge's lateral offset from the bicycle is unobserved.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides alone at 5 m/s in the middle of a 5.0 m outside lane, 2.5 m from the right edge; no other road user is in the scene, so its speed is commensurate with any nearby traffic vacuously and, a bicycle not being engaged by NRS_484B_785_1a, lawful: exception (a) holds and the duty does not arise.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the outside lane is 3.5 m wide, below the shared-lane width (exception (c), s14).

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but a parked car of the vehicle aggregate stands 10 m ahead of the bicycle on its right, at the curb (exception (c), s13).

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but an intersection lying on the highway of the roadway the bicycle occupies lies ahead, and the source declares int.left_turn for the bicycle at it (exception (b)).

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but an intersection lying on another highway, on which no roadway the bicycle occupies lies, is in the scene, and the source declares int.left_turn for the bicycle at it: that is no left turn off the roadway the bicycle is upon, so exception (b) does not hold.

segmentation.text: A pedestrian
shall not suddenly leave a curb or other place of safety and walk or run into the path of a vehicle
which is so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield.

elements.justification: 'A pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...').

Leaving 'a curb or other place of safety' is the pedestrian's footprint (rel.occupies) coming onto the roadway (st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') from a place pedestrians are safe from vehicles: the sidewalk the curb bounds (st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'), a safety zone (st.safety_zone, 'an area within the highway marked off for pedestrians only') or a median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider). st.sidewalk is not used for a crosswalk, as its exclusion requires; st.roadway is not used for the sidewalk. 'into the path of a vehicle': the vehicle is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; the pedestrian is in its path where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance). These primitives are 'Not a stand-in for' contact or danger alone; here they bound the path the vehicle will sweep, the clearance and horizon set by the reading, and the impossibility is decided by the standard.

operationalizations.standard: so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield
operationalizations.convention: stopping-distance model: the vehicle cannot yield where the time to the predicted closest approach (prim.closest_approach_time) is less than the driver's perception-reaction time plus the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) divided by twice the braking deceleration, written as a product (2·a·t_ca < 2·a·t_r + v); the deceleration is selected by the surface: icy or snow-covered (env.ice_or_snow), else wet (env.wet_road), else dry

NRS_484B_283_1b.applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) that leaves a place of safety at this observation: its footprint overlaps a roadway (st.roadway) here, and at the previous observation it overlapped no roadway and overlapped a sidewalk, a safety zone or a median or divider. The duty does not apply where NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject, nor where LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2 is engaged for a vehicle v of the scene.
NRS_484B_283_1b.obligation: There is no vehicle v (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) such that the closest approach of the subject and v falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance) and 2·a·t < 2·a·p.driver_reaction_time + speed(v), where t is prim.closest_approach_time with horizon p.conflict_horizon, speed(v) is v's kin.speed, and a is p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_decel_wet where env.wet_road holds, else p.following_decel_dry. With no vehicle in the scene, compliant.

narrowings.why: 'suddenly' is read through the vehicle's closeness at the moment the pedestrian leaves the place of safety: a departure is sudden in the law's sense where the vehicle is already too close to yield; the pedestrian's own abruptness is not measured.
'other place of safety' is read only through the sidewalk the curb bounds, a safety zone and a median or dividing section.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's motion: whether the vehicle can stop, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry road. The pedestrian steps from the sidewalk onto the roadway while a car 12 m away moves toward it at 12 m/s; predicted closest approach 0.5 m in 1.0 s, below 1.5 s + 12/(2·6) s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps off while the car is 70 m away at 12 m/s: no closest approach within the horizon.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian stays on the sidewalk throughout.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car is 12 m away at 12 m/s on a collision course, but whether the pedestrian's footprint overlaps the roadway or the sidewalk is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps off the sidewalk with no vehicle in the scene: the duty binds the pedestrian alone and is met.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hayward 1972; Swedish traffic conflict technique)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.driver_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: perception-reaction time of an alert driver to an expected hazard in the stopping-distance model
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance; perception-reaction studies

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a dry paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.6)
param_proposals.source: tire-pavement friction tables of accident reconstruction handbooks

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_wet
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a wet paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.4)
param_proposals.source: tire-pavement friction tables of accident reconstruction handbooks

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.1)
param_proposals.source: tire-pavement friction tables of accident reconstruction handbooks

segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are not in place or not in operation,
the driver of a vehicle
shall yield the right-of-way,
slowing down or stopping if need be so to yield,
to a pedestrian crossing the highway within a crosswalk
when the pedestrian is upon the half of the highway upon which the vehicle is traveling or onto which the vehicle is turning,
or when the pedestrian is approaching so closely from the opposite half of the highway as to be in danger.

As used in this section, “half of the highway” means all traffic lanes of a highway which are designated for traffic traveling in one direction, and includes the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway.

elements.justification: The official traffic-control devices (DEF-NRS-484A-145: every 'sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic') that regulate a crosswalk crossing are the vehicular signal heads (dev.traffic_signal, state including 'dark') and pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal, state including 'dark') that control the travel regions the vehicle and the pedestrian are in: dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'), with rel.occupies anchoring each road user in a governed region (kind st.travel_region). 'not in operation' is a head showing 'dark' or dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'); 'not in place' is no such head governing those regions. dev.governs is used for control, not for a position, as its exclusion requires.

'the driver of a vehicle' maps, as in the run's index, to the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions decided by the reading); 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Yielding the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another') is observed as the vehicle not reaching the pedestrian: no rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap') and the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) bounded as the standard below sets; as mapped in the run's index for 'shall yield the right-of-way'.

'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'crossing the highway within a crosswalk': the crosswalk (DEF-NRS-484A-065: 'That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway ... distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing') is st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'), marked or unmarked, so the definition's whole extent is kept; rel.occupies places the pedestrian's footprint in it.

By the section's own definition, a half of the highway is 'all traffic lanes ... designated for traffic traveling in one direction': the pedestrian's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a lane (st.lane) or a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway') whose designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') points with the vehicle's heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points'): the half on which the vehicle travels, or, while it turns, the half its heading has turned onto. kin.heading is read as the direction of travel of a vehicle driven forward; st.lane 'Not a stand-in for' a half of the roadway does not apply because the half is assembled from the lanes' designated directions, as the definition itself builds it.

The section's definition of 'half of the highway' ('all traffic lanes of a highway which are designated for traffic traveling in one direction', 'the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway') is carried by the lanes (st.lane) grouped by their designated direction (st.lane_direction) and by a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'), the atoms c3 and st2 read.

operationalizations.standard: slowing down or stopping if need be so to yield (the right-of-way's 'danger of a crash unless one grants precedence')
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves (speed above the halt tolerance), a predicted closest approach of the two centres within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance is a danger of a crash the driver has not yielded to; a vehicle at rest has slowed or stopped as need be

operationalizations.standard: approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a pedestrian in the crosswalk on a lane whose designated direction points against the vehicle's heading is in danger where the predicted closest approach of the two centres falls within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance

NRS_484B_283_1a.applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), not engaged by LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. Devices are not in place or not in operation: every traffic signal head (dev.traffic_signal) that governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies shows dark or is inoperative (dev.inoperative). There is a pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps a crosswalk (st.crosswalk), such that every pedestrian signal head governing a travel region p occupies shows dark, p is not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A or LVMC_11_30_060_B, and either (a) p's footprint overlaps a lane or one-way roadway whose designated direction (st.lane_direction) has a positive dot product with the subject's heading (kin.heading) — the subject's half — or (b) otherwise (p on the opposite half) the predicted closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).
NRS_484B_283_1a.obligation: For every such pedestrian p: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and where the subject's speed (kin.speed) is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, it is not the case that the closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hayward 1972; Swedish traffic conflict technique)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsections 3 and 4,
a driver
shall not drive on the left side of the highway within such zone or drive across or on the left side of any pavement striping designed to mark such zone throughout its length.
A driver may drive across a pavement striping marking such zone
to an adjoining highway if the driver has first given the appropriate turn signal
and there will be no impediment to
oncoming or following traffic.
Except where otherwise provided,
a driver may drive across a pavement striping marking such a zone
to make a left-hand turn
if the driver has first given the appropriate turn signal
in compliance with NRS 484B.413 [NRS-484B-413-2],
if it is safe
and if it would not be an impediment to
oncoming or following traffic.

elements.justification: DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'driver' means 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle'. The driver is a relational role, not membership (ru.aggregate: 'Not a stand-in for: a relational role such as who drives or controls a vehicle'), so the role is read through the controlled motion of the vehicle (observable_reading agency) and the binder is the vehicle, 'true when the user carries an included class' of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the same mapping the index records for 'a driver'.

(i) The left side of the highway is the side to the left of the line dividing its two directions: st.centre_line, 'the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway', tied to the highway the subject occupies by st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') and rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') on st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines'; we read the way, not the roadway, so its exclusion does not apply). Being on the left side is read with prim.region_lateral_offset, 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', against half the body's width from kin.extent ('a formula reads the full length, width and height'): the body is on the left side where the line's offset is below half the width by more than p.lateral_position_tolerance. (ii) 'Such zone' is the no-passing zone the section's first subsection lets an authority indicate 'by appropriate signs or markings'. A sign: dev.zone_sign, 'a sign that begins or ends a signed zone along the road; kind in {..., no_passing, ...}; end attribute', with dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', on a st.travel_region the subject occupies (rel.occupies); the sign read is a beginning sign (end false); its 'Not a stand-in for: whether the condition holds now' does not apply since no legend condition is read. A marking: st.lane_marking, 'per side of a lane: type in {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}, colour in {white, yellow, other}', on the left side of the st.lane the subject occupies: a solid or double_solid yellow line marks the zone for that lane; a solid_broken line, whose solid half the atom does not place, leaves membership unknown. The zone's presence on the road is the evidence of its designation (status). (iii) The pavement striping designed to mark the zone is that no-passing marking (st.lane_marking type solid or double_solid, colour yellow, on the left side of the subject's lane), which on a two-way highway lies along st.centre_line. Driving across it or on its left side is the body reaching past that line: prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line ('left positive') below half the width from kin.extent less p.lateral_position_tolerance. 'Throughout its length' is read by judging every observation at which the subject is in the zone.

The permitted act is the same crossing the obligation forbids: the vehicle's body reaching past the zone's centre-line striping, prim.region_lateral_offset ('left positive') against half the kin.extent width; 'A driver' is the vehicle, as in s2.

'To an adjoining highway' states where the crossing leads, a purpose read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading purpose): within p.vehicle_turn_window ahead the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') other than the highway h of the zone and no longer occupies h. 'Has first given the appropriate turn signal': sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state in {off, left, right}', showing left, or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {..., left, ...}', meaning left, at the last observation before the crossing began (the crossing having held at every observation since). The indicator's 'Not a stand-in for: the turn or lane change itself' does not apply: the signal is read, not the manoeuvre.

The same crossing as s6 (prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line against half the kin.extent width) by the vehicle. The region at which the left-hand turn of s11 is declared is the place a left turn across this zone's striping leaves the zone's highway for: st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet'; 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there') or st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'), tied to the zone's highway h (st.highway, the one the subject occupies) by st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'): the turn made by crossing the striping of h is a turn off h at a place on h. The declared intention takes one of them as its target.

'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'; ru.aggregate is 'true when the user carries an included class'. Oncoming: rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing', with tolerance p.oncoming_heading_cos; its exclusion (not the direction a road user approaches an intersection from) does not apply, as the words concern road users meeting the subject head-on on this highway. Following: a member behind the subject, 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for ... immediately to the rear)' (rel.bearing, negative longitudinal component), with 'headings aligned' (rel.same_direction, tolerance p.contest_same_direction_cos).

As s8b: members of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic that are oncoming (rel.oncoming, 'headings opposed and closing') or following (behind by rel.bearing, 'immediately to the rear', with rel.same_direction, 'headings aligned').

The appropriate signal for a crossing to the left to make a left-hand turn is sig.turn_indicator state left or sig.hand_signal meaning left ('a driver's or rider's arm signal'), given at the last observation before the crossing began. Its manner and distance are the compliance with NRS 484B.413 composed on s13, which NRS 484B.413(2) fixes to the course change of the turn ('prior to changing the course of a vehicle'): that event can precede the crossing of the striping, since the heading turns off the lane's direction before the body reaches past the centre line, so the composition is read at the observation of that course change (the last observation, within p.vehicle_turn_window behind, at which NRS_484B_413_2 engages for the subject), through a past operator, not at the crossing observations alone. Not the turn itself (indicator's exclusion).

operationalizations.standard: no impediment to oncoming or following traffic
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a road user of traffic is impeded where its centre and the subject's, under constant velocities, approach within the conflict horizon to a centre distance below the conflict clearance; oncoming is rel.oncoming within the opposed-heading tolerance, following is a road user behind the subject (negative longitudinal bearing) with headings aligned within the same-direction tolerance; read at every observation of the crossing

operationalizations.standard: it is safe
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the crossing is safe where no road user of the scene is in contact with the subject and none approaches the subject's centre, under constant velocities, within the conflict horizon to a centre distance below the conflict clearance; read at every observation of the crossing

operationalizations.standard: no impediment to oncoming or following traffic
operationalizations.convention: as for s8: traffic-conflict technique on oncoming (rel.oncoming) and following (behind, headings aligned) members of traffic, read at every observation of the crossing

intentions.meaning: the source's current plan for the road user includes a turn to the left at the target region, the plan's preparation for that turn included

residues.why: 'Except where otherwise provided' defers to provisions it does not name; those provisions are judged by their own rules, and this rule's verdict on crossing the striping to make a left-hand turn is the same whether or not they apply.

NRS_484B_217_2.applicability: The subject, a vehicle, occupies a highway h on which a centre line c lies (st.on_way), and is within a no-passing zone: it occupies a travel region that a dev.zone_sign of kind no_passing (end false) governs, or it occupies a lane whose left-side st.lane_marking is solid or double_solid and yellow (where that marking is solid_broken, membership is unknown).
NRS_484B_217_2.obligation: For every highway h the subject occupies and every centre line c on h, at every such observation the subject's body does not reach past c to its left: the lateral offset of c from the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset, left positive) is not below half the subject's width (kin.extent) minus p.lateral_position_tolerance. A crossing is excused (E3) where, within p.vehicle_turn_window ahead, the subject occupies a highway other than h and no longer occupies h; at the last observation before the crossing began (the crossing having held at every observation since) its turn indicator showed left or its hand signal meant left; and at the observation no member of traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) other than the subject that is oncoming (rel.oncoming, p.oncoming_heading_cos) or following (behind by rel.bearing, rel.same_direction within p.contest_same_direction_cos) has a closest approach to the subject within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. A crossing is also excused (E4) where: the subject's declared intention int.left_turn holds at the observation at an intersection or a driveway/alley entrance lying on h (st.on_way); the left signal was given as in E3; the signal complied with NRS_484B_413_2 for the course change of this turn, read where that course change occurred: within the p.vehicle_turn_window behind the observation (time), at the last observation at which NRS_484B_413_2 engages for the subject (ruleApplies, its rise of a course departure), NRS_484B_413_2 is complied with (rule, atLast); where it engages at no observation of that window the composition holds (a rule not engaged counts as complied); a window reaching before the recording is unknown; no road user other than the subject is in contact with it or has such a closest approach (safe); and no oncoming or following member of traffic has such a closest approach (impediment). Otherwise the crossing is a violation.

narrowings.why: 'a driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it

The striping designed to mark the zone is read where it lies along the centre line dividing the two directions; a no-passing marking between two lanes of the same direction is not read as the zone's striping.
'to an adjoining highway' is read through the conduct it explains: the subject reaching another highway within the turn window after the crossing
'impediment' is read only through closest-approach conflicts with oncoming or following road users of traffic; a slowing of traffic without such a conflict is not read
'impediment' is read only through closest-approach conflicts with oncoming or following road users of traffic

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle occupies a lane whose left st.lane_marking is solid yellow; it moves left until prim.region_lateral_offset of the centre line is -1.0 m to overtake a slower vehicle; int.left_turn is declared false at every region and it stays on the same highway.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the same no-passing lane (left marking solid yellow) and keeps the centre line 0.9 m to its left with a body width of 1.8 m plus margin: the offset stays above half its width minus the tolerance.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject's lane has a broken white left marking and no no_passing dev.zone_sign governs any region it occupies; it crosses the centre line to overtake.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source does not observe st.lane_marking and no zone sign is in the scene; the subject's body reaches past the centre line.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: In the no-passing zone (asm.business_or_residence_district declared true at every observation) the subject's int.left_turn is declared true at a driveway_or_alley_entrance on the zone's highway; while still in its own lane its heading turns off the lane's direction to the left (NRS_484B_413_2 engages there, within the turn window before the crossing), its left indicator having been on for the last 120 m before that course change, so NRS_484B_413_2 is complied with; it then crosses the centre line; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1 but sig.turn_indicator is off and sig.hand_signal no_signal at the observation before the crossing.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1 but an oncoming vehicle (rel.oncoming) has a closest approach to the subject in 2 s at a centre distance of 1 m.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As branch_1 (asm.business_or_residence_district declared true, the heading turning left off the subject's lane direction while it still occupies that lane, before the crossing) but the left indicator came on only 10 m before that course change and stays on through the crossing, so NRS_484B_413_2 is violated at the course change although a signal was given at the observation before the crossing.

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: In the zone the subject signals left, crosses the centre line and within the turn window occupies another highway and no longer the zone's highway; no oncoming or following road user has a conflicting closest approach.

segmentation.text: When overtaking or passing
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
proceeding in the same direction,
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall exercise due care and:
If there is only one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction,
pass to the left of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter
at a safe distance, which must be not less than 3 feet between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter,
and shall not move again to the right side of the highway
until the vehicle is safely clear of the overtaken bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.
Except as otherwise provided in NRS 484B.213 and 484B.217 [NRS-484B-213-1, NRS-484B-213-2a, NRS-484B-213-2b, NRS-484B-213-2c, NRS-484B-217-2],

when passing to the left of a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter at a safe distance of not less than 3 feet between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter, this paragraph authorizes the driver, if it is safe, to pass: (1) To the left of the center of the highway. (2) In a no-passing zone.

elements.justification: 'overtaking or passing' a road user proceeding the same way is drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; it denotes the relative motion only. The pass is under way while the bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero; a projection, not a contact or a distance), within the window behind the pass's recognition.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole, as the index maps 'a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter'.

'proceeding' is the overtaken road user moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); 'in the same direction' is rel.same_direction ('headings aligned') between the subject and it, as the index maps 'proceeding in the same direction,'.
'a motor vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'). 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.standard: shall exercise due care
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the pass is made with due care where the subject's body never touches the overtaken rider's (rel.contact) and the rider is never made to brake harder than an evasive deceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal below its negative) while the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero); care is a state of mind, read only through this outcome

residues.why: the authorization lets a driver passing a rider at the stated clearance pass left of the center or in a no-passing zone, conduct other rules (NRS 484B.213, 484B.217) forbid; it relaxes those rules and leaves the duties of this paragraph unchanged: the duty of care is the same whether or not the authorization holds

NRS_484B_270_2b_o1.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. At the observation, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r) rises, with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos, for some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, which at some observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window was moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos). The authorization (b12), suspended where NRS_484B_213_1, NRS_484B_213_2a, NRS_484B_213_2b, NRS_484B_213_2c or NRS_484B_217_2 applies, does not change this duty.
NRS_484B_270_2b_o1.obligation: Surrogate. For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection): at every observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window, the subject is not in contact with r (rel.contact), and wherever the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) r's longitudinal acceleration (kin.accel_longitudinal) is not below the negative of p.rider_evasive_decel.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'due care' is read only through the pass's outcome for the rider: no contact and no evasive braking while side by side; the rule is a surrogate

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a road with one lane in the subject's direction, a bicycle is ridden ahead of the subject car; the subject car overtakes it and its mirror touches the bicyclist while side by side.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same pass, made without contact; the bicyclist keeps its speed.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car overtakes another car; no bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is in the scene. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in permit, but the source does not observe contact between bodies.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car overtakes an electric bicycle without touching it, but while they are side by side the rider brakes harder than the evasive deceleration.

elements.justification: 'overtaking or passing' a road user proceeding the same way is drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; it denotes the relative motion only, the side being read by b7. 'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole.

'only one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction' is the count of lanes in the direction of a lane (st.lane) the overtaken rider occupies (rel.occupies) being the stated one (st.lane_adjacency, 'the count of lanes in that direction'; not the marking between lanes). 'traffic' names the users of the lane; no membership is read.

'pass to the left of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter' (the overtaken road user of b2, its aggregates claimed again for these words): at every observation of the pass at which the two are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), the rider lies on the subject's right: the lateral component of its bearing in the subject's frame (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of" ...)') is negative.

operationalizations.standard: at a safe distance, which must be not less than 3 feet between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle
operationalizations.convention: lateral passing clearance: the distance between the nearest points of the two bodies (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', which is the distance between any portion of the vehicle and the rider's device) is at least the larger of the stated 3 feet and the bicyclist operating-space clearance the reading sets, at every observation at which the two are side by side

residues.why: the authorization lets a driver passing a rider at the stated clearance pass left of the center or in a no-passing zone, conduct other rules (NRS 484B.213, 484B.217) forbid; it relaxes those rules and leaves the duty to pass on the left at a safe distance unchanged

NRS_484B_270_2b_o2.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. At the observation, drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r) rises, with window p.overtake_window and same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos, for some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, which at some observation of that window was moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos); and at some observation of that window at which the two were side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), r occupied a st.lane whose count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) is the literal one.
NRS_484B_270_2b_o2.obligation: For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection): at every observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window at which the subject and r are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), r lies on the subject's right (rel.bearing from the subject, lateral component negative) and the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) is at least the larger of the literal 3 ft and p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'a safe distance' is read as one lateral clearance the reading sets, never below the stated 3 feet; the clearance does not grow with the subject's speed

and shall not move again to the right side of the highway
until the vehicle is safely clear of the overtaken bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.
Except as otherwise provided in NRS 484B.213 and 484B.217 [NRS-484B-213-1, NRS-484B-213-2a, NRS-484B-213-2b, NRS-484B-213-2c, NRS-484B-217-2],

when passing to the left of a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter at a safe distance of not less than 3 feet between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter, this paragraph authorizes the driver, if it is safe, to pass: (1) To the left of the center of the highway. (2) In a no-passing zone.

elements.justification: 'overtaking or passing' a road user proceeding the same way is drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; it denotes the relative motion only. Here the pass is read while under way - the bodies side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero; a projection, not a contact or a distance) after the rider was ahead within the window - and once completed, from the observation at which the concept rises, within the window.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole.
'proceeding' is the overtaken road user moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); 'in the same direction' is rel.same_direction ('headings aligned') between the subject and it.
'a motor vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'). 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'only one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction' is the count of lanes in the direction of a lane (st.lane) the overtaken rider occupies (rel.occupies) being the stated one (st.lane_adjacency, 'the count of lanes in that direction'). 'traffic' names the users of the lane; no membership is read.

'move again to the right side of the highway': having moved out to the left of the rider (rel.bearing from the subject, lateral component negative: the rider on its right), the subject turns back toward the side the rider keeps: drv.lane.heading_right_of_carrier(subject, L) for a lane L (st.lane) the rider occupies (rel.occupies) - 'a, moving, points to the right of the designated direction of travel of carrier region r by more than a tolerance'. The concept says nothing of whether the subject occupies L, so it reads a move back toward the rider's lane from the opposing lane or from the left part of the rider's lane alike. 'again' fixes the order: the subject first had the rider on its right.

operationalizations.standard: until the vehicle is safely clear of the overtaken bicycle
operationalizations.convention: time headway: the subject (the vehicle) is safely clear of the overtaken rider where the rider is behind it (rel.bearing longitudinal component negative, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with a gap between the bodies (rel.surface_gap) of at least the rider's speed times the following headway for the surface - ice or snow, else wet road or precipitation, else dry - so that the rider, following, keeps the headway a following road user keeps

residues.why: the authorization lets a driver passing a rider at the stated clearance pass left of the center or in a no-passing zone, conduct other rules (NRS 484B.213, 484B.217) forbid; it relaxes those rules and leaves the duty not to move back right before being clear unchanged

NRS_484B_270_2b_o3.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. Some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos), is being overtaken by the subject: at some observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window r was ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with aligned headings, and either r is not yet behind the subject or drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r) (window p.overtake_window, same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos) has risen at some observation of that window; r lies on the subject's right (rel.bearing lateral component negative); and r occupies a st.lane whose count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) is the literal one.
NRS_484B_270_2b_o3.obligation: For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection), where r is not safely clear behind the subject - that is, not (r behind the subject, rel.bearing longitudinal component negative and rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, with rel.surface_gap at least r's kin.speed times the headway: p.following_headway_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry) - the subject does not move to the right: drv.lane.heading_right_of_carrier(subject, L) with sin_tol p.course_departure_sin_tol and speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance holds for no st.lane L that r occupies (rel.occupies).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

'move again to the right side of the highway' is read as the subject's heading turned to the right of the rider's lane direction beyond the course tolerance, after it has the rider on its right; a gradual drift within that tolerance is not read
'safely clear' is read as the rider behind the subject at a time-headway gap at the rider's speed; the rider's own braking ability is not otherwise read

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Road with one lane in the subject's direction; the subject car moves out left and overtakes a bicycle; while the bicycle is still beside it, the subject car steers back to the right, its heading turning right of the lane's direction beyond the course tolerance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same pass; the subject car keeps its course until the bicycle is behind it at a gap above the bicycle's speed times the dry headway, then steers back right.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives alone on a road with one lane in its direction and steers to the right; no other road user is in the scene, so no bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is being overtaken. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe the lanes' designated direction of travel, so whether the subject's heading turned right of the rider's lane is unknown while the rider, still beside it, is decided not clear.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car completes the pass of a bicycle on a road with one lane in its direction and steers back right at once, as the pass is recognized, the bicycle behind it at a gap below its speed times the dry headway.

scenarios.name: branch_2
