`NRS_484B_307_8b`: the repair session withdrew it — the vocabulary lacks atom `A relation between a road user and the signal head that faces it: which vehicular signal head's face is directed at a given pedestrian (the head's face orientation, or a road-user-faces-device relation), so that the head named by 'facing such a signal' is tied to the subject. The only reading the vocabulary allows is the pedestrian's heading compared with the line to the head's location (kin.heading, kin.position, dev.position). That says only that the pedestrian looks toward the head. It does not say that the head's face is addressed to the pedestrian. The gate also does not accept that comparison as tying the device variable to the subject (UNANCHORED_VARIABLE, run twice, including with the comparisons rewritten without products). The anchors the gate accepts do not carry the words. dev.governs ties a device only to travel regions. A vehicular head that a crossing pedestrian faces governs the approach lanes of traffic moving parallel to that pedestrian, or the junction itself. It does not govern the roadway the pedestrian steps onto. Requiring the faced head to govern the region entered would leave the duty unengaged in the ordinary case: a pedestrian at a corner facing the far-side head for parallel traffic and stepping into the cross street. Tying it by a distance to some governed region would add a condition the words do not state. The span decides which road users the steady red alone addresses: the pedestrians the duty concerns.` for span s3; gap G96 filed, law blocked

segmentation.text: When overtaking or passing
a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
proceeding in the same direction,
the driver of a motor vehicle
shall exercise due care and:
If there is only one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction,
pass to the left of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter
at a safe distance, which must be not less than 3 feet between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter,
and shall not move again to the right side of the highway
until the vehicle is safely clear of the overtaken bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.
Except as otherwise provided in NRS 484B.213 and 484B.217 [NRS-484B-213-1, NRS-484B-213-2a, NRS-484B-213-2b, NRS-484B-213-2c, NRS-484B-217-2],

when passing to the left of a bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter at a safe distance of not less than 3 feet between any portion of the vehicle and the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter, this paragraph authorizes the driver, if it is safe, to pass: (1) To the left of the center of the highway. (2) In a no-passing zone.

elements.justification: 'overtaking or passing' a road user proceeding the same way is drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r): 'a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; it denotes the relative motion only. Here the pass is read while under way - the bodies side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero; a projection, not a contact or a distance) after the rider was ahead within the window - and once completed, from the observation at which the concept rises, within the window.

'a bicycle' is DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'an electric bicycle' DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, 'an electric scooter' DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed to be ridden on'); each admitted aggregate claimed whole.
'proceeding' is the overtaken road user moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance); 'in the same direction' is rel.same_direction ('headings aligned') between the subject and it.
'a motor vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'). 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

'only one lane for traffic proceeding in the same direction' is the count of lanes in the direction of a lane (st.lane) the overtaken rider occupies (rel.occupies) being the stated one (st.lane_adjacency, 'the count of lanes in that direction'). 'traffic' names the users of the lane; no membership is read.

'move again to the right side of the highway': having moved out to the left of the rider (rel.bearing from the subject, lateral component negative: the rider on its right), the subject turns back toward the side the rider keeps: drv.lane.heading_right_of_carrier(subject, L) for a lane L (st.lane) the rider occupies (rel.occupies) - 'a, moving, points to the right of the designated direction of travel of carrier region r by more than a tolerance'. The concept says nothing of whether the subject occupies L, so it reads a move back toward the rider's lane from the opposing lane or from the left part of the rider's lane alike. 'again' fixes the order: the subject first had the rider on its right.

operationalizations.standard: until the vehicle is safely clear of the overtaken bicycle
operationalizations.convention: time headway: the subject (the vehicle) is safely clear of the overtaken rider where the rider is behind it (rel.bearing longitudinal component negative, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with a gap between the bodies (rel.surface_gap) of at least the rider's speed times the following headway for the surface - ice or snow, else wet road or precipitation, else dry - so that the rider, following, keeps the headway a following road user keeps

residues.why: the authorization lets a driver passing a rider at the stated clearance pass left of the center or in a no-passing zone, conduct other rules (NRS 484B.213, 484B.217) forbid; it relaxes those rules and leaves the duty not to move back right before being clear unchanged

nodes.applicability: The subject is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle. Some road user r, not the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos), is being overtaken by the subject: at some observation of the window behind of length p.overtake_window r was ahead of the subject (rel.bearing longitudinal component positive, rel.longitudinal_overlap negative) with aligned headings, and either r is not yet behind the subject or drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, r) (window p.overtake_window, same_dir_cos p.overtake_same_direction_cos) has risen at some observation of that window; r lies on the subject's right (rel.bearing lateral component negative); and r occupies a st.lane whose count of lanes in its direction (st.lane_adjacency count) is the literal one.
nodes.obligation: For every such r (re-bound with its whole selection), where r is not safely clear behind the subject - that is, not (r behind the subject, rel.bearing longitudinal component negative and rel.longitudinal_overlap negative, with rel.surface_gap at least r's kin.speed times the headway: p.following_headway_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_headway_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.following_headway_dry) - the subject does not move to the right: drv.lane.heading_right_of_carrier(subject, L) with sin_tol p.course_departure_sin_tol and speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance holds for no st.lane L that r occupies (rel.occupies).

narrowings.why: 'the driver' of a motor vehicle is read through the vehicle's controlled motion

'move again to the right side of the highway' is read as the subject's heading turned to the right of the rider's lane direction beyond the course tolerance, after it has the rider on its right; a gradual drift within that tolerance is not read
'safely clear' is read as the rider behind the subject at a time-headway gap at the rider's speed; the rider's own braking ability is not otherwise read

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Road with one lane in the subject's direction; the subject car moves out left and overtakes a bicycle; while the bicycle is still beside it, the subject car steers back to the right, its heading turning right of the lane's direction beyond the course tolerance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same pass; the subject car keeps its course until the bicycle is behind it at a gap above the bicycle's speed times the dry headway, then steers back right.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives alone on a road with one lane in its direction and steers to the right; no other road user is in the scene, so no bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is being overtaken. The duty binds the subject alone.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the source does not observe the lanes' designated direction of travel, so whether the subject's heading turned right of the rider's lane is unknown while the rider, still beside it, is decided not clear.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject car completes the pass of a bicycle on a road with one lane in its direction and steers back right at once, as the pass is recognized, the bicycle behind it at a gap below its speed times the dry headway.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The road has two lanes in the subject's direction; the subject passes a bicycle and steers back right while beside it.

segmentation.text: When the signal is circular green alone:
Pedestrians
facing such a signal
may proceed across the highway
within any marked or unmarked crosswalk,
unless directed otherwise by another device as provided in NRS 484B.283 [NRS-484B-283-1d1, NRS-484B-283-1d2, NRS-484B-283-1d3, NRS-484B-283-1d4].

elements.justification: 'the signal is circular green alone' is a dev.traffic_signal d ('a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, ...}; several states may be displayed at once') displaying circular_green and no other state of its contract. 'The signal' is the traffic-control signal of the highway the pedestrian crosses, tied to it by relation atoms, never by distance: d controls an intersection i that lies on that highway w — either directly, dev.governs(d, i) ('or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself'), or through an approach it governs, dev.governs(d, g) for a travel region g (st.travel_region, 'the union of the kinds a device can govern') with st.lane_enters(g, i) ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), since dev.governs has 'no closure to the lanes that enter it' and a head is usually recorded on its approach lanes; and st.on_way(i, w) ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on ... an intersection lies on every way that meets there'), w of kind st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines', DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way'). A head facing a crossing pedestrian governs the traffic parallel to the crossing, not the lanes crossed, so the tie is to the intersection on the crossed highway, not to the crossed lane. Which of the heads so tied the pedestrian faces is s3's.

'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

As the index maps 'pedestrians facing the signal' (NRS_484B_283_1d1): facing is read from the head's location (dev.position 'location of the device head / sign face'; not a stand-in for a stop line or crossing, none is read) and the pedestrian's kin.position and kin.heading ('direction the body points'): the head lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the pedestrian and within the angle whose cosine is p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos of its heading (compared on squares: the dot product of the vector to the head with the heading is positive and its square at least that cosine squared times the vector's squared length). No atom carries the orientation of a signal face; the head ahead of the pedestrian within that angle is the head it faces. 'Such a signal' is the same d as s1, with s1's tie to the crossed highway: the facing comparison selects among the heads of that highway, never any head of the scene.

As the index maps 'crossing a roadway' (LVMC_11_30_060_A): proceeding across the highway is the pedestrian occupying (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a roadway r (st.roadway 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') and a lane l (st.lane 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles'), both lying on the highway w (st.on_way 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, ...'; st.highway, DEF-NRS-484A-095 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way'), while drv.motion.moving_across_carrier ('a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r') holds for l: the crossing of the highway is observed where it traverses the highway's lanes of travel. The lane is not read as a half of the roadway; st.roadway is not a stand-in for a sidewalk, which the crossing does not use. The highway w is the one s1's signal is tied to.

'within any marked or unmarked crosswalk' is the pedestrian's footprint overlapping a st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute'), which carries both limbs of DEF-NRS-484A-065; rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'.

nodes.applicability: There are a roadway r (st.roadway) and a highway w (st.highway) such that the subject, a pedestrian, occupies r (rel.occupies) and r lies on w (st.on_way(r, w)); and: (s4) the subject proceeds across the highway: it occupies a lane l (st.lane, rel.occupies) lying on w (st.on_way(l, w)) for which drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, l; p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.crossing_motion_cos) holds; (s1) some traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) displays circular_green and no other state of its contract, and d is a signal of the highway crossed: some intersection i (st.intersection) lies on w (st.on_way(i, w)) and either dev.governs(d, i), or dev.governs(d, g) for some travel region g (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(g, i); (s3) the subject faces that d: with Δ the vector from the subject's kin.position to d's dev.position and h the subject's kin.heading, h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach². Not where any of NRS_484B_283_1d1, NRS_484B_283_1d2, NRS_484B_283_1d3_o1, NRS_484B_283_1d3_o2, NRS_484B_283_1d4_o1 or NRS_484B_283_1d4_o2 applies to the subject (exception compositions, subject mapped to subject: another device directs the pedestrian as NRS 484B.283 provides).
nodes.obligation: The subject occupies a crosswalk (rel.occupies(subject, x) for some x of kind st.crosswalk, marked or unmarked): the crossing it makes under the circular green is within the scope of the permission the words grant.

narrowings.why: The words grant a permission and impose no duty of their own. The permission is read as its scope: a crossing of the highway by a pedestrian facing a circular green alone is within it where the pedestrian is within a marked or unmarked crosswalk; a crossing outside every crosswalk is outside the permission and is reported as a violation of this rule. Whether that crossing is also forbidden is decided by the rules on crossing elsewhere (NRS 484B.287).

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian (ru.aggregate pedestrian) crosses a st.lane of a st.roadway, both lying on a st.highway (st.on_way), at 1.3 m/s perpendicular to the lanes' designated direction (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier holds), 30 m from any st.crosswalk. A st.intersection lies on that highway, and a dev.traffic_signal head that governs a lane entering that intersection (dev.governs, st.lane_enters) stands 25 m straight ahead of the pedestrian (dev.position within the facing angle and reach) and displays circular_green alone; no pedestrian signal governs; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same pedestrian makes the same crossing within a marked crosswalk (rel.occupies st.crosswalk).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the signal the pedestrian faces displays circular_red.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, the pedestrian crosses outside a crosswalk while the head tied to the crossed highway displays circular_green alone, but the positions of the signal heads are not observed: whether it faces the signal cannot be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As in permit, and a dev.pedestrian_signal governing the crossed lanes and roadway displays dont_walk_steady, so NRS_484B_283_1d4_o1 applies to the pedestrian: another device directs it, and this rule does not apply.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, except that the green head straight ahead governs neither an intersection on the crossed highway nor any travel region entering one: it governs only a lane entering an intersection that lies on a different highway, which the crossed roadway and lanes do not lie on. The pedestrian faces a green head, but not a signal of the highway it crosses.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As in forbid, but the head displays circular_green together with green_arrow(left): the signal is not circular green alone.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracked-object kinematics in driving datasets and simulators

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability reported in crossing-behaviour studies

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a vehicular signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: MUTCD signal head placement (Part 4D) and pedestrian heading variability

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a vehicular signal head at which the head counts as one the pedestrian faces across the intersection: a wide urban intersection (about 40 m) plus the set-back of a far-side head beyond the far crosswalk
param_proposals.source: MUTCD far-side signal head placement (Part 4D) and urban intersection widths

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a green turn arrow alone:
Pedestrians
facing such a signal
shall not enter the highway
until permitted to proceed by another device as provided in NRS 484B.283 [NRS-484B-283-1d1, NRS-484B-283-1d2, NRS-484B-283-1d3, NRS-484B-283-1d4].

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal, 'a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, circular_yellow, circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once': a green turn arrow alone is the head displaying green_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn and no state other than green turn arrows (no circular indication, no straight arrow, no yellow, red or flashing arrow). Same words, same atom as the index (NRS_484B_307_4a_o1).

The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), claimed as ru.aggregate ('membership of a legal aggregate') and never replaced by the class atom ru.pedestrian.

'facing such a signal': the head of s1, at its position (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face'), lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the pedestrian's position (kin.position, 'position of the body's reference point'), and the pedestrian's heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') makes with the line from its position to the head an angle whose cosine is at least p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos. Not a stand-in: dev.position is read as the place of the head only, never as a stop line or crossing ('the distance to a signal head is a different quantity'). Same words, same atoms as the index (NRS_484B_307_2b). The head is tied to the subject's scene not by this comparison but by the highway of s4, which the head controls.

'the highway' is the definite highway: the one at which 'such a signal' stands and whose traffic it controls. The head controls a junction x (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'): it governs x itself (dev.governs, 'an intersection, read as control of the junction itself'), or it governs a carrier l (st.travel_region, the abstract kind of every region a device can govern) that runs into x (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'). 'The highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority') is each way w (st.highway, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders') on which x lies (st.on_way, 'an intersection lies on every way that meets there'): the device of the junction is tied to its ways by relation atoms, never by distance. 'shall not enter': the pedestrian's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a roadway (st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder') lying on w (st.on_way), having overlapped none at the previous observation. The pedestrian who faces the head from the sidewalk or the curb already lies within the highway's width, so the only entry the words can forbid is the step onto its roadway (narrowing on s4); st.roadway's exclusion ('Not a stand-in for: the sidewalk') is the distinction wanted.

nodes.applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian). At the judged observation there are a traffic signal head s (dev.traffic_signal), an intersection x (st.intersection) and a highway w (st.highway) such that: the subject faces s — s's position (dev.position) lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the subject's position (kin.position), and the cosine of the angle between the subject's heading (kin.heading) and the line from its position to s is at least p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos; s displays a green turn arrow alone (green_arrow with direction left, right or u_turn, and no state other than green turn arrows); s controls x: dev.governs(s, x), or dev.governs(s, l) for some travel region l (st.travel_region) with st.lane_enters(l, x); x lies on w (st.on_way(x, w)); and at the previous observation the subject's footprint overlapped (rel.occupies) no roadway r (st.roadway) with st.on_way(r, w). The duty does not apply where NRS_484B_283_1d1 or NRS_484B_283_1d2 applies to the subject (a pedestrian signal permits it to proceed across), nor where NRS_484B_283_1d3_o2 or NRS_484B_283_1d4_o2 applies (a pedestrian who entered lawfully continuing to cross).
nodes.obligation: For every head s, intersection x and highway w selected again with the applicability's whole selection (the subject faces s as stated there; s displays a green turn arrow alone; s governs x or a travel region that enters x; x lies on w; at the previous observation the subject overlapped no roadway lying on w), and for every roadway r (st.roadway) with st.on_way(r, w): the subject's footprint does not overlap r (rel.occupies). It does not step from the sidewalk, curb or other place off the roadway onto the roadway of the highway the signal controls while it faces the green turn arrow alone. Where whether a roadway lies on w, or whether the subject overlaps it, is unobserved and the verdict turns on it, unknown.

narrowings.why: 'enter the highway' is read as coming onto the roadway of a highway on which the junction the signal controls lies (the junction it governs, or the one a carrier it governs enters). The highway's defined extent includes the sidewalk, on which a pedestrian facing the head already stands, so read literally the words would never be engaged by the pedestrians they address; the entry they forbid is the step onto the vehicular part of the highway at that signal. Entry onto a shoulder or verge alone is not read as entry, and a roadway of a way that does not meet at that junction is not 'the highway'.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian stands on the corner sidewalk of a highway that meets another at a signalized intersection, 25 m from a vehicular head it faces (heading within 10 degrees of the line to the head) that governs a lane entering the intersection and displays green_arrow(left) alone; the pedestrian head it faces displays dont_walk_steady. At the next observation its footprint overlaps the roadway of a highway on which the intersection lies.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the pedestrian stays on the sidewalk while the head displays green_arrow(left) alone; its footprint never overlaps the roadway.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The head the pedestrian faces displays circular_green alone; it steps onto the roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source supplies no heading for the pedestrian: whether it faces the head is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the pedestrian head it faces displays walk: NRS_484B_283_1d1 applies to it and the duty of this paragraph does not.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the roadway the pedestrian steps onto lies on a way that does not meet at the intersection the head controls (no st.on_way to any highway on which that intersection lies); it never overlaps a roadway of the highway at the signal.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the head governs the intersection itself (dev.governs on the intersection) rather than an approach lane; the pedestrian steps onto the roadway of a highway on which that intersection lies.

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a vehicular signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_307_2b; repeated unchanged

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a vehicular signal head at which the head counts as one the pedestrian faces across the intersection: a wide urban intersection (about 40 m) plus the set-back of a far-side head beyond the far crosswalk
param_proposals.source: proposed this iteration by NRS_484B_307_2b; repeated unchanged
